### examples/common/info_log.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file examples/common/info_log.hpp
/// @brief The senders' log: the core's default sink prints Warning and Error
///        only, so serve_stream and fuse_orbbec install a handler that prints
///        Info too, as networking::StreamServer logs each viewer joining and
///        leaving at Info.

#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/log.hpp"

namespace vgrid_example {

/// @brief A log handler that writes each Info, Warning and Error message to
///        @p out as the core's default sink writes a line,
///        `[<source> <level>] <message>`, and drops Debug.
///
/// Each line goes out in one fwrite, so concurrent lines do not interleave.
inline volumetric_kit::core::LogHandler info_log_handler(std::FILE* out) {
  using volumetric_kit::core::LogLevel;
  return [out](LogLevel level, std::string_view source, std::string_view text) {
    if (level == LogLevel::Debug) return;
    const char* name = level == LogLevel::Info      ? "info"
                       : level == LogLevel::Warning ? "warning"
                                                    : "error";
    std::string line = "[";
    line.append(source.data(), source.size());
    line += ' ';
    line += name;
    line += "] ";
    line.append(text.data(), text.size());
    line += '\n';
    std::fwrite(line.data(), 1, line.size(), out);
  };
}

/// @brief Install @ref info_log_handler on stderr for the process.
inline void print_info_log() {
  volumetric_kit::core::set_log_handler(info_log_handler(stderr));
}

}  // namespace vgrid_example
```

### examples/common/interrupt.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file examples/common/interrupt.hpp
/// @brief Ctrl+C (or a SIGTERM) in the terminal ends a live example's run as
///        its own end would, rather than the process there, so the cameras
///        are released and what the run writes is finished. Killed outright,
///        the process would leave the cameras to notice the dropped
///        connection. The handler restores that signal's default, so a
///        second Ctrl+C, or a second SIGTERM, still ends a run that has hung.

#include <atomic>
#include <csignal>

namespace vgrid_example {

/// Set by the handler @ref catch_interrupts installs. Lock-free, as a signal
/// handler may only touch such an atomic.
inline std::atomic<bool> g_interrupted{false};
static_assert(std::atomic<bool>::is_always_lock_free,
              "the interrupt flag must be safe to set from a signal handler");

extern "C" inline void vgrid_example_on_interrupt(int signal) {
  g_interrupted.store(true);
  std::signal(signal, SIG_DFL);
}

/// @brief Catch SIGINT and SIGTERM: the first of either sets
///        @ref interrupted and restores that signal's default.
inline void catch_interrupts() {
  std::signal(SIGINT, vgrid_example_on_interrupt);
  std::signal(SIGTERM, vgrid_example_on_interrupt);
}

/// @return Whether a SIGINT or a SIGTERM has come since
///         @ref catch_interrupts.
inline bool interrupted() noexcept { return g_interrupted.load(); }

}  // namespace vgrid_example
```

### examples/common/stage_table.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file examples/common/stage_table.hpp
/// @brief The one table the examples print stage rows in: host busy, wait and
///        device milliseconds per unit of work. Header-only, the core's
///        `StageMetrics` alone.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"

namespace vgrid_example {

namespace vkc = volumetric_kit::core;

/// @return The nearest-rank @p percent th percentile of @p sorted, ascending
///         and not empty: its ceil(@p percent / 100 n)-th smallest.
template <typename T>
T nearest_rank(const std::vector<T>& sorted, std::size_t percent) {
  return sorted[(sorted.size() * percent + 99) / 100 - 1];
}

/// @return The mean, p50, p95 and max of @p values, each `%8.3f` and
///         space-separated, the percentiles by @ref nearest_rank: the cells
///         a table over many units of work prints for one figure.
/// @pre @p values is not empty.
inline std::string format_stats(std::vector<double> values) {
  std::sort(values.begin(), values.end());
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (const double v : values) sum += v;
  char text[64];
  std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%8.3f %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f",
                sum / static_cast<double>(values.size()),
                nearest_rank(values, 50), nearest_rank(values, 95),
                values.back());
  return text;
}

/// @return @p rows' row named @p name, or null.
inline const vkc::StageRow* find_row(const vkc::StageMetrics& rows,
                                     const char* name) {
  for (const vkc::StageRow& row : rows.rows()) {
    if (std::strcmp(row.name, name) == 0) return &row;
  }
  return nullptr;
}

/// @brief @p rows as a table, each divided by @p per:
///
///     <title> (ms: host busy / wait / device):
///       frame prep            0.934     0.300     0.800
///       allocate              0.500     0.000         -
///       integrate             1.100     2.400       n/t
///
/// Busy is the host span less its wait, the time it blocked on the device
/// (`StageRow::wait_ms`); the device column reads `n/t`
/// where the row's device work ran untimed, `n/a` where the queue cannot
/// time, and `-` for a host-only row. A breakdown row
/// (`StageMetrics::kBreakdownPrefix`) keeps its indent.
/// @param indent  Spaces before the title; the rows sit two further in.
/// @return The table, or an empty string when @p per is 0 or there is no
///         row.
inline std::string format_stage_rows(const std::string& title,
                                     const vkc::StageMetrics& rows,
                                     std::size_t per, int indent = 0) {
  if (per == 0 || rows.empty()) return {};
  const double n = static_cast<double>(per);
  const std::string pad(static_cast<std::size_t>(indent), ' ');
  std::string out = pad + title + " (ms: host busy / wait / device):\n";
  for (const vkc::StageRow& row : rows.rows()) {
    char device[32] = "-";
    switch (row.device) {
      case vkc::DeviceTime::Measured:
        std::snprintf(device, sizeof device, "%.3f", row.gpu_ms / n);
        break;
      case vkc::DeviceTime::NotTimed:
        std::snprintf(device, sizeof device, "n/t");
        break;
      case vkc::DeviceTime::Unavailable:
        std::snprintf(device, sizeof device, "n/a");
        break;
      case vkc::DeviceTime::None:
        break;
    }
    char line[160];
    std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "%s  %-18s %9.3f %9.3f %9s\n", pad.c_str(),
                  row.name, (row.cpu_ms - row.wait_ms) / n, row.wait_ms / n,
                  device);
    out += line;
  }
  return out;
}

/// @brief Print @ref format_stage_rows to stdout.
inline void print_stage_rows(const std::string& title,
                             const vkc::StageMetrics& rows, std::size_t per,
                             int indent = 0) {
  std::fputs(format_stage_rows(title, rows, per, indent).c_str(), stdout);
}

}  // namespace vgrid_example
```

### examples/common/stream_replay.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file examples/common/stream_replay.hpp
/// @brief A recorded track replayed in a loop as if live, as serve_stream
///        sends it.

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp"

namespace vgrid_example {

namespace vgrid = volumetric_kit::grid;
namespace vkc = volumetric_kit::core;

/// @brief One track's records, replayed pass after pass: each due at its pts
///        from the pass's start, and restamped so that seq keeps rising and
///        key pts never go back, as a live sender's do.
class ReplayLoop {
 public:
  using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

  /// @brief The loop over @p reader's track @p track: its records from its
  ///        first key read whole, in file order; a span the reader finds
  ///        damaged is left out.
  /// @return The loop; `InvalidArgument` for a track the session lacks;
  ///         `NotFound` for a track with no key read whole; the reader's
  ///         `IoError`; `OutOfMemory`, the reader's or the loop's own.
  static vkc::Result<ReplayLoop> create(
      const vgrid::stream::StreamReader& reader, std::uint16_t track = 0) {
    try {
      VKC_ASSIGN(vgrid::stream::Position pos, reader.key(track, 0));
      ReplayLoop loop;
      for (;;) {
        vgrid::stream::Record record;
        const vkc::Result<bool> more = reader.next(&pos, &record);
        if (!more.ok()) {
          // Only damage leaves pos past it; anything else is the loop's
          // failure, as an allocation's, which may leave pos where it was.
          const vkc::Status::Code code = more.status().domain();
          if (code != vkc::Status::Code::InvalidArgument &&
              code != vkc::Status::Code::Unsupported) {
            return more.status();
          }
          continue;  // damage: pos is past it
        }
        if (!*more) break;
        // Start at a key read whole: the P-frames after a damaged first key
        // lack theirs.
        if (record.info.track == track &&
            (record.info.key || !loop.records_.empty())) {
          loop.records_.push_back(record);
        }
      }
      if (loop.records_.empty()) {
        return vkc::Status::not_found("ReplayLoop: every key of track " +
                                      std::to_string(track) + " is damaged");
      }
      std::uint64_t least = loop.records_.front().info.pts_ns;
      std::uint64_t most = least;
      for (const vgrid::stream::Record& r : loop.records_) {
        least = std::min(least, r.info.pts_ns);
        most = std::max(most, r.info.pts_ns);
      }
      // One mean step past the span; with one record, or all at one pts, the
      // track's nominal period.
      std::uint64_t step = 0;
      if (loop.records_.size() > 1) {
        step = (most - least) / (loop.records_.size() - 1);
      }
      if (step == 0) {
        step = vgrid::stream::nominal_period_ns(
            reader.session().tracks[track].rate);
      }
      loop.first_pts_ = least;
      loop.pass_ns_ = most - least + step;
      loop.pass_seqs_ =
          loop.records_.back().info.seq - loop.records_.front().info.seq + 1;
      return loop;
    } catch (...) {
      return vkc::exception_status("ReplayLoop",
                                   vkc::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
    }
  }

  /// @return The records each pass replays, in file order.
  const std::vector<vgrid::stream::Record>& records() const noexcept {
    return records_;
  }

  /// @return When the record at @p pts_ns is due in pass @p pass of a loop
  ///         started at @p start: its pts after the records' least, a pass's
  ///         span after the pass before.
  Clock::time_point due(Clock::time_point start, std::uint64_t pass,
                        std::uint64_t pts_ns) const {
    return start +
           std::chrono::duration_cast<Clock::duration>(
               std::chrono::nanoseconds(pass * pass_ns_ + pts_ns - first_pts_));
  }

  /// @return @p info as pass @p pass sends it: seq past the passes' before,
  ///         and pts a pass's span (the records' pts span and one mean step)
  ///         later each pass. Pass 0 is unchanged.
  vgrid::stream::RecordInfo restamp(vgrid::stream::RecordInfo info,
                                    std::uint64_t pass) const {
    info.seq += pass * pass_seqs_;
    info.pts_ns += pass * pass_ns_;
    return info;
  }

  /// @brief Sends pass @p pass of a loop started at @p start: each record,
  ///        once @ref due, read from @p reader and @ref restamp ed, as
  ///        `send(info, payload)`. A payload that fails its CRC
  ///        (`InvalidArgument`) is not sent, nor are the P-frames after it,
  ///        which lack their reference, up to the pass's next key; pass 0
  ///        prints each such record to stderr, as every pass meets the same.
  /// @param reader  The reader the loop was made from.
  /// @param send    Called as `vkc::Status send(const
  /// vgrid::stream::RecordInfo&,
  ///                const std::vector<std::uint8_t>&)`.
  /// @return OK; `NotFound` when no key's payload reads whole, so the pass
  ///         sends nothing; the reader's other errors; or @p send 's.
  template <typename Send>
  vkc::Status send_pass(const vgrid::stream::StreamReader& reader,
                        Clock::time_point start, std::uint64_t pass,
                        Send&& send) const {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> payload;
    bool resync = false;  // past a damaged payload, until the next key
    bool sent = false;
    for (const vgrid::stream::Record& record : records_) {
      if (resync && !record.info.key) continue;
      resync = false;
      std::this_thread::sleep_until(due(start, pass, record.info.pts_ns));
      const vkc::Status read = reader.read(record, &payload);
      if (read.domain() == vkc::Status::Code::InvalidArgument) {
        if (pass == 0) {
          std::fprintf(stderr,
                       "serve_stream: %s; every pass skips seq %llu up to the "
                       "next key\n",
                       read.message().c_str(),
                       static_cast<unsigned long long>(record.info.seq));
        }
        resync = true;
        continue;
      }
      VKC_TRY(read);
      VKC_TRY(send(restamp(record.info, pass), payload));
      sent = true;
    }
    if (!sent) {
      return vkc::Status::not_found("ReplayLoop: no key's payload reads whole");
    }
    return {};
  }

 private:
  ReplayLoop() = default;

  std::vector<vgrid::stream::Record> records_;
  std::uint64_t first_pts_ = 0;  // the records' least pts
  std::uint64_t pass_ns_ = 0;    // a pass's pts span and one mean step
  std::uint64_t pass_seqs_ = 0;  // a pass's seq span and one
};

}  // namespace vgrid_example
```

### examples/serve_stream/main.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// serve_stream: serve a recorded .vrst live, paced by its pts and looping
// until Ctrl+C: a sender with no camera, for a player to connect to.
//
//   serve_stream <in.vrst> [--port N]
//
// It serves every interface on port 47801, or N (0 takes a free one, which it
// prints), and prints each viewer joining and leaving. No scenario file: its
// whole input is a file and a port.

#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "info_log.hpp"
#include "stream_replay.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp"

namespace vkc = volumetric_kit::core;
namespace networking = volumetric_kit::grid::networking;
namespace stream = volumetric_kit::grid::stream;

namespace {

constexpr const char* kUsage =
    "usage: serve_stream <in.vrst> [--port N]\n"
    "  Serves the recording live on every interface, paced by its pts and\n"
    "  looping until Ctrl+C. --port N: the port (default 47801; 0 takes a\n"
    "  free one).";

struct Args {
  std::string path;
  std::uint16_t port = networking::kDefaultPort;
  bool help = false;
};

// The arguments, or why they are refused.
std::optional<Args> parse(int argc, char** argv, std::string* why) {
  Args args;
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {
    const std::string arg = argv[i];
    if (arg == "--help" || arg == "-h") {
      args.help = true;
    } else if (arg == "--port") {
      if (i + 1 == argc) {
        *why = "--port needs a number";
        return std::nullopt;
      }
      const char* text = argv[++i];
      char* end = nullptr;
      errno = 0;
      const unsigned long port = std::strtoul(text, &end, 10);
      if (*text < '0' || *text > '9' || *end != '\0' || errno != 0 ||
          port > 65535) {
        *why = std::string("--port ") + text + " is not a port (0 to 65535)";
        return std::nullopt;
      }
      args.port = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(port);
    } else if (arg.size() > 1 && arg[0] == '-') {
      *why = "unknown option " + arg;
      return std::nullopt;
    } else if (!args.path.empty()) {
      *why = "one recording, not " + args.path + " and " + arg;
      return std::nullopt;
    } else {
      args.path = arg;
    }
  }
  if (args.path.empty() && !args.help) {
    *why = "no recording named";
    return std::nullopt;
  }
  return args;
}

// Serve until stopped; returns only a failure.
vkc::Status serve(const Args& args) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const auto reader, stream::StreamReader::open(args.path));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const vgrid_example::ReplayLoop loop,
             vgrid_example::ReplayLoop::create(*reader));
  networking::ServerOptions options;
  options.port = args.port;
  // A recording cannot make a key: a joiner takes the GOP since the newest.
  options.replay_gop = true;
  VKC_ASSIGN(const auto server,
             networking::StreamServer::start(reader->session(), options));
  std::printf("serving %s on port %u: %zu records a pass\n", args.path.c_str(),
              unsigned{server->port()}, loop.records().size());
  std::fflush(stdout);
  const vgrid_example::ReplayLoop::Clock::time_point start =
      vgrid_example::ReplayLoop::Clock::now();
  const auto publish = [&](const stream::RecordInfo& info,
                           const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& payload) {
    return server->publish(info, payload.data(), payload.size());
  };
  for (std::uint64_t pass = 0;; ++pass) {
    VKC_TRY(loop.send_pass(*reader, start, pass, publish));
  }
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  std::string why;
  const std::optional<Args> args = parse(argc, argv, &why);
  if (!args) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "serve_stream: %s\n%s\n", why.c_str(), kUsage);
    return 2;
  }
  if (args->help) {
    std::printf("%s\n", kUsage);
    return 0;
  }
  vgrid_example::print_info_log();  // each viewer joining and leaving
  const vkc::Status failed = serve(*args);
  std::fprintf(stderr, "serve_stream: %s\n", failed.message().c_str());
  return 1;
}
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file device_requirements.hpp
/// @brief What grid's kernels require of a device.
///
/// The device is volumetric_kit_core's (`core/vulkan/device.hpp`). What grid
/// adds is @ref device_requirements, the one statement of what grid's kernels
/// need, which a standalone caller passes to `Instance::select_physical_device`
/// and `Device::create`, and an embedder merges with its own (`merge`, or a
/// `SharedDeviceConfig`) before building a shared device.
///
/// @code
/// const core::DeviceRequirements reqs = device_requirements();
/// VKC_ASSIGN(core::PhysicalDeviceInfo gpu,
///            instance.select_physical_device(reqs));
/// VKC_ASSIGN(core::Device device, core::Device::create(instance, gpu, reqs));
/// @endcode

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device_requirements.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid {

/// @brief What grid's kernels require of a device.
///
/// A compute queue with timeline semaphores (the core's defaults) and
/// `scalarBlockLayout`, the buffer ABI every grid shader declares
/// (`layout(scalar)`; DECISIONS.md, 2026-07-05).
///
/// Pass these to every `Device::create` and `Device::adopt` grid runs on.
/// The core's default requirements leave `scalarBlockLayout` off, and a
/// grid class that builds kernels refuses such a device
/// (@ref check_device_requirements).
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(core::Device device,
///            core::Device::create(instance, gpu, device_requirements()));
/// @endcode
/// @return The requirements; a caller may add to them before creating.
inline core::DeviceRequirements device_requirements() {
  core::DeviceRequirements reqs;
  reqs.scalar_block_layout = true;
  return reqs;
}

/// @brief Refuse a device that did not enable what grid's kernels need.
///
/// Called first by every grid `create` that builds kernels: on a device
/// without `scalarBlockLayout` the kernels would build and run without an
/// error, reading their buffers at the wrong offsets.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "MarchingCubes::create"));
/// @endcode
/// @param device  The device the kernels are for.
/// @param who     The caller, prefixed to a refusal.
/// @return OK; or `Device::check_enabled`'s `Status::Code::Unsupported`
///         naming what @ref device_requirements needs and the device did not
///         enable.
inline core::Status check_device_requirements(const core::Device& device,
                                              const char* who) {
  return device.check_enabled(device_requirements()).with_context(who);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file dispatch.hpp
/// @brief A loop that records a 1-D dispatch of items whose group count can
///        pass the device's limit, its test seam, and the same split for a
///        pass whose size a kernel finds on the device.
///
/// Public for the tiers of a project that links grid, as recon's tsdf does,
/// and outside grid's versioned API: its names are in `detail`. Vulkan
/// guarantees only 65535 groups along x (`maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0]`),
/// which a room's blocks already pass, so such a dispatch is recorded as
/// several rather than refused. The seam carries `VGRID_BASE_API` so a test
/// reaches it in a shared-library build too.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/export.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::detail {

/// @return The groups one dispatch of @ref dispatch_items holds:
///         @p max_groups, the device's `maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0]`, or the
///         cap @ref set_test_groups_per_dispatch set, if lower.
VGRID_BASE_API std::uint32_t groups_per_dispatch(std::uint32_t max_groups);

/// @brief For tests only: cap @ref groups_per_dispatch at @p groups, so a
///        small input takes the split path a device's limit gives a large
///        one; 0 lifts the cap. Process-wide.
VGRID_BASE_API void set_test_groups_per_dispatch(std::uint32_t groups);

/// Record @p kernel over @p items invocations of @p lanes a workgroup, in as
/// many dispatches of @ref groups_per_dispatch groups as it takes; each pushes
/// @p push with the first item it covers as `item_base`, and binds @p set, or
/// the kernel's own set when it is null. The batch's barrier between
/// dispatches orders each after the one before.
template <typename Push>
core::Status dispatch_items(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                            const core::ComputeKernel& kernel, Push push,
                            std::uint64_t items, std::uint32_t lanes,
                            std::uint32_t max_groups,
                            core::GpuStageScope* stage,
                            const core::DescriptorSet* set = nullptr) {
  const std::uint64_t per_dispatch =
      std::uint64_t(groups_per_dispatch(max_groups)) * lanes;
  for (std::uint64_t base = 0; base < items; base += per_dispatch) {
    push.item_base = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(base);
    const std::uint64_t count =
        std::min<std::uint64_t>(per_dispatch, items - base);
    const auto groups = static_cast<std::uint32_t>((count + lanes - 1) / lanes);
    VKC_TRY(set != nullptr ? batch.dispatch(kernel, *set, &push, sizeof(push),
                                            groups, max_groups, stage)
                           : batch.dispatch(kernel, &push, sizeof(push), groups,
                                            max_groups, stage));
  }
  return {};
}

/// The indirect slices of one pass whose size a kernel wrote on the device
/// (`base/shaders/dispatch_slices.glsl`): @ref dispatches
/// `VkDispatchIndirectCommand`s from @ref offset of @ref buffer, each of up
/// to @ref per_dispatch groups of @ref lanes items, split as
/// @ref dispatch_items splits a pass the host knows.
struct IndirectSlices {
  const core::Buffer* buffer = nullptr;
  VkDeviceSize offset = 0;
  std::uint32_t dispatches = 0;
  std::uint32_t per_dispatch = 0;
  std::uint32_t lanes = 1;
};

/// @return The slices a pass of at most @p max_items items, @p lanes a group,
///         takes at @p per_dispatch groups a slice: at least 1.
VGRID_BASE_API std::uint32_t slice_count(std::uint64_t max_items,
                                         std::uint32_t lanes,
                                         std::uint32_t per_dispatch);

/// Record @p kernel over @p slices, each pushing @p push with its first item
/// as `item_base`, binding the kernel's own set.
template <typename Push>
core::Status dispatch_slices(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                             const core::ComputeKernel& kernel, Push push,
                             const IndirectSlices& slices,
                             core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  for (std::uint32_t d = 0; d < slices.dispatches; ++d) {
    push.item_base = d * slices.per_dispatch * slices.lanes;
    VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch_indirect(
        kernel, &push, sizeof(push), *slices.buffer,
        slices.offset + VkDeviceSize(d) * sizeof(VkDispatchIndirectCommand),
        stage));
  }
  return {};
}

/// @brief What @ref record_dispatch_args sizes: a count -- the word at
///        @ref offset of @ref buffer, read as at most @ref bound, or
///        @ref bound itself when @ref buffer is null -- of entries of
///        @ref multiplier items each, and the gate that makes it 0 -- the
///        word at @ref gate_offset of @ref gate -- unless @ref gate is null.
struct SlicedCount {
  const core::Buffer* buffer = nullptr;
  VkDeviceSize offset = 0;
  std::uint32_t bound = 0;
  std::uint32_t multiplier = 1;
  const core::Buffer* gate = nullptr;
  VkDeviceSize gate_offset = 0;
};

/// Add grid's one count-to-indirect-slices kernel
/// (`base/shaders/dispatch_args.comp`) to @p kb as @p kernel, named @p name.
/// Each owner builds an instance of its own: a kernel and the buffer of the
/// slices it writes (@ref record_dispatch_args).
VGRID_BASE_API core::Status add_dispatch_args(core::KernelSetBuilder& kb,
                                              core::ComputeKernel& kernel,
                                              const char* name);

/// Record into @p batch the sizing of passes of @p count at @p lanes items a
/// group into @p slices, and at @p second_lanes (0 for none) into @p second,
/// so a count on the device, or a gate there, sizes them without reaching the
/// host: @p kernel (from @ref add_dispatch_args) writes them into @p buffer,
/// grown to the slices @p count's bound needs and named @p name. Every batch
/// that read @p buffer before must have resolved.
/// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a misaligned word or a
///         bound past 32-bit items; or a buffer failure.
VGRID_BASE_API core::Status record_dispatch_args(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
    core::ComputeKernel& kernel, core::Buffer& buffer, const char* name,
    const SlicedCount& count, std::uint32_t lanes, IndirectSlices* slices,
    std::uint32_t second_lanes, IndirectSlices* second,
    std::uint32_t max_groups, core::GpuStageScope* stage);

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::detail
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file codec/codec_params.hpp
/// @brief The knobs of the per-frame TSDF geometry codec: how many DCT
///        coefficients each block keeps and how coarsely they are quantized.

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {

/// The only block edge the codec transforms. Its zigzag order and cosine table
/// are 8-specific, so a grid with another `block_size` is refused, never
/// transformed wrong.
inline constexpr std::int32_t kBlockSize = 8;

/// Voxels (and so DCT coefficients) in one block: `kBlockSize^3`.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kVoxelsPerBlock =
    static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kBlockSize * kBlockSize * kBlockSize);

/// Bits in one word of the observed mask.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaskWordBits =
    std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::digits;

/// Words in one block's observed mask: one bit per voxel.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaskWordsPerBlock =
    kVoxelsPerBlock / kMaskWordBits;
static_assert(kVoxelsPerBlock % kMaskWordBits == 0,
              "a block's mask must fill whole words");

/// The magnitude a quantized coefficient is clamped to: `INT16_MAX`, so a
/// coefficient and its negation both fit in 16 bits, the range the entropy
/// coder's alphabet is sized by.
inline constexpr std::int32_t kMaxQuantizedMagnitude =
    std::numeric_limits<std::int16_t>::max();

/// @brief The smallest quantization step the codec accepts, as a fraction of
///        `trunc_dist`: `sqrt(kVoxelsPerBlock) / kMaxQuantizedMagnitude`.
///
/// The transform is orthonormal and runs on SDF normalized into [-1, 1], so
/// every coefficient is a dot product of a unit basis vector with a vector of
/// norm at most `sqrt(kVoxelsPerBlock)` (~22.63). A step at or above this
/// therefore keeps every quantized value inside @ref kMaxQuantizedMagnitude, so
/// the clamp is a guard against float drift and never a silent loss.
/// @ref CodecParams::validate refuses anything finer.
///
/// A literal, the formula's float, rather than the formula: `std::sqrt` is not
/// `constexpr`, so the formula was initialized at run time, and a validate()
/// in another file's static initializer could read it as 0. The params test
/// holds the two equal.
inline constexpr float kMinStep = 6.90555025e-4f;

/// @brief The coarsest quantization step the codec accepts, as a fraction of
///        `trunc_dist`.
///
/// Past `2 sqrt(kVoxelsPerBlock)` (~45.3) every coefficient quantizes to 0, so
/// a coarser step codes nothing more, and this is the power of two past it.
/// It is what keeps a decoded frame finite: a step from a corrupt header
/// times a coefficient of up to @ref kMaxQuantizedMagnitude stays far inside
/// a float, where 1e38 would make it infinite and the inverse transform's
/// sums of opposite infinities NaN. @ref CodecParams::validate refuses
/// anything coarser.
inline constexpr float kMaxStep = 64.0f;
static_assert(kMaxStep * kMaxStep >= 4.0f * kVoxelsPerBlock,
              "kMaxStep must quantize every coefficient to 0");

/// The longest segment a frame holds, in entries: a rule of the format, so
/// every valid frame decodes on the device. A frame's segment size (blocks)
/// and a P-frame's update size (reference entries) are each from 1 to this;
/// a reader refuses a frame past it, and the @ref Encoder a `segment_size`
/// past it (`Status::Code::InvalidArgument`). One invocation decodes a whole
/// segment, at 30 to 45 us a block on Apple M5 Max and RTX 5090; this keeps
/// one invocation near 50 ms there, well inside a GPU watchdog's limit on a
/// slower device.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize = 1024;

/// @brief What a frame is: byte 6 of its header (@ref FrameInfo::type).
enum class FrameType : std::uint8_t {
  /// Self-contained: decodes with no other frame.
  kIntra = 0,
  /// A P-frame: decodes against the frame its @ref Decoder decoded before
  /// it, its reference, as the @ref Encoder coded it against the frame it
  /// returned before (@ref EncoderConfig::intra_period).
  kInter = 1,
};

/// @brief How a frame's blocks are transformed and quantized.
///
/// A coefficient at frequency `(x, y, z)` is quantized with step
/// `quantization_scale * quantization_weights[x + 8*y + 64*z]`, a fraction of
/// the grid's `trunc_dist`. The transform runs on SDF divided by `trunc_dist`,
/// so one setting holds across scenes whatever their truncation band. DC is
/// the ordinary entry at `(0, 0, 0)`.
///
/// The table controls relative precision; the scale changes overall quality.
/// Multiplying the table and dividing the scale by the same positive number
/// describes the same steps. Presets should use weight 1 at DC to make their
/// scales comparable, but this is a convention, not a validation requirement.
///
/// Defaults keep K = 64 and a uniform step of 0.2, the provisional room0
/// settings. TODO(codec): tune per-basis tables at matched rates across room0,
/// normalized Rafa2 and the analytic sphere before changing the defaults;
/// the first band/radial candidates did not establish a consistent win.
struct VGRID_CODEC_API CodecParams {
  /// Coefficients kept per block, taken in 3-D zigzag order (lowest `x+y+z`
  /// first). In [1, @ref kVoxelsPerBlock]; @ref kVoxelsPerBlock keeps the
  /// whole transform. This cutoff is independent of the quantization table.
  std::uint32_t coefficient_count = 64;
  /// Positive normal scale shared by every basis; effective steps are
  /// fractions of `trunc_dist` and must each lie in
  /// [@ref kMinStep, @ref kMaxStep].
  float quantization_scale = 0.2f;
  /// Positive normal relative steps in canonical frequency order
  /// `x + 8*y + 64*z`, with each frequency in [0, 7], not in zigzag order.
  /// Only the K frequencies the zigzag cutoff keeps are used, checked and
  /// carried in a frame; the rest are ignored and decode as 1.
  std::array<float, kVoxelsPerBlock> quantization_weights = [] {
    std::array<float, kVoxelsPerBlock> weights{};
    for (float& weight : weights) weight = 1.0f;
    return weights;
  }();

  /// @brief Check that every field is one the transform can honour.
  /// @return OK, or `Status::invalid_argument` naming the field: a
  ///         @ref coefficient_count outside [1, @ref kVoxelsPerBlock], a
  ///         scale or kept weight that is not positive and normal (zero,
  ///         subnormal, infinite or NaN), or a kept frequency's effective
  ///         step outside [@ref kMinStep, @ref kMaxStep].
  core::Status validate() const;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decode_grid.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file codec/decode_grid.hpp
/// @brief A player's grid: built from a frame's header, and grown when a
///        frame outgrows it, which the @ref Decoder itself refuses to do.
///
/// A frame's size does not bound its block count, so both helpers take the
/// caller's ceiling, `max_blocks`: the most blocks a frame may hold. Nothing
/// past it is allocated: a frame of more blocks is refused before it is
/// decoded, and a grow to more slots than @ref make_decode_grid builds for a
/// frame of `max_blocks` before it is made. Each refusal is
/// `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`, a frame to skip. A player of frames it
/// did not code (a file, a socket) sets the ceiling from its memory budget.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decoder.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {

/// @brief Build a grid to decode a stream into, from one of its frames.
///
/// The grid is what @ref Decoder::decode takes: the frame's `voxel_size` and
/// `trunc_dist` (@ref read_frame_info) in @ref volume::block_grid_params'
/// layout, with 4-byte float `tsdf` and `weight` alone, and
/// `ceil(2 * block_count / kDefaultBucketSize)` buckets, at least 1024: the
/// frame fills at most half its blocks. The block count is
/// checked against the frame's segment table first, as @ref Decoder::decode
/// checks it, so a header cannot claim blocks its frame does not carry.
/// @param device      The compute device (must outlive the grid).
/// @param allocator   The allocator its buffers come from (must outlive the
///                    grid).
/// @param frame       A frame of the stream, usually its first, intra or a
///                    P-frame; it is parsed, not decoded.
/// @param size        Its exact length.
/// @param max_blocks  The ceiling: the most blocks a frame may hold.
/// @return The grid, empty; @ref read_frame_info's refusal of the header;
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for more than @p max_blocks
///         blocks; the refusals @ref Decoder::decode makes of the frame's
///         sections and segment table; or
///         @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid::create's error, an allocation failure
///         included. Host allocation failures, including header diagnostics,
///         return `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<volume::VoxelBlockGrid> make_decode_grid(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator, const std::uint8_t* frame,
    std::size_t size, std::uint32_t max_blocks);

/// @brief What @ref finish_growing did besides finishing the frame.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::Finished done,
///            codec::finish_growing(decoder, frame, grid, max_blocks));
/// if (done.redone) remesh();  // its extract ran gated off
/// @endcode
struct Finished {
  /// The frame failed on the device (the grid too small, or contention past
  /// the rounds) and was decoded again from its own slot, blocking. Whatever
  /// its batch recorded after it, such as an extract, ran gated off.
  bool redone = false;
};

/// @brief @ref Decoder::record @p slot's record into @p batch, first growing
///        @p grid, blocking, when the frame holds more blocks than its heap.
///
/// The grow is @ref decode_growing's: to twice the grid's buckets or the
/// frame's @ref make_decode_grid buckets, whichever is more.
/// @param decoder     The decoder.
/// @param batch       Records the frame; the caller submits it.
/// @param slot        From @ref Decoder::claim_input, the record at its start.
/// @param size        The record's exact length.
/// @param grid        As @ref Decoder::record takes it.
/// @param max_blocks  The most blocks a frame may hold.
/// @param metrics     Optional: @ref Decoder::record's rows, and a grow's
///                    `"  ..grow"`, which their `"codec decode"` holds.
/// @return As @ref Decoder::record, out of device memory included, which no
///         grow cures; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a frame or a grow
///         past @p max_blocks; or `volume::grow_grid`'s failure.
/// @pre As @ref Decoder::record. A grow frees the grid's buffers at once.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<PendingDecode> record_growing(
    Decoder& decoder, core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::HostSlot& slot,
    std::size_t size, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

/// @brief @ref Decoder::finish @p pending, recovering as @ref decode_growing
///        does: decoding the frame again from @p pending's own slot, after a
///        grow for `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` (once), or as it is for
///        `Status::Code::IoError` (twice at most).
///
/// Each recovery blocks, in batches of its own, and is timed whole, its
/// decode again included, as `"  ..grow"` or `"  ..retry"` inside a
/// `"codec decode"` row. It needs no other input slot.
/// @param decoder     The decoder that recorded @p pending.
/// @param pending     Its batch resolved.
/// @param grid        The grid it recorded into.
/// @param max_blocks  The most blocks a frame may hold.
/// @param metrics     Optional: the recoveries' rows.
/// @return What it did; or the last finish's error as @ref decode_growing
///         returns it, with the reference unchanged; or `volume::grow_grid`'s
///         failure.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<Finished> finish_growing(
    Decoder& decoder, const PendingDecode& pending,
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

/// @brief @ref Decoder::decode @p frame into @p grid, growing the grid once
///        if the frame outgrows it.
///
/// It recovers as @ref record_growing and @ref finish_growing do, around one
/// submit of its own.
///
/// `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`, the decoder's word for a grid too small,
/// grows @p grid once (@ref volume::grow_grid) to twice its buckets or the
/// frame's @ref make_decode_grid buckets, whichever is more, and decodes
/// again; it is returned the second time. The first can also be the
/// device's own, out of memory for the decode's buffers, which the grow does
/// not cure. Growing a grid @ref make_decode_grid built leaves the frame at
/// most half its heap, so there the second is always the device's.
/// `Status::Code::IoError`, bucket-lock contention that outlasted the
/// decoder's own rounds, decodes again, twice at most. Any other error is
/// returned as the decoder gave it, `Status::Code::NotFound` for a P-frame
/// without its reference included. A grow, a
/// @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid::resize, replaces the grid's buffers and shows
/// as a larger `grid.grid().num_buckets`.
/// @param decoder     The decoder.
/// @param frame       The frame.
/// @param size        Its exact length.
/// @param grid        The grid to decode into, as @ref Decoder::decode takes
///                    it.
/// @param max_blocks  The ceiling: the most blocks a frame may hold.
/// @param metrics     Optional `StageMetrics` collecting, once the decode
///                    succeeds, the rows @ref Decoder::decode gives for the
///                    first attempt and, after a recovery, its row as
///                    @ref finish_growing times it. `nullptr` measures
///                    nothing.
/// @return OK; @ref read_frame_info's refusal of the header;
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a frame or a grow past
///         @p max_blocks; the last decode's
///         error; @ref volume::grow_grid's, such as
///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` at the device's largest grid; or
///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for a host allocation failure before
///         the decode succeeds.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status decode_growing(
    Decoder& decoder, const std::uint8_t* frame, std::size_t size,
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

/// @brief @ref decode_growing a record already in an input slot: one an
///        encoder's frame was copied into, head then payload, with no other
///        copy (the other form copies its bytes into one).
/// @param slot  From @ref Decoder::claim_input, the record at its start.
/// @param size  The record's exact length.
/// @return As the other form.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status decode_growing(
    Decoder& decoder, const core::HostSlot& slot, std::size_t size,
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decoder.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file codec/decoder.hpp
/// @brief Decode a frame -- intra, or a P-frame against the frame decoded
///        before it -- into a @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid, smoothed across its
///        block faces on request, and read a frame's header without decoding
///        it.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/gpu_timer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/host_ring.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {

namespace detail {
class BlockLists;
class DctTransform;
class Deblock;
class DeviceFrameReader;
class FrameGate;
class ReferenceStore;
struct RecordedFrame;
}  // namespace detail

/// @brief What a frame's header says: enough to build a grid it decodes into.
struct FrameInfo {
  /// Metres per voxel edge. A grid decoding the frame must match it exactly.
  float voxel_size = 0.0f;
  /// Metres. A grid decoding the frame must match it exactly: the
  /// coefficients are fractions of it.
  float trunc_dist = 0.0f;
  /// Blocks the decoded frame holds (a P-frame's reference blocks that
  /// survive, and its new ones); a grid decoding it needs at least this many
  /// (`num_blocks`), plus the hash-table room to place them.
  std::uint32_t block_count = 0;
  /// The coefficient count, scale, and kept bases' weights it was coded with;
  /// weights beyond the K cutoff are not carried and read as 1.
  CodecParams params;
  /// Intra, or a P-frame, which decodes only after the frame it was coded
  /// against (@ref Decoder).
  FrameType type = FrameType::kIntra;
};

/// @brief What the deblock did to the frame a @ref Decoder last decoded or
///        rebuilt (@ref Decoder::set_deblock): enough for a player to show,
///        say, "LF, 12 of 1,920 blocks exact".
struct DeblockInfo {
  /// The filter the frame's steps chose and the decoder ran on its fully
  /// observed blocks: `"LF"`, a line fit across each block face; `"LG"`,
  /// that and a light Gaussian; `"R"`, that and a stronger one; or `"off"`,
  /// for the deblock off or a step too fine to need one. A string literal.
  const char* filter = "off";
  /// T, in metres: the largest change one quantum of the frame's
  /// lowest-frequency coefficients makes to a voxel, by which the filter is
  /// chosen and its changes are clipped. The frame's, the deblock on or off.
  float step = 0.0f;
  /// The frame's blocks.
  std::uint32_t block_count = 0;
  /// Of them, those the per-block fallback kept at their exact decode: with
  /// a filter, the blocks holding an unobserved voxel, which it never writes
  /// (@ref Decoder::set_deblock), counted on the device; with `"off"`,
  /// every block. A fully observed block the filter happens to leave
  /// unchanged is not counted. A frame with them all decodes exactly as with
  /// the deblock off.
  std::uint32_t exact_blocks = 0;
};

/// @brief Read a frame's complete header, including its quantization weights.
///
/// What a player calls on its first frame to build a grid of the geometry the
/// stream carries (`voxel_size`, `trunc_dist`, `block_size` 8, and room for
/// `block_count` blocks), before it can @ref Decoder::decode anything;
/// @ref make_decode_grid builds that grid. No entropy payload is read.
/// @param data  The frame (at least its complete header: 44 bytes plus four
///              per kept coefficient).
/// @param size  Bytes available at @p data.
/// @return The header, a P-frame's included, or
///         `Status::Code::Unsupported` for another version, a frame type
///         past @ref FrameType::kInter or another block size, and
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for anything else malformed. It
///         does not check the rest of the frame, which @ref Decoder::decode
///         does.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<FrameInfo> read_frame_info(
    const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);

/// @brief A frame recorded into a caller's batch (@ref Decoder::record), for
///        @ref Decoder::finish or @ref Decoder::abandon once that batch has
///        resolved.
///
/// A token: the decoder keeps what finishing needs, and its next record
/// supersedes an unfinished one. Its @ref gate lives in the decoder's own
/// heap-held buffers, so it survives a move of the decoder.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(core::HostSlot slot, decoder.claim_input(record.size));
/// VKC_TRY(reader.read(record, slot.data(), slot.capacity()));
/// VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::PendingDecode frame,
///            decoder.record(batch, slot, record.size, grid));
/// @endcode
struct PendingDecode {
  /// Which of the decoder's records this is; 0 for none.
  std::uint64_t serial = 0;
  /// N: the blocks the grid holds once the frame is in, which an extract
  /// recorded after it plans for.
  std::uint32_t blocks = 0;
  /// 1 once every step succeeded on the device, else 0 (bound 1): what an
  /// extract recorded after it gates on.
  volume::DeviceCount gate;
  /// The slot the record was parsed from (`core::HostSlot`), held so the
  /// frame can be decoded again (@ref finish_growing).
  core::HostSlot input;
  /// The record's bytes at the start of @ref input.
  std::size_t size = 0;
};

/// @brief Decodes frames into a caller's @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid -- the
///        codec's playback side (the 2026-09-26 decision).
///
/// After a successful @ref decode the grid holds **exactly** the frame's
/// blocks, whatever it held before: blocks the frame lacks are removed (and
/// their attributes zeroed), missing ones are allocated, and every frame
/// block's `tsdf` and `weight` are rewritten in full -- an observed voxel with
/// its decoded SDF (smoothed where the deblock runs) and weight 1.0, an
/// unobserved one as a fresh block holds it. So a player decodes frame after
/// frame into one grid and meshes it after each; nothing is cleared between
/// frames, and a block present in both costs no allocation. A block the decode
/// leaves different is stamped `changed` (@ref volume::BlockStamp), and with
/// the deblock off one it leaves as it was is not, so a consumer of the
/// stamps sees only what the stream changed.
///
/// The deblock (@ref set_deblock, off by default) smooths each frame it runs
/// on across its block faces, where quantization leaves steps the mesher
/// would draw, by a filter the frame's header chooses (@ref DeblockInfo), on
/// the device inside the decode's batch. It is out of loop -- a P-frame
/// decodes from its reference's coefficients, never from a grid -- so it may
/// change between any two frames, and it costs no bits. It writes the `tsdf`
/// of fully observed blocks alone -- a block holding an unobserved voxel keeps
/// its exact decode -- and stamps a block it writes `changed`. With it on,
/// the stamps can also name a block whose values end as they were -- the
/// inverse compares the exact decode with the smoothed values the grid held
/// -- but never miss one that changed.
///
/// Only `tsdf` and `weight` are written, so a grid that declares any other
/// attribute is refused: a block kept across frames would carry that
/// attribute's previous values (a `color`, say) under the new geometry, and
/// nothing could tell which blocks those were.
///
/// A P-frame (@ref FrameType::kInter) decodes against the last frame this
/// decoder decoded, its reference, which the decoder keeps on the device as
/// it decoded it -- quantized coefficients, masks and block list, never
/// rebuilt from a grid -- so it decodes into any grid of its geometry,
/// a fresh one included, to exactly the blocks an intra frame of the same
/// content decodes to. Every decode that succeeds, intra or P, makes its
/// frame the reference; one refused or failed keeps the reference it had, so
/// the same frame decoded again, after a resize say, decodes against it.
/// The reference and the frame being decoded take `80 + 4 * ceil(K / 2)`
/// bytes of device memory a block each, and the frame 24 more (its sources,
/// and the blocks the grid lacks); the rANS decode takes
/// `64 + 4 * ceil(K / 2)` an entry it decodes (a P-frame's reference entries
/// and its new blocks), 16 more a new block and 8 a reference entry, and
/// 16 KiB a frequency table for its slot lookup, beside the frame's payload
/// and tables; the blocks the grid must drop take 16 bytes a hash slot; and
/// with the deblock on, a frame it filters takes 4 bytes a block slot of the
/// grid's heap, and one whose filter has a Gaussian 1,184 bytes a block
/// more, each grown with 1.5x headroom. All of it is kept, sized for the
/// largest frame decoded. The record itself is read in place from one of two
/// input slots (@ref claim_input), and its results land in one of two
/// results slots, each a `core::HostRing` slot.
///
/// Everything but I/O and control runs on the device: the rANS decode, one
/// segment an invocation; the reader's verdict; the merge of a P-frame's
/// survivors with its new blocks; and the diff of the grid's blocks against
/// the frame's. The host parses the header and tables; every verdict and
/// count stays on the device, where a one-thread gate judges rows 11 to 13
/// before the grid changes, and every later grid write in the frame's batch,
/// the deblock's included, is gated on it. A frame the device refuses changes
/// neither the grid's blocks nor the reference, but moves the map's
/// `topology_epoch` and tick. A frame the device cannot hold is refused,
/// never decoded on the host.
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one call at a time, and
///          nothing else may modify the grid during one.
class VGRID_CODEC_API Decoder {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the kernels: the rANS decoder's, the block lists' (the
  ///        merge's and the grid diff's among them), the gate's, the apply's,
  ///        the inverse transform's and the deblock's; and make the input and
  ///        results rings, two slots each.
  /// @param device     The compute device (must outlive this object).
  /// @param allocator  The allocator per-call buffers come from (must outlive
  ///                   this object).
  /// @return The decoder, or a pipeline or allocation failure: a device
  ///         whose kernels do not build has no decoder.
  static core::Result<Decoder> create(core::Device& device,
                                      core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~Decoder();
  Decoder(Decoder&& other) noexcept;
  Decoder& operator=(Decoder&& other) noexcept;
  Decoder(const Decoder&) = delete;
  Decoder& operator=(const Decoder&) = delete;

  /// @brief Decode one frame into @p grid: an intra frame, or a P-frame
  ///        against the reference this decoder holds.
  ///
  /// Everything that can be checked before the grid is touched is: the grid's
  /// attributes, its geometry against the frame's header, the whole frame
  /// parsed and entropy-decoded, a P-frame against the held reference, and
  /// the grid's heap against its block count. A refusal there leaves @p grid
  /// exactly as it was. A failure **after** the grid starts to change -- the
  /// hash table cannot place every block, its bucket locks keep losing races,
  /// a dispatch fails, or an internal fault -- leaves it valid but holding
  /// **neither** frame: blocks the two frames share still hold the previous
  /// frame's voxels, and blocks new to this one are empty, so it is not worth
  /// meshing. The next successful decode restores it exactly, since each
  /// decode starts from whatever the grid holds.
  ///
  /// It is @ref claim_input, a copy of @p data, @ref record, one submit and
  /// @ref finish.
  /// @param data     The frame.
  /// @param size     Its exact length.
  /// @param grid     The grid to decode into: 4-byte float `tsdf` and
  ///                 `weight` and no other attribute, `block_size` 8, and the
  ///                 frame's `voxel_size` and `trunc_dist` exactly (see
  ///                 @ref read_frame_info).
  /// @param metrics  Optional `StageMetrics` collecting a `"codec decode"`
  ///                 row with its host, wait and device halves -- the whole
  ///                 decode's, the deblock's included -- over the breakdown
  ///                 rows, each with all three, that tile its one submit:
  ///                 `"  ..rans decode"` (parsing the frame, decoding it,
  ///                 merging a P-frame's blocks with its reference's, and
  ///                 diffing the grid's block set against the frame's),
  ///                 `"  ..apply"` (the gate, then removing and allocating
  ///                 blocks: the zeroing, the hash deletes and the
  ///                 allocations, every round) and `"  ..inverse"` (making
  ///                 the frame's blocks from the reference and the payload,
  ///                 the transform and the deblock, then gathering the
  ///                 results). Named apart from the @ref Encoder's, so both
  ///                 timed into one `StageMetrics` stay apart. `nullptr`
  ///                 measures nothing.
  /// @return OK, or: whatever the frame reader refuses
  ///         (`Status::Code::Unsupported`,
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a malformed or corrupt
  ///         frame, a segment longer than @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize
  ///         and a P-frame whose coding parameters are not its reference's
  ///         included); `Status::Code::NotFound` for a P-frame whose
  ///         reference this decoder does not hold (none, or another frame):
  ///         the stream's P-frames decode again from its next I-frame; a
  ///         frame the device cannot hold: `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`
  ///         for a buffer past `maxStorageBufferRange`,
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` past free device memory, which a
  ///         resize does not recover;
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a moved-from decoder, a
  ///         grid that is moved-from, has another block size or geometry,
  ///         lacks a float `tsdf` / `weight`, or declares any other
  ///         attribute, or a grid whose free heap refuses a removed block
  ///         (its accounting was already broken, which nothing here mends),
  ///         or, after the grid changed, an internal fault: a block's source
  ///         outside the reference or payload bound (a bug, never a sound
  ///         frame's);
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when the grid is too small for
  ///         the frame -- fewer block slots (`num_blocks`) than the frame has
  ///         blocks, or a hash table that cannot place them all -- which
  ///         @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid::resize and decoding again recovers
  ///         (@ref decode_growing does both);
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` only when bucket-lock contention
  ///         outlasts the device rounds
  ///         (`volume::VoxelHashMap::kRecordedRounds`) over a table with room
  ///         (decode again; a resize would not help); otherwise a buffer or
  ///         dispatch failure.
  core::Status decode(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size,
                      volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                      core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

  /// @brief @ref decode the record already at the start of @p slot: @ref
  ///        record, one submit and @ref finish, with no copy -- what
  ///        @ref finish_growing decodes a frame again with.
  /// @param slot     From @ref claim_input, the record at its start.
  /// @param size     The record's exact length.
  /// @param grid     As @ref decode.
  /// @param metrics  As @ref decode.
  /// @return As @ref decode and @ref record.
  core::Status decode(const core::HostSlot& slot, std::size_t size,
                      volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                      core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

  /// @brief A slot of this decoder's input ring with room for a record of
  ///        @p bytes and the 8 bytes of slack after it: read the record into
  ///        `data()`, then @ref record it.
  ///
  /// Two persistent slots, grown as a larger record asks: one held by a
  /// recorded frame until its batch has resolved and its token is dropped,
  /// and one being filled. @ref record zeroes the slack.
  /// @param bytes  The record's exact size; not 0.
  /// @return The slot; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a moved-from
  ///         decoder, 0 bytes, or both slots held; or an allocation failure.
  core::Result<core::HostSlot> claim_input(std::size_t bytes);

  /// @brief Record decoding the record at the start of @p slot into @p grid,
  ///        into @p batch: the whole decode, every count on the device,
  ///        nothing read back.
  ///
  /// The host parses the record in place and checks what @ref decode checks
  /// before the grid changes: the grid, the header, sections and tables, a
  /// P-frame's reference, and N against the grid's heap. Then it records:
  /// - the rANS decode, the merge and the diff (`"  ..rans decode"`);
  /// - the gate, and the removal and allocation rounds, which fold their
  ///   outcome into @ref PendingDecode::gate (`"  ..apply"`);
  /// - the apply, the inverse, the deblock as @ref set_deblock stands now
  ///   (each sized by N and gated), then the results @ref finish reads
  ///   (`"  ..inverse"`).
  /// @param batch    Records the decode; the caller submits it.
  /// @param slot     From @ref claim_input, the record at its start; unchanged
  ///                 until the batch has resolved.
  /// @param size     The record's exact length.
  /// @param grid     As @ref decode takes it; nothing but @p batch changes it
  ///                 until the batch has resolved.
  /// @param metrics  As @ref decode's rows: host halves now, device halves
  ///                 from `PendingBatch::device_rows`.
  /// @return The pending frame; or, with nothing recorded:
  ///         - what the frame reader refuses (`Status::Code::Unsupported`;
  ///           `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a malformed frame);
  ///         - `Status::Code::NotFound` for a P-frame whose reference this
  ///           decoder does not hold;
  ///         - `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for more blocks than the grid's
  ///           heap (@ref record_growing grows it first);
  ///         - `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a moved-from decoder, a
  ///           slot shorter than @p size and its slack, or a grid
  ///           @ref decode refuses.
  ///
  ///         Or, possibly after the first commands, so the caller drops
  ///         @p batch: `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` past free device memory,
  ///         or another buffer failure.
  /// @pre The batch of this decoder's last record has resolved.
  core::Result<PendingDecode> record(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                     const core::HostSlot& slot,
                                     std::size_t size,
                                     volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                     core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

  /// @brief Once @p pending's batch has resolved: judge it and, for a frame
  ///        that succeeded, make it the reference.
  ///
  /// Settles the grid's map from the rounds, reads the results (the verdict,
  /// row 13's collision, the apply's faults, the inverse's rejects, the
  /// blocks the deblock kept), then sets @ref last_deblock and
  /// @ref last_rounds.
  /// @param pending  From this decoder's last @ref record.
  /// @param grid     The grid it recorded into.
  /// @return OK; or, the reference unchanged, the statuses @ref decode
  ///         returns once a frame is parsed (rows 11 to 13's
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` with the grid's blocks untouched,
  ///         a heap that refused a removed block, `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`
  ///         for a table that cannot place the frame, `Status::Code::IoError`
  ///         for lost races past the rounds, the apply's and the inverse's
  ///         faults); or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a pending this
  ///         decoder no longer holds, or another grid.
  core::Status finish(const PendingDecode& pending,
                      volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid);

  /// @brief Drop @p pending without judging it: its batch failed, was never
  ///        submitted, or ran a frame no longer wanted. The reference stays;
  ///        the grid holds what the batch left, and the map's heap copy stays
  ///        as it was, until the next decode.
  /// @param pending  From this decoder; one it no longer holds, or another
  ///                 decoder's, is ignored.
  void abandon(const PendingDecode& pending) noexcept;

  /// @return The most rounds the removal or the allocation ran in the frame
  ///         the last @ref finish judged (`AllocFailures::rounds`), for M2's
  ///         histogram; 0 before one.
  std::uint32_t last_rounds() const noexcept { return last_rounds_; }

  /// @brief Turn the deblock on or off for every frame recorded or rebuilt
  ///        from here on (@ref record and @ref rebuild read it): on, a frame
  ///        is smoothed across its block faces by the filter its header picks
  ///        (none at a fine step), after its inverse transform, in the same
  ///        batch; off, the default, the grid holds the exact decode.
  ///
  /// The per-block fallback: a block holding an unobserved voxel -- as
  /// nearly every block of a fused RGB-D frame does, and a true-SDF frame's
  /// few blocks with cut voxels (@ref EncoderConfig::true_sdf) -- keeps its
  /// exact decode. No pass writes it and no line is fitted across a face it
  /// shares, so neither side of that face is line-fitted; the Gaussian of a
  /// neighbour reads its observed voxels as decoded, its unobserved ones not
  /// at all. Only fully observed blocks are smoothed, so a frame all of whose
  /// blocks are masked decodes exactly as with the deblock off;
  /// @ref DeblockInfo::exact_blocks counts the blocks kept.
  void set_deblock(bool on) noexcept { deblock_on_ = on; }
  /// @return Whether the deblock is on.
  bool deblock() const noexcept { return deblock_on_; }

  /// @brief Rebuild the frame this decoder last decoded into @p grid, from
  ///        the reference it holds, with the deblock as it is now: what a
  ///        paused player calls after @ref set_deblock to show the change on
  ///        the frame it shows, without reading the frame again.
  ///
  /// One batch, submitted and waited on: the diff of the grid's blocks
  /// against the frame's, then the inverse transform and the deblock as the
  /// decode records them, gated on that diff and stamping as they do, and
  /// the results gathered into a results slot. The reference is unchanged.
  /// @param grid     The grid the last decode wrote: the frame's geometry,
  ///                 and exactly its blocks, whatever their values.
  /// @param metrics  Optional; a `"codec decode"` row with its host, wait and
  ///                 device halves.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::NotFound` before a decode has succeeded;
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a moved-from decoder, a
  ///         grid @ref decode refuses before it changes one, or one whose
  ///         blocks are not exactly the frame's, found on the device before
  ///         anything is written (decode the frame into it instead);
  ///         otherwise a buffer or dispatch failure, after which the grid
  ///         holds a partial rebuild until a decode or rebuild succeeds.
  /// @pre The batch of this decoder's last @ref record has resolved.
  core::Status rebuild(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                       core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr);

  /// @return What the deblock did to the frame the last @ref finish or
  ///         @ref rebuild that succeeded left; `"off"` and zeros before one.
  const DeblockInfo& last_deblock() const noexcept { return last_deblock_; }

  /// @return `true` if this owns a live transform (`false` when moved-from).
  bool valid() const noexcept;

 private:
  Decoder();

  // The body of record and decode, under the "codec decode" row their
  // caller opened.
  core::Result<PendingDecode> record_frame(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                           const core::HostSlot& slot,
                                           std::size_t size,
                                           volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                           core::StageMetrics* metrics);
  // Whether @p pending is this decoder's unfinished last record.
  bool holds(const PendingDecode& pending) const noexcept;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this); what the decode's batches run on.
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::unique_ptr<detail::DctTransform> transform_;
  std::unique_ptr<detail::DeviceFrameReader> reader_;
  // The reference a P-frame decodes against, and the apply into it.
  std::unique_ptr<detail::ReferenceStore> store_;
  // The frame's blocks merged into frame order, and diffed against the grid.
  std::unique_ptr<detail::BlockLists> lists_;
  // The deblock's kernels and snapshot, and its switch.
  std::unique_ptr<detail::Deblock> deblock_;
  // The gate, its slices and the results gather.
  std::unique_ptr<detail::FrameGate> gate_;
  // The records' input slots and the frames' result slots, two each.
  std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing> inputs_;
  std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing> results_;
  // The frame recorded and not yet finished or abandoned, and the serial
  // the next record takes.
  std::unique_ptr<detail::RecordedFrame> pending_;
  std::uint64_t serial_ = 0;
  bool deblock_on_ = false;
  DeblockInfo last_deblock_;
  std::uint32_t last_rounds_ = 0;
  // Device spans for the transform; idle until a caller asks for metrics.
  core::GpuTimer gpu_timer_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/encoder.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file codec/encoder.hpp
/// @brief Encode a grid's geometry, frame after frame, as intra frames or
///        P-frames against the frame encoded before.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/gpu_timer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/host_ring.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {

namespace detail {
class BlockLists;
class DctTransform;
class DeviceFrameWriter;
class ReferenceStore;
struct RecordedEncode;
}  // namespace detail

/// The band, in voxels from the zero level, that holds every voxel an
/// @ref EncoderConfig::true_sdf frame codes: `ceil(1 + 8 sqrt(3))`.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kTrueSdfBandVoxels = 15;

/// @brief How an @ref Encoder codes a frame.
struct VGRID_CODEC_API EncoderConfig {
  /// Coefficients kept per block and their quantization steps.
  CodecParams params;
  /// Blocks per independently coded segment, from 1 to
  /// @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize. The device codes and decodes one
  /// segment an invocation, so smaller segments give it more parallelism, at
  /// a little more size (each segment restates its first coordinate); the
  /// default costs 2-3% of a frame.
  std::uint32_t segment_size = 64;
  /// A P-frame's reference entries per independently coded update segment:
  /// 0, the default, takes @ref segment_size, which gives a P-frame at least
  /// as many segments as its reference has coded intra, at any segment size
  /// (the 2026-10-17 decision); otherwise 1 to
  /// @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize. As @ref segment_size is for its new
  /// blocks, smaller segments give the device more parallelism, at a little
  /// more size (each segment costs a 4-byte length and its stream's 4-byte
  /// final state); at a @ref segment_size of 64, 256 against 64 would save
  /// about 4% of a stream at a period of 30 and code its P-frames 20-140%
  /// slower (the 2026-10-16 decision). An I-frame has no update segments.
  std::uint32_t update_size = 0;
  /// Frames from one I-frame to the next, at least 1. At 1, the default,
  /// every frame is an I-frame; at N, an I-frame and N - 1 P-frames
  /// (@ref FrameType::kInter) take turns; a period past the stream's length
  /// codes P-frames after the first frame for as long as the rules on
  /// @ref Encoder::encode allow.
  std::uint32_t intra_period = 1;
  /// Whether the grid holds a true (Euclidean) signed distance, as
  /// @ref voxelize::MeshIntegrator converts a mesh to. `false`, the default,
  /// codes every block with an observed voxel under its observed mask, as
  /// fused depth needs. `true` codes, without writing the grid:
  /// - only the blocks holding a corner of a cell whose 8 voxels, across
  ///   block faces too, are observed and not cut, and whose sign changes or
  ///   that has a corner within one voxel of zero;
  /// - each of their observed voxels as observed, but the cut: every corner
  ///   farther than `sqrt(3)` voxels from zero of a cell whose 8 voxels are
  ///   observed and whose sign changes.
  ///
  /// Every voxel of those blocks lies within @ref kTrueSdfBandVoxels voxels
  /// of the zero level, so a grid observed that far out codes every mask as
  /// all ones but the cuts, and every voxel of a coded block but the cuts
  /// decodes with weight 1; a narrower band leaves the voxels past it
  /// unobserved.
  /// @warning Only for a true distance: fused depth has crossings with
  ///          corners past `sqrt(3)` voxels, which the cut would erase.
  bool true_sdf = false;

  /// @brief The update segment size a P-frame of this config codes with.
  /// @return @ref update_size, or @ref segment_size when @ref update_size is
  ///         0: what @ref validate checks and @ref Encoder::create keeps.
  constexpr std::uint32_t resolved_update_size() const noexcept {
    return update_size != 0 ? update_size : segment_size;
  }

  /// @brief Check every field against what the @ref Encoder takes: what
  ///        @ref Encoder::create checks first, and what a caller checks
  ///        before any GPU work.
  /// @return OK, or `Status::invalid_argument` naming the field: invalid
  ///         @ref params (@ref CodecParams::validate), a @ref segment_size of
  ///         0, a @ref segment_size or nonzero @ref update_size past
  ///         @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize, or an @ref intra_period of 0.
  core::Status validate() const;
};

/// @brief A frame whose front half was recorded into a caller's batch
///        (@ref Encoder::record_front): for @ref Encoder::record_back,
///        @ref Encoder::finish or @ref Encoder::abandon.
///
/// A token: the encoder keeps what the halves need, and its next
/// @ref Encoder::record_front supersedes an unfinished one.
struct PendingEncode {
  /// Which record this is, unique in the process; 0 for none.
  std::uint64_t serial = 0;
  /// What the frame is coded as, decided at record by @ref Encoder::encode's
  /// rules; a P-frame whose grid turns out to hold no block to code finishes
  /// as an I-frame of none.
  FrameType type = FrameType::kIntra;
};

/// @brief A frame @ref Encoder::finish returned: its bytes are @ref head then
///        the payload, back to back, the payload where the device wrote it in
///        one of the encoder's slots, held until this is dropped.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::EncodedFrame frame, encoder.finish(pending));
/// const stream::RecordPayload bytes = stream::RecordPayload::of(
///     frame.head.data(), frame.head.size(), frame.payload,
///     frame.payload_size);
/// @endcode
struct EncodedFrame {
  FrameType type = FrameType::kIntra;  ///< An I-frame or a P-frame.
  std::uint32_t blocks = 0;            ///< The blocks it carries.
  /// The header, the section table and every section but PAYLOAD's body,
  /// which comes last.
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> head;
  /// The PAYLOAD section's body, @ref payload_size bytes in @ref slot; null
  /// for a frame of no blocks.
  const std::uint8_t* payload = nullptr;
  std::size_t payload_size = 0;  ///< Its bytes.
  core::HostSlot slot;           ///< Holds @ref payload.
  /// @return The frame's bytes: the head's and the payload's.
  std::size_t size() const noexcept { return head.size() + payload_size; }
};

/// @brief Encodes a @ref volume::VoxelBlockGrid's geometry as frames -- the
///        codec's capture side (the 2026-09-26 decision).
///
/// A frame holds every active block that has at least one observed voxel
/// (`weight >= volume::kObservedWeight`), or with @ref EncoderConfig::true_sdf
/// every block that holds surface: its coordinate, a 1-bit-per-voxel observed
/// mask, and the first K coefficients of its 8^3 DCT, entropy-coded (the
/// 2026-09-27 format). A block with **no** observed voxel is left out -- the
/// mesher uses nothing from it, and a fused grid allocates a whole truncation
/// band, much of which is never integrated -- so a decoded grid can hold
/// fewer blocks than the one encoded, and the same surface (with
/// @ref EncoderConfig::true_sdf, the surface less its cuts).
///
/// The blocks are coded in (z, y, x) order, whatever order the hash table
/// holds them in, so the same content always makes the same bytes on the same
/// device (a frame is reproducible per device, decodable on any): at an
/// @ref EncoderConfig::intra_period of 1 any frame, and above it the same
/// chain of grids, from a fresh encoder or after the same I-frame.
///
/// A P-frame (@ref FrameType::kInter) codes a frame against the last one
/// @ref encode returned, its reference, which the encoder keeps on the
/// device as it coded it -- quantized coefficients, masks and block
/// list -- so the reference is the one a @ref Decoder holds after decoding
/// that frame: each block is skipped when unchanged, kept as residuals
/// against the reference, recoded in full, or removed, and blocks the
/// reference lacks follow as in an intra frame. A frame decodes to the same
/// grid whichever type it is. Only a frame @ref encode returns becomes the
/// reference, so a refusal keeps the chain, and a frame returned and then
/// lost -- never decoded, or decoded out of order -- breaks it until the
/// next I-frame: call @ref force_intra. The reference and the frame being
/// encoded take `80 + 4 * ceil(K / 2)` bytes of device memory a block each,
/// and the frame 8 more; a P-frame's entries `80 + 4 * ceil(K / 2)` a block
/// of the frame and `72 + 4 * ceil(K / 2)` a reference block, all kept,
/// sized for the largest frame; @ref EncoderConfig::true_sdf 68 bytes more
/// a block slot of the grid's heap, kept too.
///
/// Geometry only: colour is not coded. A player textures the decoded mesh
/// from RGB that travels beside the frame.
///
