### include/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_client.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file networking/stream_client.hpp
/// @brief Read a session a @ref StreamServer serves, as it arrives.

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.hpp"  // kDefaultPort
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking {

/// @brief How a @ref StreamClient reads.
struct ClientOptions {
  /// No byte for this long, counted from @ref StreamClient::connect (the
  /// name lookup and the TCP connect included), ends the connection with
  /// `Status::Code::IoError`: a sender that stalled, or a path that died (the
  /// VPN dropped). @ref StreamClient::next judges it after taking what has
  /// come (the lookup's answer, the connect's end, bytes), so a caller back
  /// late keeps a sender that kept sending. Positive; `milliseconds::max()`
  /// is never.
  std::chrono::milliseconds idle_limit{10'000};
};

/// @brief Reads one connection to a @ref StreamServer: its session, then its
///        records in order, each checked against both CRCs
///        (`stream::ChunkParser`).
///
/// A chunk that fails a check ends the connection; nothing is resynced. A
/// seq may jump where the server skipped to a newer key, and a geometry
/// consumer then decodes again from the next key (`codec::Decoder`'s
/// `NotFound`). Its receive buffer is 2 MiB, set before the connect: the most
/// a stream carries a round trip, and what a reader that falls behind can
/// hide from the server's drop rule. Linux holds it to `net.core.rmem_max`.
///
/// **Messages.** Every error @ref next returns reads
/// `"StreamClient: <host>:<port>: <reason>"`, the host and port as given to
/// @ref connect, and the reason never names them again: a caller showing the
/// address drops the prefix. The reasons: "cannot look up the name: …" (the
/// resolver's words, or "no IPv4 address for TCP") and "cannot connect: …"
/// (the system's); past the idle limit, the stage it ended: "the lookup gave
/// no answer within N ms", "cannot connect within N ms", "connected, but no
/// session within N ms" or "no byte for N ms"; "the sender closed the
/// connection", with " before its session (it may already serve its most
/// viewers)" when none had come; a failed check's `stream::ChunkParser`
/// message; a socket call's ("cannot receive: …"); or "out of memory" for an
/// allocation that failed, bare when even the prefix cannot be allocated.
/// @ref connect's own refusals read `"StreamClient::connect: <reason>"`.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(auto client, networking::StreamClient::connect(
///                             "192.168.21.217", networking::kDefaultPort));
/// stream::Record record;
/// std::vector<std::uint8_t> payload;
/// for (;;) {
///   VKC_ASSIGN(const bool got, client->next(10ms, &record, &payload));
///   if (got) decode(client->session()->tracks[record.info.track], payload);
///   // else: nothing yet, look at quit and park here
/// }
/// @endcode
///
/// @warning Not thread-safe: one thread uses it.
class VGRID_NETWORKING_API StreamClient {
 public:
  /// @brief A client of @p host's sender; never blocks. A name is looked up
  ///        at once, on a detached helper thread, which the client abandons
  ///        if it is destroyed first; @ref next makes the TCP connect. Since
  ///        @ref ClientOptions::idle_limit counts from here, call @ref next
  ///        soon after.
  /// @param host     A name, or a numeric IPv4 address.
  /// @param port     The sender's port.
  /// @param options  How it reads.
  /// @return The client; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for an empty host,
  ///         port 0 or an `idle_limit` of 0 or less;
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` when the lookup's thread
  ///         cannot start; `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when the client
  ///         cannot be allocated.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamClient>> connect(
      const std::string& host, std::uint16_t port,
      const ClientOptions& options = {});

  /// @brief Closes the connection; never waits for a lookup.
  ~StreamClient();
  StreamClient(const StreamClient&) = delete;
  StreamClient& operator=(const StreamClient&) = delete;
  StreamClient(StreamClient&&) = delete;
  StreamClient& operator=(StreamClient&&) = delete;

  /// @return The session once its chunk has arrived, which is before the
  ///         first record; null before.
  const stream::Session* session() const noexcept;

  /// @brief Wait up to @p wait for the next record, finishing the lookup and
  ///        the connect first. Each address is tried in turn; any connect
  ///        error moves to the next.
  /// @param wait          The longest to wait: however fast bytes come, a
  ///                      call ends within it and one receive (up to
  ///                      2 MiB) more. 0 takes only that receive of what
  ///                      has come; `milliseconds::max()` has no end.
  /// @param[out] record   Its header. Its `offset` is the chunk's offset in
  ///                      the bytes received, as in the file they would make.
  /// @param[out] payload  Its payload, resized to fit; or null to leave it
  ///                      for @ref read, as `stream::ChunkParser::next` does.
  /// @return `true` with a record; `false` when none was whole by then;
  ///         `Status::Code::NotFound` for a name that does not resolve;
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` for a lookup that fails otherwise, a
  ///         connection refused at every address, reset or closed, or idle
  ///         past @ref ClientOptions::idle_limit;
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for bytes that are not a `.vrst`
  ///         stream, fail a check, or hold a session body over
  ///         `stream::kMaxSessionBytes`; `Status::Code::Unsupported` for
  ///         another version or session flags; `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`
  ///         for another chunk's body over
  ///         `stream::ChunkParser::kMaxBodyBytes` (64 MiB), before reading
  ///         it, or an allocation failure. A record setting an unknown flag
  ///         is skipped. After an error the connection is closed, and every
  ///         call returns that error again.
  core::Result<bool> next(std::chrono::milliseconds wait,
                          stream::Record* record,
                          std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload);

  /// @brief Read as @ref next, also reporting progress without a whole record.
  /// @param wait          The longest wait, as in the three-argument overload.
  /// @param[out] record   The next record's header, when one is returned.
  /// @param[out] payload  Its payload, resized to fit, when one is returned;
  ///                      or null, as in the three-argument overload.
  /// @param[out] progressed Optional; reset to false on every call. True if
  ///                       the call returned a record (already buffered or
  ///                       newly received), completed a lookup/connect step,
  ///                       or received bytes successfully. Remains true if a
  ///                       later step is idle. A false result with true
  ///                       progress can be a partial chunk: call again to
  ///                       drain available input before waiting elsewhere.
  ///                       On error, reports only earlier successful steps;
  ///                       the error still closes the connection.
  /// @return The same record, timeout and error results as the three-argument
  ///         overload. A false result with false progress means this call
  ///         found no record and made no progress.
  core::Result<bool> next(std::chrono::milliseconds wait,
                          stream::Record* record,
                          std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload, bool* progressed);

  /// @brief Copy the payload of the record the last @ref next returned with
  ///        no payload into caller memory, such as a decoder's input slot:
  ///        no host vector between the socket's bytes and the slot.
  ///
  /// @code
  /// VKC_ASSIGN(const bool got, client->next(10ms, &record, nullptr));
  /// if (got) {
  ///   VKC_ASSIGN(core::HostSlot slot, decoder.claim_input(record.size));
  ///   VKC_TRY(client->read(record, slot.data(), slot.capacity()));
  /// }
  /// @endcode
  /// @param record    That record.
  /// @param dst       Receives the payload, `record.size` bytes.
  /// @param capacity  Bytes at @p dst.
  /// @return OK; or `stream::ChunkParser::read`'s refusals, which leave the
  ///         connection open and the record held; or the connection's error,
  ///         as @ref next returns it.
  core::Status read(const stream::Record& record, std::uint8_t* dst,
                    std::size_t capacity);

 private:
  struct Impl;
  explicit StreamClient(std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl) noexcept;
  std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file networking/stream_server.hpp
/// @brief Serve a session to viewers over TCP as it is recorded.

#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking {

/// The port a sender serves on, and a viewer connects to when none is named.
inline constexpr std::uint16_t kDefaultPort = 47801;

/// @brief Where and how a @ref StreamServer serves.
struct ServerOptions {
  /// A numeric IPv4 address to listen on; empty listens on every interface.
  std::string host;
  /// The port; 0 takes a free one, which @ref StreamServer::port names.
  std::uint16_t port = kDefaultPort;
  /// Viewers served at once, first come: a connection past them is closed at
  /// accept, the first such refusal and then one in 10 s at most logged at
  /// Warning, the rest at Debug. With no authentication, any host reaching
  /// the port can take a slot, and keeps it until it leaves or stalls
  /// (@ref stall_limit).
  std::size_t max_viewers = 4;
  /// With @ref replay_gop, the most one GOP (a key record and every record
  /// after it) may hold: a record that would pass it is dropped with the
  /// whole GOP, and so is every record until the next key, the viewers frozen
  /// until it. Without, how far behind the newest record a viewer may fall:
  /// one that a record would take past it waits for the next key, alone, and
  /// a record past it on its own goes to none, logged at Warning.
  std::uint64_t max_gop_bytes = std::uint64_t{64} << 20;
  /// A viewer that takes no byte for this long, with bytes waiting for it, is
  /// closed: a peer that vanished. A byte its end acknowledges is taken, so a
  /// slow reader keeps its slot while its end acknowledges a byte within the
  /// limit (one behind a large receive buffer may not), as does one with
  /// nothing waiting (before the first key, or while nothing is published).
  /// Positive; `milliseconds::max()` is never.
  std::chrono::milliseconds stall_limit{10'000};
  /// true: a joiner gets the GOP since the newest key, which the server
  /// keeps, so a sender that cannot make a key, as one replaying a file,
  /// still serves a joiner at once. false, for a sender that makes a key when
  /// @ref StreamServer::key_wanted rises: a joiner waits for the next key,
  /// and the log keeps only what connected viewers still need, at most
  /// @ref max_gop_bytes behind; a viewer that would fall further waits for
  /// the next key. Newest key wins either way.
  bool replay_gop = true;
};

/// @brief Serves one session to viewers over TCP as it is recorded: each
///        gets the session header, the records from the newest key on, or
///        from the next (@ref ServerOptions::replay_gop), then every record
///        as it is published (a @ref StreamClient reads them).
///
/// **The wire is the file.** A viewer receives the `VRST` chunk, then `RECD`
/// chunks byte for byte as `stream::StreamWriter` writes them, with no footer
/// (`stream::ChunkEncoder`).
///
/// A viewer takes its next record only while its socket holds under 128 KiB
/// unsent (`TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT`), so little backlog hides in the kernel. A
/// P-frame is never sent without the records it is predicted from.
///
/// **Newest key wins.** When a newer key arrives before a viewer has sent
/// the records before it, the viewer finishes the chunk under way, skips the
/// rest and goes on from that key, so one slower than the stream stays
/// within about a GOP of it.
///
/// **Joining at the GOP** (@ref ServerOptions::replay_gop, the default). The
/// server keeps one GOP: the newest key record and every record after it. A
/// viewer joins at that key, so it decodes at once. A viewer's first record,
/// after its `VRST` chunk, is the GOP's key, and the server keeps every
/// record since. So once a viewer has the session, it misses no record
/// published after, except by newest key wins.
///
/// **Keys on demand** (`replay_gop` false). A viewer joins waiting for the
/// next key, and from it gets every record, in order, except by newest key
/// wins, while it stays within @ref ServerOptions::max_gop_bytes of the
/// newest. One that a record would take further behind finishes the chunk
/// under way and waits for the next key again. The server keeps only the
/// records a viewer still has to send. Each join and each fall-back counts in
/// @ref key_wanted, so a live sender makes its next frame a key and the
/// viewer waits one frame.
///
/// **Threads.** @ref publish never waits on a socket or a viewer: it copies
/// the record once, takes one lock and wakes the viewers. One thread accepts
/// and one thread per viewer sends. A viewer that joins, leaves or fails is
/// logged at Info, and never reaches @ref publish.
///
/// @code
/// stream::Session session;
/// session.writer = "serve_stream";
/// session.tracks.push_back({stream::TrackKind::Geometry});
/// VKC_ASSIGN(auto server, networking::StreamServer::start(session));
/// VKC_TRY(server->publish(info, frame.data(), frame.size()));
/// @endcode
///
/// @warning Call @ref publish from one thread at a time.
class VGRID_NETWORKING_API StreamServer {
 public:
  /// @brief Listen on @p options' address and start accepting viewers.
  /// @param session  What each viewer gets first: a session
  ///                 `stream::StreamWriter::create` takes, of one track.
  /// @param options  Where and how it serves.
  /// @return The server; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a session the
  ///         writer would refuse, a host that is not numeric IPv4, a
  ///         `max_viewers` of 0 or a `stall_limit` of 0 or less;
  ///         `Status::Code::Unsupported` for more than
  ///         one track; `Status::Code::IoError` for a port that cannot be
  ///         bound (in use) or a thread that cannot start;
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when the session's chunk cannot be
  ///         allocated.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamServer>> start(
      const stream::Session& session, const ServerOptions& options = {});

  /// @brief Close every connection and join every thread: within one poll
  ///        slice (about 20 ms) and the write under way.
  ~StreamServer();
  StreamServer(const StreamServer&) = delete;
  StreamServer& operator=(const StreamServer&) = delete;
  StreamServer(StreamServer&&) = delete;
  StreamServer& operator=(StreamServer&&) = delete;

  /// @brief Hand one record to every viewer, now or as each catches up.
  /// @param info  By `stream::StreamWriter::append`'s rules, checked by the
  ///              same code: a track the session has, seq above the track's
  ///              last, a key's pts no lower than the last key's.
  /// @param data  The payload; may be null when @p size is 0.
  /// @param size  The payload's bytes.
  /// @return OK, with viewers or none; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a
  ///         record breaking the rules, or a payload over
  ///         `stream::ChunkParser::kMaxBodyBytes` (64 MiB), which no viewer
  ///         reads, with nothing sent;
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when it cannot be copied, which
  ///         drops it and every record until the next key, as an overflow
  ///         does. Never a viewer's failure.
  core::Status publish(const stream::RecordInfo& info, const std::uint8_t* data,
                       std::size_t size);

  /// @brief @ref publish a payload in up to two runs: its one copy made from
  ///        both, its CRC the one @p payload carries, not computed again.
  /// @return As the other @ref publish.
  core::Status publish(const stream::RecordInfo& info,
                       const stream::RecordPayload& payload);

  /// @return The port listened on: the one asked for, or the one taken for 0.
  std::uint16_t port() const noexcept;

  /// @brief Viewers that joined or fell back to waiting for a key: without
  ///        @ref ServerOptions::replay_gop, each viewer counted as it joins,
  ///        and again each time it falls back, past `max_gop_bytes` behind or
  ///        when a record is lost (`publish`'s `OutOfMemory`), a waiting
  ///        viewer too when the lost record is a key. A key within
  ///        `max_gop_bytes` counts none, as every viewer goes on from it. A
  ///        sender that sees it rise makes its next frame a key. Safe from
  ///        any thread.
  /// @return The count so far, which never falls; always 0 with
  ///         `replay_gop`, whose joiners start at the GOP's key.
  std::uint64_t key_wanted() const noexcept;

  /// @brief The viewers being served now: each counted from its accepted
  ///        connection, before its first byte, until the server closes it as
  ///        it leaves, fails or stalls past @ref ServerOptions::stall_limit.
  ///        A viewer waiting for a key counts; a connection refused at
  ///        @ref ServerOptions::max_viewers never does. Safe from any thread.
  /// @return The count, at most `max_viewers`.
  std::size_t viewers() const noexcept;

 private:
  struct Impl;
  explicit StreamServer(std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl) noexcept;
  std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file stream/chunks.hpp
/// @brief The `.vrst` chunks in memory (stream/session.hpp): what
///        @ref StreamWriter writes, made without a file, and what
///        @ref StreamReader checks, read from bytes as they arrive.

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {

/// @brief A record's payload as one or two runs of bytes, and their CRC,
///        computed once, by @ref of, for every chunk that frames it: a
///        file's and a server's.
///
/// Borrowed: the bytes must outlive every call given this, unchanged since
/// @ref of. A chunk framed from it carries the CRC @ref of computed, whatever
/// the bytes hold by then.
///
/// @code
/// const stream::RecordPayload payload =
///     stream::RecordPayload::of(head.data(), head.size(), body, body_size);
/// VKC_TRY(writer->append(info, payload));   // one writev, no joined copy
/// VKC_TRY(server->publish(info, payload));  // its one copy, no second CRC
/// @endcode
class VGRID_STREAM_API RecordPayload {
 public:
  /// @brief The payload @p first then @p second, and its CRC.
  /// @param first        Its first run; may be null when @p first_size is 0.
  /// @param first_size   Its bytes.
  /// @param second       Its second run, or null for none.
  /// @param second_size  Its bytes; 0 with a null @p second.
  /// @return The payload. A null run with bytes is a programmer error
  ///         (`VKC_CHECK`).
  static RecordPayload of(const std::uint8_t* first, std::size_t first_size,
                          const std::uint8_t* second = nullptr,
                          std::size_t second_size = 0) noexcept;
  /// @return The first run.
  const std::uint8_t* first() const noexcept { return first_; }
  /// @return Its bytes.
  std::size_t first_size() const noexcept { return first_size_; }
  /// @return The second run, or null.
  const std::uint8_t* second() const noexcept { return second_; }
  /// @return Its bytes.
  std::size_t second_size() const noexcept { return second_size_; }
  /// @return Both runs' bytes.
  std::size_t size() const noexcept { return first_size_ + second_size_; }
  /// @return The CRC of both, as a `RECD` header carries it.
  std::uint32_t crc() const noexcept { return crc_; }

 private:
  RecordPayload() = default;

  const std::uint8_t* first_ = nullptr;
  std::size_t first_size_ = 0;
  const std::uint8_t* second_ = nullptr;
  std::size_t second_size_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t crc_ = 0;
};

/// @brief What @ref StreamWriter writes, without a file: the session chunk,
///        then each record's framing, by the writer's rules.
///
/// The session chunk, then each record's header, payload and padding, are
/// byte for byte the file a @ref StreamWriter makes of the same session and
/// records, less its footer: the writer frames through one.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(stream::ChunkEncoder encoder,
///            stream::ChunkEncoder::create(session));
/// send(encoder.session_chunk());
/// VKC_ASSIGN(const stream::ChunkEncoder::RecordFraming framing,
///            encoder.frame(info, payload.data(), payload.size()));
/// send(framing.header, payload, framing.padding);  // the padding zero bytes
/// @endcode
///
/// @warning Not thread-safe: call @ref frame from one thread.
class VGRID_STREAM_API ChunkEncoder {
 public:
  /// @brief Encode @p session's chunk.
  /// @param session  As @ref StreamWriter::create takes it: at least one
  ///                 track and at most 65535, each of a nonzero kind with a
  ///                 nonzero `rate.den`, and a body of at most
  ///                 @ref kMaxSessionBytes.
  /// @return The encoder, with no record framed;
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a session refused above;
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when the chunk or a diagnostic
  ///         cannot be allocated.
  static core::Result<ChunkEncoder> create(const Session& session);

  /// @return The `VRST` chunk, padding included.
  const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& session_chunk() const noexcept;

  /// @brief A record's chunk is `header`, the payload, then `padding` zero
  ///        bytes, which end it at a multiple of 8.
  struct RecordFraming {
    std::array<std::uint8_t, 56> header{};  ///< The `RECD` header (H = 56).
    std::size_t padding = 0;                ///< 0 to 7.
  };

  /// @brief Frame one record, by @ref StreamWriter::append's rules.
  /// @param info  Its track (below the track count) and fields; @ref
  ///              RecordInfo::seq above the track's last framed record's,
  ///              and a key's pts no lower than the track's last framed
  ///              key's.
  /// @param data  The payload, whose CRC the header carries; may be null
  ///              when @p size is 0.
  /// @param size  The payload's bytes.
  /// @return The framing, with the record counted as the track's last;
  ///         with nothing counted, `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a
  ///         record breaking the rules above or a null @p data with a
  ///         nonzero @p size, and `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when a
  ///         diagnostic cannot be allocated.
  core::Result<RecordFraming> frame(const RecordInfo& info,
                                    const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);

  /// @brief @ref frame a payload in up to two runs, its CRC the one
  ///        @p payload carries, not computed again.
  /// @return As the other @ref frame.
  core::Result<RecordFraming> frame(const RecordInfo& info,
                                    const RecordPayload& payload);

 private:
  // What the record rules check of a track's last framed records.
  struct TrackState {
    bool any = false;      // a record framed
    bool any_key = false;  // a key framed
    std::uint64_t last_seq = 0;
    std::uint64_t last_key_pts_ns = 0;
  };

  ChunkEncoder(std::vector<std::uint8_t> session_chunk, std::size_t tracks);

  std::vector<std::uint8_t> session_chunk_;
  std::vector<TrackState> state_;  // by track
};

/// @brief Reads `.vrst` bytes as they arrive: the session, then each
///        record, with @ref StreamReader's checks. A failed check is final.
///
/// **A header before its body.** The bytes must start with the session
/// chunk. Each check runs once the bytes it needs are in, a chunk header's
/// before any of its body is needed: the `VRST` magic, the version and the
/// flags; H, a multiple of 8 from the least its tag takes to 4096; the
/// header's CRC; a `RECD`'s track; and B, at most @ref kMaxSessionBytes for
/// the session and @ref kMaxBodyBytes for any other chunk. Every chunk's
/// body CRC is checked once the body is whole.
///
/// **What is skipped.** A chunk of another tag (`INDX` and `TAIL`, a
/// finished file's footer, included) and a `RECD` setting a flag this
/// version does not know are skipped by their size, once checked, so a
/// whole file whose chunks are within the limits above parses, finished or
/// not. Nothing resyncs: after a failure, every call returns it again.
///
/// **Memory.** @ref feed copies its bytes. The parser holds the chunk it is
/// reading and what was fed after it: about one chunk, when it is fed a piece
/// at a time and @ref next is called until it returns `false` before the
/// next piece.
///
/// @code
/// stream::ChunkParser parser;
/// stream::Record record;
/// std::vector<std::uint8_t> payload;
/// for (;;) {
///   const std::size_t n = receive(buffer);  // some bytes, as they come
///   VKC_TRY(parser.feed(buffer.data(), n));
///   for (;;) {
///     VKC_ASSIGN(const bool got, parser.next(&record, &payload));
///     if (!got) break;
///     decode(parser.session()->tracks[record.info.track], payload);
///   }
/// }
/// @endcode
///
/// @warning Not thread-safe: one thread uses it.
class VGRID_STREAM_API ChunkParser {
 public:
  /// The largest body of a chunk other than the session's: a larger one is
  /// refused once its header is in, whatever of its body has come.
  static constexpr std::uint64_t kMaxBodyBytes = std::uint64_t{64} << 20;

  /// @brief Take the next @p size bytes, and check what they complete.
  /// @param data  The bytes, copied; may be null when @p size is 0.
  /// @param size  Their count.
  /// @return OK; or the failure, which every later call returns again:
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for bytes that do not start
  ///         with `VRST`, a chunk header out of range or of a `RECD` of a
  ///         track the session lacks, a CRC that fails, a session body above
  ///         @ref kMaxSessionBytes or not parsing exactly;
  ///         `Status::Code::Unsupported` for a session of another version or
  ///         setting a flag; `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for another body
  ///         above @ref kMaxBodyBytes, or an allocation failure.
  core::Status feed(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);

  /// @return The session, once its chunk is in, which is before the first
  ///         record; null before.
  const Session* session() const noexcept;

  /// @brief Take the next record, skipping other chunks.
  ///
  /// With a payload, the @ref read below into it, resized to fit.
  /// @param[out] record   Its header. Its `offset` is its chunk's offset in
  ///                      the bytes fed, as in the file they would make.
  /// @param[out] payload  Its payload, resized to fit; unspecified after a
  ///                      failure. Or null: its body, checked against its
  ///                      CRC, stays here for @ref read until the next call
  ///                      of this, which drops it unread.
  /// @return `true` with a record; `false` when it needs more bytes; or the
  ///         failure, as @ref feed returns it.
  core::Result<bool> next(Record* record, std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload);

  /// @brief Copy the body of the record the last @ref next returned with no
  ///        payload into caller memory, such as a decoder's input slot.
  /// @param record    That record.
  /// @param dst       Receives the body, `record.size` bytes.
  /// @param capacity  Bytes at @p dst.
  /// @return OK, the record taken; with nothing copied and the record still
  ///         held, `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a @p capacity under
  ///         `record.size`, a null @p dst for a body of any bytes, or a
  ///         record that is not the one held; or the failure, as @ref feed
  ///         returns it. A read that succeeds allocates nothing.
  core::Status read(const Record& record, std::uint8_t* dst,
                    std::size_t capacity);

 private:
  // Check what was fed, up to the next record: true when one is whole and
  // checked at `next_`.
  core::Result<bool> advance();
  // Save `failure`, which every later call returns, and return it.
  core::Status fail(core::Status failure);
  // fail() for the exception being handled, within a catch.
  core::Status fail_on_exception() noexcept;

  std::vector<std::uint8_t> buffer_;  // the bytes fed from base_ on
  std::uint64_t base_ = 0;            // buffer_[0]'s offset in the bytes fed
  std::uint64_t next_ = 0;  // the next chunk's offset; past the bytes fed
                            // while its padding is still to come
  bool ready_ = false;      // a checked record starts at next_
  // The bytes of the chunk at next_ that next() returned and read() has not
  // taken; 0 for none.
  std::uint64_t held_ = 0;
  std::optional<Session> session_;
  core::Status failure_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file stream/session.hpp
/// @brief A recording session as a `.vrst` file holds it, and the file's
///        byte layout, version 0.
///
/// A `.vrst` file is a session header and the records appended after it, in
/// tracks, each payload stored and returned byte for byte as appended.
/// @ref StreamWriter writes one and @ref StreamReader reads it.
///
/// **Chunks.** All fields are little-endian. The file is a sequence of
/// chunks, each starting at a multiple of 8 from the start of the file, all
/// framed alike (for every tag and version):
///
/// @code
///   offset  size  field
///        0     4  tag, 4 ASCII bytes
///        4     4  H, the header size: a multiple of 8, 24 <= H <= 4096
///        8     8  B, the body size
///       16     4  body_crc: CRC-32 of the B body bytes (0 when B = 0)
///       20  H-24  the tag's own fields
///      H-4     4  header_crc: CRC-32 of bytes [0, H-4)
/// @endcode
///
/// The body starts at offset H and the next chunk at `offset + H +
/// align8(B)`; the padding bytes are zero and covered by neither CRC. The
/// CRC is zlib's and PNG's CRC-32 (reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial
/// value and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF; `crc32("123456789") = 0xCBF43926`), so
/// Python's `zlib.crc32` checks any chunk.
///
/// **`VRST`**, the session header: the first chunk, its tag the file's
/// magic (H = 56).
///
/// @code
///       20     4  version (0)
///       24    16  session_id (all zero: none)
///       40     8  created_ns: system_clock ns since the Unix epoch; 0 unknown
///       48     2  T, the track count (1..65535)
///       50     2  flags (0)
///       52     4  header_crc
/// @endcode
///
/// Its body, at most @ref kMaxSessionBytes and parsed exactly: T track
/// entries of 24 bytes, then strings, each a `u32` length and its bytes: the
/// writer, the calibration, and for each track its sensor, then its params.
/// A track's id is its index in the table.
///
/// @code
///   track entry
///        0     2  kind (never 0)
///        2     2  clock (0: the host's system_clock; n >= 1: clock domain n)
///        4     4  rate_num (0: unknown)
///        8     4  rate_den (>= 1)
///       12     4  width
///       16     4  height (both 0 when the track is not pictures)
///       20     4  reserved
/// @endcode
///
/// **`RECD`**, one record (H = 56); its body is the payload.
///
/// @code
///       20     2  track (< T)
///       22     2  flags: bit 0 key
///       24     8  pts_ns, on the track's clock
///       32     8  seq
///       40     8  set (all ones: kNoSet)
///       48     4  reserved
///       52     4  header_crc
/// @endcode
///
/// **`INDX`**, the footer index (H = 40), and **`TAIL`**, the last 40 bytes
/// of a finished file (H = 40, B = 0), which names where `INDX` starts.
///
/// @code
///   INDX                                   TAIL
///       20     4  T                            20     4  reserved
///       24     8  K, the key records           24     8  index_offset
///       32     4  reserved                     32     4  reserved
///       36     4  header_crc                   36     4  header_crc
/// @endcode
///
/// The `INDX` body, B = 40 T + 32 K: T @ref TrackStats of five `u64`s, in
/// field order, then K key entries in file order: the `u64` offset of the
/// `RECD` chunk, `u64` pts_ns, `u64` set, `u16` track, 6 reserved bytes.
///
/// **Rules.**
/// - A record's track's records are in decode order, its seq strictly
///   increasing (a jump: records lost before the writer saw them), and a key
///   record's pts never below the previous key's; other pts may go back.
///   Tracks interleave in append order.
/// - A reader skips an unknown tag by its size and ignores the trailing
///   fields of an H larger than it knows. Reserved fields are written as zero
///   and ignored when read.
/// - A flag bit a reader does not know is `Unsupported`: at file level for
///   `VRST`, for that record alone for `RECD`.
/// - The version changes only for a change an old reader must not ignore.

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {

/// @brief What a track's payloads are. A kind comes with its first writer;
///        a reader passes the values it does not know through as read.
enum class TrackKind : std::uint16_t {
  /// One codec frame per record, exactly what `codec::Encoder::encode`
  /// returned; a key record is an intra frame. The track has no width,
  /// height or sensor: the frame's own header says what it is. Its params
  /// are empty, or the bytes of `mesh_io::encode_transform`
  /// (io/mesh_normalization.hpp): the transform that placed a mesh source in
  /// metres.
  Geometry = 1,
};

/// @brief The clock of @ref Track::clock that is the host's
///        `std::chrono::system_clock`: ns since the Unix epoch, comparable
///        across every track on it. Any other value is a clock domain whose
///        origin is arbitrary, comparable only among tracks naming it.
inline constexpr std::uint16_t kHostClock = 0;

/// @brief The @ref RecordInfo::set of a record in no set.
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kNoSet = ~std::uint64_t{0};

/// @brief The most a session's `VRST` body -- its track table and strings
///        -- may hold.
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kMaxSessionBytes = std::uint64_t{64} << 20;

/// @brief A rate as a fraction, records a second for a track.
struct Rate {
  std::uint32_t num = 0;  ///< 0 when unknown.
  std::uint32_t den = 1;  ///< At least 1.
};

/// @brief How far apart a track's records are nominally, for a reader that
///        paces them where their pts cannot.
/// @param rate  The track's @ref Track::rate.
/// @return @p rate 's period in ns, rounded down; for an unknown rate (a
///         `num` or `den` of 0), 30 a second's, so every reader paces an
///         unknown rate alike.
inline constexpr std::uint64_t nominal_period_ns(Rate rate) noexcept {
  constexpr std::uint64_t kNsPerSecond = 1'000'000'000;
  if (rate.num == 0 || rate.den == 0) return kNsPerSecond / 30;
  return kNsPerSecond * rate.den / rate.num;
}

/// @brief One track of a session: a stream of records of one kind.
struct Track {
  TrackKind kind{};  ///< Never 0.
  /// @ref kHostClock, or the clock domain its pts are on.
  std::uint16_t clock = 1;
  Rate rate;                 ///< Its nominal rate.
  std::uint32_t width = 0;   ///< Picture width; 0 when not pictures.
  std::uint32_t height = 0;  ///< Picture height; 0 when not pictures.
  std::string sensor;        ///< The sensor's id, or empty.
  std::string params;        ///< What the kind defines (@ref TrackKind).
};

/// @brief What a session header holds.
///
/// @code
/// stream::Session session;
/// session.writer = "codec_replica";
/// session.tracks.push_back({stream::TrackKind::Geometry});
/// @endcode
struct Session {
  std::array<std::uint8_t, 16> id{};  ///< All zero for none.
  /// The host's `system_clock` at the start, ns since the Unix epoch; 0 when
  /// unknown. The writer records what it is given, so two runs given the
  /// same session write the same bytes.
  std::uint64_t created_ns = 0;
  std::string writer;  ///< The program that wrote the file (UTF-8).
  /// The camera tier's calibration document, byte for byte, or empty.
  std::string calibration;
  std::vector<Track> tracks;  ///< At least 1, at most 65535.
};

/// @brief What a record's header says about its payload.
struct RecordInfo {
  std::uint16_t track = 0;  ///< Its track's index in @ref Session::tracks.
  /// A record decoding can start at: for Geometry, an intra frame.
  bool key = false;
  std::uint64_t pts_ns = 0;  ///< Its time on its track's clock.
  /// Its number in its track, strictly increasing; a jump says records were
  /// lost before the writer saw them.
  std::uint64_t seq = 0;
  /// The capture set it belongs to, across tracks, or @ref kNoSet.
  std::uint64_t set = kNoSet;
};

/// @brief A track's records, as the footer index and a scan both count
///        them.
struct TrackStats {
  std::uint64_t records = 0;        ///< Its records.
  std::uint64_t keys = 0;           ///< Its key records.
  std::uint64_t payload_bytes = 0;  ///< Its payloads' bytes.
  std::uint64_t min_pts_ns = 0;     ///< Its least pts; 0 with no records.
  std::uint64_t max_pts_ns = 0;     ///< Its greatest pts; 0 with no records.
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file stream/stream_reader.hpp
/// @brief Read a `.vrst` file: its session, its records in file order, and
///        its key records by track, from a finished file or a killed
///        writer's.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/unique_fd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {

/// @brief How a @ref StreamReader reads.
struct ReaderOptions {
  /// The largest payload @ref StreamReader::read allocates; a larger one is
  /// `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` before any allocation.
  std::size_t max_payload_bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>().max_size();
};

/// @brief What opening a file found besides its records.
///
/// None of it is an error: a killed writer leaves no footer and perhaps
/// part of a record, and damage in the middle costs only the records it
/// hit. A file opened from its footer is not scanned, so damage among its
/// records shows only where @ref StreamReader::next meets it.
struct Recovery {
  /// The file ends with the footer @ref StreamWriter::finish writes, and
  /// @ref StreamReader::open took the counts and key records from it,
  /// reading no record: a `TAIL` naming the `INDX` that ends where it
  /// starts, which passes both its CRCs, is sized for the session's tracks
  /// and its key count (at most the file's size / 56), and lists key records
  /// in file order, each of a track the session has and at a multiple of 8
  /// between the session header and the index, no track's pts decreasing,
  /// and as many of each track as its summary counts. What the index lists
  /// is not compared with the records: at a key position it got wrong,
  /// @ref StreamReader::next meets what is there as it would anywhere.
  bool finished = false;
  /// Not @ref finished, though the scan found a chunk tagged `TAIL`, its
  /// header intact or not, where the footer's `TAIL` starts: the 40 bytes
  /// before the file's end.
  bool footer_damaged = false;
  /// Where the records end: what follows is @ref torn_bytes.
  std::uint64_t end = 0;
  /// The bytes from @ref end on: a chunk whose body the file cuts short, or
  /// damage after which no chunk header passes its checks.
  std::uint64_t torn_bytes = 0;
  /// The bytes of the damaged spans, each from a chunk header that fails its
  /// checks to the next `RECD`, `INDX` or `TAIL` header that passes them.
  std::uint64_t damaged_bytes = 0;
  std::uint64_t damaged_spans = 0;  ///< Their count.
};

/// @brief Where a @ref StreamReader::next reads from: a chunk's offset in
///        the file.
struct Position {
  std::uint64_t offset = 0;  ///< A multiple of 8, past the session header.
};

/// @brief A record's header, as @ref StreamReader::next found it.
struct Record {
  RecordInfo info;           ///< What the header says.
  std::uint64_t offset = 0;  ///< Its `RECD` chunk's offset in the file.
  std::uint64_t size = 0;    ///< Its payload's bytes.
};

/// @brief Reads one `.vrst` file (stream/session.hpp).
///
/// **Open reads the footer, or scans.** @ref open checks the session header,
/// then takes the records' counts (@ref stats) and each track's key records
/// (@ref key, @ref key_at) from a finished file's footer index
/// (@ref Recovery::finished). Any other file it scans, reading one small
/// chunk header after another, never a payload. A chunk header that fails
/// its CRC, or holds what no chunk can, starts a search, 8 bytes at a time,
/// for the next `RECD`, `INDX` or `TAIL` with a valid header; the bytes
/// skipped are a damaged span (@ref Recovery), and with no chunk after
/// them, the torn tail.
///
/// **Reading.** @ref next returns record headers in file order from a
/// @ref Position the caller holds, and @ref read a record's payload, checked
/// against its CRC. A failed @ref next moves the position past the damage,
/// so iteration continues; a geometry consumer then resynchronises at the
/// next key record.
///
/// The file is read as it was at @ref open: its size then is where reading
/// stops.
/// Host allocation failures, including building a diagnostic for invalid
/// arguments or missing keys, return `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`.
///
/// @code
/// VKC_ASSIGN(auto reader, stream::StreamReader::open(path));
/// stream::Position pos = reader->begin();
/// stream::Record record;
/// std::vector<std::uint8_t> payload;
/// for (;;) {
///   const core::Result<bool> more = reader->next(&pos, &record);
///   if (!more.ok()) continue;  // damage: pos is past it
///   if (!more.value()) break;
///   if (reader->read(record, &payload).ok()) decode(payload);
/// }
/// @endcode
///
/// Every method is `const` and safe to call from several threads at once,
/// each with its own @ref Position.
class VGRID_STREAM_API StreamReader {
 public:
  /// @brief Open the file at @p path, from its footer when it is finished,
  ///        otherwise by a scan.
  /// @param path     A `.vrst` file.
  /// @param options  How it is read.
  /// @return The reader; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for an empty path or
  ///         one with a NUL, something other than a regular file, a file
  ///         under 56 bytes or without the `VRST` magic, or a session header
  ///         out of range, failing a CRC or unparsable;
  ///         `Status::Code::Unsupported` for a session header of another
  ///         version or setting a flag; `Status::Code::NotFound` when the
  ///         file or its directory does not exist; otherwise
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` or `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamReader>> open(
      const std::string& path, const ReaderOptions& options = {});

  ~StreamReader() = default;
  StreamReader(const StreamReader&) = delete;
  StreamReader& operator=(const StreamReader&) = delete;
  StreamReader(StreamReader&&) = delete;
  StreamReader& operator=(StreamReader&&) = delete;

  /// @return The session header.
  const Session& session() const noexcept;
  /// @return What opening the file found besides the records.
  const Recovery& recovery() const noexcept;
  /// @return Each track's records, by track: as the footer index counts
  ///         them, or else the scan, which does not count a record setting
  ///         a flag this version does not know.
  const std::vector<TrackStats>& stats() const noexcept;

  /// @param track  A track's index.
  /// @return The key records of @p track; 0 for a track that does not
  ///         exist.
  std::size_t key_count(std::uint16_t track) const noexcept;

  /// @brief Where @p track 's key record @p n is.
  /// @param track  A track's index.
  /// @param n      Which key, from 0 in file order.
  /// @return Its position, as the footer index or the scan found it;
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a track that does not exist;
  ///         `Status::Code::NotFound` for @p n of @ref key_count or more.
  core::Result<Position> key(std::uint16_t track, std::size_t n) const;

  /// @brief Where @p track 's last key record with a pts at or before
  ///        @p pts_ns is: where playback seeking to @p pts_ns starts.
  /// @param track   A track's index.
  /// @param pts_ns  The time sought, on the track's clock.
  /// @return Its position; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a track that
  ///         does not exist, or whose key pts decrease (a file this
  ///         library's writer did not make); `Status::Code::NotFound` when
  ///         its first key is later than @p pts_ns, or it has none.
  core::Result<Position> key_at(std::uint16_t track,
                                std::uint64_t pts_ns) const;

  /// @return The position of the first chunk after the session header.
  Position begin() const noexcept;

  /// @brief Read the header of the next record at or after @p pos, skipping
  ///        other chunks.
  /// @param[in,out] pos     Where to read; moved past what was read, or
  ///                        past the damage on a failure.
  /// @param[out]    record  The record's header, on `true`.
  /// @return `true` with a record; `false` at the end; or, with @p pos past
  ///         the damage, `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a chunk header
  ///         failing its CRC or out of range, or a record of a track that
  ///         does not exist, and `Status::Code::Unsupported` for a record
  ///         setting a flag this version does not know.
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` too, with @p pos unchanged, for
  ///         a position that is not a multiple of 8 or lies before
  ///         @ref begin; otherwise `Status::Code::IoError`.
  core::Result<bool> next(Position* pos, Record* record) const;

  /// @brief Read a record's payload, checking its header again and its
  ///        payload against its CRC.
  ///
  /// The read below, into a vector resized to fit.
  /// @param record   A record @ref next returned from this reader.
  /// @param payload  Receives the payload, resized to fit; what it holds
  ///                 after a failure is unspecified.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` naming the offset when the
  ///         payload fails its CRC or the header is no longer
  ///         @p record 's; `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for a payload above
  ///         `ReaderOptions::max_payload_bytes` or an allocation failure;
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` for a read failure or a file shorter
  ///         than at open.
  core::Status read(const Record& record,
                    std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload) const;

  /// @brief Read a record's payload into caller memory, such as a decoder's
  ///        input slot, checking its header again and its payload against its
  ///        CRC.
  /// @param record    A record @ref next returned from this reader.
  /// @param dst       Receives the payload, `record.size` bytes; unspecified
  ///                  after a failure.
  /// @param capacity  Bytes at @p dst.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a @p capacity under
  ///         `record.size` or a null @p dst for a payload of any bytes (both
  ///         before anything is read),
  ///         a payload failing its CRC, or a header no longer @p record 's;
  ///         or `Status::Code::IoError` for a read failure or a file shorter
  ///         than at open. A read that succeeds allocates nothing.
  core::Status read(const Record& record, std::uint8_t* dst,
                    std::size_t capacity) const;

 private:
  // A key record, as the footer index or the scan found it.
  struct KeyPoint {
    std::uint64_t offset = 0;
    std::uint64_t pts_ns = 0;
  };

  StreamReader() = default;

  // Take the stats and the key records from the footer: false when the file
  // has none that passes the checks Recovery::finished lists.
  core::Result<bool> read_footer();

  // Count the records and find the key records from `begin_` to the file's
  // end, and whether a footer's TAIL is there.
  core::Status scan();

  core::UniqueFd fd_;
  std::string path_;
  ReaderOptions options_;
  std::uint64_t file_size_ = 0;  // at open
  std::uint64_t begin_ = 0;      // the first chunk after the session header
  Session session_;
  Recovery recovery_;
  std::vector<TrackStats> stats_;
  std::vector<std::vector<KeyPoint>> keys_;  // by track, in file order
  std::vector<bool> keys_unordered_;         // by track: key pts decrease
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_writer.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file stream/stream_writer.hpp
/// @brief Record a session to a new `.vrst` file, a record at a time.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/unique_fd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {

/// @brief Writes one `.vrst` file (stream/session.hpp): the session header,
///        then each record as it is appended, then on @ref finish the
///        footer index. The chunks, and the rules a record follows, are
///        @ref ChunkEncoder's.
///
/// **Visible and recoverable while written.** The file appears at its path
/// when @ref create makes it, and every @ref append is one `writev` with no
/// buffering here, so a killed process loses nothing it appended, and a
/// reader recovers every whole record from a file that was never finished.
/// A power loss can lose what came after the last @ref sync.
///
/// **A failed write sticks.** After a write or flush fails, every call
/// returns the saved failure and writes nothing more; the file reads as a
/// killed writer's. After @ref finish, every call is refused.
/// Host allocation failures, including building or copying a diagnostic,
/// return `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`. Validation or preparation allocation
/// failures leave the writer unchanged; a failed write or flush remains
/// sticky even when its diagnostic cannot be allocated.
///
/// @code
/// stream::Session session;
/// session.writer = "codec_replica";
/// session.tracks.push_back({stream::TrackKind::Geometry});
/// VKC_ASSIGN(auto writer, stream::StreamWriter::create(path, session));
/// for (std::uint64_t i = 0; i < frames.size(); ++i) {
///   stream::RecordInfo info;
///   info.key = true;
///   info.pts_ns = i * 33'333'333;
///   info.seq = i;
///   VKC_TRY(writer->append(info, frames[i].data(), frames[i].size()));
/// }
/// VKC_TRY(writer->finish());
/// @endcode
///
/// @warning Not thread-safe: call it from one thread.
class VGRID_STREAM_API StreamWriter {
 public:
  /// @brief Create the file at @p path and write @p session's header to it,
  ///        flushed to storage with its directory entry.
  /// @param path     Where the new file goes; nothing may be there, and its
  ///                 directory must exist.
  /// @param session  The header. At least one track and at most 65535, each
  ///                 of a nonzero kind with a nonzero `rate.den`, and a body
  ///                 of at most @ref kMaxSessionBytes.
  /// @return The writer; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for an empty path or
  ///         one with a NUL, a session refused above (with nothing created),
  ///         or anything already at @p path, a symbolic link included (left
  ///         untouched); `Status::Code::NotFound` when the directory does not
  ///         exist; otherwise `Status::Code::IoError` or
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`, with any file it made removed.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamWriter>> create(
      const std::string& path, const Session& session);

  /// @brief Closes the file. Without @ref finish it has no footer, and reads
  ///        as a killed writer's: every record it holds, `finished` false.
  ~StreamWriter();
  StreamWriter(const StreamWriter&) = delete;
  StreamWriter& operator=(const StreamWriter&) = delete;
  StreamWriter(StreamWriter&&) = delete;
  StreamWriter& operator=(StreamWriter&&) = delete;

  /// @brief Append one record: its header and @p size payload bytes, stored
  ///        as given.
  /// @param info  Its track (below the track count) and fields; @ref
  ///              RecordInfo::seq above the track's last record's, and a
  ///              key's pts no lower than the track's last key's.
  /// @param data  The payload; may be null when @p size is 0.
  /// @param size  The payload's bytes.
  /// @return OK once written; with nothing written,
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a record breaking the rules
  ///         above, a null @p data with a nonzero @p size, or a finished
  ///         writer, and `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when a key's room in the
  ///         footer index cannot be allocated; or the saved I/O failure.
  ///         Diagnostic allocation failures are also
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory`.
  core::Status append(const RecordInfo& info, const std::uint8_t* data,
                      std::size_t size);

  /// @brief @ref append a payload in up to two runs: one `writev` of the
  ///        record's header, both runs and the padding, its CRC the one
  ///        @p payload carries, not computed again.
  /// @return As the other @ref append.
  core::Status append(const RecordInfo& info, const RecordPayload& payload);

  /// @brief Flush what is written to storage: `fsync`, or on Apple
  ///        `F_FULLFSYNC`, as `fsync` there stops at the drive's cache.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` once finished; the saved I/O
  ///         failure; or `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for diagnostic allocation.
  core::Status sync();

  /// @brief Write the footer (`INDX` and `TAIL`), flush and close the file.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` once finished;
  ///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` when the index cannot be built (the
  ///         writer unchanged) or a diagnostic cannot be allocated; or the
  ///         saved I/O failure.
  core::Status finish();

  /// @return The file's bytes written so far.
  std::uint64_t size() const noexcept;

 private:
  StreamWriter(core::UniqueFd fd, std::string path, ChunkEncoder encoder,
               std::size_t tracks);

  // The sticky failure, or the refusal of a call after `finish`.
  core::Status check_open(std::string_view api) const;

  core::UniqueFd fd_;
  std::string path_;
  ChunkEncoder encoder_;  // the session's chunk and the record rules
  std::uint64_t size_ = 0;
  std::vector<TrackStats> stats_;  // by track
  // The footer index's key entries, encoded as they are appended.
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> index_keys_;
  core::Status failure_;  // the sticky write or flush failure
  bool finished_ = false;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/frustum.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file volume/frustum.hpp
/// @brief Camera view-frustum planes for culling the active voxel-block set.

#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include <glm/gtc/matrix_inverse.hpp>

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/math/vector_types.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// @brief The six planes of a camera view frustum, in world space.
///
/// Each plane is `(nx, ny, nz, d)` in **Hessian normal form** with an
/// inward-pointing unit normal: a world point `p` is inside when
/// `dot(n, p) + d >= 0` for all six. Order is left, right, top, bottom, near,
/// far. This is exactly what the `hash_compact_frustum` kernel reads, six
/// `vec4` a frustum after the frusta's count under scalar block layout, so
/// the array uploads verbatim.
using FrustumPlanes = std::array<Vec4f, 6>;
// Pin the upload size the way every other shader-fed POD does (2026-07-05 ABI):
// the `vgrid::` backing type is swappable, so a Vec4f layout change is a
// compile error here, not a silent frustum misprojection.
static_assert(sizeof(FrustumPlanes) == 96,
              "FrustumPlanes must be 96 bytes (6 x vec4) to match the shader's "
              "scalar-layout planes, six a frustum");

/// @brief Build the world-space frustum planes for a pinhole camera.
///
/// The four side planes come from the image borders (a pixel `(u, v)` is inside
/// when `0 <= u <= width` and `0 <= v <= height`, the camera looking down +Z as
/// in @ref VoxelHashMap::allocate_from_depth); near/far clip in depth. The side
/// planes are widened ~10% (focal lengths scaled by 0.9) so a block straddling
/// the image edge is kept rather than clipped -- the cull is deliberately
/// conservative, while the principal point lies inside the image: outside
/// it, scaling the focal length moves that side's plane inward. Each
/// camera-space plane is carried to world space by the inverse-transpose
/// of @p cam_to_world and renormalized to unit normal.
/// @param fx,fy          Focal lengths (pixels).
/// @param cx,cy          Principal point (pixels).
/// @param width,height   Image dimensions (pixels).
/// @param near_z,far_z   Near/far clip distances (metres, along camera +Z).
/// @param cam_to_world   Camera->world rigid transform (column-major).
/// @return The six inward-normal, unit-length frustum planes.
inline FrustumPlanes make_frustum_planes(float fx, float fy, float cx, float cy,
                                         std::uint32_t width,
                                         std::uint32_t height, float near_z,
                                         float far_z,
                                         const Mat4f& cam_to_world) {
  const float w = static_cast<float>(width);
  const float h = static_cast<float>(height);
  // Widen the lateral planes ~10% so an edge-straddling block survives the
  // cull.
  constexpr float kSideMargin = 0.9f;
  const float sx = fx * kSideMargin;
  const float sy = fy * kSideMargin;

  // Camera-space planes (inward normals; camera looks down +Z): left/right from
  // 0 <= u <= w, top/bottom from 0 <= v <= h, near/far from near_z <= z <=
  // far_z.
  const std::array<Vec4f, 6> camera_planes = {
      Vec4f(sx, 0.0f, cx, 0.0f),         // left:   sx*x + cx*z >= 0
      Vec4f(-sx, 0.0f, w - cx, 0.0f),    // right:  -sx*x + (w-cx)*z >= 0
      Vec4f(0.0f, sy, cy, 0.0f),         // top:    sy*y + cy*z >= 0
      Vec4f(0.0f, -sy, h - cy, 0.0f),    // bottom: -sy*y + (h-cy)*z >= 0
      Vec4f(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f, -near_z),  // near:   z - near_z >= 0
      Vec4f(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f, far_z),   // far:    far_z - z >= 0
  };

  // A plane transforms by the inverse-transpose of the point transform.
  const Mat4f to_world = glm::inverseTranspose(cam_to_world);
  FrustumPlanes planes;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < planes.size(); ++i) {
    const Vec4f p = to_world * camera_planes[i];
    const float len = glm::length(Vec3f(p));
    planes[i] = len > 0.0f ? p / len : p;
  }
  return planes;
}

/// @brief Build the world-space frustum planes from a camera's combined
///        view-projection matrix -- the *render* camera's form of the overload
///        above.
///
/// That one takes intrinsics in pixels, in the OpenCV convention the fusion
/// tiers pose a depth camera in (+Z forward, y down). A viewer's camera has
/// neither: it carries a projection built for clip space, and its handedness is
/// the renderer's. This reads the planes off the matrix itself
/// (Gribb-Hartmann), so it holds for whatever view and projection the caller
/// combined -- which is what culling the *meshed* set to what is on screen
/// needs, a question the depth camera's frustum answers only in follow-camera
/// mode.
///
/// @warning @p view_proj must map depth to **`[0, 1]`** -- Vulkan clip space,
///          which is what `volumetric_kit_gfx`'s `Camera::view_proj` emits (it
///          forces `GLM_FORCE_DEPTH_ZERO_TO_ONE` before including glm). The
///          near plane is read as row 2 alone; under OpenGL's `[-1, 1]` it
///          would be row 3 + row 2. A GL-convention matrix passed here does
///          *not* clip at the eye: row 2 alone normalizes to `z >= 2nf/(n+f)`,
///          the harmonic mean of the caller's near and far, which is always in
///          `(n, 2n)`. So it over-culls a shell roughly one near-distance thick
///          in front of every camera -- mild, and invisible unless something is
///          meant to be meshed that close.
///
/// @warning @p view_proj is a **view-projection**, not a pose. A `cam_to_world`
///          is the same type and compiles, and returns six well-formed planes
///          describing a degenerate box that culls essentially everything --
///          an empty mesh with no error anywhere. A bare scalar is rejected at
///          compile time (see the deleted overload below), but a rigid
///          transform cannot be.
///
/// @param view_proj  `proj * view`, column-major, mapping world -> clip.
/// @param margin_m   Push every plane *except the near one* outward by this
///                   many metres, keeping what is *nearly* visible rather than
///                   only what is. 0 (the default) is the exact frustum.
///                   Non-zero is what a consumer whose cull runs on a different
///                   thread from its draw wants: the mesh a frame draws was
///                   culled against a pose several frames old, and an exact
///                   frustum pops at the screen edge while the camera turns. A
///                   metre and not a focal scale -- the planes are normalized
///                   below, so the offset is a real world-space distance and
///                   stays comparable across fields of view.
///
///                   The near plane is excluded because widening it is the one
///                   direction that changes what the cull *means*: at
///                   `margin_m > z_near` it moves behind the eye, and the
///                   also-widened side planes then admit a real cone of
///                   geometry BEHIND the camera (at a 0.5 m margin on a 0.1 m
///                   near plane, blocks up to 0.36 m behind it and 0.56 m
///                   off-axis). The pinhole overload above widens only its four
///                   lateral planes for the same reason. The cost is a block
///                   crossing `z_near` while the camera moves forward, which
///                   pops at the very edge of the near plane rather than at the
///                   screen edge.
/// @return The six inward-normal, unit-length planes, in the left, right, top,
///         bottom, near, far order the pinhole overload also returns -- with
///         one caveat on the y pair. Which of indices 2 and 3 is the image
///         *top* follows the sign of `view_proj[1][1]`: glm's unflipped
///         `perspectiveRH_ZO` puts the top at index 3, while the y-flip gfx
///         applies for Vulkan puts it at index 2. Cull with all six (which is
///         what `hash_compact_frustum` does) and the distinction never arises;
///         index a single named plane and check the sign first.
inline FrustumPlanes make_frustum_planes(const Mat4f& view_proj,
                                         float margin_m = 0.0f) {
  // Row i of a column-major glm matrix, which indexes m[column][row].
  const auto row = [&view_proj](int i) {
    return Vec4f(view_proj[0][i], view_proj[1][i], view_proj[2][i],
                 view_proj[3][i]);
  };
  const Vec4f r0 = row(0);
  const Vec4f r1 = row(1);
  const Vec4f r2 = row(2);
  const Vec4f r3 = row(3);
  // Each plane is the half-space one clip-space bound describes: -w <= x <= w,
  // -w <= y <= w, and 0 <= z <= w for Vulkan's [0, 1] depth. The two y planes
  // are NOT labelled top and bottom here: which is which follows the sign of
  // the caller's `view_proj[1][1]`, so naming them would be right for gfx's
  // y-flipped projection and wrong for glm's unflipped one. See @return.
  const std::array<Vec4f, 6> clip_planes = {
      r3 + r0,  // left
      r3 - r0,  // right
      r3 + r1,  // y, the `y >= -w` bound
      r3 - r1,  // y, the `y <= w` bound
      r2,       // near
      r3 - r2,  // far
  };
  // The one plane the margin is withheld from; see @param margin_m.
  constexpr std::size_t kNearPlane = 4;
  FrustumPlanes planes;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < planes.size(); ++i) {
    const float len = glm::length(Vec3f(clip_planes[i]));
    // `len > 0.0f` alone is false for a NaN length as well as a zero one, so
    // both used to fall through to the "keep it unnormalized" branch and then
    // still take the margin below -- on a zero plane that makes the test
    // `margin_m >= 0`, which keeps every block and turns the cull into a silent
    // no-op. Neither input is exotic: an all-zero Mat4f is what `Mat4f{}`
    // gives, `glm::infinitePerspectiveRH_ZO` emits an exactly-zero far row, and
    // a zero-width viewport puts inf/NaN through the whole matrix. Handled
    // explicitly instead, adding no margin -- the same shape as the pinhole
    // overload's degenerate branch, and it degrades toward keeping blocks
    // rather than dropping them.
    if (!(len > 0.0f && std::isfinite(len))) {
      planes[i] = clip_planes[i];
      continue;
    }
    planes[i] = clip_planes[i] / len;
    if (i != kNearPlane) {
      // Applied AFTER normalizing, which is the whole reason the margin can be
      // stated in metres: on a unit normal, `dot(n, p) + d` is a signed
      // distance, so raising d moves the plane outward by exactly that far.
      planes[i].w += margin_m;
    }
  }
  return planes;
}

/// @brief Deleted: a bare scalar is not a view-projection matrix.
///
/// glm's scalar-diagonal `mat4` constructor is implicit unless
/// `GLM_FORCE_EXPLICIT_CTOR` is defined, which this repo never does. So
/// `make_frustum_planes(0.5f)` would otherwise compile as
/// `make_frustum_planes(Mat4f(0.5f))` -- six well-formed planes describing a
/// unit box at the origin -- and `make_frustum_planes(100.0f, 100.0f)` as a
/// frustum that keeps everything, both under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` with no
/// diagnostic at all. A template beats the `const Mat4f&` overload on any
/// scalar (exact match versus a user conversion) and loses to it on a real
/// matrix (non-templates win ties), so this rejects exactly the mistakes.
template <typename T>
FrustumPlanes make_frustum_planes(T, float = 0.0f) = delete;

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file volume/hash_types.hpp
/// @brief POD storage layouts for the sparse voxel hash map.
///
/// These are the compute shaders' storage layouts, as plain structs with
/// `static_assert`'d sizes and offsets. `BlockIndex` and `BlockStamp` cross
/// the host/device boundary -- a compacted list, a coordinate list a caller
/// uploads, the stamps read back -- so a layout drift there is a silent
/// corruption bug, made a compile error on the host side. The shaders read
/// them through scalar block layout, not `std430` (the gotchas in DESIGN.md).
///
/// The sparse-hashing scheme (a hash table of block coordinates into a heap of
/// fixed-size voxel blocks) keeps memory proportional to the observed surface
/// rather than the bounding volume. The prior engine's per-voxel neural
/// "feature"/triplane channels are intentionally absent here (see the exclusion
/// policy in AGENTS.md): this carries only SDF, weight, and optional color.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/math/vector_types.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// Active-block reference used in compacted block lists.
struct BlockIndex {
  Vec3i coord;       ///< Voxel-block coordinate.
  std::int32_t ptr;  ///< Offset into the voxel-block array.
};
static_assert(sizeof(BlockIndex) == 16, "BlockIndex must be 16 bytes");
static_assert(offsetof(BlockIndex, coord) == 0, "BlockIndex layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(BlockIndex, ptr) == 12, "BlockIndex layout drift");

/// @return `true` if block coordinate @p a sorts before @p b: by z, then y,
///         then x. The one order every sorted block list here uses, the
///         codec's frames included; `vgridCoordLess` in
///         `volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl` mirrors it for kernels.
inline bool coord_less(const Vec3i& a, const Vec3i& b) noexcept {
  if (a.z != b.z) return a.z < b.z;
  if (a.y != b.y) return a.y < b.y;
  return a.x < b.x;
}

/// @brief One block slot's stamps: ticks of the map's clock
///        (@ref VoxelHashMap::tick), each written by the pass that knows its
///        fact, so a consumer reads a block's age against a tick of its own
///        rather than a flag someone must reset.
///
/// Indexed by block slot, `BlockIndex::ptr / voxels_per_block`. A slot's
/// record is zeroed when its block is freed, and 0 is no tick. Mirrored by
/// `volume/shaders/grid_types.glsl`, with @ref BlockIndex and
/// @ref tick_after.
struct BlockStamp {
  /// The last tick an allocation asked for the block, whether it inserted the
  /// block or found it there.
  std::uint32_t requested = 0;
  /// The last tick a @ref VoxelBlockGrid::free_stale_blocks pass found any of
  /// the block's voxels holding weight; 0 until one does.
  std::uint32_t weighted = 0;
  /// The last tick a pass that writes voxels changed any of the block's:
  /// `tsdf::TsdfIntegrator` and the codec's decoder, its deblock included,
  /// where a value changed, `voxelize::MeshIntegrator` on every block it
  /// writes.
  /// 0 until one does.
  std::uint32_t changed = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(BlockStamp) == 12, "BlockStamp must be 12 bytes");
static_assert(offsetof(BlockStamp, weighted) == 4, "BlockStamp layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(BlockStamp, changed) == 8, "BlockStamp layout drift");

/// @brief Whether tick @p a is later than tick @p b, modulo 2^32: right while
///        the two are under 2^31 ticks apart, across the clock's wrap too.
constexpr bool tick_after(std::uint32_t a, std::uint32_t b) noexcept {
  return static_cast<std::int32_t>(a - b) > 0;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/triangle_candidates.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file volume/triangle_candidates.hpp
/// @brief The work decomposition every triangle-driven kernel dispatches over:
///        one work item per (triangle, candidate block) pair.

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/math/vector_types.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// @brief Count each triangle's candidate blocks, as an exclusive prefix sum.
///
/// A triangle's candidates are the blocks of its world bounding box grown by
/// `trunc_dist`. A kernel handed these offsets runs one work item per
/// candidate, finds its triangle by binary search, and decodes the block with
/// `volume/shaders/triangle_candidates.glsl`, which recomputes the box from the
/// vertices bit-for-bit. That shader also holds the band test that prunes a
/// candidate to the blocks the band actually reaches.
/// @ref VoxelHashMap::allocate_from_triangles allocates over this
/// decomposition and `voxelize::MeshIntegrator` bins triangles over it. Sharing
/// one definition is what guarantees the integrator finds every block the
/// allocation made.
///
/// Work per item stays bounded however large a triangle is, which is why the
/// unit is the block and not the triangle (the 2026-08-31 decision).
///
/// A triangle with a non-finite vertex, or of zero area, is **skipped**: it
/// gets a zero count, and so `offsets[t] == offsets[t + 1]`. Every other
/// triangle has at least one candidate, so a non-empty range is exactly
/// "this triangle is used". A zero-area triangle is the one input that makes
/// the closest-point solve divide by zero, and a mesh file routinely carries a
/// few, so it is dropped rather than refused.
///
/// This is also the only place an index is bounds-checked. The kernels index
/// the vertex buffer with it directly, and `robustBufferAccess` is enabled
/// nowhere in this repo.
/// @param grid            The block lattice and `trunc_dist` to draw
///                        candidates on.
/// @param vertices        World-space vertex positions, metres.
/// @param vertex_count    How many @p vertices.
/// @param indices         `3 * triangle_count` indices into @p vertices.
/// @param triangle_count  How many triangles.
/// @param who             Names the caller, for the error message (null names
///                        this function instead).
/// @return `triangle_count + 1` offsets, the last being the total work-item
///         count (0 when every triangle was skipped); or
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a null @p vertices or
///         @p indices with triangles to read, an index at or past
///         @p vertex_count, or a total past 2^32 (a mesh grossly mis-scaled
///         against the grid -- millimetres read as metres, say).
VGRID_VOLUME_API core::Result<std::vector<std::uint32_t>>
triangle_candidate_offsets(const VoxelGridParams& grid, const Vec3f* vertices,
                           std::uint32_t vertex_count,
                           const std::uint32_t* indices,
                           std::uint32_t triangle_count, const char* who);

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### include/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp
/// @brief Sparse voxel block grid: a @ref VoxelHashMap block index plus a set
/// of
///        independently-allocated, named per-voxel attribute arrays (SoA).

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/gpu_timer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_grid.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_hash_map.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// @brief Declares one per-voxel attribute array to allocate: a name and the
///        byte size of its per-voxel element.
///
/// The element size folds dtype and channel count into a single stride (a
/// 32-bit float SDF is 4, an 8-bit RGB colour is 3), so attributes of
/// different shapes are each allocated as their own device buffer
/// (structure-of-arrays), not interleaved.
struct AttributeSpec {
  std::string_view name;       ///< Attribute name, e.g. "tsdf", "weight".
  std::uint32_t element_size;  ///< Bytes per voxel (e.g. 4 for a float).
};

/// @brief Non-owning view of one attribute's backing store.
///
/// @ref buffer is the device-local buffer to bind to a compute kernel (the
/// host reaches it through a `CommandBatch`); it holds
/// @ref element_count voxels of @ref element_size bytes each. Re-fetch the view
/// (do not cache @ref buffer or its handle) across a move **or a
/// @ref VoxelBlockGrid::resize** of the owning grid -- resize replaces every
/// attribute buffer, so a held view or handle dangles.
struct AttributeView {
  const core::Buffer* buffer = nullptr;  ///< The attribute's device buffer.
  std::uint32_t element_size = 0;        ///< Bytes per voxel.
  std::uint64_t element_count = 0;  ///< Voxels (num_blocks * voxels_per_block).
};

/// @brief The `weight` at or above which a voxel counts as observed.
///
/// Small and positive, so a never-integrated voxel (weight 0) is excluded while
/// any genuine integration counts. Defined here, the one tier both readers
/// link, because the two must agree: the mesher skips any cell with a corner
/// below it, and the codec's observed mask marks exactly the voxels at or above
/// it -- a mask that disagreed would decode holes, or voxels the mesher would
/// have skipped.
inline constexpr float kObservedWeight = 1e-6f;

/// @name The attributes the grid's tiers share
/// Fusion writes them, the mesher and the codec read them, and each looks one
/// up by its name (@ref VoxelBlockGrid::attribute).
/// @{
/// The truncated signed distance, a `float` (4 bytes) a voxel, in metres.
inline constexpr std::string_view kTsdfAttribute = "tsdf";
/// The fusion weight, a `float` (4 bytes) a voxel; observed from
/// @ref kObservedWeight up.
inline constexpr std::string_view kWeightAttribute = "weight";
/// The colour, a `uint32_t` (4 bytes) a voxel, in the format
/// `volume/voxel_color.hpp` gives.
inline constexpr std::string_view kColorAttribute = "color";
/// @}
