namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

// --- The models. -------------------------------------------------------------
//
// shaders/frame_models.glsl, the kernels' own GLSL, compiled here as C++ once
// these two names are defined: in a namespace of their own, so a model
// function this file does not call is not an unused one.
namespace glsl {

using uint = std::uint32_t;
using glm::uvec2;

#include "shaders/frame_models.glsl"

}  // namespace glsl

namespace {

using namespace glsl;

static_assert(kMaskWords == kMaskWordsPerBlock &&
                  kLinesPerPlane == std::uint32_t(kBlockSize) &&
                  kPlanes == std::uint32_t(kBlockSize),
              "the frame's block is the codec's");
static_assert(std::uint32_t(FrameType::kIntra) == kFrameIntra &&
                  std::uint32_t(FrameType::kInter) == kFrameInter,
              "the frame types are the models'");
static_assert(std::uint32_t(BlockMode::kKeep) == kModeKeep &&
                  std::uint32_t(BlockMode::kSkip) == kModeSkip &&
                  std::uint32_t(BlockMode::kZero) == kModeZero &&
                  std::uint32_t(BlockMode::kRemove) == kModeRemove &&
                  std::uint32_t(BlockMode::kMotion) == kModeMotion &&
                  kModeSymbols == kModeMotion + 1,
              "BlockMode is the mode model's alphabet");

}  // namespace

std::uint32_t frame_model_count(FrameType type, std::uint32_t k) {
  return model_count(static_cast<uint>(type), k);
}

std::uint32_t frame_model_base(std::uint32_t model, std::uint32_t k) {
  return model_base(model, k);
}

namespace {

// --- Byte-level serialization.
// ------------------------------------------------

class ByteWriter {
 public:
  explicit ByteWriter(std::vector<std::uint8_t>& out) : out_(out) {}
  void u8(std::uint32_t v) { out_.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)); }
  void u16(std::uint32_t v) {
    u8(v & 0xFFu);
    u8((v >> 8) & 0xFFu);
  }
  void u32(std::uint32_t v) {
    u16(v & 0xFFFFu);
    u16(v >> 16);
  }
  void f32(float f) {
    std::uint32_t bits = 0;
    std::memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof(bits));
    u32(bits);
  }
  void varint(std::uint32_t v) {  // LEB128
    while (v >= 0x80u) {
      u8((v & 0x7Fu) | 0x80u);
      v >>= 7;
    }
    u8(v);
  }
  void bytes(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& b) {
    out_.insert(out_.end(), b.begin(), b.end());
  }

 private:
  std::vector<std::uint8_t>& out_;
};

// Bounds-checked and sticky: a read past the end sets failed and returns 0,
// so a parser checks once per structure rather than per field.
class ByteReader {
 public:
  ByteReader(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size)
      : data_(data), size_(size) {}
  std::uint32_t u8() {
    if (pos_ >= size_) {
      failed_ = true;
      return 0;
    }
    return data_[pos_++];
  }
  std::uint32_t u16() {
    const std::uint32_t lo = u8();
    return lo | (u8() << 8);
  }
  std::uint32_t u32() {
    const std::uint32_t lo = u16();
    return lo | (u16() << 16);
  }
  float f32() {
    const std::uint32_t bits = u32();
    float f = 0.0f;
    std::memcpy(&f, &bits, sizeof(f));
    return f;
  }
  // Canonical LEB128 only, the one encoding ByteWriter::varint makes: a
  // final byte of 0 after the first adds nothing, so {0x80, 0x00} is refused
  // rather than read as a second spelling of 0.
  std::uint32_t varint() {
    std::uint32_t v = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t shift = 0; shift < 35; shift += 7) {
      const std::uint32_t b = u8();
      if (shift == 28 && (b & 0xF0u) != 0) {
        failed_ = true;  // more than 32 bits, or a sixth byte
        return 0;
      }
      v |= (b & 0x7Fu) << shift;
      if ((b & 0x80u) == 0) {
        if (b == 0 && shift != 0) {
          failed_ = true;  // overlong
          return 0;
        }
        return v;
      }
    }
    failed_ = true;
    return 0;
  }
  bool failed() const noexcept { return failed_; }
  bool at_end() const noexcept { return pos_ == size_; }

 private:
  const std::uint8_t* data_;
  std::size_t size_;
  std::size_t pos_ = 0;
  bool failed_ = false;
};

core::Status bad(const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument("codec frame: " + why);
}

core::Status bad_write(const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument("frame writer: " + why);
}

bool positive_finite(float f) { return std::isfinite(f) && f > 0.0f; }

bool same_bits(float a, float b) { return std::memcmp(&a, &b, sizeof(a)) == 0; }

}  // namespace

const char* coding_difference(const FrameHeader& reference, float voxel_size,
                              float trunc_dist, const CodecParams& params) {
  const CodecParams& held = reference.params;
  if (!same_bits(voxel_size, reference.voxel_size)) return "voxel_size";
  if (!same_bits(trunc_dist, reference.trunc_dist)) return "trunc_dist";
  if (params.coefficient_count != held.coefficient_count) {
    return "coefficient count";
  }
  if (!same_bits(params.quantization_scale, held.quantization_scale)) {
    return "quantization scale";
  }
  static const auto zigzag = zigzag_order();
  for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < params.coefficient_count; ++j) {
    if (!same_bits(params.quantization_weights[zigzag[j]],
                   held.quantization_weights[zigzag[j]])) {
      return "kept quantization weights";
    }
  }
  return nullptr;
}

namespace {

// Tables: per model, a varint count of used symbols, then per used symbol the
// gap from the previous one (the first counts from -1) and its frequency.
void write_tables(ByteWriter& w, const std::vector<FrequencyTable>& tables) {
  for (const FrequencyTable& t : tables) {
    std::uint32_t used = 0;
    for (std::uint16_t f : t.freq) {
      used += f != 0 ? 1u : 0u;
    }
    w.varint(used);
    std::uint32_t next = 0;  // the first symbol the gap counts from
    for (std::uint32_t s = 0; s < t.freq.size(); ++s) {
      if (t.freq[s] != 0) {
        w.varint(s - next);
        w.varint(t.freq[s]);
        next = s + 1;
      }
    }
  }
}

core::Status read_tables(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size,
                         FrameType type, std::uint32_t k,
                         std::vector<FrequencyTable>& tables) {
  ByteReader r(data, size);
  const std::uint32_t models = frame_model_count(type, k);
  tables.assign(models, FrequencyTable{});
  for (std::uint32_t m = 0; m < models; ++m) {
    const std::uint32_t n = model_alphabet(m, k);
    FrequencyTable& t = tables[m];
    t.freq.assign(n, 0);
    const std::uint32_t used = r.varint();
    if (r.failed() || used > n) {
      return bad("table " + std::to_string(m) + " is malformed");
    }
    std::uint64_t next = 0;
    std::uint32_t sum = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
      const std::uint64_t s = next + r.varint();
      const std::uint32_t f = r.varint();
      if (r.failed() || s >= n || f == 0 || f > kRansScale) {
        return bad("table " + std::to_string(m) + " is malformed");
      }
      t.freq[s] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(f);
      sum += f;
      next = s + 1;
    }
    if (used != 0 && sum != kRansScale) {
      return bad("table " + std::to_string(m) + " does not sum to 4096");
    }
    t.finalize();
  }
  // Right after the mode table, the last: a later motion design may append
  // models there only when motion has a frequency (frame_models.glsl).
  if (type == FrameType::kInter &&
      tables[mode_model(k)].freq[kModeMotion] != 0) {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "codec frame: a P-frame that uses the motion mode, which this reader "
        "does not decode");
  }
  if (!r.at_end()) {
    return bad("the TABLES section has trailing bytes");
  }
  return {};
}

// Where a known section's body sits in the frame.
struct SectionBody {
  const std::uint8_t* data = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t size = 0;
};

const SectionBody& section(const std::array<SectionBody, kSectionCount>& found,
                           SectionId id) {
  return found[static_cast<std::size_t>(id) - 1];
}

}  // namespace

core::Status check_frame_type(FrameType type, const char* who) {
  if (static_cast<uint>(type) <= static_cast<uint>(FrameType::kInter)) {
    return {};
  }
  return core::Status::unsupported(std::string(who) + ": frame type " +
                                   std::to_string(static_cast<uint>(type)) +
                                   " (only intra and P-frames are coded)");
}

core::Status check_segment_size(const char* who, const char* name,
                                std::uint32_t size) {
  if (size >= 1 && size <= kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize) return {};
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(
      std::string(who) + ": " + name + " " + std::to_string(size) +
      " is not in [1, " + std::to_string(kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize) + "]");
}

core::Status check_coding(float voxel_size, float trunc_dist,
                          const CodecParams& params) {
  if (!positive_finite(voxel_size)) {
    return bad_write("voxel_size must be finite and positive");
  }
  if (!positive_finite(trunc_dist)) {
    return bad_write("trunc_dist must be finite and positive");
  }
  return params.validate();
}

core::Status check_entries(std::uint32_t largest_mode, bool motion,
                           bool out_of_range) {
  if (largest_mode != 0) {
    return bad_write("mode " + std::to_string(largest_mode) + " is not a mode");
  }
  if (motion) {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "frame writer: the motion mode, which this writer does not code");
  }
  if (out_of_range) {
    return bad_write("a coefficient or residual is outside +-" +
                     std::to_string(kMaxQuantizedMagnitude));
  }
  return {};
}

std::vector<FrequencyTable> frame_tables(
    const std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>>& counts) {
  std::vector<FrequencyTable> tables;
  tables.reserve(counts.size());
  for (const std::vector<std::uint64_t>& c : counts) {
    tables.push_back(normalize_counts(c));
  }
  return tables;
}

core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> assemble_frame(
    FrameType type, const CodedFrame& frame) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(std::vector<std::uint8_t> out,
             assemble_head(type, frame, frame.payload.size()));
  out.insert(out.end(), frame.payload.begin(), frame.payload.end());
  return out;
}

core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> assemble_head(
    FrameType type, const CodedFrame& frame, std::uint64_t payload_size) {
  VKC_TRY(check_frame_type(type, "assemble_frame"));
  const bool inter = type == FrameType::kInter;
  // The header's fields, which the caller coded the segments for.
  VKC_TRY(check_coding(frame.voxel_size, frame.trunc_dist, frame.params));
  VKC_TRY(
      check_segment_size("frame writer", "segment_size", frame.segment_size));
  const std::uint64_t m = frame.reference.header.block_count;
  if (!inter) {
    const char* set = frame.reference.hash != 0 ? "reference hash"
                      : m != 0                  ? "reference block count"
                      : frame.update_size != 0  ? "update_size"
                      : frame.new_count != 0    ? "new_count"
                                                : nullptr;
    if (set != nullptr) {
      return bad_write(
          std::string("an intra frame has no reference, but its ") + set +
          " is not 0");
    }
  }
  if (inter) {
    VKC_TRY(
        check_segment_size("frame writer", "update_size", frame.update_size));
  }
  // An intra frame's blocks are all new, against no reference.
  const std::uint64_t a = inter ? frame.new_count : frame.block_count;
  if (m + a > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
    return bad_write("more than 2^32 - 1 entries");
  }
  if (frame.block_count < a || frame.block_count > m + a) {
    return bad_write(
        "the block count is not the survivors plus the new "
        "blocks");
  }
  if (inter) {
    if (const char* d =
            coding_difference(frame.reference.header, frame.voxel_size,
                              frame.trunc_dist, frame.params)) {
      return bad_write(std::string("the P-frame's ") + d +
                       " is not its reference's");
    }
  }
  const std::uint32_t k = frame.params.coefficient_count;
  const std::uint64_t segments = frame_segment_count(m, frame.update_size) +
                                 frame_segment_count(a, frame.segment_size);
  if (segments > kMaxFrameSegments) {
    return bad_write(
        "more than 2^30 - 1 segments: SEGMENTS would outgrow its "
        "u32 length");
  }
  if (frame.tables.size() != frame_model_count(type, k) ||
      frame.segment_lengths.size() != segments) {
    return bad_write("tables or segment lengths disagree with the header");
  }
  // Every segment's length is at most the payload's, so this bounds both.
  if (payload_size > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
    return bad_write("the payload outgrows its u32 length (4 GiB)");
  }
  std::uint64_t total = 0;
  for (std::uint32_t length : frame.segment_lengths) total += length;
  if (total != payload_size) {
    return bad_write("the segment lengths do not sum to the payload");
  }
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> segments_body;
  ByteWriter sw(segments_body);
  for (std::uint32_t length : frame.segment_lengths) {
    sw.u32(length);
  }

  std::vector<std::uint8_t> tables_body;  // under 32 KB
  ByteWriter tw(tables_body);
  write_tables(tw, frame.tables);

  // REFERENCE, a P-frame's, first.
  std::vector<std::pair<SectionId, const std::vector<std::uint8_t>*>> sections;
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> reference_body;
  if (inter) {
    ByteWriter rw(reference_body);
    rw.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frame.reference.hash));
    rw.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frame.reference.hash >> 32));
    rw.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(m));
    rw.u32(frame.update_size);
    rw.u32(frame.new_count);
    sections.emplace_back(SectionId::kReference, &reference_body);
  }
  sections.emplace_back(SectionId::kTables, &tables_body);
  sections.emplace_back(SectionId::kSegments, &segments_body);

  std::vector<std::uint8_t> out;
  ByteWriter w(out);
  for (std::uint8_t c : kFrameMagic) {
    w.u8(c);
  }
  w.u16(kFrameVersion);
  w.u8(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(type));
  w.u8(0);  // reserved
  w.f32(frame.voxel_size);
  w.f32(frame.trunc_dist);
  w.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kBlockSize));
  w.u32(k);
  w.f32(frame.params.quantization_scale);
  w.u32(k);  // one weight per kept basis
  w.u32(frame.block_count);
  w.u32(frame.segment_size);
  w.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(sections.size() + 1));  // and PAYLOAD
  static const auto zigzag = zigzag_order();
  for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < k; ++j) {
    w.f32(frame.params.quantization_weights[zigzag[j]]);
  }
  for (const auto& [id, body] : sections) {
    w.u16(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(id));
    w.u16(kSectionRequired);
    w.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(body->size()));  // each bounded above
  }
  // PAYLOAD last, its body the caller's.
  w.u16(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(SectionId::kPayload));
  w.u16(kSectionRequired);
  w.u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(payload_size));
  for (const auto& [id, body] : sections) {
    w.bytes(*body);
  }
  return out;
}

core::Result<FrameHeader> read_frame_header(const std::uint8_t* data,
                                            std::size_t size) {
  if (data == nullptr || size < 8) {
    return bad("shorter than a frame header");
  }
  if (std::memcmp(data, kFrameMagic, sizeof(kFrameMagic)) != 0) {
    return bad("not a codec frame (bad magic)");
  }
  ByteReader h(data + sizeof(kFrameMagic), size - sizeof(kFrameMagic));
  const std::uint32_t version = h.u16();
  const std::uint32_t type = h.u8();
  const std::uint32_t reserved = h.u8();
  if (version != kFrameVersion) {
    return core::Status::unsupported("codec frame: version " +
                                     std::to_string(version) + " (this reads " +
                                     std::to_string(kFrameVersion) + ")");
  }
  if (size < kFramePrefixBytes) {
    return bad("shorter than a frame header");
  }
  FrameHeader header;
  header.voxel_size = h.f32();
  header.trunc_dist = h.f32();
  const std::uint32_t block_size = h.u32();
  header.params.coefficient_count = h.u32();
  header.params.quantization_scale = h.f32();
  const std::uint32_t weight_count = h.u32();
  header.block_count = h.u32();
  header.segment_size = h.u32();
  header.section_count = h.u32();
  // K bounds the weights to read; validate() below checks the rest.
  const std::uint32_t k = header.params.coefficient_count;
  if (k < 1 || k > kVoxelsPerBlock) {
    return bad("coefficient count must be in [1, " +
               std::to_string(kVoxelsPerBlock) + "]");
  }
  if (weight_count != k) {
    return bad("quantization weight count must equal the coefficient count");
  }
  if (size < frame_header_bytes(k)) {
    return bad(
        "shorter than a frame header (including the quantization weights)");
  }
  static const auto zigzag = zigzag_order();
  for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < k; ++j) {
    header.params.quantization_weights[zigzag[j]] = h.f32();
  }

  header.type = static_cast<FrameType>(type);
  VKC_TRY(check_frame_type(header.type, "codec frame"));
  if (reserved != 0) {
    return bad("the reserved header byte is not zero");
  }
  if (block_size != static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kBlockSize)) {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "codec frame: block size " + std::to_string(block_size) +
        " (the codec's is " + std::to_string(kBlockSize) + ")");
  }
  if (!positive_finite(header.voxel_size) ||
      !positive_finite(header.trunc_dist)) {
    return bad("voxel_size and trunc_dist must be finite and positive");
  }
  if (core::Status s = header.params.validate(); !s.ok()) {
    return bad("invalid codec params: " + s.message());
  }
  VKC_TRY(
      check_segment_size("codec frame", "segment size", header.segment_size));
  return header;
}

core::Result<ParsedFrame> parse_frame(const std::uint8_t* data,
                                      std::size_t size,
                                      std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                                      const FrameReference* reference) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const FrameHeader header, read_frame_header(data, size));
  ParsedFrame frame;
  frame.header = header;
  const bool inter = header.type == FrameType::kInter;
  const std::uint32_t n = header.block_count;
  const std::uint32_t r_size = header.segment_size;
  const std::uint32_t section_count = header.section_count;
  const std::size_t header_bytes =
      frame_header_bytes(header.params.coefficient_count);

  // The section table, then each body's place in the frame. Lengths are summed
  // in 64 bits, and must account for every byte after the table exactly.
  if (section_count > (size - header_bytes) / kSectionEntryBytes) {
    return bad("the section table runs past the end");
  }
  ByteReader st(data + header_bytes, section_count * kSectionEntryBytes);
  const std::uint8_t* body =
      data + header_bytes + section_count * kSectionEntryBytes;
  const std::uint64_t body_bytes =
      size - header_bytes - section_count * kSectionEntryBytes;
  std::uint64_t offset = 0;
  std::array<SectionBody, kSectionCount> found{};  // by id - 1
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < section_count; ++i) {
    const std::uint32_t id = st.u16();
    const std::uint32_t flags = st.u16();
    const std::uint32_t length = st.u32();
    if (offset + length > body_bytes) {
      return bad("a section runs past the end");
    }
    if (id >= 1 && id <= kSectionCount) {
      if ((flags & ~std::uint32_t(kSectionKnownFlags)) != 0) {
        return core::Status::unsupported(
            "codec frame: section " + std::to_string(id) + " sets flags " +
            std::to_string(flags) + ", which v3 does not define");
      }
      SectionBody& f = found[id - 1];
      if (f.data != nullptr) {
        return bad("section " + std::to_string(id) + " appears twice");
      }
      f = SectionBody{body + offset, length};
    } else if ((flags & kSectionRequired) != 0) {
      return core::Status::unsupported(
          "codec frame: unknown required section " + std::to_string(id));
    }
    offset += length;
  }
  if (offset != body_bytes) {
    return bad("bytes after the last section");
  }
  // Every section, but REFERENCE on a P-frame alone.
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < kSectionCount; ++i) {
    const bool present = found[i].data != nullptr;
    if (static_cast<SectionId>(i + 1) == SectionId::kReference) {
      if (present != inter) {
        return bad(inter ? "a P-frame's REFERENCE section is missing"
                         : "an intra frame has a REFERENCE section");
      }
    } else if (!present) {
      return bad("section " + std::to_string(i + 1) + " is missing");
    }
  }
  const SectionBody& tables_section = section(found, SectionId::kTables);
  const SectionBody& segments_section = section(found, SectionId::kSegments);
  const SectionBody& payload_section = section(found, SectionId::kPayload);

  // A P-frame's M reference entries in update segments of U, then its A new
  // blocks; an intra frame's blocks are all new.
  std::uint64_t reference_hash = 0;
  std::uint32_t m = 0;
  std::uint32_t u_size = 0;
  std::uint32_t a = n;
  if (inter) {
    const SectionBody& r = section(found, SectionId::kReference);
    if (r.size != kReferenceBodyBytes) {
      return bad("the REFERENCE section is not " +
                 std::to_string(kReferenceBodyBytes) + " bytes");
    }
    ByteReader rr(r.data, r.size);
    const std::uint64_t low = rr.u32();
    reference_hash = low | std::uint64_t(rr.u32()) << 32;
    m = rr.u32();
    u_size = rr.u32();
    a = rr.u32();
    VKC_TRY(check_segment_size("codec frame", "update size", u_size));
    if (a > n || n > std::uint64_t(m) + a) {
      return bad("it holds " + std::to_string(n) + " blocks, not between its " +
                 std::to_string(a) + " new blocks and those plus the " +
                 std::to_string(m) + " of its reference");
    }
    // Stream positions are u32, on the device too.
    if (std::uint64_t(m) + a > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
      return bad("more than 2^32 - 1 entries");
    }
  }

  const std::uint32_t k = header.params.coefficient_count;
  VKC_TRY(read_tables(tables_section.data, tables_section.size, header.type, k,
                      frame.tables));

  const std::uint64_t segments =
      frame_segment_count(m, u_size) + frame_segment_count(a, r_size);
  if (segments_section.size != segments * 4) {
    return bad("the SEGMENTS section does not list one length per segment");
  }
  ByteReader lens(segments_section.data, segments_section.size);
  std::vector<std::uint32_t>& lengths = frame.segment_lengths;
  lengths.resize(segments);
  std::uint64_t total = 0;
  for (std::uint64_t s = 0; s < segments; ++s) {
    lengths[s] = lens.u32();
    if (lengths[s] < 4 || lengths[s] % 2 != 0) {
      return bad("segment " + std::to_string(s) + " has an impossible length");
    }
    total += lengths[s];
  }
  if (total != payload_section.size) {
    return bad("the segment lengths do not add up to the PAYLOAD section");
  }
  // A P-frame against the caller's reference only now, so a corrupt frame
  // stays InvalidArgument and a motion frame Unsupported whatever is held;
  // M, a count the caller holds, then bounds the reader's M + A entries.
  if (inter) {
    if (reference == nullptr) {
      return core::Status::not_found(
          "codec frame: a P-frame, and no reference frame is held; decode an "
          "I-frame first");
    }
    if (reference_hash != reference->hash ||
        m != reference->header.block_count) {
      return core::Status::not_found(
          "codec frame: a P-frame against a reference of " + std::to_string(m) +
          " blocks that is not the one held (" +
          std::to_string(reference->header.block_count) +
          " blocks); decode an I-frame first");
    }
    if (const char* d = coding_difference(reference->header, header.voxel_size,
                                          header.trunc_dist, header.params)) {
      return bad(std::string("the P-frame's ") + d + " is not its reference's");
    }
    frame.reference = *reference;
    frame.update_size = u_size;
    frame.new_count = a;
  }
  // A block count that is not consistent with the segment table is a corrupt
  // frame, and one that is but exceeds the caller's room is a sound frame too
  // big to hold -- which the caller answers by growing, not by dropping the
  // frame.
  if (n > max_blocks) {
    return core::Status::out_of_memory(
        "codec frame: it holds " + std::to_string(n) +
        " blocks, more than the " + std::to_string(max_blocks) +
        " the caller can hold");
  }
  frame.payload = payload_section.data;
  frame.payload_size = payload_section.size;
  return frame;
}

core::Status check_segment(std::uint64_t s, SegmentFault fault) {
  switch (fault) {
    case SegmentFault::kNone:
      return {};
    case SegmentFault::kCoordOverflow:
      return bad("segment " + std::to_string(s) +
                 " steps a coordinate outside int32");
    case SegmentFault::kOutOfOrder:
      return bad("segment " + std::to_string(s) +
                 " does not start after the one before ends");
    case SegmentFault::kCorrupt:
      break;
  }
  return bad("segment " + std::to_string(s) + " is corrupt");
}

core::Status check_survivors(std::uint64_t survivors, std::uint32_t n,
                             std::uint32_t a) {
  if (survivors + a != n) {
    return bad(std::to_string(survivors) + " reference blocks survive and " +
               std::to_string(a) + " are new, but the frame holds " +
               std::to_string(n));
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status check_new_block(std::uint32_t q, std::uint32_t e) {
  return bad("new block " + std::to_string(q) + " is on reference block " +
             std::to_string(e));
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/bitstream.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file bitstream.hpp
/// @brief The v3 frame: what a frame holds, and its byte layout.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed): the `Encoder` and `Decoder` build
/// and consume it; nothing outside the tier should see the layout. The layout
/// is the 2026-09-27 decision's, all little-endian:
///
/// @code
///   offset  size  field
///        0     4  magic "VRTC"
///        4     2  version (3)
///        6     1  frame type (0 = intra, 1 = P-frame)
///        7     1  reserved, 0
///        8     4  voxel_size          (f32, metres)
///       12     4  trunc_dist          (f32, metres)
///       16     4  block_size          (8)
///       20     4  coefficient_count K
///       24     4  quantization_scale  (f32, fraction of trunc_dist)
///       28     4  quantization weight count (K)
///       32     4  block_count N
///       36     4  segment_size R
///       40     4  section_count S
///       44   4 K  quantization weights (K f32, kept bases, zigzag order)
///   44+4K  8 * S  section table: {u16 id, u16 flags, u32 length} each
///       ...        the section bodies, in table order, back to back
/// @endcode
///
/// Sections: TABLES (the frame's frequency tables), SEGMENTS (each segment's
/// stream length, u32), PAYLOAD (the segment streams). A segment is R
/// consecutive blocks coded as one independent rANS stream (@ref rans.hpp);
/// the last may be shorter. R is from 1 to @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize,
/// the longest segment one GPU invocation decodes, so every valid frame
/// decodes on the device; every writer and reader holds a frame to it
/// (@ref check_segment_size). A decoder refuses an unknown section flagged
/// @ref kSectionRequired and skips an unknown optional one. Every other flag
/// bit is reserved: zero in v3, and a decoder refuses a known section that
/// sets one, since a later version may define a flag that changes how the
/// body reads.
///
/// Inside a segment the blocks follow the block grammar of
/// `shaders/frame_grammar.glsl`, through the models of
/// `shaders/frame_models.glsl`: the one text the kernels, and the tests' CPU
/// oracle, code a frame with. A frame's blocks are strictly increasing in
/// (z, y, x) order (@ref coord_less), which keeps the coordinate deltas
/// small and every decoded list duplicate-free: within a segment the delta
/// code cannot step backwards, and a reader checks each segment's first
/// coordinate, raw bits, against the block segment before's last
/// (@ref SegmentFault::kOutOfOrder).
///
/// Version 3 replaces DC/AC steps with a global scale and a weight for each of
/// the K kept bases, 256 bytes at the default K = 64; weights beyond K never
/// apply and are not carried. Older versions are refused. The fixed header
/// includes the weights, so `read_frame_info` needs no entropy decode and
/// returns every parameter the transform uses.
///
/// Version 2 (2026-10-01) is version 1 with the grammar's mask code and sign;
/// version 1 sent a partial mask as 64 bytes through one table and a sign as
/// a field of its own.
///
/// **P-frames** (type 1) code a frame against its reference, the frame
/// decoded before it, named by @ref frame_hash of the reference's exact
/// bytes (@ref FrameReference). A P-frame adds a REFERENCE section (id 4),
/// required on type 1 and refused on type 0, whose 20-byte body is {u64 hash,
/// u32 M, the reference's block count, u32 U, reference entries per update
/// segment (from 1 to the same limit as R), u32 A, new blocks}. N stays the
/// decoded frame's block count: the reference blocks that survive plus the A
/// new ones, so A <= N <= M + A, and M + A < 2^32, since stream positions are
/// u32. R counts new blocks per segment.
///
/// `frame_segment_count(M, U)` update segments come first, then
/// `frame_segment_count(A, R)` new-block segments, their lengths in SEGMENTS
/// and their streams in PAYLOAD in that order. Reference entry e sits at
/// stream position e and new block q at M + q (`segment_range` in
/// `frame_models.glsl`); an intra frame is the case M = 0. An update segment
/// holds its entries in reference order, each a mode symbol, then a payload by
/// mode:
///
/// @code
///   mode    survives  payload
///   keep    yes       the mask XOR the reference's, then K residuals,
///                     int16((q - q_ref) mod 2^16)
///   skip    yes       none: the reference block as it is
///   zero    yes       the mask and K coefficients, as an intra block's
///   remove  no        none
///   motion  reserved  none defined: a frame that uses it is Unsupported
/// @endcode
///
/// A new-block segment is an intra segment. The new coordinates strictly
/// increase across all A, and none is a reference coordinate (a reference
/// block is recoded with zero, never removed and added), so the decoder
/// merges survivors and new blocks into the frame's order with no ties. Keep,
/// zero and new blocks code through the intra models, and the modes through
/// the mode model (`frame_models.glsl`). A P-frame's `voxel_size`,
/// `trunc_dist`, K, scale and kept weights equal its reference's bit for bit.
///
/// A reader refuses a P-frame in this order: the header; the section table
/// (an unknown required section or an undefined flag `Unsupported`, a
/// duplicate, an overrun, trailing bytes or REFERENCE's presence
/// `InvalidArgument`); REFERENCE's body, then TABLES (`InvalidArgument`), a
/// nonzero motion frequency (`Unsupported`, before anything after the mode
/// table is read), then SEGMENTS (`InvalidArgument`); then against the held
/// reference: none held, or another hash or M, `NotFound` (the frame is sound
/// and decodes once its reference is held), other coding parameters
/// `InvalidArgument`; N past the caller's room `OutOfMemory`; then each
/// segment (@ref check_segment), the survivor count (@ref check_survivors)
/// and the new coordinates against the reference's (@ref check_new_block),
/// each `InvalidArgument`.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <vector>

#include "rans.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/math/vector_types.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// The four bytes every frame starts with.
inline constexpr std::uint8_t kFrameMagic[4] = {'V', 'R', 'T', 'C'};
/// The layout this file writes and reads.
inline constexpr std::uint16_t kFrameVersion = 3;
/// Bytes before the quantization weights (the metadata prefix).
inline constexpr std::size_t kFramePrefixBytes = 44;
/// Bytes before the section table of a frame keeping @p k coefficients:
/// the prefix and one weight per kept basis.
constexpr std::size_t frame_header_bytes(std::uint32_t k) {
  return kFramePrefixBytes + std::size_t{k} * sizeof(float);
}
/// Bytes per section-table entry.
inline constexpr std::size_t kSectionEntryBytes = 8;
/// Section flag: a decoder that does not know the section must refuse the
/// frame rather than skip it.
inline constexpr std::uint16_t kSectionRequired = 1;
/// Every section flag v3 defines. A known section with any other bit set is
/// refused as `Status::Code::Unsupported`.
inline constexpr std::uint16_t kSectionKnownFlags = kSectionRequired;
/// Blocks per segment by default: @ref EncoderConfig::segment_size's, whose
/// doc gives its cost.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kDefaultSegmentSize = 64;
/// The most segments a frame holds: SEGMENTS' u32 length bounds it.
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kMaxFrameSegments =
    std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max() / 4;
/// Bytes in a REFERENCE section's body.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kReferenceBodyBytes = 20;

/// @return How many segments a frame of @p blocks blocks has at
///         @p segment_size (at least 1) blocks a segment.
constexpr std::uint64_t frame_segment_count(std::uint64_t blocks,
                                            std::uint32_t segment_size) {
  return blocks == 0 ? 0 : (blocks - 1) / segment_size + 1;
}

/// What a frame is (codec_params.hpp): byte 6 of its header.
using codec::FrameType;

/// @brief The type check every writer and reader makes.
/// @param who  The caller, which a refusal names.
/// @return OK for an intra frame or a P-frame; otherwise
///         `Status::Code::Unsupported`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_frame_type(FrameType type, const char* who);

/// @brief The segment-size rule every writer and reader holds a frame to: R,
///        and a P-frame's U, from 1 to @ref kMaxDeviceDecodeSegmentSize.
/// @param who   The caller, which a refusal names.
/// @param name  The size's name, which a refusal names too.
/// @return OK, or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_segment_size(const char* who,
                                                const char* name,
                                                std::uint32_t size);

/// The sections v3 defines, numbered `1..kSectionCount`.
enum class SectionId : std::uint16_t {
  kTables = 1,     ///< The frequency tables, one per model.
  kSegments = 2,   ///< Each segment's stream length in bytes, u32.
  kPayload = 3,    ///< The segment streams, back to back.
  kReference = 4,  ///< A P-frame's reference and its stream counts.
};
/// How many sections v3 defines.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kSectionCount = 4;
static_assert(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(SectionId::kReference) ==
                  kSectionCount,
              "section ids run 1..kSectionCount");

/// A P-frame's mode for one entry of its reference: one symbol of the mode
/// model, `frame_models.glsl`'s `kMode*`.
enum class BlockMode : std::uint8_t {
  kKeep = 0,    ///< Survives: an XOR mask and K residuals.
  kSkip = 1,    ///< Survives as it is: no payload.
  kZero = 2,    ///< Survives, recoded: a mask and K coefficients.
  kRemove = 3,  ///< Gone: no payload.
  kMotion = 4,  ///< Reserved for motion compensation; refused everywhere.
};

/// The frame's order: @ref volume::coord_less, by z, then y, then x -- so a
/// run of blocks along x is a run of consecutive entries. The kernels sort
/// and search by its mirror, `volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl`.
using volume::coord_less;

/// @brief A frame's header, parsed and checked without decoding anything.
struct FrameHeader {
  /// What the frame is: a type this reader decodes.
  FrameType type = FrameType::kIntra;
  float voxel_size = 0.0f;  ///< Metres per voxel edge.
  float trunc_dist = 0.0f;  ///< Metres; the steps are fractions of it.
  CodecParams params;       ///< K, global scale, and the kept bases' weights.
  std::uint32_t block_count = 0;    ///< Blocks the frame holds.
  std::uint32_t segment_size = 0;   ///< Blocks per segment, R.
  std::uint32_t section_count = 0;  ///< Entries in the section table.
};

/// @brief The frame a P-frame codes against: what a writer and a reader hold
///        of it.
struct FrameReference {
  /// @ref frame_hash of the reference frame's exact bytes.
  std::uint64_t hash = 0;
  /// Its header: M is `header.block_count`, and the coding parameters a
  /// P-frame must repeat.
  FrameHeader header;
};

/// @brief Parse and check a frame's fixed header -- the first
///        @ref frame_header_bytes -- and nothing after it.
/// @return The header, or the same header refusals as @ref parse_frame.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<FrameHeader> read_frame_header(
    const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);

/// @brief The refusals every writer makes after the type's, of the coding
///        parameters, which @ref assemble_frame and the device writer make
///        first: one place for their codes and words.
/// @return OK, or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a non-positive or
///         non-finite @p voxel_size or @p trunc_dist, or invalid @p params.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_coding(float voxel_size, float trunc_dist,
                                          const CodecParams& params);

/// @brief The rule a P-frame's coding parameters keep: its reference's, bit
///        for bit. The one check the reader, the writers and the encoder's
///        choice of frame type make.
/// @return The first of @p voxel_size, @p trunc_dist and @p params' K,
///         scale and kept weights that is not @p reference's, by name; null
///         when none is.
VGRID_CODEC_API const char* coding_difference(const FrameHeader& reference,
                                              float voxel_size,
                                              float trunc_dist,
                                              const CodecParams& params);

/// @brief The last refusals a writer makes, of what its entries hold, which
///        the device writer's count pass finds: one place for their codes
///        and words.
/// @param largest_mode  The largest mode past @ref BlockMode::kMotion; 0 for
///                      none.
/// @param motion        Whether a mode is @ref BlockMode::kMotion.
/// @param out_of_range  Whether a written coefficient or residual (a keep,
///                      zero or new entry's) is outside ±32767.
/// @return OK, or in this order: `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a mode
///         past the alphabet, `Status::Code::Unsupported` for motion, and
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a value out of range.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_entries(std::uint32_t largest_mode,
                                           bool motion, bool out_of_range);

/// @return How many frequency tables a frame of @p type keeping @p k
///         coefficients carries, in TABLES order.
VGRID_CODEC_API std::uint32_t frame_model_count(FrameType type,
                                                std::uint32_t k);
/// @return The first entry of table @p model at @p k in the kernels'
///         per-symbol arrays, every table's symbols back to back in TABLES
///         order; for @ref frame_model_count, the arrays' size.
VGRID_CODEC_API std::uint32_t frame_model_base(std::uint32_t model,
                                               std::uint32_t k);

/// @brief Normalize a frame's per-model symbol counts into its tables, the
///        one way every writer builds them.
VGRID_CODEC_API std::vector<FrequencyTable> frame_tables(
    const std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>>& counts);

/// @brief A frame whose segments are already coded, which
///        @ref assemble_frame lays out.
struct CodedFrame {
  float voxel_size = 0.0f;
  float trunc_dist = 0.0f;
  CodecParams params;
  std::uint32_t block_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t segment_size = 0;
  /// A P-frame's reference, and its update size and new block count; for an
  /// intra frame, hash, block counts and sizes 0.
  FrameReference reference;
  std::uint32_t update_size = 0;
  std::uint32_t new_count = 0;
  /// @ref frame_model_count tables, in TABLES order.
  std::vector<FrequencyTable> tables;
  /// Each segment's stream length in bytes.
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> segment_lengths;
  /// The segment streams, back to back.
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> payload;
};

/// @brief Lay out a coded frame: header, section table, then REFERENCE for a
///        P-frame, TABLES, SEGMENTS and PAYLOAD. Every writer's container,
///        the device writer's and the tests' CPU oracle's, so theirs cannot
///        differ.
/// @param type  Written to byte 6 as given: the caller coded the segments
///              for it.
/// @return The frame's bytes; `Status::Code::Unsupported` for a type past
///         @ref FrameType::kInter; or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a
///         non-positive or non-finite `voxel_size` / `trunc_dist`, invalid
///         params, a segment size or a P-frame's update size that
///         @ref check_segment_size refuses, M + A past 2^32 - 1, a block
///         count outside [A, M + A], coding
///         parameters other than the reference's, reference fields set on an
///         intra frame, tables or segment lengths whose count the header
///         disagrees with, lengths that do not sum to the payload, a payload
///         past 4 GiB or more than 2^30 - 1 segments.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> assemble_frame(
    FrameType type, const CodedFrame& frame);

/// @brief @ref assemble_frame's bytes but PAYLOAD's body, which comes last:
///        the head, for a payload of @p payload_size bytes the caller holds
///        elsewhere (the encoder's payload slot). @p frame's `payload` is not
///        read. The head then the payload are @ref assemble_frame's bytes.
/// @return The head; or @ref assemble_frame's refusals, the segment lengths
///         summed against @p payload_size.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> assemble_head(
    FrameType type, const CodedFrame& frame, std::uint64_t payload_size);

/// @brief A frame parsed and checked up to its segment streams: what the
///        device reader, and the tests' CPU oracle, decode them from.
struct ParsedFrame {
  FrameHeader header;
  /// A P-frame's reference, as the caller held it (M is
  /// `reference.header.block_count`); none for an intra frame, whose M is
  /// 0.
  FrameReference reference;
  /// A P-frame's reference entries per update segment, and its new blocks;
  /// 0 for an intra frame, as in @ref CodedFrame.
  std::uint32_t update_size = 0;
  std::uint32_t new_count = 0;
  /// @ref frame_model_count tables, in TABLES order.
  std::vector<FrequencyTable> tables;
  /// Each segment's stream length in bytes: even, at least 4, summing to
  /// `payload_size`.
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> segment_lengths;
  /// The segment streams, back to back, inside the caller's frame.
  const std::uint8_t* payload = nullptr;
  std::size_t payload_size = 0;
};

/// @brief Everything a reader checks before it decodes a segment: the
///        header, the sections, the tables, the segment lengths, a P-frame
///        against @p reference, and the block count against @p max_blocks.
///
/// Reads nothing outside `[data, data + size)`, whatever the bytes say.
/// @param data        The frame.
/// @param size        Its length; must be exact (trailing bytes are refused).
/// @param max_blocks  The most blocks the caller can hold. A frame's size does
///                    not bound its block count -- a block whose every symbol
///                    has probability one costs no bits -- so this is what
///                    bounds the work and the allocation. Checked once the
///                    block count agrees with the segment table, so a corrupt
///                    count is refused as corrupt and only a sound frame is
///                    refused for its size. A P-frame's M reference entries
///                    are bounded by the reference the caller holds.
/// @param reference   The reference the caller holds, for a P-frame; null
///                    for none.
/// @return The parsed frame, or: `Status::Code::Unsupported` for another
///         version, frame type, block size, an unknown required section, a
///         known section with a flag v3 does not define, or a P-frame that
///         uses the motion mode; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for anything
///         malformed, truncated or inconsistent (a P-frame whose coding
///         parameters are not its reference's included);
///         `Status::Code::NotFound` for a P-frame whose reference is not
///         @p reference (none held, or another hash or block count);
///         `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` for a well-formed frame of more than
///         @p max_blocks blocks. The order the refusals are made in is this
///         file's; a segment's own are @ref check_segment's.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Result<ParsedFrame> parse_frame(
    const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    const FrameReference* reference);

/// How a segment failed, in the order a reader judges it: its own stream's
/// faults, which the decode finds, then its order against the segment
/// before, which a reader finds after.
enum class SegmentFault : std::uint32_t {
  kNone = 0,
  /// A delta stepped a coordinate outside int32, before anything else
  /// failed.
  kCoordOverflow = 1,
  /// The stream did not decode cleanly and completely: a read past its end,
  /// a symbol from an empty table, or words left or a state other than `L`
  /// at its end (rans.hpp).
  kCorrupt = 2,
  /// A block segment's first coordinate, raw bits, which no end check sees,
  /// does not follow the block segment before's last. Without this a flipped
  /// bit decodes a duplicate, and the inverse races two workgroups on one
  /// block.
  kOutOfOrder = 3,
};

/// @brief The refusal of a frame at segment @p s, the first that failed:
///        one place for both readers' codes and words.
/// @return OK for @ref SegmentFault::kNone; otherwise
///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_segment(std::uint64_t s, SegmentFault fault);

/// @brief A P-frame's survivor count, which only a whole decode knows: one
///        place for both readers' refusal.
/// @return OK when @p survivors, its reference entries that keep, skip or
///         zero, are @p n - @p a; otherwise `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_survivors(std::uint64_t survivors,
                                             std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t a);

/// @brief The refusal of a P-frame whose new block @p q is on reference
///        entry @p e -- one spelling per block: a reference block is recoded
///        with zero, never removed and added -- whatever that entry's mode.
///        The decoder's merge finds the first such pair.
/// @return `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`.
VGRID_CODEC_API core::Status check_new_block(std::uint32_t q, std::uint32_t e);

/// @ref ApplySource's value for a field the block does not take.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kNoSource = ~0u;

/// @brief Where one block of a decoded frame comes from: two u32, as the
///        decoder's merge kernel writes it and the apply kernel reads it.
struct ApplySource {
  /// Its reference entry, for keep and skip; else @ref kNoSource.
  std::uint32_t reference = kNoSource;
  /// Its stream position, for keep, zero and a new block; else
  /// @ref kNoSource.
  std::uint32_t payload = kNoSource;
};
static_assert(sizeof(ApplySource) == 8 &&
                  offsetof(ApplySource, reference) == 0 &&
                  offsetof(ApplySource, payload) == 4,
              "ApplySource is two u32, as the apply kernel reads it");

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/block_lists.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "block_lists.hpp"

#include <string>

#include "rans_dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_map_internal.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_hash_map.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "block_sort_merge_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "block_sort_tile_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "frame_merge_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "grid_diff_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// Mirrors `Push` in block_lists_push.glsl.
struct ListsPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base = 0;
  std::uint32_t count = 0;
  std::uint32_t count_word = 0;
  std::uint32_t run_length = 0;
  std::uint32_t reference_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t new_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t block_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t pass = 0;
  std::int32_t num_buckets = 0;
  std::int32_t bucket_size = 0;
  std::int32_t max_chain = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(ListsPush) == 44, "ListsPush must be 44 bytes");

// The entries block_sort_tile.comp sorts a workgroup (kSortTile there), and
// the other kernels' width.
constexpr std::uint32_t kSortTile = 256;
constexpr std::uint32_t kLanes = 256;

constexpr VkDeviceSize kEntryBytes = sizeof(volume::BlockIndex);
constexpr VkDeviceSize kWordBytes = sizeof(std::uint32_t);
// The merge's collision pair, and the diff's two counts.
constexpr VkDeviceSize kPairBytes = 2 * kWordBytes;

core::Status fail(const char* op, const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string("BlockLists::") + op +
                                        ": " + why);
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<BlockLists>> BlockLists::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "BlockLists::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<BlockLists> owned(new BlockLists());
  BlockLists& l = *owned;
  l.device_ = &device;
  l.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(ListsPush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(l.sort_tile_kernel_, "codec_block_sort_tile",
                 vgrid_block_sort_tile_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_block_sort_tile_comp_spv_size, 3, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(l.sort_merge_kernel_, "codec_block_sort_merge",
                 vgrid_block_sort_merge_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_block_sort_merge_comp_spv_size, 3, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(l.frame_merge_kernel_, "codec_frame_merge",
                 vgrid_frame_merge_comp_spv, vgrid_frame_merge_comp_spv_size, 7,
                 &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(l.grid_diff_kernel_, "codec_grid_diff",
                 vgrid_grid_diff_comp_spv, vgrid_grid_diff_comp_spv_size, 5,
                 &push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(l.pool_, kb.build());
  VKC_TRY(l.sort_merge_sets_.reserve(device, l.sort_merge_kernel_, 3));
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  l.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  l.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  // The words that come back, and an entry of each list, so a frame of no
  // blocks, or a grid of none, binds a buffer.
  struct First {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const First first[] = {
      {l.collision_, kPairBytes, "codec.merge_collision"},
      {l.diff_counts_, kPairBytes, "codec.diff_counts"},
      {l.gone_, kEntryBytes, "codec.diff_gone"},
      {l.missing_, kEntryBytes, "codec.diff_missing"},
  };
  for (const First& f : first) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(device, allocator, f.buffer, f.bytes,
                                        l.max_storage_buffer_range_, f.name));
  }
  return owned;
}

core::Status BlockLists::record_sort(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                     const core::Buffer& list,
                                     const volume::DeviceCount& count,
                                     const core::Buffer& out,
                                     core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const std::uint32_t bound = count.bound;
  if (bound == 0) return {};
  const VkDeviceSize bytes = VkDeviceSize(bound) * kEntryBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize range = max_storage_buffer_range_;
  VKC_TRY(core::StorageInput(list).check("BlockLists::record_sort: the list",
                                         bytes));
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("BlockLists::record_sort: the list",
                                           bytes, range));
  if (count.buffer == nullptr || !count.buffer->valid() ||
      count.offset % kWordBytes != 0 ||
      count.buffer->size() < count.offset + kWordBytes || out.size() < bytes) {
    return fail("record_sort",
                "the count's word is missing, misaligned or past its buffer, "
                "or the output holds fewer than the bound's entries");
  }
  // The levels the bound needs: each doubles the sorted runs, from the
  // tiles' to the whole list. The count may need fewer, and a level past
  // them copies its entries through; the last level, or the tile pass with
  // none, writes the output.
  std::uint32_t levels = 0;
  for (std::uint64_t run = kSortTile; run < bound; run *= 2) ++levels;
  for (std::uint32_t h = 0; h < std::min<std::uint32_t>(levels, 2); ++h) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, sorted_[h],
                                        bytes, range, "codec.sorted_blocks",
                                        &batch));
  }
  const core::Buffer& tiles = levels == 0 ? out : sorted_[0];
  sort_tile_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(0, list.handle(), 0, bytes);
  sort_tile_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(1, tiles.handle(), 0, bytes);
  sort_tile_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(2, count.buffer->handle(), 0,
                                             VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  // Level l merges sorted_[l % 2] into the other half, through set l % 2,
  // but the last, which merges into the output through set 2.
  const auto bind = [&](std::uint32_t set, const core::Buffer& src,
                        const core::Buffer& dst) {
    sort_merge_sets_[set].write_storage_buffer(0, src.handle(), 0, bytes);
    sort_merge_sets_[set].write_storage_buffer(1, dst.handle(), 0, bytes);
    sort_merge_sets_[set].write_storage_buffer(2, count.buffer->handle(), 0,
                                               VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  };
  if (levels >= 2) bind(0, sorted_[0], sorted_[1]);
  if (levels >= 3) bind(1, sorted_[1], sorted_[0]);
  if (levels >= 1) bind(2, sorted_[(levels - 1) % 2], out);
  // Every pass over the bound's groups: a group past the count returns.
  ListsPush push;
  push.count = bound;
  push.count_word = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(count.offset / kWordBytes);
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, sort_tile_kernel_, push, bound, kSortTile,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  std::uint32_t level = 0;
  for (std::uint64_t run = kSortTile; run < bound; run *= 2, ++level) {
    push.run_length = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(run);
    const core::DescriptorSet& set =
        sort_merge_sets_[level + 1 == levels ? 2u : level % 2];
    VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, sort_merge_kernel_, push, bound, kLanes,
                           max_workgroup_count_x_, stage, &set));
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status BlockLists::reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t slots) {
  struct Scratch {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const Scratch scratch[] = {
      {gone_, VkDeviceSize(slots) * kEntryBytes, "codec.diff_gone"},
      {missing_, VkDeviceSize(n) * kEntryBytes, "codec.diff_missing"},
  };
  // Every range first, so a frame the device cannot hold grows nothing.
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(b.name, b.bytes,
                                             max_storage_buffer_range_));
  }
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, b.buffer,
                                        b.bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                        b.name));
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status BlockLists::record_merge(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                      const ResidentBlocks& decoded,
                                      const core::Buffer& reference,
                                      FrameBuffers frame, std::uint32_t n,
                                      core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const std::uint32_t m = decoded.reference_count;
  const std::uint32_t a = decoded.count - m;
  const VkDeviceSize ref_bytes = binding_range(m * kEntryBytes, kEntryBytes);
  const VkDeviceSize added_bytes = binding_range(a * kEntryBytes, kEntryBytes);
  const VkDeviceSize mode_bytes = binding_range(m * kWordBytes, kWordBytes);
  const VkDeviceSize rank_bytes = (VkDeviceSize(m) + 1) * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize frame_bytes = binding_range(n * kEntryBytes, kEntryBytes);
  const VkDeviceSize source_bytes =
      binding_range(VkDeviceSize(n) * sizeof(ApplySource), sizeof(ApplySource));
  const bool entries = decoded.count != 0;
  if (entries &&
      (decoded.list == nullptr || (m != 0 && decoded.modes == nullptr) ||
       decoded.ranks == nullptr || frame.list == nullptr ||
       frame.sources == nullptr || decoded.list->size() < added_bytes ||
       (m != 0 && decoded.modes->size() < mode_bytes) ||
       decoded.ranks->size() < rank_bytes || reference.size() < ref_bytes ||
       frame.list->size() < frame_bytes ||
       frame.sources->size() < source_bytes)) {
    return fail("record_merge", "the buffers do not hold " + std::to_string(m) +
                                    " reference entries, " + std::to_string(a) +
                                    " new blocks and " + std::to_string(n) +
                                    " frame blocks");
  }
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(collision_, 0, kPairBytes, kNoSource));
  if (entries) {
    const core::DescriptorSet& set = frame_merge_kernel_.set;
    set.write_storage_buffer(0, reference.handle(), 0, ref_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(1, decoded.list->handle(), 0, added_bytes);
    // An intra frame's modes are never read; its ranks stand in.
    set.write_storage_buffer(
        2, m != 0 ? decoded.modes->handle() : decoded.ranks->handle(), 0,
        mode_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(3, decoded.ranks->handle(), 0, rank_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(4, frame.list->handle(), 0, frame_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(5, frame.sources->handle(), 0, source_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(6, collision_.handle(), 0, kPairBytes);
    ListsPush push;
    push.count = decoded.count;
    push.reference_count = m;
    push.new_count = a;
    push.block_count = n;
    VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, frame_merge_kernel_, push, decoded.count,
                           kLanes, max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status BlockLists::record_diff(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                     const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                     const core::Buffer& frame_list,
                                     std::uint32_t n,
                                     core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  if (!grid.valid()) return fail("record_diff", "moved-from grid");
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  const auto slots =
      static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_buckets * gp.bucket_size);
  // Another tier sized the table (and every resize doubles it), so it is
  // bound at its real size and range-checked, and fetched for this call: a
  // resize replaces it.
  const VkDeviceSize entries_bytes =
      volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer_size(grid.map());
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("BlockLists: the hash entries",
                                           entries_bytes,
                                           max_storage_buffer_range_));
  const VkDeviceSize frame_bytes = binding_range(n * kEntryBytes, kEntryBytes);
  const VkDeviceSize gone_bytes =
      binding_range(VkDeviceSize(slots) * kEntryBytes, kEntryBytes);
  if (gone_.size() < gone_bytes || missing_.size() < frame_bytes ||
      frame_list.size() < frame_bytes) {
    return fail("record_diff", std::to_string(n) + " frame blocks and " +
                                   std::to_string(slots) +
                                   " slots, more than were reserved");
  }
  const core::DescriptorSet& set = grid_diff_kernel_.set;
  set.write_storage_buffer(
      0, volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer(grid.map()), 0,
      entries_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(1, frame_list.handle(), 0, frame_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(2, gone_.handle(), 0, gone_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(3, missing_.handle(), 0, frame_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(4, diff_counts_.handle(), 0, kPairBytes);
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(diff_counts_, 0, kPairBytes, 0u));
  ListsPush push;
  push.block_count = n;
  push.num_buckets = gp.num_buckets;
  push.bucket_size = gp.bucket_size;
  push.max_chain = gp.max_chain;
  // The table's slots against the frame, then the frame against the table.
  for (const std::uint32_t pass : {0u, 1u}) {
    push.pass = pass;
    push.count = pass == 0 ? slots : n;
    VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, grid_diff_kernel_, push, push.count, kLanes,
                           max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/block_lists.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file block_lists.hpp
/// @brief The codec's work on block coordinates, on the device: the
///        encoder's blocks sorted into frame order, and the decoder's frame
///        merged from its reference and diffed against the grid.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). The kernels order coordinates by
/// `volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl`, the mirror of @ref coord_less.

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "reference_store.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// @brief Block lists in frame order, made on the device: the encoder's
///        observed blocks sorted by coordinate, and a decoded frame's blocks
///        merged from its reference and new blocks, then diffed against the
///        grid it decodes into.
///
/// The sort is a stable rank-merge sort on @ref coord_less itself, so it
/// takes every int32 coordinate with no key transform. A tile kernel sorts
/// each 256 entries in shared memory; each level after it merges pairs of
/// sorted runs, an entry an invocation, each placed at its index in its run
/// plus a binary search of its sibling run. So a bound of n entries takes
/// `1 + ceil(log2(ceil(n / 256)))` dispatches, and every entry's place depends
/// only on the keys: unique keys, as a hash table's are, give one order
/// whatever order they came in.
///
/// The decoder never sorts. A frame's blocks are a merge of two strictly
/// increasing lists, the reference's survivors and the new blocks, so each
/// block's place is a count -- the survivors below it, from the reader's
/// ranks, plus the new blocks below it, by binary search -- which
/// @ref record_merge writes with each block's sources; a new block on a
/// reference block is row 13's refusal (@ref check_new_block). Then
/// @ref record_diff finds what the grid must lose and gain without sorting
/// it: a grid block whose coordinate a search of the frame misses is gone,
/// and a frame block the hash table does not hold is missing. Both record
/// into the decode's batch and leave their findings on the device
/// (@ref collision, @ref diff_counts), for the decoder's gate and results.
///
/// Every buffer is device-local and retained, grown as a call needs
/// (`ensure_device_scratch`).
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one call at a time.
class VGRID_CODEC_API BlockLists {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the kernels.
  /// @return The lists, or a pipeline or pool failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<BlockLists>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~BlockLists() = default;
  BlockLists(const BlockLists&) = delete;
  BlockLists& operator=(const BlockLists&) = delete;
  BlockLists(BlockLists&&) = delete;
  BlockLists& operator=(BlockLists&&) = delete;

  /// @brief Record a stable sort of the first `n` `volume::BlockIndex`
  ///        entries of @p list, by @ref coord_less, into @p out, `n` the
  ///        word @p count names, so it never reaches the host.
  ///
  /// The tile pass and every level the bound needs are recorded over the
  /// bound's groups, a group past `n` returning, and a level past what `n`
  /// needs copies its entries through: the order is `n` entries' sort,
  /// whatever the bound. The last level, or the tile pass when the bound
  /// needs none, writes @p out, so the sorted list lands where its reader
  /// binds it with no copy. @p list is read, never written. The levels bind
  /// sets this object keeps, so a batch holds at most one of these calls.
  /// @param batch  The batch to record into; submitted by the caller.
  /// @param list   A storage buffer of at least the bound's entries.
  /// @param count  `n`, a word a kernel wrote, at most its bound.
  /// @param out    Where the sorted entries go: at least the bound's.
  /// @param stage  Optional scope the caller's stage row is open under; the
  ///               dispatches record their device spans into it.
  /// @return OK, recording nothing for a bound of 0; or
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a @p list
  ///         `StorageInput::check` refuses, entries past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`, a count word missing, misaligned or past
  ///         its buffer, or an @p out short of the bound; otherwise a buffer
  ///         failure.
  core::Status record_sort(core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::Buffer& list,
                           const volume::DeviceCount& count,
                           const core::Buffer& out,
                           core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Make the diff's lists hold a frame of @p n blocks into a grid of
  ///        @p slots hash slots, before anything is recorded.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a list past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`, which grows nothing; or an
  ///         allocation's failure.
  core::Status reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t slots);

  /// @brief Record the merge of a decoded frame's @p n blocks into
  ///        @p frame, in frame order: each block's coordinate, `ptr` 0, and
  ///        its sources -- keep `{e, e}`, skip `{e, none}`, zero `{none, e}`,
  ///        new block q `{none, M + q}` -- and row 13's first collision.
  ///
  /// Sound once rows 11 and 12 pass (the reader's check, after the submit):
  /// on a frame they refuse the outputs are garbage, but every write stays
  /// below @p n and the searches end.
  /// @param batch      The decode's batch, after the reader's decode.
  /// @param decoded    The reader's entries: its M modes, its ranks and its
  ///                   A new blocks.
  /// @param reference  The held reference's M blocks, strictly increasing.
  /// @param frame      Where the blocks and sources go, @p n of each.
  /// @param n          N, the frame's blocks.
  /// @param stage      As @ref record_sort.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for buffers missing or
  ///         smaller than the counts need; otherwise a buffer failure.
  core::Status record_merge(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                            const ResidentBlocks& decoded,
                            const core::Buffer& reference, FrameBuffers frame,
                            std::uint32_t n,
                            core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Record the diff of @p grid's block set against a frame's first
  ///        @p n blocks of @p frame_list, strictly increasing: what the grid
  ///        holds and the frame lacks into @ref gone, with each block's
  ///        `ptr`, and what the frame holds and the grid lacks into
  ///        @ref missing, `ptr` 0, each in no order.
  ///
  /// Binds the hash table as it is when the batch runs, so nothing may
  /// allocate into or remove from @p grid until then.
  /// @param batch       The decode's batch, after the merge.
  /// @param grid        The grid the frame decodes into.
  /// @param frame_list  The frame's blocks, as the merge wrote them.
  /// @param n           N.
  /// @param stage       As @ref record_sort.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a moved-from grid, a
  ///         hash table past `maxStorageBufferRange`, or more blocks or
  ///         slots than @ref reserve made room for; otherwise a buffer
  ///         failure.
  core::Status record_diff(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                           const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                           const core::Buffer& frame_list, std::uint32_t n,
                           core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @return Row 13's finding once the last merge's batch ran: the first new
  ///         block on a reference entry, and that entry, a u32 each;
  ///         @ref kNoSource for none.
  const core::Buffer& collision() const noexcept { return collision_; }
  /// @return The last diff's counts once its batch ran: the grid blocks
  ///         @ref gone lists, then the frame blocks @ref missing lists, a u32
  ///         each.
  const core::Buffer& diff_counts() const noexcept { return diff_counts_; }
  /// @return The grid blocks the last diff found the frame lacks, the first
  ///         `diff_counts()[0]` of them.
  const core::Buffer& gone() const noexcept { return gone_; }
  /// @return The frame blocks the last diff found the grid lacks, the first
  ///         `diff_counts()[1]` of them.
  const core::Buffer& missing() const noexcept { return missing_; }

 private:
  BlockLists() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel sort_tile_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel sort_merge_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel frame_merge_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel grid_diff_kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;
  // The merge levels' sets: sorted_[0] into sorted_[1], back, and the last
  // level's half into the caller's output.
  core::KernelSets sort_merge_sets_;

  // Device-local, retained: the sort's two halves, which its levels
  // ping-pong between; the diff's lists; and the merge's collision and the
  // diff's counts.
  core::Buffer sorted_[2];
  core::Buffer gone_;
  core::Buffer missing_;
  core::Buffer collision_;
  core::Buffer diff_counts_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <string>

#include "dct_tables.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {
namespace {

core::Status check_step(std::size_t index, float step) {
  // Negated, so a NaN is refused too.
  if (!(step >= kMinStep && step <= kMaxStep)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "CodecParams: effective step at frequency index " +
        std::to_string(index) + " must be in [" + std::to_string(kMinStep) +
        ", " + std::to_string(kMaxStep) +
        "] (a fraction of trunc_dist): finer, a quantized coefficient could "
        "overflow its clamp; coarser codes nothing more");
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace

core::Status CodecParams::validate() const {
  if (coefficient_count < 1 || coefficient_count > kVoxelsPerBlock) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "CodecParams: coefficient_count must be in [1, " +
        std::to_string(kVoxelsPerBlock) + "]");
  }
  // Normal, not merely positive: a host or device that flushes subnormals to
  // zero would otherwise disagree about whether the frame is valid.
  if (!(quantization_scale > 0.0f) || !std::isnormal(quantization_scale)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "CodecParams: quantization_scale must be normal and positive");
  }
  // Only the K kept frequencies are quantized, so only their weights count.
  static const auto zigzag = detail::zigzag_order();
  for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < coefficient_count; ++j) {
    const std::size_t i = zigzag[j];
    const float weight = quantization_weights[i];
    if (!(weight > 0.0f) || !std::isnormal(weight)) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "CodecParams: quantization_weights[" + std::to_string(i) +
          "] must be normal and positive");
    }
    VKC_TRY(check_step(i, quantization_scale * weight));
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
