// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "deblock.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <string>

#include "dct_tables.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_map_internal.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "deblock_flags_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "deblock_gauss_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "deblock_line_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "deblock_store_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// Mirrors `PushConstants` in deblock_common.glsl. All 4-byte scalars, so
// scalar layout puts each at its host offset.
struct PushConstants {
  std::uint32_t item_base;  // the first list entry a dispatch covers
  std::uint32_t num_blocks;
  std::uint32_t axis;
  std::uint32_t tick;
  std::int32_t num_buckets;
  std::int32_t bucket_size;
  std::int32_t max_chain;
  float trunc_dist;
  float inv_trunc;
  float observed_weight;
  float saturated;
  float c0;
  float c1;
  float c2;
  float line_clip;
  float gauss_g1;
  float gauss_clip;
};
static_assert(sizeof(PushConstants) == 68, "PushConstants must be 68 bytes");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, axis) == 8, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, tick) == 12, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, num_buckets) == 16, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, trunc_dist) == 28, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, observed_weight) == 36, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, saturated) == 40, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, c0) == 44, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, line_clip) == 56, "layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(PushConstants, gauss_clip) == 64, "layout drift");

// The set-0 bindings, mirroring the VGRID_DEBLOCK_BINDING_* defines in
// deblock_common.glsl.
enum Binding : std::uint32_t {
  kBindingBlocks = 0,
  kBindingMasks = 1,
  kBindingEntries = 2,
  kBindingTsdf = 3,
  kBindingWeight = 4,
  kBindingStamps = 5,
  kBindingShell = 6,
  kBindingFull = 7,
  kBindingExact = 8,
  kBindingCount = 9,
};

static_assert(kShellVoxels == 296, "deblock_common.glsl's kShellVoxels");
static_assert(kMaskWordsPerBlock == 16, "deblock_common.glsl's kMaskWords");

// The workgroup width of every kernel (kLanes in deblock_common.glsl): the
// flags kernel's blocks a workgroup.
static_assert(Deblock::kFlagLanes == 64, "deblock_common.glsl's kLanes");

// |v| at or above this is the clamp's kink, where a line is not fitted.
constexpr float kSaturated = 1.0f - 1e-5f;

constexpr VkDeviceSize kShellBytes = kShellVoxels * sizeof(float);
constexpr VkDeviceSize kFlagBytes = sizeof(std::uint32_t);

// Every row of the rule runs the line fit with a positive clip, and a
// Gaussian, when it has one, with a positive clip too: a clip of 0 would
// read as "unclipped" in the study's code and as "no change" here.
constexpr bool rule_valid() {
  for (const DeblockRow& row : kDeblockRule) {
    if (!(row.line_clip > 0.0f) || row.sigma < 0.0f ||
        (row.sigma > 0.0f && !(row.gauss_clip > 0.0f))) {
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}
static_assert(rule_valid(), "a kDeblockRule row without a positive clip");

core::Status fail(const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument("Deblock::record: " + why);
}

}  // namespace

float step_scale(const CodecParams& params) {
  const std::array<double, kBasisSize> basis = dct_basis<double>();
  // A frequency's peak over the block: the product of its 1-D bases' peaks,
  // DC's sqrt(1/8) and the first AC's at its first sample.
  const double phi0 = basis[0];
  const double phi1 = basis[kEdge];
  double t = static_cast<double>(params.quantization_scale *
                                 params.quantization_weights[0]) *
             phi0 * phi0 * phi0;
  // The zigzag's positions 1..3, one step along each axis.
  const std::array<std::uint32_t, kVoxelsPerBlock> zigzag = zigzag_order();
  for (std::uint32_t j = 1; j <= 3 && j < params.coefficient_count; ++j) {
    t = std::max(t, double(params.quantization_scale) *
                        double(params.quantization_weights[zigzag[j]]) * phi1 *
                        phi0 * phi0);
  }
  return static_cast<float>(t);
}

const DeblockRow* deblock_rule(std::uint32_t k, double t_mm) {
  for (const DeblockRow& row : kDeblockRule) {
    if (k <= row.max_k && t_mm >= row.min_t_mm) {
      return &row;
    }
  }
  return nullptr;
}

DeblockPasses deblock_passes(const DeblockRow& row, float t) {
  DeblockPasses p;
  p.linfit = true;
  p.line_clip = static_cast<float>(double(row.line_clip) * double(t));
  if (row.sigma > 0.0f) {
    const double sigma = row.sigma;
    p.gauss = true;
    p.gauss_g1 = static_cast<float>(std::exp(-1.0 / (2.0 * sigma * sigma)));
    p.gauss_clip = static_cast<float>(double(row.gauss_clip) * double(t));
  }
  return p;
}

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<Deblock>> Deblock::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "Deblock::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<Deblock> owned(new Deblock());
  Deblock& d = *owned;
  d.device_ = &device;
  d.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(PushConstants);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(d.flags_kernel_, "codec_deblock_flags",
                 vgrid_deblock_flags_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_deblock_flags_comp_spv_size, kBindingCount, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(d.line_kernel_, "codec_deblock_line",
                 vgrid_deblock_line_comp_spv, vgrid_deblock_line_comp_spv_size,
                 kBindingCount, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(d.gauss_kernel_, "codec_deblock_gauss",
                 vgrid_deblock_gauss_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_deblock_gauss_comp_spv_size, kBindingCount, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(d.store_kernel_, "codec_deblock_store",
                 vgrid_deblock_store_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_deblock_store_comp_spv_size, kBindingCount, &push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.pool_, kb.build());
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  d.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  // One slot's and one block's, so every call's binding names a buffer.
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(device, allocator, d.full_, kFlagBytes,
                                      d.max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                      "codec.deblock_full"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(device, allocator, d.shell_, kShellBytes,
                                      d.max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                      "codec.deblock_shell"));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.exact_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                         core::debug_object_handle(d.exact_.handle()),
                         "codec.deblock_exact");
  return owned;
}

core::Status Deblock::reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t slots,
                              const DeblockPasses& passes) {
  if (!passes.linfit && !passes.gauss) {
    return {};
  }
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(
      *device_, *allocator_, full_, VkDeviceSize(slots) * kFlagBytes,
      max_storage_buffer_range_, "codec.deblock_full"));
  if (!passes.gauss) {
    return {};
  }
  return core::ensure_device_scratch(
      *device_, *allocator_, shell_, VkDeviceSize(n) * kShellBytes,
      max_storage_buffer_range_, "codec.deblock_shell");
}

core::Status Deblock::record(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
    const ResidentBlocks& frame, const DeblockPasses& passes,
    const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& blocks,
    const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& flags,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const std::uint32_t n = frame.count;
  if ((!passes.linfit && !passes.gauss) || n == 0) {
    return {};
  }
  if ((passes.linfit && !(passes.line_clip > 0.0f)) ||
      (passes.gauss && !(passes.gauss_clip > 0.0f))) {
    return fail("a pass without a positive clip");
  }
  if (!grid.valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from grid");
  }
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  if (gp.block_size != kBlockSize) {
    return fail("the grid's block_size is " + std::to_string(gp.block_size) +
                ", not " + std::to_string(kBlockSize));
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView tsdf,
             grid.attribute(volume::kTsdfAttribute));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView weight,
             grid.attribute(volume::kWeightAttribute));
  if (tsdf.element_size != sizeof(float) ||
      weight.element_size != sizeof(float)) {
    return fail("the grid's tsdf and weight must be 4-byte floats");
  }
  if (frame.reference_count != 0) {
    return fail("the entries are a P-frame's stream positions, not its blocks");
  }
  if (n > static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks)) {
    return fail(std::to_string(n) + " blocks, more than this grid's heap (" +
                std::to_string(gp.num_blocks) + ")");
  }
  const VkDeviceSize list_bytes = VkDeviceSize(n) * sizeof(volume::BlockIndex);
  const VkDeviceSize mask_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(n) * kMaskWordsPerBlock * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  if (frame.list == nullptr || frame.masks == nullptr ||
      frame.list->size() < list_bytes || frame.masks->size() < mask_bytes) {
    return fail("the frame's buffers do not hold " + std::to_string(n) +
                " blocks");
  }
  const VkDeviceSize shell_bytes = VkDeviceSize(n) * kShellBytes;
  if (passes.gauss && shell_.size() < shell_bytes) {
    return fail(std::to_string(n) + " blocks, more than reserve made room for");
  }
  const VkDeviceSize full_bytes = VkDeviceSize(gp.num_blocks) * kFlagBytes;
  if (full_.size() < full_bytes) {
    return fail("a grid of " + std::to_string(gp.num_blocks) +
                " block slots, more than reserve made room for");
  }
  const VkDeviceSize entries_bytes =
      volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer_size(grid.map());
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(
      "Deblock: the hash entries", entries_bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_));

  // The sets of the kernels this filter runs, each written before its
  // dispatches.
  for (core::ComputeKernel* kernel :
       {&flags_kernel_, &line_kernel_, &gauss_kernel_, &store_kernel_}) {
    if (kernel == &line_kernel_ && !passes.linfit) continue;
    if ((kernel == &gauss_kernel_ || kernel == &store_kernel_) &&
        !passes.gauss) {
      continue;
    }
    const core::DescriptorSet& set = kernel->set;
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingBlocks, frame.list->handle(), 0,
                             list_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingMasks, frame.masks->handle(), 0,
                             mask_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(
        kBindingEntries,
        volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer(grid.map()), 0,
        entries_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingTsdf, tsdf.buffer->handle(), 0,
                             VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingWeight, weight.buffer->handle(), 0,
                             VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
    set.write_storage_buffer(
        kBindingStamps, grid.map().stamps_buffer().handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingShell, shell_.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingFull, full_.handle(), 0, full_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(kBindingExact, exact_.handle(), 0,
                             sizeof(std::uint32_t));
  }

  PushConstants push{};
  push.num_blocks = n;
  push.tick = grid.map().tick();
  push.num_buckets = gp.num_buckets;
  push.bucket_size = gp.bucket_size;
  push.max_chain = gp.max_chain;
  push.trunc_dist = gp.trunc_dist;
  push.inv_trunc = static_cast<float>(1.0 / double(gp.trunc_dist));
  push.observed_weight = volume::kObservedWeight;
  push.saturated = kSaturated;
  // The least-squares line through samples 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 from the face,
  // at the face.
  push.c0 = static_cast<float>(13.0 / 12.0);
  push.c1 = static_cast<float>(4.0 / 12.0);
  push.c2 = static_cast<float>(-5.0 / 12.0);
  push.line_clip = passes.line_clip;
  push.gauss_g1 = passes.gauss_g1;
  push.gauss_clip = passes.gauss_clip;
  // A workgroup a block, over the slices the device sized: none for a frame
  // its gate refused, so such a frame writes no voxel and no stamp. The
  // batch barriers every dispatch, so each pass sees all of the last one's
  // writes, a slice's included. The flags first, an invocation a block, over
  // the zeroed flags and count, which touch no grid buffer and stay ungated.
  const auto run = [&](const core::ComputeKernel& kernel) -> core::Status {
    return volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(batch, kernel, push,
                                                         blocks, stage);
  };
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(full_, 0, full_bytes, 0u));
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(exact_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u));
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(batch, flags_kernel_,
                                                        push, flags, stage));
  if (passes.linfit) {
    for (std::uint32_t axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
      push.axis = axis;
      VKC_TRY(run(line_kernel_));
    }
  }
  if (passes.gauss) {
    VKC_TRY(run(gauss_kernel_));
    VKC_TRY(run(store_kernel_));
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/deblock.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file deblock.hpp
/// @brief The decoder-side deblock: a decoded frame smoothed across its block
///        faces on the device, by a filter its header's steps choose.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed): the `Decoder` runs it, inside the
/// decode's last submit, when `Decoder::set_deblock` is on. It carries
/// `VGRID_CODEC_API` so the tier's tests reach it in a shared-library build.
///
/// The filters are the 2026-10-21 quantization study's, on the field
/// `v = tsdf / trunc_dist`, under the per-block fallback (that decision's
/// 2026-10-23 amendment): a **masked** block, one holding an unobserved
/// voxel, keeps its exact decode -- no pass writes it -- and only a **fully
/// observed** block, its mask all ones, is filtered. A missing block is no
/// neighbour.
///
/// - **The line fit** (linfit, n 2, m 3). For each axis, x then y then z, and
///   each block B whose +axis neighbour N exists, B and N both fully
///   observed, each of the 64 lines across their face: p_i is B's voxel at
///   7 - i along the axis and q_i N's at i. When none of p_0..2 and q_0..2
///   has |v| at or above 1 - 1e-5 (the clamp's kink), the offset between the
///   two sides' least-squares lines at the face,
///   `delta = sum_i c_i (q_i - p_i)` with c = (13, 4, -5) / 12, clipped to
///   +-`line_clip`, is spread as a tent: p_0 and q_0 move 0.375 delta toward
///   each other, p_1 and q_1 0.125, each clamped to [-1, 1]. A face with a
///   masked side is not fitted, so the line passes leave both its sides as
///   they were.
/// - **The Gaussian** (r 1). Along x, then y, then z, each voxel of a fully
///   observed block becomes the mean of itself and its observed axis
///   neighbours, weighted 1 and `gauss_g1`, its change clipped to
///   +-`gauss_clip`, then clamped to [-1, 1]. A masked block's voxels keep
///   their values through every pass, so a neighbour's taps read its observed
///   voxels as decoded; its unobserved ones drop out.
///
/// Each pass reads the field as the previous pass left it. A voxel whose
/// value comes out with the bits it went in with is not written, so it keeps
/// its metres exactly.
///
/// On the device: a first kernel, an invocation a frame block, sets the flag
/// by slot of each fully observed block, the rest zeroed before it, and
/// counts the masked blocks into @ref Deblock::exact, for the decoder's
/// results. Then one 64-lane workgroup per frame block in every kernel, which
/// returns
/// at once for a block its own mask words mark masked. The line passes run in
/// place on `tsdf`, a dispatch an axis: a voxel lies on at most one line of a
/// pass, read before it is written. The Gaussian is one fused kernel per
/// block over the block and the 1-voxel halo of its 26 neighbours, x, y and z
/// in shared memory; it writes the block's interior in place, which no other
/// workgroup reads, and its shell (the voxels with a coordinate 0 or 7, which
/// neighbours' halos read) into a snapshot by list position, which a store
/// kernel then copies into `tsdf`. A neighbour is fully observed by its flag,
/// and a masked neighbour's observed voxels are found by their weights;
/// blocks are found by coordinate through the grid's hash, so no list `ptr`
/// is read. A block a pass writes is stamped `changed` with the map's
/// current tick.

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/codec_params.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// A block's shell: its voxels with a coordinate 0 or 7 on some axis, which a
/// neighbour's 1-voxel halo reaches.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kShellVoxels = kVoxelsPerBlock - 6 * 6 * 6;

/// @brief One frame's filter, as the kernels take it, in units of the
///        normalized field.
struct DeblockPasses {
  /// The line passes run, each line's offset clipped to +-@ref line_clip
  /// (positive).
  bool linfit = false;
  float line_clip = 0.0f;
  /// The Gaussian runs after them, a neighbour weighted @ref gauss_g1 against
  /// the voxel's 1, each pass's change clipped to +-@ref gauss_clip
  /// (positive).
  bool gauss = false;
  float gauss_g1 = 0.0f;
  float gauss_clip = 0.0f;
};

/// @brief One row of the step-keyed rule: a frame of K <= @ref max_k whose
///        T_mm is at least @ref min_t_mm runs the row's filter.
struct DeblockRow {
  const char* filter;  ///< Its name: "LF", "LG" or "R".
  std::uint32_t max_k;
  double min_t_mm;
  float line_clip;   ///< In units of T.
  float sigma;       ///< Voxels; 0 runs no Gaussian.
  float gauss_clip;  ///< In units of T.
};

/// The rule the 2026-10-21 study fitted on its rounding streams, first match
/// wins; a frame no row matches runs no filter. The study fitted K 35 and
/// below, and 56 and above; K 36-55 takes the latter's rows.
inline constexpr DeblockRow kDeblockRule[] = {
    {"R", 35, 0.0, 4.0f, 0.75f, 0.75f},
    {"R", kVoxelsPerBlock, 0.6, 4.0f, 0.75f, 0.75f},
    {"LG", kVoxelsPerBlock, 0.3, 4.0f, 0.5f, 0.375f},
    {"LF", kVoxelsPerBlock, 0.075, 4.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f},
};

/// @return T, in units of the normalized field: the largest change one
///         quantum of a kept lowest-frequency coefficient -- DC, and the
///         zigzag's next three, (0,0,1), (0,1,0), (1,0,0) -- makes to a
///         voxel, its step times its basis function's peak, in the study's
///         arithmetic (DC's step the transform's float product, the others'
///         in double) so the rule's thresholds fall where the study's did.
VGRID_CODEC_API float step_scale(const CodecParams& params);

/// @return The first row of @ref kDeblockRule that K @p k and @p t_mm
///         (T in millimetres) match, or null for none.
VGRID_CODEC_API const DeblockRow* deblock_rule(std::uint32_t k, double t_mm);

/// @return @p row's filter at T @p t: its clips times @p t in double, and
///         `exp(-1 / (2 sigma^2))`, each rounded to float.
VGRID_CODEC_API DeblockPasses deblock_passes(const DeblockRow& row, float t);

/// @brief The deblock's kernels, its flags and its shell snapshot.
///
/// The flags take a word a slot of the largest grid heap a filter ran on, and
/// the snapshot @ref kShellVoxels floats a block of the largest frame a
/// Gaussian ran on; each grows with 1.5x headroom (`ensure_device_scratch`),
/// and a frame without a filter takes neither.
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must outlive
///          this object. Not thread-safe.
class VGRID_CODEC_API Deblock {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the four kernels, a one-slot flags buffer and a one-block
  ///        snapshot.
  /// @return The deblock, or a pipeline, pool or allocation failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<Deblock>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~Deblock() = default;
  Deblock(const Deblock&) = delete;
  Deblock& operator=(const Deblock&) = delete;
  Deblock(Deblock&&) = delete;
  Deblock& operator=(Deblock&&) = delete;

  /// @brief Make room for a frame of @p n blocks in a grid of @p slots block
  ///        slots under @p passes -- the flags, and the snapshot when a
  ///        Gaussian runs -- before anything is recorded.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a buffer past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`, which grows nothing; or an
  ///         allocation's failure.
  core::Status reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t slots,
                       const DeblockPasses& passes);

  /// @brief Record @p passes over @p frame's blocks into @p batch, after the
  ///        writes they read (the inverse transform's), each kernel over its
  ///        slices, which the device sized and gated; the caller submits.
  ///
  /// @p frame must name every block @p grid holds, each once, as a decode
  /// leaves them: a block it lacks reads as masked, and one it names twice
  /// races. Its order and `ptr`s are ignored. Records nothing for passes
  /// that run nothing or no blocks; @ref exact then holds nothing the frame
  /// needs, since every block is left as decoded.
  /// @param batch   The batch to record into; submitted by the caller.
  /// @param grid    The grid, its `tsdf` filtered in place; 4-byte `tsdf` and
  ///                `weight`, `block_size` 8.
  /// @param frame   The frame's list and masks, by list position, as the
  ///                reference store holds them; no reference entries.
  /// @param passes  The filter.
  /// @param blocks  The passes' slices, a workgroup a block, for @p frame's
  ///                count.
  /// @param flags   The flags kernel's, a workgroup 64 blocks.
  /// @param stage   Optional scope the dispatches record their device spans
  ///                into.
  /// @return OK, or, before anything is recorded,
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a grid of another block
  ///         size or without float `tsdf` and `weight`, a pass without a
  ///         positive clip, a P-frame's entries, more blocks than the grid's
  ///         heap, or more blocks or slots than @ref reserve made room for,
  ///         buffers smaller than the count, or a hash table past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`.
  core::Status record(
      core::CommandBatch& batch, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
      const ResidentBlocks& frame, const DeblockPasses& passes,
      const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& blocks,
      const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& flags,
      core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @return The blocks the last @ref record's passes left as decoded, the
  ///         frame's masked blocks, a u32, once its batch ran.
  const core::Buffer& exact() const noexcept { return exact_; }

  /// The flags kernel's blocks a workgroup (`kLanes` in deblock_common.glsl).
  static constexpr std::uint32_t kFlagLanes = 64;

 private:
  Deblock() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;

  // One layout for the four (deblock_common.glsl); declared before pool_,
  // so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel flags_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel line_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel gauss_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel store_kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;
  // The per-block fallback's flags, a word a slot of the grid's heap.
  core::Buffer full_;
  // The frame's masked blocks, one word, zeroed in each record's batch.
  core::Buffer exact_;
  // The Gaussian's shell snapshot, kShellVoxels floats an entry.
  core::Buffer shell_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decode_grid.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decode_grid.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <new>
#include <string>
#include <utility>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/grid_growth.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {
namespace {

// The grid's fewest buckets.
constexpr std::int32_t kMinBuckets = 1024;
// Decodes again after the decoder's IoError, its lock contention.
constexpr int kContendedRetries = 2;

static_assert(volume::block_grid_params(1.0f, 1.0f, 1).block_size == kBlockSize,
              "a decode grid's blocks are the codec's");

// Buckets for twice @p blocks, at least kMinBuckets. Capped so the heap's
// slot count fits an int32_t; no grid holds that many blocks anyway, which
// VoxelBlockGrid::create and grow_grid refuse.
std::int32_t decode_buckets(std::uint32_t blocks) {
  constexpr std::int32_t kBucket = volume::kDefaultBucketSize;
  const std::int64_t need = (2 * std::int64_t(blocks) + kBucket - 1) / kBucket;
  return std::int32_t(std::clamp<std::int64_t>(
      need, kMinBuckets, std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max() / kBucket));
}

// The caller's ceiling on a frame's blocks, refused as a frame to skip.
core::Status check_ceiling(const char* who, std::uint32_t blocks,
                           std::uint32_t max_blocks) {
  if (blocks <= max_blocks) return {};
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(
      std::string(who) + ": the frame holds " + std::to_string(blocks) +
      " blocks, more than the caller's ceiling of " +
      std::to_string(max_blocks));
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<volume::VoxelBlockGrid> make_decode_grid(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator, const std::uint8_t* frame,
    std::size_t size, std::uint32_t max_blocks) try {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const FrameInfo info, read_frame_info(frame, size));
  VKC_TRY(check_ceiling("make_decode_grid", info.block_count, max_blocks));
  // The block count against the segment table, as the decoder parses the
  // frame. A sound P-frame stops at the reference only a decoder holds
  // (NotFound); anything else is the decoder's refusal of the frame.
  {
    const core::Result<detail::ParsedFrame> parsed =
        detail::parse_frame(frame, size, info.block_count, nullptr);
    if (!parsed.ok() &&
        parsed.status().domain() != core::Status::Code::NotFound) {
      return parsed.status();
    }
  }
  const volume::AttributeSpec attrs[] = {
      {volume::kTsdfAttribute, sizeof(float)},
      {volume::kWeightAttribute, sizeof(float)}};
  return volume::VoxelBlockGrid::create(
      device, allocator,
      volume::block_grid_params(info.voxel_size, info.trunc_dist,
                                decode_buckets(info.block_count)),
      attrs, 2);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("make_decode_grid",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

namespace {

// Grow @p grid once for a frame of @p blocks that the decoder refused as too
// small (@p refused), unless that passes @p max_blocks' grid: to twice its
// buckets or the frame's make_decode_grid buckets, whichever is more.
core::Status grow_for(const char* who, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                      std::uint32_t blocks, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                      const core::Status& refused) {
  // grow_grid's target, in slots, against make_decode_grid's grid for the
  // ceiling.
  const std::int32_t at_least = decode_buckets(blocks);
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  const std::int64_t slots =
      std::int64_t(gp.bucket_size) *
      std::max<std::int64_t>(2 * std::int64_t(gp.num_buckets), at_least);
  const std::int64_t ceiling =
      std::int64_t(volume::kDefaultBucketSize) * decode_buckets(max_blocks);
  if (slots > ceiling) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(who) + ": growing the grid to " + std::to_string(slots) +
        " slots would pass the " + std::to_string(ceiling) +
        " the caller's ceiling of " + std::to_string(max_blocks) +
        " blocks allows (" + refused.message() + ")");
  }
  return volume::grow_grid(grid, at_least);
}

// Decode the record of @p blocks blocks at the start of @p slot again,
// blocking, in batches of its own, as the decoder's refusal @p s asks: after
// a grow for `Status::Code::OutOfMemory` (once), or as it is for
// `Status::Code::IoError` (twice at most). Each recovery, its decode again
// included, is one `"  ..grow"` or `"  ..retry"` row of @p metrics inside a
// `"codec decode"` span, so the stage's row holds it. Returns OK, or the last
// error.
core::Status recover(Decoder& decoder, const core::HostSlot& slot,
                     std::size_t size, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                     std::uint32_t blocks, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                     core::Status s, core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  int contended = 0;
  bool grown = false;
  // The stage's row above its breakdown's, though its span closes after.
  if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->seed("codec decode");
  for (;;) {
    const bool grow = s.domain() == core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory && !grown;
    if (!grow && (s.domain() != core::Status::Code::IoError ||
                  contended == kContendedRetries)) {
      return s;
    }
    const core::StageScope stage(metrics, "codec decode");
    const core::StageScope row(metrics, grow ? "  ..grow" : "  ..retry");
    if (grow) {
      VKC_TRY(grow_for("decode_growing", grid, blocks, max_blocks, s));
      grown = true;
    } else {
      ++contended;
    }
    s = decoder.decode(slot, size, grid, nullptr);
    if (s.ok()) return s;
  }
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<PendingDecode> record_growing(
    Decoder& decoder, core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::HostSlot& slot,
    std::size_t size, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const FrameInfo info, read_frame_info(slot.data(), size));
  VKC_TRY(check_ceiling("record_growing", info.block_count, max_blocks));
  core::Result<PendingDecode> recorded =
      decoder.record(batch, slot, size, grid, metrics);
  // A heap too small is refused with nothing recorded, so the frame records
  // again once the grid has grown. The device's own out of memory can come
  // after the first commands, so the batch is the caller's to drop.
  if (recorded.ok() ||
      recorded.status().domain() != core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory ||
      info.block_count <= static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().num_blocks)) {
    return recorded;
  }
  {
    // Part of the decode, whose row the record above opened.
    const core::StageScope stage(metrics, "codec decode");
    const core::StageScope grow(metrics, "  ..grow");
    VKC_TRY(grow_for("record_growing", grid, info.block_count, max_blocks,
                     recorded.status()));
  }
  return decoder.record(batch, slot, size, grid, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("record_growing",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Result<Finished> finish_growing(Decoder& decoder,
                                      const PendingDecode& pending,
                                      volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                      std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                                      core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  const core::Status s = decoder.finish(pending, grid);
  if (s.ok()) return Finished{};
  VKC_TRY(recover(decoder, pending.input, pending.size, grid, pending.blocks,
                  max_blocks, s, metrics));
  return Finished{true};
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("finish_growing",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Status decode_growing(Decoder& decoder, const std::uint8_t* frame,
                            std::size_t size, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                            std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                            core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const FrameInfo info, read_frame_info(frame, size));
  VKC_TRY(check_ceiling("decode_growing", info.block_count, max_blocks));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const core::HostSlot slot, decoder.claim_input(size));
  std::memcpy(slot.data(), frame, size);
  return decode_growing(decoder, slot, size, grid, max_blocks, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("decode_growing",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Status decode_growing(Decoder& decoder, const core::HostSlot& slot,
                            std::size_t size, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                            std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                            core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  if (!slot.valid() || size > slot.capacity()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "decode_growing: the slot does not hold the record");
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const FrameInfo info, read_frame_info(slot.data(), size));
  VKC_TRY(check_ceiling("decode_growing", info.block_count, max_blocks));
  // The whole call is timed, the first decode and a recovery, and its rows
  // land in the caller's metrics once the decode succeeds. A heap too small
  // is the record's refusal and a table that cannot place the frame the
  // finish's, and either recovers alike.
  core::StageMetrics call;
  core::StageMetrics* const rows = metrics != nullptr ? &call : nullptr;
  const core::Status s = decoder.decode(slot, size, grid, rows);
  if (!s.ok()) {
    VKC_TRY(recover(decoder, slot, size, grid, info.block_count, max_blocks, s,
                    rows));
  }
  if (metrics != nullptr) {
    try {
      core::StageMetrics merged = *metrics;
      merged.merge(call);
      *metrics = std::move(merged);
    } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
      // The decoder already committed its reference. Dropping this decode's
      // diagnostics must not turn that success into a failure the caller
      // would retry; keep the caller's previous rows intact.
    }
  }
  return {};
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("decode_growing",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decoder.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decoder.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstring>
#include <new>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "block_lists.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "deblock.hpp"
#include "device_frame_reader.hpp"
#include "frame_gate.hpp"
#include "frame_hash.hpp"
#include "reference_store.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/check.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {
namespace detail {

// What finish needs of a recorded frame: the reference it becomes, its new
// blocks, what the deblock ran on it, where its rounds and its results land,
// and the grid it was recorded into.
struct RecordedFrame {
  std::uint64_t serial = 0;
  FrameReference reference;
  std::uint32_t new_count = 0;
  DeblockInfo deblock;
  bool filtered = false;
  core::HostSlot results;
  volume::RecordedRounds removed;
  volume::RecordedRounds allocated;
  const volume::VoxelBlockGrid* grid = nullptr;
};

}  // namespace detail

namespace {

// The zeroed bytes after a record in its input slot: the word holding the
// payload's last byte, which the decode reads whole, stays inside the
// binding.
constexpr std::size_t kSlack = 8;
// The input slots' first size, about a rafa2 I-frame's; a larger record
// grows the slot it claims.
constexpr VkDeviceSize kFirstInputBytes = VkDeviceSize{64} << 10;

core::Status fail(const std::string& why, const char* op = "decode") {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string("Decoder::") + op + ": " +
                                        why);
}

// The grid checks a decode and a rebuild make before anything is recorded:
// 8^3 blocks, and a 4-byte float tsdf and weight and no other attribute.
core::Status check_grid(const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, const char* op) {
  if (!grid.valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from grid", op);
  }
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  if (gp.block_size != kBlockSize) {
    return fail(
        "the codec decodes into 8^3 blocks, and this grid's "
        "block_size is " +
            std::to_string(gp.block_size),
        op);
  }
  for (const std::string_view name :
       {volume::kTsdfAttribute, volume::kWeightAttribute}) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView view, grid.attribute(name));
    if (view.element_size != sizeof(float)) {
      return fail("the grid's " + std::string(name) + " is not a 4-byte float",
                  op);
    }
  }
  // Those two are all a frame carries, so any other attribute of a block kept
  // across frames would hold the previous frame's values under this one's
  // geometry, with nothing to say which blocks those are.
  if (grid.attribute_count() != 2) {
    return fail("the grid declares " + std::to_string(grid.attribute_count()) +
                    " attributes; a frame carries tsdf and weight alone, so a "
                    "grid it decodes into must declare only those",
                op);
  }
  return {};
}

// The frame's geometry against the grid's, exactly, not approximately: the
// coordinates are in this grid's voxels, and the coefficients are fractions
// of its band. A frame from a grid of other geometry would decode into the
// wrong place at the wrong scale and say OK.
core::Status check_geometry(const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                            const detail::FrameHeader& header, const char* op) {
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  if (header.voxel_size != gp.voxel_size ||
      header.trunc_dist != gp.trunc_dist) {
    return fail("the frame's geometry (voxel_size " +
                    std::to_string(header.voxel_size) + ", trunc_dist " +
                    std::to_string(header.trunc_dist) +
                    ") is not this grid's (" + std::to_string(gp.voxel_size) +
                    ", " + std::to_string(gp.trunc_dist) +
                    "); build the grid from read_frame_info",
                op);
  }
  return {};
}

// What the deblock runs on a frame of @p header, and reports: the rule's
// filter at the frame's T, or none when @p on is false; finish and rebuild
// add the blocks it kept.
struct FrameDeblock {
  DeblockInfo info;
  detail::DeblockPasses passes;
  bool runs() const noexcept { return passes.linfit || passes.gauss; }
};

FrameDeblock frame_deblock(const detail::FrameHeader& header, bool on) {
  FrameDeblock out;
  const float t = detail::step_scale(header.params);
  out.info.step = t * header.trunc_dist;
  if (!on) return out;
  const double t_mm = double(t) * double(header.trunc_dist) * 1e3;
  const detail::DeblockRow* row =
      detail::deblock_rule(header.params.coefficient_count, t_mm);
  if (row == nullptr) return out;
  out.info.filter = row->filter;
  out.passes = detail::deblock_passes(*row, t);
  return out;
}

// What the deblock did to a frame of @p n blocks: the filter @p info names,
// and the blocks it left as decoded, those holding an unobserved voxel (the
// 2026-10-21 decision's 2026-10-23 amendment), or every block when no filter
// @p ran. A frame of no blocks records no filter (Deblock::record), so its
// @p exact is an earlier frame's.
DeblockInfo deblock_ran(const DeblockInfo& info, bool ran, std::uint32_t n,
                        std::uint32_t exact) {
  DeblockInfo out = info;
  out.block_count = n;
  out.exact_blocks = ran && n != 0 ? exact : n;
  return out;
}

// Every round's residue lost bucket-lock races over a table with room: not a
// capacity limit, so the answer is to decode again, and a resize would double
// every attribute array for nothing (see volume::AllocFailures).
core::Status contended(const char* doing, std::uint32_t blocks) {
  return core::Status::io_error(
      "Decoder::decode: " + std::to_string(blocks) +
      " blocks lost bucket-lock races in every round of " + doing +
      ", over a table with room for them; decode again "
      "(a resize would not help)");
}

detail::DecodeResults read_results(const core::HostSlot& slot) {
  detail::DecodeResults r;
  std::memcpy(&r, slot.data(), sizeof(r));
  return r;
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<FrameInfo> read_frame_info(const std::uint8_t* data,
                                        std::size_t size) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::FrameHeader header,
             detail::read_frame_header(data, size));
  FrameInfo info;
  info.type = header.type;
  info.voxel_size = header.voxel_size;
  info.trunc_dist = header.trunc_dist;
  info.block_count = header.block_count;
  info.params = header.params;
  return info;
}

Decoder::Decoder() = default;
Decoder::~Decoder() = default;
Decoder::Decoder(Decoder&& other) noexcept = default;
Decoder& Decoder::operator=(Decoder&& other) noexcept = default;

bool Decoder::valid() const noexcept { return transform_ != nullptr; }

core::Result<Decoder> Decoder::create(core::Device& device,
                                      core::Allocator& allocator) {
  Decoder d;
  d.device_ = &device;
  d.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.transform_, detail::DctTransform::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.reader_, detail::DeviceFrameReader::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.store_, detail::ReferenceStore::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.lists_, detail::BlockLists::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.deblock_, detail::Deblock::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.gate_, detail::FrameGate::create(device, allocator));
  // Two slots each: one a recorded frame holds until its batch has resolved,
  // and one the host fills meanwhile.
  core::HostRingDesc inputs;
  inputs.slot_bytes = kFirstInputBytes;
  inputs.name = "codec.decode_input";
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.inputs_, core::HostRing::create(device, allocator, inputs));
  core::HostRingDesc results;
  results.slot_bytes = sizeof(detail::DecodeResults);
  results.name = "codec.decode_results";
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.results_, core::HostRing::create(device, allocator, results));
  VKC_ASSIGN(d.gpu_timer_, core::GpuTimer::create(device));
  return d;
}

core::Result<core::HostSlot> Decoder::claim_input(std::size_t bytes) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from decoder", "claim_input");
  }
  if (bytes == 0) {
    return fail("a record of 0 bytes", "claim_input");
  }
  return inputs_->claim(VkDeviceSize(bytes) + kSlack);
}

core::Status Decoder::decode(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size,
                             volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                             core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  if (!valid()) {
    core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
    return fail("moved-from decoder");
  }
  // No record is the header's refusal, as an empty frame always was.
  if (data == nullptr || size == 0) {
    core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
    return detail::read_frame_header(data, size).status();
  }
  core::Result<core::HostSlot> slot = claim_input(size);
  if (!slot.ok()) {
    core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
    return slot.status();
  }
  std::memcpy(slot->data(), data, size);
  return decode(*slot, size, grid, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Decoder::decode",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Status Decoder::decode(const core::HostSlot& slot, std::size_t size,
                             volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                             core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  // Before any refusal, so a refused call still costs its row; its wait,
  // and the device halves the batch hands back, land in it too.
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
  if (!valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from decoder");
  }
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(const PendingDecode pending,
             record_frame(batch, slot, size, grid, metrics));
  const core::Status ran = [&]() -> core::Status {
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch done, batch.submit_async({}, {}));
    VKC_TRY(done.wait());
    if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->merge_device(done.device_rows());
    return {};
  }();
  if (!ran.ok()) {
    abandon(pending);
    return ran;
  }
  return finish(pending, grid);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Decoder::decode",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Result<PendingDecode> Decoder::record(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                            const core::HostSlot& slot,
                                            std::size_t size,
                                            volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                            core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
  return record_frame(batch, slot, size, grid, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Decoder::record",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Result<PendingDecode> Decoder::record_frame(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                                  const core::HostSlot& slot,
                                                  std::size_t size,
                                                  volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                                  core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from decoder", "record");
  }

  // --- Everything checkable before anything is recorded. ----------------
  VKC_TRY(check_grid(grid, "decode"));
  if (!slot.valid() || size > slot.capacity() ||
      slot.capacity() - size < kSlack) {
    return fail("the slot holds " + std::to_string(slot.capacity()) +
                    " bytes, fewer than the record's " + std::to_string(size) +
                    " and " + std::to_string(kSlack) + " of slack",
                "record");
  }
  std::uint8_t* const data = slot.data();
  // The geometry, read off the header before the frame is parsed, so a
  // frame of another geometry is never mistaken for one the grid is too
  // small for.
  VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::FrameHeader header,
             detail::read_frame_header(data, size));
  VKC_TRY(check_geometry(grid, header, "decode"));
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  const std::uint32_t n = header.block_count;
  const FrameDeblock filter = frame_deblock(header, deblock_on_);
  // The whole frame, parsed in place, a P-frame against the reference held:
  // a corrupt frame, or one on another reference, is refused here, with the
  // grid and the reference untouched. The heap bounds the block count the
  // reader will allocate for, so a frame the grid cannot hold is refused here
  // too; a frame the device cannot hold is refused as the reader refuses it.
  core::Result<detail::ParsedFrame> parsed = detail::parse_frame(
      data, size, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks), store_->held());
  if (!parsed.ok()) {
    const core::Status& s = parsed.status();
    if (s.domain() != core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory) return s;
    return core::Status::out_of_memory(
        "Decoder::decode: " + s.message() +
        " (the grid's num_blocks); grow it with VoxelBlockGrid::resize and "
        "decode again");
  }
  // Prepare the replacement before superseding an unfinished record, so a
  // host allocation failure leaves that token finishable. Its batch has
  // resolved (the @pre), so the ring's other results slot is free.
  auto recorded = std::make_unique<detail::RecordedFrame>();
  core::Result<core::HostSlot> results =
      results_->claim(sizeof(detail::DecodeResults));
  VKC_CHECK(results.ok(),
            "Decoder::record: the last record's batch has resolved, so a "
            "results slot is free");
  recorded->reference =
      detail::FrameReference{detail::frame_hash(data, size), header};
  recorded->new_count = parsed->new_count;
  recorded->deblock = filter.info;
  recorded->filtered = filter.runs();
  recorded->results = std::move(results).value();
  recorded->grid = &grid;
  // Reserving a larger frame may replace the spare buffers this token
  // needs, so retire it before any reserve can invalidate those contents.
  pending_.reset();
  // Room on the device for its N blocks before anything is recorded: the
  // store's spare, list and sources, the diff's lists, and the deblock's
  // flags and snapshot. Each, like every buffer the inverse and the
  // deblock bind -- K <= 512 coefficients, 16 mask words and 296 floats of
  // snapshot a block, 20 bytes of hash entry a slot, 16 bytes of gone list
  // and 4 of flag a slot --
  // is at most the 4-byte tsdf array once the frame fits the heap, and
  // VoxelBlockGrid::create / resize bound that array to
  // maxStorageBufferRange (attribute() confirmed it covers the live grid),
  // so no range check refuses a frame the parse passed: only a device out
  // of memory can, which is no refusal of the frame. A P-frame's reader
  // bounds its M + A entries itself: a fresh grid sized from N does not
  // bound M.
  const auto slots =
      static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_buckets * gp.bucket_size);
  VKC_TRY(store_->reserve(n, header.params.coefficient_count));
  VKC_TRY(lists_->reserve(n, slots));
  VKC_TRY(deblock_->reserve(n, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks),
                            filter.passes));
  // Stands in for the zero pad a staged payload had.
  std::memset(data + size, 0, kSlack);

  // --- The whole decode, into the caller's batch. Every update first: the
  // steps here, the tables and segment words in the reader's recording,
  // ahead of its first dispatch, so MoltenVK opens no blit encoder mid-batch.
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer input, batch.input(slot, 0, size + kSlack));
  VKC_TRY(transform_->record_steps(batch, header.params));
  const detail::ResultSources words{
      &reader_->verdict(), &lists_->collision(),    &lists_->diff_counts(),
      &store_->faults(),   &transform_->rejected(), &deblock_->exact()};
  detail::ResidentBlocks payload;
  {
    // The frame entropy-decoded, a P-frame's survivors merged with its new
    // blocks into frame order, and the grid's blocks diffed against it.
    core::GpuStageScope read(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..rans decode");
    VKC_ASSIGN(payload, reader_->record_decode(
                            batch, parsed.value(), input, size + kSlack,
                            VkDeviceSize(parsed->payload - data), &read));
    const detail::FrameBuffers frame = store_->frame_buffers();
    VKC_TRY(lists_->record_merge(batch, payload, store_->reference_list(),
                                 frame, n, &read));
    VKC_TRY(lists_->record_diff(batch, grid, *frame.list, n, &read));
  }
  const volume::DeviceCount gate{&gate_->gate(), 0, 1};
  {
    // Rows 11 to 13 judged on the device, then the grid's block set made the
    // frame's behind that gate: what the grid holds that the frame lacks is
    // removed (record_remove zeroes it, so a later reuse of its slot starts
    // fresh), and what the frame holds that the grid lacks is allocated, each
    // from the diff's list and count. Blocks in both are kept in their slots,
    // and their tsdf/weight are rewritten in full below, so nothing of the
    // previous frame survives in them. Each kind's rounds close the gate on
    // their own failure.
    core::GpuStageScope apply(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..apply");
    VKC_TRY(gate_->record_gate(
        batch, words,
        detail::GateCheck{false, header.type == FrameType::kInter, n,
                          parsed->new_count},
        &apply));
    VKC_ASSIGN(recorded->removed,
               grid.record_remove(
                   batch, lists_->gone(),
                   volume::DeviceCount{&lists_->diff_counts(), 0, slots}, &gate,
                   &apply));
    VKC_ASSIGN(recorded->allocated,
               grid.map().record_allocate(
                   batch, lists_->missing(),
                   volume::DeviceCount{&lists_->diff_counts(),
                                       sizeof(std::uint32_t), n},
                   &gate, &apply));
  }
  {
    // The frame's blocks, made, reconstructed and deblocked behind the gate:
    // each from the reference and the payload into the store's spare, then
    // by coordinate alone -- the inverse finds each block in the hash table,
    // so the slots the allocation drew need not be read back, and a frame
    // block the grid does not hold, a grid changed under this call, is
    // counted there rather than written. Then every count into the results
    // slot.
    core::GpuStageScope inverse(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..inverse");
    VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::FrameSlices slices,
               gate_->record_slices(batch, n, &inverse));
    VKC_ASSIGN(
        const detail::ResidentBlocks blocks,
        store_->record_apply(batch, payload, n, slices.blocks, &inverse));
    VKC_TRY(transform_->record_inverse(batch, grid, blocks, header.params,
                                       slices.blocks, &inverse));
    VKC_TRY(deblock_->record(batch, grid, blocks, filter.passes, slices.blocks,
                             slices.flags, &inverse));
    VKC_TRY(gate_->record_results(batch, recorded->results, words, &inverse));
  }
  recorded->serial = ++serial_;
  pending_ = std::move(recorded);
  return PendingDecode{pending_->serial, n, gate, slot, size};
}

core::Status Decoder::finish(const PendingDecode& pending,
                             volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from decoder", "finish");
  }
  if (!holds(pending)) {
    return fail(
        "the pending frame is not this decoder's last record (finished, "
        "abandoned, superseded, or another decoder's)",
        "finish");
  }
  if (&grid != pending_->grid) {
    return fail("the grid is not the one the frame was recorded into",
                "finish");
  }
  const std::unique_ptr<detail::RecordedFrame> frame = std::move(pending_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AllocFailures removed,
             grid.map().settle(frame->removed));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AllocFailures allocated,
             grid.map().settle(frame->allocated));
  last_rounds_ = std::max(removed.rounds, allocated.rounds);
  const detail::DecodeResults r = read_results(frame->results);
  const detail::FrameHeader& header = frame->reference.header;
  const std::uint32_t n = header.block_count;
  // Rows 11 and 12, then 13, the last refusal, which the gate made before
  // the grid changed.
  VKC_TRY(detail::DeviceFrameReader::judge(header.type, n, frame->new_count,
                                           r.failed, r.survivors));
  if (r.collision_q != detail::kNoSource) {
    return detail::check_new_block(r.collision_q, r.collision_e);
  }
  // Out of the table but refused by the heap: the heap only takes back what
  // it handed out, so this is a grid whose accounting is already broken, and
  // every later frame would find it a block shorter. Not IoError, which says
  // decode again: no retry mends it.
  if (removed.terminal != 0) {
    return fail("the grid's free heap refused " +
                std::to_string(removed.terminal) +
                " removed blocks; its block accounting is broken, which "
                "neither decoding again nor a resize mends");
  }
  if (removed.total != 0) {
    return contended("removing", removed.total);
  }
  if (allocated.capacity_limited()) {
    return core::Status::out_of_memory(
        "Decoder::decode: the grid's hash table cannot place " +
        std::to_string(allocated.total) + " of the frame's " +
        std::to_string(n) +
        " blocks; grow it with VoxelBlockGrid::resize and decode again");
  }
  if (allocated.total != 0) {
    return contended("allocating", allocated.total);
  }
  VKC_TRY(detail::ReferenceStore::check_faults(r.faults));
  VKC_TRY(detail::DctTransform::check_rejected("inverse", r.rejected, n));
  // Only a frame that succeeded moves the reference.
  store_->commit(frame->reference);
  last_deblock_ = deblock_ran(frame->deblock, frame->filtered, n, r.exact);
  return {};
}

void Decoder::abandon(const PendingDecode& pending) noexcept {
  if (holds(pending)) pending_.reset();
}

// The serial counts this decoder's records alone; the gate's word, its own
// buffer, tells another decoder's token from one of its own.
bool Decoder::holds(const PendingDecode& pending) const noexcept {
  return pending_ != nullptr && pending.serial != 0 &&
         pending.serial == pending_->serial &&
         pending.gate.buffer == &gate_->gate();
}

core::Status Decoder::rebuild(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                              core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec decode");
  if (!valid()) {
    return fail("moved-from decoder", "rebuild");
  }
  const detail::FrameReference* held = store_->held();
  if (held == nullptr) {
    return core::Status::not_found(
        "Decoder::rebuild: no frame decoded yet; decode one first");
  }
  VKC_TRY(check_grid(grid, "rebuild"));
  const detail::FrameHeader& header = held->header;
  VKC_TRY(check_geometry(grid, header, "rebuild"));
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  const std::uint32_t n = header.block_count;
  const FrameDeblock filter = frame_deblock(header, deblock_on_);
  VKC_TRY(lists_->reserve(
      n, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_buckets * gp.bucket_size)));
  VKC_TRY(deblock_->reserve(n, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks),
                            filter.passes));
  // A slot of its own: a frame recorded and unfinished may hold the other.
  core::Result<core::HostSlot> results =
      results_->claim(sizeof(detail::DecodeResults));
  VKC_CHECK(results.ok(),
            "Decoder::rebuild: no batch of this decoder is in flight, so a "
            "results slot is free");
  // One batch: the grid's blocks against the frame's -- a block the frame
  // lacks would be read as a neighbour -- then the inverse and the deblock
  // behind that gate, so nothing is written to a grid that fails it, and the
  // results.
  const detail::ResultSources words{
      &reader_->verdict(), &lists_->collision(),    &lists_->diff_counts(),
      &store_->faults(),   &transform_->rejected(), &deblock_->exact()};
  const detail::ResidentBlocks blocks = store_->reference_blocks();
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  VKC_TRY(transform_->record_steps(batch, header.params));
  VKC_TRY(
      lists_->record_diff(batch, grid, store_->reference_list(), n, &stage));
  VKC_TRY(gate_->record_gate(batch, words, detail::GateCheck{true, false, n, 0},
                             &stage));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::FrameSlices slices,
             gate_->record_slices(batch, n, &stage));
  VKC_TRY(transform_->record_inverse(batch, grid, blocks, header.params,
                                     slices.blocks, &stage));
  VKC_TRY(deblock_->record(batch, grid, blocks, filter.passes, slices.blocks,
                           slices.flags, &stage));
  VKC_TRY(gate_->record_results(batch, *results, words, &stage));
  VKC_TRY(batch.submit());
  const detail::DecodeResults r = read_results(*results);
  if (r.gate == 0) {
    return fail("the grid holds " + std::to_string(r.gone) +
                    " blocks the frame lacks and lacks " +
                    std::to_string(r.missing) +
                    " it holds; decode the frame into it instead",
                "rebuild");
  }
  VKC_TRY(detail::DctTransform::check_rejected("inverse", r.rejected, n));
  last_deblock_ = deblock_ran(filter.info, filter.runs(), n, r.exact);
  return {};
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "device_frame_reader.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

#include "rans_dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "rans_decode_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_slots_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_verdict_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "survivor_ranks_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// The kernels' workgroup widths; survivor_ranks.comp is one workgroup.
constexpr std::uint32_t kSlotsLanes = 256;
constexpr std::uint32_t kDecodeLanes = 1;
constexpr std::uint32_t kVerdictLanes = 64;

static_assert((kMaxFrameSegments - 1) << 2 < kNoVerdict - 3,
              "a failing segment's verdict word is below kNoVerdict");

constexpr VkDeviceSize kVerdictBytes = 2 * sizeof(std::uint32_t);

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameReader>> DeviceFrameReader::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "DeviceFrameReader::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameReader> owned(new DeviceFrameReader());
  DeviceFrameReader& r = *owned;
  r.device_ = &device;
  r.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(RansPush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(r.slots_kernel_, "codec_rans_slots", vgrid_rans_slots_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_rans_slots_comp_spv_size, 2, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(r.decode_kernel_, "codec_rans_decode",
                 vgrid_rans_decode_comp_spv, vgrid_rans_decode_comp_spv_size, 8,
                 &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(r.verdict_kernel_, "codec_rans_verdict",
                 vgrid_rans_verdict_comp_spv, vgrid_rans_verdict_comp_spv_size,
                 3, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(r.ranks_kernel_, "codec_survivor_ranks",
                 vgrid_survivor_ranks_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_survivor_ranks_comp_spv_size, 3, &push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(r.pool_, kb.build());
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  r.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  r.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  r.min_offset_alignment_ =
      std::max<VkDeviceSize>(props.limits.minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment, 4);
  // The verdict, and the ranks of a frame with no reference entries, which
  // even a frame of no segments hands the merge.
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(
      device, allocator, r.verdict_, kVerdictBytes, r.max_storage_buffer_range_,
      "codec.rans_verdict"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(
      device, allocator, r.ranks_, sizeof(std::uint32_t),
      r.max_storage_buffer_range_, "codec.survivor_ranks"));
  return owned;
}

core::Result<ResidentBlocks> DeviceFrameReader::record_decode(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const ParsedFrame& frame, VkBuffer input,
    VkDeviceSize input_bytes, VkDeviceSize payload_at,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  VKC_TRY(
      check_frame_type(frame.header.type, "DeviceFrameReader::record_decode"));
  const FrameType type = frame.header.type;
  const bool inter = type == FrameType::kInter;
  const std::uint32_t n = frame.header.block_count;
  const std::uint32_t k = frame.header.params.coefficient_count;
  const std::uint32_t r_size = frame.header.segment_size;
  // An intra frame is M = 0: its blocks are all new.
  const std::uint32_t m = inter ? frame.reference.header.block_count : 0;
  const std::uint32_t u_size = inter ? frame.update_size : 0;
  const std::uint32_t a = inter ? frame.new_count : n;
  const std::uint32_t entries = m + a;  // below 2^32 (parse_frame)
  const auto segments =
      static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frame.segment_lengths.size());
  // One invocation decodes a whole segment, so the rule parse_frame holds
  // the sizes to is what bounds it; checked again, as the type is, on a
  // caller's parsed frame.
  VKC_TRY(check_segment_size("DeviceFrameReader::record_decode", "segment size",
                             r_size));
  if (inter) {
    VKC_TRY(check_segment_size("DeviceFrameReader::record_decode",
                               "update size", u_size));
  }
  // The verdict reset, once nothing else can refuse the frame, which a frame
  // of no segments leaves as it is.
  auto reset = [&]() -> core::Status {
    VKC_TRY(batch.fill(verdict_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), kNoVerdict));
    VKC_TRY(
        batch.fill(verdict_, sizeof(std::uint32_t), sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u));
    return {};
  };
  ResidentBlocks out;
  out.coefficient_count = k;
  out.ranks = &ranks_;
  if (segments == 0) {
    VKC_TRY(reset());
    return out;
  }
  // The payload, bound from its offset aligned down to what a binding allows,
  // read from the byte after (pc.payload_byte), to the word its last byte is
  // in -- inside the record's slack.
  const VkDeviceSize bind_at = payload_at - payload_at % min_offset_alignment_;
  const VkDeviceSize payload_byte = payload_at - bind_at;
  const VkDeviceSize payload_bytes =
      (payload_byte + frame.payload_size + 3) & ~VkDeviceSize{3};
  if (payload_at > input_bytes || payload_bytes > input_bytes - bind_at) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "DeviceFrameReader::record_decode: the payload lies past the input");
  }

  // Every size first, so a frame the device cannot hold grows nothing.
  const std::vector<std::uint32_t> table_entries =
      rans_table_entries(frame.tables);
  const std::uint32_t models = frame_model_count(type, k);
  const VkDeviceSize entry_bytes = table_entries.size() * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize slot_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(models) * kRansScale * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize word_bytes =
      (VkDeviceSize(segments) + 1) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize list_bytes = VkDeviceSize(a) * sizeof(volume::BlockIndex);
  const VkDeviceSize mask_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(entries) * kMaskWordsPerBlock * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize coeff_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(entries) * coefficient_words(k) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize mode_bytes = VkDeviceSize(m) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize fault_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(segments) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize rank_bytes = (VkDeviceSize(m) + 1) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  struct Scratch {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const Scratch scratch[] = {
      {tables_, entry_bytes, "codec.rans_decode_tables"},
      {slots_, slot_bytes, "codec.rans_slots"},
      {segment_words_, word_bytes, "codec.rans_segment_words"},
      {list_, binding_range(list_bytes, sizeof(volume::BlockIndex)),
       "codec.rans_decode_list"},
      {masks_, mask_bytes, "codec.rans_decode_masks"},
      {coefficients_, coeff_bytes, "codec.rans_decode_coefficients"},
      {modes_, binding_range(mode_bytes, sizeof(std::uint32_t)),
       "codec.rans_decode_modes"},
      {faults_, fault_bytes, "codec.rans_faults"},
      {ranks_, rank_bytes, "codec.survivor_ranks"},
  };
  const VkDeviceSize range = max_storage_buffer_range_;
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("codec.decode_input", payload_bytes,
                                           range));
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(b.name, b.bytes, range));
  }
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, b.buffer,
                                        b.bytes, range, b.name));
  }
  // Each segment's first 16-bit word. The lengths sum to the payload, which
  // the range check above holds under 4 GiB, so every offset fits.
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> segment_words(std::size_t(segments) + 1, 0);
  for (std::uint32_t s = 0; s < segments; ++s) {
    segment_words[s + 1] = segment_words[s] + frame.segment_lengths[s] / 2;
  }
  VKC_TRY(reset());

  // Inline, as the decode's batch writes every update ahead of its first
  // dispatch.
  VKC_TRY(batch.upload(tables_, 0, table_entries.data(), entry_bytes));
  VKC_TRY(batch.upload(segment_words_, 0, segment_words.data(), word_bytes));

  slots_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(0, tables_.handle(), 0, entry_bytes);
  slots_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(1, slots_.handle(), 0, slot_bytes);
  core::ComputeKernel& decode = decode_kernel_;
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(0, slots_.handle(), 0, slot_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(1, input, bind_at, payload_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(2, segment_words_.handle(), 0, word_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(
      3, list_.handle(), 0,
      binding_range(list_bytes, sizeof(volume::BlockIndex)));
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(4, masks_.handle(), 0, mask_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(5, coefficients_.handle(), 0, coeff_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(6, faults_.handle(), 0, fault_bytes);
  decode.set.write_storage_buffer(
      7, modes_.handle(), 0, binding_range(mode_bytes, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  const core::DescriptorSet& verdict = verdict_kernel_.set;
  verdict.write_storage_buffer(0, faults_.handle(), 0, fault_bytes);
  verdict.write_storage_buffer(
      1, list_.handle(), 0,
      binding_range(list_bytes, sizeof(volume::BlockIndex)));
  verdict.write_storage_buffer(2, verdict_.handle(), 0, kVerdictBytes);
  const core::DescriptorSet& ranks = ranks_kernel_.set;
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(0, modes_.handle(), 0,
                             binding_range(mode_bytes, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(1, ranks_.handle(), 0, rank_bytes);
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(2, verdict_.handle(), 0, kVerdictBytes);

  RansPush push;
  push.num_entries = entries;
  push.coefficient_count = k;
  push.segment_size = r_size;
  push.segment_count = segments;
  push.frame_type = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(type);
  push.reference_count = m;
  push.update_size = u_size;
  push.payload_byte = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(payload_byte);
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, slots_kernel_, push,
                         std::uint64_t(models) * kRansScale, kSlotsLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, decode, push, segments, kDecodeLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, verdict_kernel_, push, segments, kVerdictLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch(ranks_kernel_, &push, sizeof(push), 1,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));

  out.list = &list_;
  out.masks = &masks_;
  out.coefficients = &coefficients_;
  out.modes = m != 0 ? &modes_ : nullptr;
  out.count = entries;
  out.reference_count = m;
  return out;
}

core::Status DeviceFrameReader::judge(FrameType type, std::uint32_t n,
                                      std::uint32_t a, std::uint32_t failed,
                                      std::uint32_t survivors) {
  if (failed != kNoVerdict) {
    VKC_TRY(check_segment(failed >> 2, static_cast<SegmentFault>(failed & 3u)));
  }
  if (type != FrameType::kInter) return {};
  return check_survivors(survivors, n, a);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
