### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/device_frame_reader.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file device_frame_reader.hpp
/// @brief Decodes a frame's segments on the device, intra or P: the
///        `Decoder`'s only reader, whose entries the tests' CPU oracle pins.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). The host parses the frame
/// (@ref parse_frame) in the decoder's input slot and uploads only its
/// tables and segment words; the payload is read where the slot holds it.
/// The decoded entries and the verdict stay in device memory, where the
/// decoder's merge, its gate and the inverse transform read them. Every bulk
/// buffer is device-local and retained between frames
/// (`ensure_device_scratch`).

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// The verdict word with no failing segment: a failing one is `s << 2 |
/// kind`, kind 1 to 3, and s below @ref kMaxFrameSegments, so it is never
/// this. The decoder's gate (`frame_gate.comp`) mirrors it.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kNoVerdict = ~0u;

/// @brief Decodes frames on the device: one invocation per segment, as the
///        2026-09-27 format allows.
///
/// Recorded into the decode's batch: the tables go up and are expanded on the
/// device into each model's slot lookup, each segment decodes its entries
/// from the record where the input slot holds it into the inverse
/// transform's layout at their stream positions (@ref ResidentBlocks), the
/// segments are judged (`rans_verdict.comp`: the first that failed, its fault
/// or its order against the segment before), and the survivor ranks are
/// scanned (`survivor_ranks.comp`). The verdict -- the first failing segment
/// and the survivor count -- stays in @ref verdict, which the decoder's gate
/// and its results read; @ref judge words it. A skip or remove entry's
/// payload is left as it was: nothing reads it.
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one frame at a time.
class VGRID_CODEC_API DeviceFrameReader {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the four kernels.
  /// @return The reader, or a pipeline or pool failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameReader>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~DeviceFrameReader() = default;
  DeviceFrameReader(const DeviceFrameReader&) = delete;
  DeviceFrameReader& operator=(const DeviceFrameReader&) = delete;

  /// @brief Record the decode of @p frame's segments, and its verdict, into
  ///        @p batch.
  /// @param batch       The batch to record into; submitted by the caller.
  /// @param frame       Parsed from the bytes @p input holds on the device.
  /// @param input       The record and its slack (`CommandBatch::input`).
  /// @param input_bytes Its bytes bound, the slack included.
  /// @param payload_at  The payload's first byte in @p input.
  /// @param stage       Optional scope the dispatches record into.
  /// @return The decoded entries where the device holds them, with the
  ///         survivor ranks, valid until the next call (no entries for a
  ///         frame of no segments, which records only the verdict's reset);
  ///         `Status::Code::Unsupported`, recording nothing, for a
  ///         type it does not decode (@ref check_frame_type);
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument`, before any buffer grows, for a
  ///         size @ref check_segment_size refuses, a payload past
  ///         @p input_bytes, or a buffer past `maxStorageBufferRange`;
  ///         otherwise a buffer failure.
  core::Result<ResidentBlocks> record_decode(
      core::CommandBatch& batch, const ParsedFrame& frame, VkBuffer input,
      VkDeviceSize input_bytes, VkDeviceSize payload_at,
      core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @return The verdict the last recorded decode leaves once its batch has
  ///         run: the first failing segment as `s << 2 | kind`
  ///         (@ref kNoVerdict for none), then the survivor count, a u32 each.
  const core::Buffer& verdict() const noexcept { return verdict_; }

  /// @return The refusal a frame of @p type, @p n blocks and @p a new ones
  ///         earns for verdict words @p failed and @p survivors: the first
  ///         segment that failed (@ref check_segment) and, for a P-frame,
  ///         its survivors (@ref check_survivors); or OK.
  static core::Status judge(FrameType type, std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t a,
                            std::uint32_t failed, std::uint32_t survivors);

 private:
  DeviceFrameReader() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize min_offset_alignment_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel slots_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel decode_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel verdict_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel ranks_kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;

  // Device-local, retained and grown by ensure_device_scratch.
  core::Buffer tables_;         // per model, per symbol: cum | freq << 16
  core::Buffer slots_;          // per model, per slot: rans_slots.comp's entry
  core::Buffer segment_words_;  // each segment's first 16-bit word, count + 1
  core::Buffer list_;           // volume::BlockIndex a new block
  core::Buffer masks_;          // kMaskWordsPerBlock words an entry
  core::Buffer coefficients_;   // coefficient_words(K) words an entry
  core::Buffer modes_;          // a u32 a reference entry
  core::Buffer faults_;         // a SegmentFault a segment
  core::Buffer ranks_;          // M + 1 u32: the survivors before each entry
  core::Buffer verdict_;        // the first failing segment, the survivors
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/device_frame_writer.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "device_frame_writer.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <string>
#include <utility>

#include "rans_dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "encode_results_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_count_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_encode_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_gather_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_ops_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "rans_scan_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// The kernels' workgroup widths.
constexpr std::uint32_t kCountLanes = 64;
constexpr std::uint32_t kOpsLanes = 64;
constexpr std::uint32_t kEncodeLanes = 32;

// The copied payload's prediction before any frame of a type: about three
// times what room0 codes in an intra frame.
constexpr std::uint64_t kFirstPayloadPerEntry = 32;

constexpr VkDeviceSize kWordBytes = sizeof(std::uint32_t);

// Mirrors `Push` in encode_results.comp.
struct ResultsPush {
  std::uint32_t count_words = 0;
  std::uint32_t has_transform = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(ResultsPush) == 8, "ResultsPush must be 8 bytes");

// The walk's bindings (rans_walk.glsl), which the count and coder-step
// kernels share. A side the entries lack -- new blocks, or reference entries
// and their modes -- binds the masks, which it never reads.
void bind_walk(core::ComputeKernel& kernel, const ResidentBlocks& blocks) {
  const VkDeviceSize entries = blocks.count;
  const VkDeviceSize m = blocks.reference_count;
  const VkDeviceSize mask_bytes =
      entries * kMaskWordsPerBlock * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const core::Buffer* list = entries > m ? blocks.list : blocks.masks;
  const core::Buffer* modes = m != 0 ? blocks.modes : blocks.masks;
  kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(
      0, list->handle(), 0,
      binding_range((entries - m) * sizeof(volume::BlockIndex),
                    sizeof(volume::BlockIndex)));
  kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(1, blocks.masks->handle(), 0, mask_bytes);
  kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(
      2, blocks.coefficients->handle(), 0,
      entries * coefficient_words(blocks.coefficient_count) *
          sizeof(std::uint32_t));
  kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(
      3, modes->handle(), 0,
      binding_range(m * sizeof(std::uint32_t), sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
}

// The walk's push constants, for a frame of @p segments.
RansPush walk_push(const ResidentBlocks& blocks, std::uint32_t segment_size,
                   std::uint32_t update_size, std::uint64_t segments) {
  RansPush push;
  push.num_entries = blocks.count;
  push.coefficient_count = blocks.coefficient_count;
  push.segment_size = segment_size;
  push.segment_count = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(segments);
  push.reference_count = blocks.reference_count;
  push.update_size = update_size;
  return push;
}

core::Status fail(const char* op, const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string("DeviceFrameWriter::") +
                                        op + ": " + why);
}

// The symbol counts' words at @p k: a P-frame's layout, whose mode model
// comes last, so an intra frame's are its prefix.
std::uint32_t count_words(std::uint32_t k) {
  return frame_model_base(frame_model_count(FrameType::kInter, k), k);
}

// A ring of two slots of @p bytes, made at first use.
core::Status ensure_ring(std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing>& ring,
                         const core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
                         VkDeviceSize bytes, const char* name) {
  if (ring != nullptr) return {};
  core::HostRingDesc desc;
  desc.slot_bytes = bytes;
  desc.name = name;
  VKC_ASSIGN(ring, core::HostRing::create(device, allocator, desc));
  return {};
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameWriter>> DeviceFrameWriter::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "DeviceFrameWriter::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameWriter> owned(new DeviceFrameWriter());
  DeviceFrameWriter& w = *owned;
  w.device_ = &device;
  w.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(RansPush);
  VkPushConstantRange results_push = push;
  results_push.size = sizeof(ResultsPush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.count_kernel_, "codec_rans_count", vgrid_rans_count_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_rans_count_comp_spv_size, 8, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.ops_kernel_, "codec_rans_ops", vgrid_rans_ops_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_rans_ops_comp_spv_size, 7, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.encode_kernel_, "codec_rans_encode",
                 vgrid_rans_encode_comp_spv, vgrid_rans_encode_comp_spv_size, 6,
                 &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.scan_kernel_, "codec_rans_scan", vgrid_rans_scan_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_rans_scan_comp_spv_size, 5, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.gather_kernel_, "codec_rans_gather",
                 vgrid_rans_gather_comp_spv, vgrid_rans_gather_comp_spv_size, 5,
                 &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(w.results_kernel_, "codec_encode_results",
                 vgrid_encode_results_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_encode_results_comp_spv_size, 7, &results_push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(w.pool_, kb.build());
  VKC_ASSIGN(w.layout_, StepLayout::create(device, allocator));
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  w.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  w.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  struct Word {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const Word words[] = {
      {w.failed_, kWordBytes, "codec.rans_failed"},
      {w.refusal_, 2 * kWordBytes, "codec.rans_refusal"},
      {w.frame_words_, StepLayout::kFrameWordsBytes, "codec.rans_frame_words"},
  };
  for (const Word& word : words) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(word.buffer, core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, word.bytes));
    device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                           core::debug_object_handle(word.buffer.handle()),
                           word.name);
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(w.gather_args_, core::device_storage_buffer(
                                 allocator, sizeof(VkDispatchIndirectCommand),
                                 VK_BUFFER_USAGE_INDIRECT_BUFFER_BIT));
  device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                         core::debug_object_handle(w.gather_args_.handle()),
                         "codec.rans_gather_args");
  return owned;
}

core::Status DeviceFrameWriter::record_count(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const ResidentBlocks& blocks,
    std::uint32_t segment_size, std::uint32_t update_size,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage, const volume::DeviceCount* frame_blocks,
    const TransformWords& transform) {
  const std::uint32_t entries = blocks.count;
  const std::uint32_t m = blocks.reference_count;
  const std::uint32_t k = blocks.coefficient_count;
  VKC_TRY(check_segment_size("DeviceFrameWriter::record_count", "segment_size",
                             segment_size));
  if (m > entries) {
    return fail("record_count", std::to_string(m) +
                                    " reference entries, more than the " +
                                    std::to_string(entries) + " entries");
  }
  if (m != 0) {
    VKC_TRY(check_segment_size("DeviceFrameWriter::record_count", "update_size",
                               update_size));
  }
  if (entries != 0 &&
      (blocks.masks == nullptr || blocks.coefficients == nullptr ||
       (entries > m && blocks.list == nullptr) ||
       (m != 0 && blocks.modes == nullptr) ||
       (blocks.bounded && blocks.ranks == nullptr))) {
    return fail("record_count", "the entries lack a buffer they need");
  }
  if (frame_blocks != nullptr &&
      (frame_blocks->buffer == nullptr || !frame_blocks->buffer->valid() ||
       frame_blocks->offset % kWordBytes != 0 ||
       frame_blocks->buffer->size() < frame_blocks->offset + kWordBytes ||
       frame_blocks->bound != entries - m)) {
    return fail("record_count",
                "the frame's blocks word is missing, misaligned, past its "
                "buffer, or bounds other than the entries' blocks");
  }
  if ((transform.observed != nullptr &&
       transform.observed->size() < 2 * kWordBytes) ||
      (transform.rejected != nullptr &&
       transform.rejected->size() < kWordBytes) ||
      ((transform.observed == nullptr) != (transform.rejected == nullptr))) {
    return fail("record_count", "the transform's words are missing a word");
  }
  // The bound's, which the frame's never exceed.
  const std::uint64_t segments = frame_segment_count(m, update_size) +
                                 frame_segment_count(entries - m, segment_size);
  if (segments > kMaxFrameSegments) {
    return fail("record_count", "more than 2^30 - 1 segments");
  }
  const std::uint32_t words = count_words(k);
  const VkDeviceSize range = max_storage_buffer_range_;
  const VkDeviceSize count_bytes = VkDeviceSize(words) * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize step_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(std::max(entries, 1u)) * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize results_bytes = sizeof(FrontResults) + count_bytes;
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, counts_,
                                      count_bytes, range, "codec.rans_counts"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, entry_steps_,
                                      step_bytes, range,
                                      "codec.rans_entry_steps"));
  VKC_TRY(ensure_ring(front_ring_, *device_, *allocator_, results_bytes,
                      "codec.encode_front_results"));
  // A superseded frame's slots go first, so a free one is there to claim.
  drop();
  VKC_ASSIGN(front_slot_, front_ring_->claim(results_bytes));
  segment_size_ = segment_size;
  update_size_ = update_size;
  entry_count_ = entries;
  reference_count_ = m;
  coefficient_count_ = k;
  bounded_ = blocks.bounded;

  VKC_TRY(batch.zero(counts_, 0, count_bytes));
  VKC_TRY(batch.zero(refusal_, 0, 2 * kWordBytes));
  // The frame words the count and the layout take N from: the surplus, a
  // bounded frame's survivors, which its bound counts twice -- copied, since
  // binding the ranks at word M would break minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment
  // -- else 0; then the frame's blocks, a kernel's word or every block.
  VKC_TRY(blocks.bounded
              ? batch.copy(*blocks.ranks, VkDeviceSize(m) * kWordBytes,
                           frame_words_, 0, kWordBytes)
              : batch.zero(frame_words_, 0, kWordBytes));
  VKC_TRY(frame_blocks != nullptr
              ? batch.copy(*frame_blocks->buffer, frame_blocks->offset,
                           frame_words_, kWordBytes, kWordBytes)
              : batch.fill(frame_words_, kWordBytes, kWordBytes, entries - m));
  if (entries != 0) {
    core::ComputeKernel& kernel = count_kernel_;
    bind_walk(kernel, blocks);
    kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(4, counts_.handle(), 0, count_bytes);
    kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(5, entry_steps_.handle(), 0, step_bytes);
    kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(6, refusal_.handle(), 0, 2 * kWordBytes);
    kernel.set.write_storage_buffer(7, frame_words_.handle(), 0,
                                    StepLayout::kFrameWordsBytes);
    RansPush push = walk_push(blocks, segment_size, update_size, segments);
    VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, kernel, push, entries, kCountLanes,
                           max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  }
  VKC_TRY(layout_->record(batch, entry_steps_, frame_words_, entries, m,
                          update_size, segment_size, stage));

  // Then everything the host builds the frame from, into the results slot.
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer results,
             batch.output(front_slot_, 0, results_bytes));
  core::ComputeKernel& gather = results_kernel_;
  const bool has_transform = transform.observed != nullptr;
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(
      0, has_transform ? transform.observed->handle() : refusal_.handle(), 0,
      2 * kWordBytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(
      1, has_transform ? transform.rejected->handle() : refusal_.handle(), 0,
      kWordBytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(2, refusal_.handle(), 0, 2 * kWordBytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(3, frame_words_.handle(), 0,
                                  StepLayout::kFrameWordsBytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(4, layout_->totals().handle(), 0,
                                  sizeof(StepLayout::Totals));
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(5, counts_.handle(), 0, count_bytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(6, results, 0, results_bytes);
  const ResultsPush push{words, has_transform ? 1u : 0u};
  return batch.dispatch(gather, &push, sizeof(push), 1, max_workgroup_count_x_,
                        stage);
}

FrontResults DeviceFrameWriter::front() const noexcept {
  FrontResults r;
  if (front_slot_.valid()) std::memcpy(&r, front_slot_.data(), sizeof(r));
  return r;
}

core::Status DeviceFrameWriter::record_code(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                            const ResidentBlocks& counted,
                                            float voxel_size, float trunc_dist,
                                            const CodecParams& params,
                                            const FrameReference* reference,
                                            core::StageMetrics* metrics,
                                            core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  // Every writer's refusals in their order: the coding parameters first.
  VKC_TRY(check_coding(voxel_size, trunc_dist, params));
  const std::uint32_t m = counted.reference_count;
  const std::uint32_t k = params.coefficient_count;
  const std::uint32_t segment_size = segment_size_;
  const std::uint32_t update_size = update_size_;
  if (segment_size == 0 || coded_ || !front_slot_.valid() ||
      k != counted.coefficient_count || k != coefficient_count_ ||
      counted.count != entry_count_ || m != reference_count_ ||
      counted.bounded != bounded_) {
    return fail("record_code",
                "these blocks were not the ones record_count saw");
  }
  const FrontResults r = front();
  // The frame's entries: its reference entries and its blocks, less a
  // bounded frame's survivors, which the device took off as it counted; at
  // most M, and at most its blocks.
  const std::uint32_t bound_blocks = counted.count - m;
  if (r.blocks > bound_blocks) {
    return fail("record_code", "the frame's " + std::to_string(r.blocks) +
                                   " blocks are past its bound of " +
                                   std::to_string(bound_blocks));
  }
  if (r.surplus > std::min(m, r.blocks)) {
    return fail("record_code", std::to_string(r.surplus) + " survivors of " +
                                   std::to_string(m) +
                                   " reference entries and " +
                                   std::to_string(r.blocks) + " blocks");
  }
  ResidentBlocks blocks = counted;
  blocks.count = m + r.blocks - r.surplus;
  blocks.bounded = false;
  const std::uint32_t entries = blocks.count;
  const std::uint32_t a = entries - m;
  const FrameType type =
      reference != nullptr ? FrameType::kInter : FrameType::kIntra;
  const std::uint32_t held =
      reference != nullptr ? reference->header.block_count : 0;
  if (m != held) {
    return fail("record_code", "expected " + std::to_string(held) +
                                   " reference entries, one per reference "
                                   "block, got " +
                                   std::to_string(m));
  }
  // The counts, at frame_model_base in a P-frame's layout.
  const std::uint32_t words = count_words(k);
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> counts(words);
  std::memcpy(counts.data(), front_slot_.data() + sizeof(FrontResults),
              VkDeviceSize(words) * kWordBytes);
  // The last refusals, from what the count found. The mode model
  // follows an intra frame's last (frame_models.glsl).
  const std::uint32_t modes =
      frame_model_base(frame_model_count(FrameType::kIntra, k), k);
  VKC_TRY(check_entries(
      r.largest_mode,
      counts[modes + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(BlockMode::kMotion)] != 0,
      r.out_of_range != 0));
  const auto segments =
      static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frame_segment_count(m, update_size) +
                                 frame_segment_count(a, segment_size));

  // The tables, from the device's counts through the one normalization.
  CodedFrame coded;
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> table_entries;
  {
    const core::StageScope tables(metrics, "  ..tables");
    const std::uint32_t models = frame_model_count(type, k);
    std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> per_model(models);
    for (std::uint32_t model = 0; model < models; ++model) {
      per_model[model].assign(counts.begin() + frame_model_base(model, k),
                              counts.begin() + frame_model_base(model + 1, k));
    }
    coded.tables = frame_tables(per_model);
    // Each symbol's coder step; frequency 0 for one never counted, which
    // the encoder refuses.
    table_entries = rans_table_entries(coded.tables);
  }
  // The survivors: every reference entry but a removed one, motion refused.
  std::uint64_t survivors = 0;
  for (BlockMode mode :
       {BlockMode::kKeep, BlockMode::kSkip, BlockMode::kZero}) {
    survivors += counts[modes + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(mode)];
  }
  coded.voxel_size = voxel_size;
  coded.trunc_dist = trunc_dist;
  coded.params = params;
  coded.block_count = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(survivors + a);
  coded.segment_size = segment_size;
  if (reference != nullptr) {
    coded.reference = *reference;
    coded.update_size = update_size;
    coded.new_count = a;
  }
  frame_ = std::move(coded);
  type_ = type;
  entries_ = entries;
  segments_ = segments;
  if (entries == 0) {
    front_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
    coded_ = true;
    return {};
  }

  // The layout record_count made, sized from its totals, which stop where
  // these refuse.
  const std::uint64_t step_total = r.step_total;
  const std::uint64_t slot_words16 = r.slot_total;
  if (step_total * 4 > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max() ||
      slot_words16 * 2 > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
    return fail("record_code", "the coded segments could outgrow 4 GiB");
  }

  const VkDeviceSize range = max_storage_buffer_range_;
  const VkDeviceSize entry_bytes = table_entries.size() * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize start_bytes = (VkDeviceSize(entries) + 1) * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize offset_bytes = (VkDeviceSize(segments) + 1) * kWordBytes;
  // Every slot's words, and the payload's binding, whole words.
  const VkDeviceSize slot_bytes = (slot_words16 * 2 + 3) & ~VkDeviceSize{3};
  const VkDeviceSize step_bytes = step_total * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize length_bytes = VkDeviceSize(segments) * kWordBytes;
  const VkDeviceSize back_bytes = sizeof(BackResults) + length_bytes;
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, tables_,
                                      entry_bytes, range, "codec.rans_tables"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, steps_, step_bytes,
                                      range, "codec.rans_steps"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, slots_, slot_bytes,
                                      range, "codec.rans_slots"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, lengths_,
                                      length_bytes, range,
                                      "codec.rans_lengths"));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, payload_offsets_,
                                      offset_bytes, range,
                                      "codec.rans_payload_offsets"));
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("codec.encode_payload", slot_bytes,
                                           range));
  VKC_TRY(ensure_ring(back_ring_, *device_, *allocator_, back_bytes,
                      "codec.encode_back_results"));
  VKC_TRY(ensure_ring(payload_ring_, *device_, *allocator_, slot_bytes,
                      "codec.encode_payload"));
  // Keep failed attempts from holding a slot the next attempt needs, even
  // when the caller still holds the preceding EncodedFrame's payload.
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::HostSlot back_slot, back_ring_->claim(back_bytes));
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::HostSlot payload_slot, payload_ring_->claim(slot_bytes));
  slot_bytes_ = slot_bytes;
  // In place the device writes the slot itself; copied, the batch copies the
  // payload's likely size, the last frame of its type's bytes per entry plus
  // 25%, and finish any rest.
  const std::uint32_t per_entry = payload_per_entry_[static_cast<int>(type)];
  copied_ = payload_ring_->in_place()
                ? slot_bytes
                : std::min<VkDeviceSize>(
                      slot_bytes,
                      ((per_entry != 0 ? per_entry : kFirstPayloadPerEntry) *
                           entries +
                       3) &
                          ~VkDeviceSize{3});

  // The tables first, inline, ahead of the batch's first dispatch.
  VKC_TRY(batch.upload(tables_, 0, table_entries.data(), entry_bytes));
  VKC_TRY(batch.zero(failed_, 0, kWordBytes));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer back_results,
             batch.output(back_slot, 0, back_bytes));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer payload, batch.output(payload_slot, 0, copied_));

  const core::Buffer& starts = layout_->starts();
  const core::Buffer& slot_offsets = layout_->slot_offsets();
  core::ComputeKernel& ops = ops_kernel_;
  bind_walk(ops, blocks);
  ops.set.write_storage_buffer(4, tables_.handle(), 0, entry_bytes);
  ops.set.write_storage_buffer(5, starts.handle(), 0, start_bytes);
  ops.set.write_storage_buffer(6, steps_.handle(), 0, step_bytes);
  core::ComputeKernel& encode = encode_kernel_;
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(0, steps_.handle(), 0, step_bytes);
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(1, starts.handle(), 0, start_bytes);
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(2, slot_offsets.handle(), 0, offset_bytes);
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(3, slots_.handle(), 0, slot_bytes);
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(4, lengths_.handle(), 0, length_bytes);
  encode.set.write_storage_buffer(5, failed_.handle(), 0, kWordBytes);
  scan_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(0, lengths_.handle(), 0, length_bytes);
  scan_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(1, payload_offsets_.handle(), 0,
                                        offset_bytes);
  scan_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(2, gather_args_.handle(), 0,
                                        sizeof(VkDispatchIndirectCommand));
  scan_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(3, failed_.handle(), 0, kWordBytes);
  scan_kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(4, back_results, 0, back_bytes);
  core::ComputeKernel& gather = gather_kernel_;
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(0, slot_offsets.handle(), 0, offset_bytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(1, slots_.handle(), 0, slot_bytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(2, lengths_.handle(), 0, length_bytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(3, payload_offsets_.handle(), 0,
                                  offset_bytes);
  gather.set.write_storage_buffer(4, payload, 0, slot_bytes);

  RansPush push = walk_push(blocks, segment_size, update_size, segments);
  push.frame_type = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(type);
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, ops, push, entries, kOpsLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, encode, push, segments, kEncodeLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch(scan_kernel_, &push, sizeof(push), 1,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch_indirect(gather, &push, sizeof(push), gather_args_, 0,
                                  stage));
  back_slot_ = std::move(back_slot);
  payload_slot_ = std::move(payload_slot);
  // Until recording succeeds, record_back must still see the front's real
  // counts on retry, never front()'s default-zero result for a missing slot.
  front_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  coded_ = true;
  return {};
}

core::Status DeviceFrameWriter::record_none(float voxel_size, float trunc_dist,
                                            const CodecParams& params) {
  VKC_TRY(check_coding(voxel_size, trunc_dist, params));
  if (segment_size_ == 0 || coded_) {
    return fail("record_none", "no frame was counted (record_count)");
  }
  // An intra frame's tables of no symbols, as a count of nothing gives.
  const std::uint32_t k = params.coefficient_count;
  const std::uint32_t models = frame_model_count(FrameType::kIntra, k);
  std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> none(models);
  for (std::uint32_t model = 0; model < models; ++model) {
    none[model].assign(
        frame_model_base(model + 1, k) - frame_model_base(model, k), 0);
  }
  CodedFrame coded;
  coded.voxel_size = voxel_size;
  coded.trunc_dist = trunc_dist;
  coded.params = params;
  coded.segment_size = segment_size_;
  coded.tables = frame_tables(none);
  front_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  frame_ = std::move(coded);
  type_ = FrameType::kIntra;
  entries_ = 0;
  segments_ = 0;
  coded_ = true;
  return {};
}

core::Result<EncodedFrame> DeviceFrameWriter::finish(
    core::StageMetrics* metrics, core::GpuTimer& timer) {
  if (!coded_) {
    return fail("finish", "no frame was coded (record_code)");
  }
  coded_ = false;
  segment_size_ = 0;
  EncodedFrame out;
  out.type = type_;
  out.blocks = frame_.block_count;
  if (entries_ == 0) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(out.head, assemble_head(type_, frame_, 0));
    return out;
  }
  BackResults r;
  std::memcpy(&r, back_slot_.data(), sizeof(r));
  if (r.failed != 0) {
    drop();
    return core::Status::io_error(
        "DeviceFrameWriter::finish: a table refused a symbol it was counted "
        "from, or a segment outgrew its slot");
  }
  if (r.total > slot_bytes_) {
    drop();
    return core::Status::io_error(
        "DeviceFrameWriter::finish: the segments outgrew their slots");
  }
  frame_.segment_lengths.resize(segments_);
  std::memcpy(frame_.segment_lengths.data(),
              back_slot_.data() + sizeof(BackResults),
              VkDeviceSize(segments_) * kWordBytes);
  back_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  const VkDeviceSize whole = (VkDeviceSize(r.total) + 3) & ~VkDeviceSize{3};
  if (whole > copied_) {
    // Past what the batch copied: the gather again over the rest, into an
    // output range of its own, which the test policy poisons first.
    core::GpuStageScope tail(metrics, timer, "  ..tail");
    core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
    const core::Status ran = [&]() -> core::Status {
      VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer payload,
                 batch.output(payload_slot_, copied_, whole - copied_));
      core::ComputeKernel& gather = gather_kernel_;
      gather.set.write_storage_buffer(
          0, layout_->slot_offsets().handle(), 0,
          (VkDeviceSize(segments_) + 1) * kWordBytes);
      gather.set.write_storage_buffer(1, slots_.handle(), 0, slot_bytes_);
      gather.set.write_storage_buffer(2, lengths_.handle(), 0,
                                      VkDeviceSize(segments_) * kWordBytes);
      gather.set.write_storage_buffer(
          3, payload_offsets_.handle(), 0,
          (VkDeviceSize(segments_) + 1) * kWordBytes);
      gather.set.write_storage_buffer(4, payload, 0, slot_bytes_);
      RansPush push;
      push.segment_count = segments_;
      push.payload_byte = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(copied_);
      VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch_indirect(gather, &push, sizeof(push), gather_args_,
                                      0, &tail));
      return batch.submit();
    }();
    if (!ran.ok()) {
      drop();
      return ran;
    }
  }
  std::uint32_t& per_entry = payload_per_entry_[static_cast<int>(type_)];
  per_entry =
      static_cast<std::uint32_t>((r.total + r.total / 4) / entries_ + 1);
  core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> head =
      assemble_head(type_, frame_, r.total);
  if (!head.ok()) {
    drop();
    return head.status();
  }
  out.head = std::move(head).value();
  out.payload = payload_slot_.data();
  out.payload_size = r.total;
  out.slot = std::move(payload_slot_);
  payload_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  return out;
}

void DeviceFrameWriter::drop() noexcept {
  front_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  back_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  payload_slot_ = core::HostSlot{};
  coded_ = false;
  segment_size_ = 0;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/device_frame_writer.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file device_frame_writer.hpp
/// @brief Writes a frame, intra or P, with its rANS coding on the device:
///        the `Encoder`'s only writer, whose bytes the tests' CPU oracle
///        pins.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). The forward output stays in device
/// memory: the host learns only the symbol counts, to build the frame's
/// tables (@ref frame_tables), the step layout's two totals, the frame's
/// block and survivor counts, and the coded segments, each batch's in one
/// results slot it binds (`core::HostRing`). Every bulk buffer is
/// device-local and retained between frames (`ensure_device_scratch`).

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "step_layout.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/gpu_timer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/host_ring.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/encoder.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_hash_map.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// @brief What the front batch's last command gathers into its results slot
///        (`encode_results.comp`), before the symbol counts.
struct FrontResults {
  /// The transform's: entries its observed pass and its forward found no
  /// block for; 0 when the count was given none (@ref TransformWords).
  std::uint32_t observed_rejected = 0;
  std::uint32_t forward_rejected = 0;
  /// What @ref check_entries refuses: the largest mode past the alphabet,
  /// and whether a written value is -32768.
  std::uint32_t largest_mode = 0;
  std::uint32_t out_of_range = 0;
  /// The frame words as counted (`counted_entries`): the survivors a bounded
  /// P-frame's bound counts twice, and the frame's blocks.
  std::uint32_t surplus = 0;
  std::uint32_t blocks = 0;
  /// The step layout's totals (@ref StepLayout::Totals).
  std::uint32_t step_total = 0;
  std::uint32_t slot_total = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(FrontResults) == 32,
              "FrontResults mirrors encode_results.comp's struct");

/// @brief What the back batch leaves in its results slot (`rans_scan.comp`),
///        before each segment's length.
struct BackResults {
  std::uint32_t failed = 0;  ///< Nonzero when a table refused a symbol.
  std::uint32_t total = 0;   ///< The payload's bytes.
};
static_assert(sizeof(BackResults) == 8,
              "BackResults mirrors rans_scan.comp's struct");

/// @brief The transform's words a front gathers into its results, beside
///        the writer's own: the encoder's observed pass's and forward's
///        reject counts (@ref DctTransform::observed_counts,
///        @ref DctTransform::rejected).
struct TransformWords {
  const core::Buffer* observed = nullptr;  ///< Two u32: rejected, observed.
  const core::Buffer* rejected = nullptr;  ///< One u32.
};

/// @brief Codes frames on the device (the 2026-09-26 decision's fifth PR):
///        one invocation per segment, as the 2026-09-27 format allows.
///
/// A frame takes two batches, the caller's. The first carries the forward
/// transform (@ref DctTransform::record_forward) and @ref record_count, which
/// counts every model's symbols, each entry's coder steps, and what
/// @ref check_entries refuses, lays the steps out (@ref StepLayout) and
/// gathers what the host needs into a results slot. Once it has resolved,
/// @ref record_code makes those refusals, builds the tables on the host,
/// sizes the coding from the layout's totals and records it into the second:
/// the device writes each entry's steps in parallel, runs each segment's
/// serial rANS chain over its run of them into a slot sized by its steps,
/// and packs the streams into a payload slot, in place, or with the
/// payload's likely size copied (the last frame of its type's bytes per
/// entry plus 25%). @ref finish gathers any rest in a batch of its own (a
/// tail) and lays the frame out.
///
/// The entries' count may be a bound whose frame the device alone knows
/// (the encoder's forward): its blocks are a word a kernel wrote. A
/// P-frame's entries are its stream positions (@ref ResidentBlocks): each
/// reference entry's mode and payload, which the caller has made against the
/// reference (a keep entry's XOR mask and residuals), then its new blocks.
/// Over the bounded entries @ref ReferenceStore::record_diff returns, the
/// count and the layout take the survivors off on the device, and
/// @ref record_code takes them off on the host from the front's results.
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one frame at a time.
class VGRID_CODEC_API DeviceFrameWriter {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the six kernels and the step layout's.
  /// @return The writer, or a pipeline or pool failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<DeviceFrameWriter>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~DeviceFrameWriter() = default;
  DeviceFrameWriter(const DeviceFrameWriter&) = delete;
  DeviceFrameWriter& operator=(const DeviceFrameWriter&) = delete;

  /// @brief Record the counting pass over @p blocks, the layout of the steps
  ///        it counts, and the gathering of the front's results into a slot,
  ///        into @p batch.
  ///
  /// @p blocks must stay unchanged until @ref record_code. Supersedes an
  /// unfinished frame.
  /// @param blocks        The entries: the forward output, or a P-frame's
  ///                      stream positions, the new blocks' coordinates
  ///                      strictly increasing in frame order; or the
  ///                      bounded entries of a P-frame's diff, whose ranks
  ///                      the count reads its surplus from.
  /// @param segment_size  Blocks per segment: a P-frame's new blocks per
  ///                      segment.
  /// @param update_size   A P-frame's reference entries per update segment,
  ///                      read only when @p blocks holds reference entries.
  /// @param stage         Optional scope the dispatches' device spans record
  ///                      into.
  /// @param frame_blocks  Optional: the frame's blocks, a word a kernel
  ///                      wrote, at most its bound, the entries' blocks
  ///                      (`count` less M); null takes them all.
  /// @param transform     The transform's words to gather; none reads 0.
  /// @return OK, or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a size
  ///         @ref check_segment_size refuses, more reference entries than
  ///         entries, a buffer the entries need missing (a bounded set's
  ///         ranks among them), a @p frame_blocks word missing, misaligned,
  ///         past its buffer or bounding other than the entries' blocks,
  ///         more than 2^30 - 1 segments, or a buffer past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`; otherwise a buffer failure.
  core::Status record_count(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                            const ResidentBlocks& blocks,
                            std::uint32_t segment_size,
                            std::uint32_t update_size,
                            core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr,
                            const volume::DeviceCount* frame_blocks = nullptr,
                            const TransformWords& transform = {});

  /// @return The front's results once its batch resolved, from the slot
  ///         @ref record_count gathered them into; zeros before one.
  FrontResults front() const noexcept;

  /// @brief Once the batch @ref record_count recorded into has resolved:
  ///        make the frame's refusals, build its tables, and record the
  ///        coding of the frame it counted into @p batch, at the sizes it
  ///        counted with.
  ///
  /// The tables are recorded first, inline, so MoltenVK opens no blit
  /// encoder mid-batch. Records nothing for a frame of no entries.
  /// @param counted     The same entries @ref record_count was given.
  /// @param voxel_size  The grid's voxel edge, metres.
  /// @param trunc_dist  The grid's `trunc_dist`, which the coefficients are
  ///                    fractions of.
  /// @param params      The params the coefficients were made with.
  /// @param reference   A P-frame's reference, whose block count is the
  ///                    blocks' reference entries; null for an intra frame.
  /// @param metrics     Optional: the tables' `"  ..tables"`, host only.
  /// @param stage       Optional scope the dispatches' device spans record
  ///                    into.
  /// @return OK; @ref check_coding's refusals, then @ref check_entries';
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for blocks @ref record_count
  ///         did not count, a frame word past its bound or a survivor count
  ///         past the reference entries or the blocks (a bug, never a
  ///         frame's), a reference whose block count is not the blocks'
  ///         reference entries, or coded segments that could outgrow 4 GiB;
  ///         or a buffer failure.
  core::Status record_code(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                           const ResidentBlocks& counted, float voxel_size,
                           float trunc_dist, const CodecParams& params,
                           const FrameReference* reference,
                           core::StageMetrics* metrics = nullptr,
                           core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Code, in place of what @ref record_count counted, an I-frame of
  ///        no blocks: what the encoder makes of a frame whose front found
  ///        none, a planned P-frame's included. Records nothing; @ref finish
  ///        lays it out.
  /// @param voxel_size  As @ref record_code.
  /// @param trunc_dist  As @ref record_code.
  /// @param params      As @ref record_code.
  /// @return OK; @ref check_coding's refusals; or
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` with nothing counted.
  core::Status record_none(float voxel_size, float trunc_dist,
                           const CodecParams& params);

  /// @brief Once the batch @ref record_code recorded into has resolved:
  ///        check the coding, gather any payload past what that batch copied
  ///        (a tail, its batch waited on), and lay the frame out.
  /// @param metrics  Optional: a tail's `"  ..tail"`, both halves.
  /// @param timer    The tail's device span; must outlive the call.
  /// @return The frame, its payload in a slot of this writer's;
  ///         `Status::Code::IoError` if a kernel's table refused a symbol it
  ///         was counted from, or the segments outgrew their slots, which is
  ///         a bug here; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for no coded frame,
  ///         or one @ref assemble_head refuses; or a tail's failure.
  core::Result<EncodedFrame> finish(core::StageMetrics* metrics,
                                    core::GpuTimer& timer);

  /// @brief Drop the frame counted or coded, and its slots.
  void drop() noexcept;

 private:
  DeviceFrameWriter() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel count_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel ops_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel encode_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel scan_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel gather_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel results_kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;

  // Where each entry's steps go and each segment's slot (record_count).
  std::unique_ptr<StepLayout> layout_;

  // Device-local, retained and grown by ensure_device_scratch.
  core::Buffer counts_;           // per model, per symbol
  core::Buffer entry_steps_;      // coder steps per entry
  core::Buffer tables_;           // per model, per symbol: cum | freq << 16
  core::Buffer steps_;            // every coder step: start | freq << 16
  core::Buffer slots_;            // each segment's stream, at its slot's top
  core::Buffer lengths_;          // bytes per segment
  core::Buffer payload_offsets_;  // bytes, segment count + 1
  core::Buffer gather_args_;      // the gather's dispatch, which the scan sizes
  core::Buffer failed_;           // set when a table refuses a symbol
  core::Buffer refusal_;          // what check_entries refuses: two words
  core::Buffer frame_words_;      // the surplus and the blocks (StepLayout)

  // The front's results, the back's and the payload, made at first use, two
  // slots each: one a batch in flight binds, and one the host fills.
  std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing> front_ring_;
  std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing> back_ring_;
  std::unique_ptr<core::HostRing> payload_ring_;
  core::HostSlot front_slot_;
  core::HostSlot back_slot_;
  core::HostSlot payload_slot_;

  // What record_count counted with (segment size 0 before any, or after a
  // drop), and the frame record_code coded: its type and container fields,
  // its segments, what the payload's batch copied out, and whether it holds
  // any entry. Per frame type, the last frame's payload bytes per entry
  // plus 25%, the copied payload's prediction (0 before any).
  std::uint32_t segment_size_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t update_size_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t entry_count_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t reference_count_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t coefficient_count_ = 0;
  bool bounded_ = false;
  bool coded_ = false;
  FrameType type_ = FrameType::kIntra;
  CodedFrame frame_;
  std::uint32_t entries_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t segments_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize slot_bytes_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize copied_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t payload_per_entry_[2] = {};
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/encoder.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/encoder.hpp"

#include <atomic>
#include <new>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "block_lists.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "device_frame_writer.hpp"
#include "frame_hash.hpp"
#include "reference_store.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec {
namespace detail {

// What the halves need of a recorded frame: the reference a P-frame is
// coded against, the grid's geometry, the entries the front counted, the
// blocks it found, and how far the frame has come.
struct RecordedEncode {
  std::uint64_t serial = 0;
  FrameType type = FrameType::kIntra;
  FrameReference reference;
  float voxel_size = 0.0f;
  float trunc_dist = 0.0f;
  ResidentBlocks entries;
  std::uint32_t blocks = 0;
  bool back = false;
};

}  // namespace detail

namespace {

// The public default restates the frame's, which the installed header cannot
// name; this is what keeps the pair one number.
static_assert(EncoderConfig{}.segment_size == detail::kDefaultSegmentSize,
              "EncoderConfig's default segment size is the frame's");

// A record's serial, unique in the process, so a token names one encoder's
// record and no other's.
std::uint64_t next_serial() noexcept {
  static std::atomic<std::uint64_t> counter{0};
  return counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1;
}

core::Status fail(const char* op, const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string("Encoder::") + op + ": " +
                                        why);
}

}  // namespace

core::Status EncoderConfig::validate() const {
  VKC_TRY(params.validate());
  VKC_TRY(detail::check_segment_size("EncoderConfig", "segment_size",
                                     segment_size));
  VKC_TRY(detail::check_segment_size("EncoderConfig", "update_size",
                                     resolved_update_size()));
  if (intra_period == 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "EncoderConfig: intra_period 0; 1 makes every frame an I-frame");
  }
  return {};
}

Encoder::Encoder() = default;
Encoder::~Encoder() = default;

Encoder::Encoder(Encoder&& other) noexcept = default;
Encoder& Encoder::operator=(Encoder&& other) noexcept = default;

bool Encoder::valid() const noexcept { return transform_ != nullptr; }

void Encoder::force_intra() noexcept { force_intra_ = true; }

core::Result<Encoder> Encoder::create(core::Device& device,
                                      core::Allocator& allocator,
                                      const EncoderConfig& config) {
  VKC_TRY(config.validate());
  Encoder e;
  e.config_ = config;
  e.config_.update_size = config.resolved_update_size();
  e.device_ = &device;
  e.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.transform_, detail::DctTransform::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.lists_, detail::BlockLists::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.writer_, detail::DeviceFrameWriter::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.store_, detail::ReferenceStore::create(device, allocator));
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.list_count_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                         core::debug_object_handle(e.list_count_.handle()),
                         "codec.encode_list_count");
  VKC_ASSIGN(e.gpu_timer_, core::GpuTimer::create(device));
  return e;
}

core::Result<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> Encoder::encode(
    const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  // Before any refusal, so a refused call still costs its row; both
  // batches' waits, and the device halves they hand back, land in it too.
  // Its row is placed now, ahead of its breakdowns', which the batches'
  // device rows add while it is open.
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec encode");
  if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->add_cpu("codec encode", 0.0);
  // One half's batch, submitted and waited on, its device rows kept.
  const auto run = [&](core::CommandBatch& batch) -> core::Status {
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch done, batch.submit_async({}, {}));
    VKC_TRY(done.wait());
    if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->merge_device(done.device_rows());
    return {};
  };
  core::CommandBatch front_batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(const PendingEncode pending, front(front_batch, grid, metrics));
  core::Status ran = run(front_batch);
  core::CommandBatch back_batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  if (ran.ok()) ran = back(back_batch, pending, metrics);
  if (ran.ok()) ran = run(back_batch);
  if (!ran.ok()) {
    abandon(pending);
    return ran;
  }
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
  const auto frame = finish_frame(pending, metrics, &bytes);
  if (!frame.ok()) return frame.status();
  return bytes;
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Encoder::encode",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Result<PendingEncode> Encoder::record_front(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  // As encode(): the stage's row placed ahead of its breakdowns'.
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec encode");
  if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->add_cpu("codec encode", 0.0);
  return front(batch, grid, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Encoder::record_front",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Status Encoder::record_back(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                  const PendingEncode& pending,
                                  core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec encode");
  return back(batch, pending, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Encoder::record_back",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

core::Result<EncodedFrame> Encoder::finish(const PendingEncode& pending,
                                           core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "codec encode");
  return finish_frame(pending, metrics);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::exception_status("Encoder::finish",
                                core::Status::Code::OutOfMemory);
}

void Encoder::abandon(const PendingEncode& pending) noexcept {
  if (!holds(pending)) return;
  pending_.reset();
  writer_->drop();
}

bool Encoder::holds(const PendingEncode& pending) const noexcept {
  return pending_ != nullptr && pending.serial != 0 &&
         pending.serial == pending_->serial;
}

core::Result<PendingEncode> Encoder::front(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                           const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                           core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  if (!valid()) return fail("encode", "moved-from encoder");
  if (!grid.valid()) return fail("encode", "moved-from grid");
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  const CodecParams& params = config_.params;
  // Everything refusable before anything is recorded: the grid as the
  // transform takes it, and the geometry the header carries.
  VKC_TRY(transform_->check_grid(grid));
  VKC_TRY(detail::check_coding(gp.voxel_size, gp.trunc_dist, params));

  // A P-frame codes against the frame returned last, unless the rules on
  // encode() make this an I-frame. The encoder's params never change, so of
  // the coding parameters only the grid's geometry can differ. An empty
  // reference leaves nothing to predict. Whether the grid has a block to
  // code is the device's to say: a frame of none is an I-frame of none
  // (back), which costs no remove for every reference entry.
  const detail::FrameReference* reference = store_->held();
  if (reference != nullptr &&
      (force_intra_ || gop_position_ == 0 ||
       reference->header.block_count == 0 ||
       detail::coding_difference(reference->header, gp.voxel_size,
                                 gp.trunc_dist, params) != nullptr)) {
    reference = nullptr;
  }
  // Made before an unfinished record is superseded, so a host allocation
  // failure leaves that token finishable.
  auto recorded = std::make_unique<detail::RecordedEncode>();
  recorded->type = reference != nullptr ? FrameType::kInter : FrameType::kIntra;
  if (reference != nullptr) recorded->reference = *reference;
  recorded->voxel_size = gp.voxel_size;
  recorded->trunc_dist = gp.trunc_dist;
  pending_.reset();
  writer_->drop();

  // Every step is sized for the grid's block slots, the most the active
  // set, and so the frame, can hold; the device finds the counts.
  const auto bound = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks);
  const std::uint32_t k = params.coefficient_count;
  VKC_TRY(store_->reserve(bound, k));
  // The steps the forward reads, inline, ahead of this half's dispatches --
  // not the batch's first in a sender's batch, whose prep and fusion come
  // before -- until a frame has finished with them: they never change, so a
  // warm encoder records no update here.
  if (!steps_held_) VKC_TRY(transform_->record_steps(batch, params));

  // Each breakdown's host half is the stage's own, so they record into a
  // scratch row set and keep their device halves alone, which the batch's
  // device rows hand back by name. Each one's row is placed in the caller's
  // rows as it opens, its host half 0, so a caller sharing the batch tells
  // the encode's device rows by the rows it holds.
  core::StageMetrics parts;
  core::StageMetrics* const breakdowns = metrics != nullptr ? &parts : nullptr;
  const auto place = [metrics](const char* name) {
    if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->add_cpu(name, 0.0);
  };
  // The active set: the map's list while it still holds, its count set
  // here, or one compacted into this batch ("  ..encode set": apart from a
  // fuse's "  ..active set" timed into the same rows), its count left on
  // the device.
  const core::Buffer* list = nullptr;
  volume::DeviceCount list_count{&list_count_, 0, bound};
  if (const std::optional<volume::DeviceBlockList> held =
          grid.map().held_device_list()) {
    VKC_TRY(batch.fill(list_count_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), held->count));
    list = held->buffer;
  } else {
    core::GpuStageScope compaction(breakdowns, gpu_timer_, "  ..encode set");
    place("  ..encode set");
    VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::RecordedBlockList active,
               grid.map().record_compaction(batch, nullptr, &compaction));
    list = active.buffer;
    list_count.buffer = active.count;
  }
  // Only the blocks with an observed voxel are coded -- with true_sdf, only
  // those holding surface, the cut set left beside them -- found on the
  // device before the transform: a fused band is mostly never integrated.
  {
    core::GpuStageScope row(breakdowns, gpu_timer_, "  ..observed");
    place("  ..observed");
    VKC_TRY(transform_->record_observed(batch, grid, *list, list_count,
                                        config_.true_sdf, &row));
  }
  // Then into the order the frame requires -- the hash table's order is
  // whatever the allocate atomics left, so sorting is also what makes the
  // same content give the same bytes -- the sort's last level writing the
  // reference store's spare list, and through the forward into the spare:
  // the frame the decoder will hold, which this one holds too once it
  // returns the frame. A P-frame's entries are coded against the reference
  // there too, bounded at M plus the frame's blocks; the count takes the
  // survivors off on the device. Either frame's symbols are counted, laid
  // out and gathered for the host in the same batch.
  // TODO(codec): trim a P-frame's host overhead at small R, where its encode
  // is still slower than intra's (DECISIONS, the 2026-10-17 freeze).
  {
    core::GpuStageScope forward(breakdowns, gpu_timer_, "  ..forward");
    place("  ..forward");
    const detail::FrameBuffers frame = store_->frame_buffers();
    const volume::DeviceCount observed = transform_->observed_count();
    VKC_TRY(lists_->record_sort(batch, transform_->observed_list(), observed,
                                *frame.list, &forward));
    VKC_ASSIGN(
        recorded->entries,
        transform_->record_forward(
            batch, grid, *frame.list, observed, params, *frame.masks,
            *frame.coefficients,
            config_.true_sdf ? &transform_->cut_set() : nullptr, &forward));
    if (reference != nullptr) {
      VKC_ASSIGN(recorded->entries,
                 store_->record_diff(batch, observed, k, &forward));
    }
    VKC_TRY(writer_->record_count(
        batch, recorded->entries, config_.segment_size, config_.update_size,
        &forward, &observed,
        detail::TransformWords{&transform_->observed_counts(),
                               &transform_->rejected()}));
  }
  recorded->serial = next_serial();
  pending_ = std::move(recorded);
  return PendingEncode{pending_->serial, pending_->type};
}

core::Status Encoder::back(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                           const PendingEncode& pending,
                           core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  if (!holds(pending)) {
    return fail("record_back",
                "the pending frame is not this encoder's last record "
                "(finished, abandoned, superseded, or another encoder's)");
  }
  detail::RecordedEncode& set = *pending_;
  if (set.back) {
    return fail("record_back", "the frame's back half is already recorded");
  }
  // The front's refusals: entries the transform found no block for, which a
  // grid changed under the batch would leave.
  const detail::FrontResults r = writer_->front();
  const std::uint32_t bound = set.entries.count - set.entries.reference_count;
  VKC_TRY(detail::DctTransform::check_rejected("observed", r.observed_rejected,
                                               bound));
  VKC_TRY(detail::DctTransform::check_rejected("forward", r.forward_rejected,
                                               r.blocks));
  set.blocks = r.blocks;
  if (r.blocks == 0) {
    // No block to code: an I-frame of none, the smaller, with no back batch.
    VKC_TRY(
        writer_->record_none(set.voxel_size, set.trunc_dist, config_.params));
    set.type = FrameType::kIntra;
    set.back = true;
    return {};
  }
  core::StageMetrics parts;
  core::GpuStageScope entropy(metrics != nullptr ? &parts : nullptr, gpu_timer_,
                              "  ..rans encode");
  VKC_TRY(writer_->record_code(
      batch, set.entries, set.voxel_size, set.trunc_dist, config_.params,
      set.type == FrameType::kInter ? &set.reference : nullptr, metrics,
      &entropy));
  set.back = true;
  return {};
}

core::Result<EncodedFrame> Encoder::finish_frame(
    const PendingEncode& pending, core::StageMetrics* metrics,
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>* bytes) {
  if (!holds(pending)) {
    return fail("finish",
                "the pending frame is not this encoder's last record "
                "(finished, abandoned, superseded, or another encoder's)");
  }
  if (!pending_->back) {
    return fail("finish", "the frame's back half is not recorded");
  }
  const std::unique_ptr<detail::RecordedEncode> set = std::move(pending_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(EncodedFrame frame, writer_->finish(metrics, gpu_timer_));
  // Only a frame returned becomes the reference, and counts toward the
  // period. It holds every block the forward made -- a P-frame's survivors
  // and new blocks, an I-frame's all -- which the spare holds in frame order,
  // so the next P-frame's M is the spare's list.
  VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::FrameHeader header,
             detail::read_frame_header(frame.head.data(), frame.head.size()));
  if (header.block_count != set->blocks) {
    return fail("encode", "the frame holds " +
                              std::to_string(header.block_count) +
                              " blocks of the " + std::to_string(set->blocks) +
                              " the forward made (a bug)");
  }
  // encode() returns contiguous bytes, so its allocation must succeed before
  // this frame replaces the reference or consumes the period/force request.
  if (bytes != nullptr) {
    bytes->reserve(frame.size());
    bytes->assign(frame.head.begin(), frame.head.end());
    if (frame.payload_size != 0) {
      bytes->insert(bytes->end(), frame.payload,
                    frame.payload + frame.payload_size);
    }
  }
  store_->commit(detail::FrameReference{
      detail::frame_hash(frame.head.data(), frame.head.size(), frame.payload,
                         frame.payload_size),
      header});
  gop_position_ = (frame.type == FrameType::kInter ? gop_position_ : 0) + 1;
  if (gop_position_ == config_.intra_period) gop_position_ = 0;
  force_intra_ = false;
  steps_held_ = true;  // its front batch ran, writing them
  return frame;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec
```

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "frame_gate.hpp"

#include "deblock.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "frame_gate_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "frame_results_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// Mirrors `Push` in frame_gate.comp.
struct GatePush {
  std::uint32_t rebuild;
  std::uint32_t inter;
  std::uint32_t blocks;
  std::uint32_t new_count;
};
static_assert(sizeof(GatePush) == 16, "GatePush must be 16 bytes");

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<FrameGate>> FrameGate::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "FrameGate::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<FrameGate> owned(new FrameGate());
  FrameGate& g = *owned;
  g.device_ = &device;
  g.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(GatePush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(g.gate_kernel_, "codec_frame_gate", vgrid_frame_gate_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_frame_gate_comp_spv_size, 4, &push));
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::add_dispatch_args(
      kb, g.args_kernel_, "codec_frame_slices"));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(g.results_kernel_, "codec_frame_results",
                 vgrid_frame_results_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_frame_results_comp_spv_size, 8, nullptr));
  VKC_ASSIGN(g.pool_, kb.build());
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  g.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  VKC_ASSIGN(g.gate_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                         core::debug_object_handle(g.gate_.handle()),
                         "codec.frame_gate");
  return owned;
}

core::Status FrameGate::record_gate(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                    const ResultSources& sources,
                                    const GateCheck& check,
                                    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const core::DescriptorSet& set = gate_kernel_.set;
  set.write_storage_buffer(0, sources.verdict->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(1, sources.collision->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(2, sources.diff_counts->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(3, gate_.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  const GatePush push{check.rebuild ? 1u : 0u, check.inter ? 1u : 0u,
                      check.blocks, check.new_count};
  return batch.dispatch(gate_kernel_, &push, sizeof(push), 1,
                        max_workgroup_count_x_, stage);
}

core::Result<FrameSlices> FrameGate::record_slices(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                                   std::uint32_t n,
                                                   core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  // N, which the host knows, behind the gate: every slice empty for a frame
  // refused on the device.
  FrameSlices out;
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::record_dispatch_args(
      batch, *device_, *allocator_, args_kernel_, slices_, "codec.frame_slices",
      volumetric_kit::grid::detail::SlicedCount{nullptr, 0, n, 1, &gate_, 0}, 1,
      &out.blocks, Deblock::kFlagLanes, &out.flags, max_workgroup_count_x_,
      stage));
  return out;
}

core::Status FrameGate::record_results(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                       const core::HostSlot& slot,
                                       const ResultSources& sources,
                                       core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer result,
             batch.output(slot, 0, sizeof(DecodeResults)));
  const core::DescriptorSet& set = results_kernel_.set;
  const core::Buffer* words[] = {
      sources.verdict, sources.collision, sources.diff_counts,
      sources.faults,  sources.rejected,  sources.exact,
      &gate_};
  for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < 7; ++b) {
    set.write_storage_buffer(b, words[b]->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  }
  set.write_storage_buffer(7, result, 0, sizeof(DecodeResults));
  return batch.dispatch(results_kernel_, nullptr, 0, 1, max_workgroup_count_x_,
                        stage);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/frame_gate.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file frame_gate.hpp
/// @brief The decoder's judgement on the device: the gate a recorded frame's
///        grid writes run behind, their slices, and the results the host
///        reads once the frame's batch has run.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). It carries `VGRID_CODEC_API` so the
/// tier's tests reach it in a shared-library build.

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/allocator.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/host_ring.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// @brief What a frame's batch leaves in the decoder's results slot, written
///        whole by `frame_results.comp`: every count `Decoder::finish` and
///        `Decoder::rebuild` judge a frame by.
struct DecodeResults {
  std::uint32_t failed;       ///< The first failing segment (kNoVerdict).
  std::uint32_t survivors;    ///< A P-frame's surviving reference entries.
  std::uint32_t collision_q;  ///< Row 13's new block (kNoSource for none).
  std::uint32_t collision_e;  ///< ... and its reference entry.
  std::uint32_t gone;         ///< The grid blocks the frame lacks.
  std::uint32_t missing;      ///< The frame blocks the grid lacks.
  std::uint32_t faults;       ///< The apply's sources past what was bound.
  std::uint32_t rejected;     ///< The inverse's entries the grid lacks.
  std::uint32_t exact;        ///< The deblock's masked blocks.
  std::uint32_t gate;         ///< 1 when every step succeeded.
};
static_assert(sizeof(DecodeResults) == 4 * 10,
              "DecodeResults is ten words, as frame_results.comp writes it");

/// @brief What @ref FrameGate::record_gate judges.
struct GateCheck {
  bool rebuild = false;         ///< A rebuild's grid, not a decode's frame.
  bool inter = false;           ///< A P-frame.
  std::uint32_t blocks = 0;     ///< N.
  std::uint32_t new_count = 0;  ///< A.
};

/// @brief The words the gate and the results read: each piece's own, left
///        on the device by the frame's batch.
struct ResultSources {
  const core::Buffer* verdict = nullptr;      ///< The reader's two words.
  const core::Buffer* collision = nullptr;    ///< The merge's two words.
  const core::Buffer* diff_counts = nullptr;  ///< The diff's two words.
  const core::Buffer* faults = nullptr;       ///< The apply's word.
  const core::Buffer* rejected = nullptr;     ///< The inverse's word.
  const core::Buffer* exact = nullptr;        ///< The deblock's word.
};

/// @brief The slices of a frame's apply, inverse and deblock: a workgroup a
///        block, and the deblock flags' 64 blocks a workgroup.
struct FrameSlices {
  volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices blocks;
  volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices flags;
};

/// @brief The decoder's gate, its slices and its results.
///
/// The gate is one word (@ref gate): `frame_gate.comp` writes it from the
/// frame's verdict -- rows 11 to 13 for a decode, the grid's blocks against
/// the frame's for a rebuild -- the map's rounds close it on their own
/// failures, and grid's count-to-slices kernel sizes the apply, the inverse
/// and the deblock from N behind it (@ref record_slices), so a frame refused
/// on the device writes no voxel and no stamp. `frame_results.comp` gathers
/// every count into the decoder's results slot (@ref record_results).
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must outlive
///          this object. Not thread-safe.
class VGRID_CODEC_API FrameGate {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the three kernels and the gate word.
  /// @return The gate, or a pipeline, pool or allocation failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<FrameGate>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~FrameGate() = default;
  FrameGate(const FrameGate&) = delete;
  FrameGate& operator=(const FrameGate&) = delete;
  FrameGate(FrameGate&&) = delete;
  FrameGate& operator=(FrameGate&&) = delete;

  /// @return The gate word, a u32 at offset 0.
  const core::Buffer& gate() const noexcept { return gate_; }

  /// @brief Record the gate's judgement of @p check from @p sources' verdict,
  ///        collision and diff counts into @p batch, after what wrote them.
  core::Status record_gate(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                           const ResultSources& sources, const GateCheck& check,
                           core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Record the sizing of a frame's @p n blocks behind the gate.
  /// @return The slices, valid until the next call; or a buffer failure.
  core::Result<FrameSlices> record_slices(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                          std::uint32_t n,
                                          core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Record the gather of @p sources and the gate into @p slot, last.
  core::Status record_results(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                              const core::HostSlot& slot,
                              const ResultSources& sources,
                              core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

 private:
  FrameGate() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel gate_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel args_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel results_kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;
  core::Buffer gate_;
  core::Buffer slices_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
