### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/frame_hash.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "frame_hash.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

constexpr std::uint64_t kPrime1 = 0x9E3779B185EBCA87ull;
constexpr std::uint64_t kPrime2 = 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4Full;
constexpr std::uint64_t kPrime3 = 0x165667B19E3779F9ull;
constexpr std::uint64_t kPrime4 = 0x85EBCA77C2B2AE63ull;
constexpr std::uint64_t kPrime5 = 0x27D4EB2F165667C5ull;
constexpr std::size_t kStripe = 32;

std::uint64_t rotl(std::uint64_t x, int r) {
  return (x << r) | (x >> (64 - r));
}

// Little-endian, a byte at a time.
std::uint64_t read64(const std::uint8_t* p) {
  std::uint64_t v = 0;
  for (int i = 7; i >= 0; --i) v = (v << 8) | p[i];
  return v;
}

std::uint64_t read32(const std::uint8_t* p) {
  return std::uint64_t(p[0]) | std::uint64_t(p[1]) << 8 |
         std::uint64_t(p[2]) << 16 | std::uint64_t(p[3]) << 24;
}

std::uint64_t lane_round(std::uint64_t acc, std::uint64_t lane) {
  return rotl(acc + lane * kPrime2, 31) * kPrime1;
}

std::uint64_t merge_lane(std::uint64_t acc, std::uint64_t lane) {
  return (acc ^ lane_round(0, lane)) * kPrime1 + kPrime4;
}

// XXH64 over bytes that arrive in runs: the four lanes take each 32-byte
// stripe whichever runs it spans, and the bytes short of a stripe wait.
class Xxh64 {
 public:
  void update(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t size) {
    total_ += size;
    if (buffered_ != 0) {
      const std::size_t take = std::min(size, kStripe - buffered_);
      std::copy(p, p + take, buffer_ + buffered_);
      buffered_ += take;
      p += take;
      size -= take;
      if (buffered_ < kStripe) return;
      stripe(buffer_);
      buffered_ = 0;
    }
    for (; size >= kStripe; p += kStripe, size -= kStripe) stripe(p);
    std::copy(p, p + size, buffer_);
    buffered_ = size;
  }

  std::uint64_t digest() const {
    std::uint64_t acc = 0;
    if (total_ >= kStripe) {
      acc = rotl(v_[0], 1) + rotl(v_[1], 7) + rotl(v_[2], 12) + rotl(v_[3], 18);
      for (const std::uint64_t v : v_) acc = merge_lane(acc, v);
    } else {
      acc = kPrime5;
    }
    acc += total_;
    const std::uint8_t* p = buffer_;
    const std::uint8_t* const end = buffer_ + buffered_;
    for (; end - p >= 8; p += 8) {
      acc = rotl(acc ^ lane_round(0, read64(p)), 27) * kPrime1 + kPrime4;
    }
    if (end - p >= 4) {
      acc = rotl(acc ^ (read32(p) * kPrime1), 23) * kPrime2 + kPrime3;
      p += 4;
    }
    for (; p < end; ++p) {
      acc = rotl(acc ^ (*p * kPrime5), 11) * kPrime1;
    }
    // The avalanche.
    acc ^= acc >> 33;
    acc *= kPrime2;
    acc ^= acc >> 29;
    acc *= kPrime3;
    acc ^= acc >> 32;
    return acc;
  }

 private:
  void stripe(const std::uint8_t* p) {
    for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) {
      v_[lane] = lane_round(v_[lane], read64(p + 8 * lane));
    }
  }

  std::uint64_t v_[4] = {kPrime1 + kPrime2, kPrime2, 0, 0 - kPrime1};
  std::uint8_t buffer_[kStripe] = {};
  std::size_t buffered_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t total_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace

std::uint64_t frame_hash(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
  return frame_hash(data, size, nullptr, 0);
}

std::uint64_t frame_hash(const std::uint8_t* head, std::size_t head_size,
                         const std::uint8_t* payload,
                         std::size_t payload_size) {
  Xxh64 h;
  if (head_size != 0) h.update(head, head_size);
  if (payload_size != 0) h.update(payload, payload_size);
  return h.digest();
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/rans.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file rans.hpp
/// @brief The codec's entropy code: static-table rANS with a 32-bit state,
///        16-bit output words and 12-bit probabilities, and the frequency
///        tables a frame carries.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). The kernels code it
/// (`shaders/rans_*.comp`); the tests' CPU coder
/// (`tests/codec_oracle_rans.hpp`) is the oracle that pins their bytes.
/// Everything is integer arithmetic on fixed widths, and nothing needs more
/// than 32-bit arithmetic.
///
/// The scheme is Giesen's word-oriented rANS: the state `x` lives in
/// `[L, L << 16)` with `L = 2^16`, a symbol of frequency `f` at cumulative
/// start `c` (out of `M = 2^12`) encodes as
/// `x' = (x / f) * M + x % f + c`, and one 16-bit word leaves the state first
/// whenever `x >= f << 20` -- one is always enough, in both directions. That
/// bound is tested as `(x >> 20) >= f`, since `f << 20` is 2^32 at a
/// probability of one and wraps to 0 in 32 bits. A symbol with `f == M` costs
/// nothing, which is what makes an all-zero band free rather than cheap. A raw
/// field of up to 32 bits is coded low chunk first, in chunks of at most 12
/// bits, each a symbol of frequency `2^(12 - n)` for its `n` bits.
///
/// A segment's stream is the final state as two 16-bit words (high first),
/// then the renormalization words in the order the decoder reads them, every
/// word little-endian: always even, and at least 4 bytes. The encoder starts
/// in state `L`, so a correct decode consumes every word and ends there.
/// rANS decodes in the reverse of the order it encodes, so a coder takes a
/// segment's symbols in decode order and encodes them last first.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// Probability precision: every table's frequencies sum to `2^12`.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kRansScaleBits = 12;
/// `M`, the total every non-empty table's frequencies sum to.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kRansScale = 1u << kRansScaleBits;

/// @brief A normalized frequency table over an alphabet of
///        `freq.size()` symbols.
///
/// Either **empty** (every frequency zero: the model was never used, and a
/// decoder that reaches for it has been handed a corrupt stream) or summing to
/// exactly @ref kRansScale with every used symbol at least 1.
struct FrequencyTable {
  std::vector<std::uint16_t> freq;  ///< Per symbol.
  std::vector<std::uint16_t> cum;   ///< `cum[s]` = sum of `freq[0..s)`; size
                                    ///< alphabet + 1.

  /// Recompute @ref cum from @ref freq (after building or parsing one).
  void finalize() {
    cum.assign(freq.size() + 1, 0);
    for (std::size_t s = 0; s < freq.size(); ++s) {
      cum[s + 1] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(cum[s] + freq[s]);
    }
  }
};

/// @brief Normalize symbol counts to a @ref FrequencyTable.
///
/// Integer-only and deterministic, so a frame's tables are the same wherever
/// its counts were made. Every counted symbol gets at least 1 (it must stay
/// encodable), the rest is proportional, and the rounding residue goes to (or
/// comes from) the most frequent symbols, lowest index first on a tie.
/// @param counts  One count per symbol of the alphabet (at most 256 symbols,
///                at most @ref kRansScale of them counted).
/// @return The table; empty when every count is zero.
inline FrequencyTable normalize_counts(
    const std::vector<std::uint64_t>& counts) {
  FrequencyTable t;
  t.freq.assign(counts.size(), 0);
  std::uint64_t total = 0;
  for (std::uint64_t c : counts) {
    total += c;
  }
  if (total == 0) {
    t.finalize();
    return t;
  }
  std::uint32_t sum = 0;
  std::size_t top = 0;  // the most frequent symbol, lowest index on a tie
  for (std::size_t s = 0; s < counts.size(); ++s) {
    if (counts[s] == 0) {
      continue;
    }
    // counts[s] * M fits: a frame holds far fewer than 2^52 symbols per model.
    const std::uint64_t scaled = counts[s] * kRansScale / total;
    t.freq[s] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(std::max<std::uint64_t>(1, scaled));
    sum += t.freq[s];
    if (counts[s] > counts[top]) {
      top = s;
    }
  }
  // Floor rounding leaves sum <= M, except where the at-least-1 bumps push it
  // over. Give a shortfall to the most frequent symbol, and take an excess
  // from whichever symbol has the most to spare, one unit at a time.
  if (sum < kRansScale) {
    t.freq[top] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(t.freq[top] + (kRansScale - sum));
  }
  while (sum > kRansScale) {
    std::size_t widest = 0;
    for (std::size_t s = 1; s < t.freq.size(); ++s) {
      if (t.freq[s] > t.freq[widest]) {
        widest = s;
      }
    }
    --t.freq[widest];
    --sum;
  }
  t.finalize();
  return t;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file rans_dispatch.hpp
/// @brief The host side of the rANS kernels, which the device frame writer
///        and reader share: their push constants and the table entries they
///        read. They and the block lists' kernels dispatch through
///        `vgrid::detail::dispatch_items` (base/dispatch.hpp).
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed).

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

#include "rans.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

using volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_items;

/// Mirrors `Push` in rans_push.glsl.
struct RansPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base = 0;
  /// M + A, every stream position; or for the count and layout a bound
  /// whose surplus they bind (`counted_entries`).
  std::uint32_t num_entries = 0;
  std::uint32_t coefficient_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t segment_size = 0;
  std::uint32_t segment_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t frame_type = 0;
  std::uint32_t reference_count = 0;  ///< M.
  std::uint32_t update_size = 0;      ///< U.
  /// The decode's payload's first byte in its binding.
  std::uint32_t payload_byte = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(RansPush) == 36, "RansPush must be 36 bytes");

/// @return Every model's symbols back to back, in TABLES order (each model
///         at @ref frame_model_base), as the kernels read them:
///         `cum | freq << 16`.
inline std::vector<std::uint32_t> rans_table_entries(
    const std::vector<FrequencyTable>& tables) {
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> entries;
  for (const FrequencyTable& t : tables) {
    for (std::size_t s = 0; s < t.freq.size(); ++s) {
      entries.push_back(std::uint32_t(t.cum[s]) |
                        (std::uint32_t(t.freq[s]) << 16));
    }
  }
  return entries;
}

/// @return A binding's range of @p bytes, but never less than one
///         @p element: a side a frame lacks (reference entries, or new
///         blocks) still binds a valid range, which its kernel never reads.
inline VkDeviceSize binding_range(VkDeviceSize bytes, VkDeviceSize element) {
  return std::max(bytes, element);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/reference_store.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "reference_store.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <limits>
#include <string>

#include "rans_dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "inter_apply_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "inter_diff_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "survivor_ranks_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

// Mirrors `Push` in inter_apply.comp.
struct ApplyPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base = 0;
  std::uint32_t num_blocks = 0;
  std::uint32_t coefficient_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t reference_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t payload_count = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(ApplyPush) == 20, "ApplyPush must be 20 bytes");

// Mirrors `Push` in inter_diff.comp.
struct DiffPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base = 0;
  std::uint32_t reference_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t target_bound = 0;
  std::uint32_t coefficient_count = 0;
  std::uint32_t pass = 0;
  std::uint32_t target_word = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(DiffPush) == 24, "DiffPush must be 24 bytes");

constexpr std::uint32_t kApplyBindings = 8;
constexpr std::uint32_t kDiffBindings = 12;
constexpr std::uint32_t kRanksBindings = 3;
// inter_diff.comp's workgroup width.
constexpr std::uint32_t kDiffLanes = 64;
constexpr VkDeviceSize kEntryBytes = sizeof(volume::BlockIndex);
constexpr VkDeviceSize kWordBytes = sizeof(std::uint32_t);
constexpr VkDeviceSize kMaskBytes = kMaskWordsPerBlock * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
static_assert(kMaskWordsPerBlock == 16, "inter_apply.comp's kMaskWords is 16");
// survivor_ranks.comp's verdict and survivor count.
constexpr VkDeviceSize kSurvivorBytes = 2 * kWordBytes;

// Bytes of one entry's coefficients, as the transform reads them.
VkDeviceSize coefficient_bytes(std::uint32_t k) {
  return VkDeviceSize(coefficient_words(k)) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
}

// A binding's range of @p entries of @p bytes each, never less than one: a
// side the frame lacks still binds a valid range, which the kernel never
// reads. Every buffer is made at least that large at create.
VkDeviceSize range(std::uint64_t entries, VkDeviceSize bytes) {
  return std::max<VkDeviceSize>(entries, 1) * bytes;
}

core::Status fail(const char* op, const std::string& why) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string("ReferenceStore::") + op +
                                        ": " + why);
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<ReferenceStore>> ReferenceStore::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "ReferenceStore::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<ReferenceStore> owned(new ReferenceStore());
  ReferenceStore& s = *owned;
  s.device_ = &device;
  s.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(ApplyPush);
  VkPushConstantRange diff_push = push;
  diff_push.size = sizeof(DiffPush);
  VkPushConstantRange ranks_push = push;
  ranks_push.size = sizeof(RansPush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(s.apply_kernel_, "codec_inter_apply",
                 vgrid_inter_apply_comp_spv, vgrid_inter_apply_comp_spv_size,
                 kApplyBindings, &push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(s.diff_kernel_, "codec_inter_diff", vgrid_inter_diff_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_inter_diff_comp_spv_size, kDiffBindings, &diff_push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(
      s.ranks_kernel_, "codec_survivor_ranks", vgrid_survivor_ranks_comp_spv,
      vgrid_survivor_ranks_comp_spv_size, kRanksBindings, &ranks_push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(s.pool_, kb.build());
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  s.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  s.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  // One entry of each, so a side with none -- the reference of an intra
  // frame, a frame with no new blocks -- binds a buffer; and the counts.
  struct First {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const VkDeviceSize widest = coefficient_bytes(kVoxelsPerBlock);
  const First first[] = {
      {s.slots_[0].masks, kMaskBytes, "codec.reference_masks"},
      {s.slots_[0].coefficients, widest, "codec.reference_coefficients"},
      {s.slots_[0].list, sizeof(volume::BlockIndex), "codec.reference_list"},
      {s.slots_[1].masks, kMaskBytes, "codec.reference_masks"},
      {s.slots_[1].coefficients, widest, "codec.reference_coefficients"},
      {s.slots_[1].list, sizeof(volume::BlockIndex), "codec.reference_list"},
      {s.sources_, sizeof(ApplySource), "codec.apply_sources"},
      {s.faults_, kWordBytes, "codec.apply_faults"},
      {s.diff_masks_, kMaskBytes, "codec.diff_masks"},
      {s.diff_coefficients_, widest, "codec.diff_coefficients"},
      {s.modes_, kWordBytes, "codec.diff_modes"},
      {s.ranks_, kWordBytes, "codec.diff_ranks"},
      {s.added_, kEntryBytes, "codec.diff_added"},
      {s.survivors_, kSurvivorBytes, "codec.diff_survivors"},
  };
  for (const First& f : first) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(device, allocator, f.buffer, f.bytes,
                                        s.max_storage_buffer_range_, f.name));
  }
  return owned;
}

core::Status ReferenceStore::reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t k) {
  Slot& spare = slots_[current_ ^ 1u];
  struct Scratch {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const Scratch scratch[] = {
      {spare.masks, VkDeviceSize(n) * kMaskBytes, "codec.reference_masks"},
      {spare.coefficients, VkDeviceSize(n) * coefficient_bytes(k),
       "codec.reference_coefficients"},
      {spare.list, VkDeviceSize(n) * sizeof(volume::BlockIndex),
       "codec.reference_list"},
      {sources_, VkDeviceSize(n) * sizeof(ApplySource), "codec.apply_sources"},
  };
  // Every range first, so a frame the device cannot hold grows nothing.
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(b.name, b.bytes,
                                             max_storage_buffer_range_));
  }
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, b.buffer,
                                        b.bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                        b.name));
  }
  return {};
}

core::Result<ResidentBlocks> ReferenceStore::record_apply(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const ResidentBlocks& payload, std::uint32_t n,
    const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& slices,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const std::uint32_t k = payload.coefficient_count;
  const Slot& reference = slots_[current_];
  const Slot& spare = slots_[current_ ^ 1u];
  const VkDeviceSize blocks = n;
  if (blocks * kMaskBytes > spare.masks.size() ||
      blocks * coefficient_bytes(k) > spare.coefficients.size() ||
      blocks * sizeof(volume::BlockIndex) > spare.list.size() ||
      blocks * sizeof(ApplySource) > sources_.size()) {
    return fail("record_apply",
                std::to_string(n) + " blocks, more than were reserved");
  }
  if (n != 0 && (payload.masks == nullptr || payload.coefficients == nullptr)) {
    return fail("record_apply", "no payload buffers");
  }
  // A P-frame's entries read the reference, which is laid out at its own K;
  // an intra frame's read none, whatever is held.
  const std::uint32_t m = payload.reference_count;
  const std::uint32_t held_m = held_ ? reference_.header.block_count : 0;
  const std::uint32_t held_k =
      held_ ? reference_.header.params.coefficient_count : 1;
  if (m != 0 && (m != held_m || k != held_k)) {
    return fail("record_apply", "a P-frame of " + std::to_string(m) +
                                    " reference entries at K " +
                                    std::to_string(k) + ", on a reference of " +
                                    std::to_string(held_m) + " at K " +
                                    std::to_string(held_k));
  }
  ResidentBlocks out;
  out.list = &spare.list;
  out.masks = &spare.masks;
  out.coefficients = &spare.coefficients;
  out.count = n;
  out.coefficient_count = k;
  // The faults read as none for a frame that applies nothing.
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(faults_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u));
  if (n == 0) return out;

  const VkDeviceSize row_bytes = coefficient_bytes(k);
  core::ComputeKernel& apply = apply_kernel_;
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(0, sources_.handle(), 0,
                                 blocks * sizeof(ApplySource));
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(1, reference.masks.handle(), 0,
                                 range(m, kMaskBytes));
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(2, reference.coefficients.handle(), 0,
                                 range(m, coefficient_bytes(held_k)));
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(3, payload.masks->handle(), 0,
                                 range(payload.count, kMaskBytes));
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(4, payload.coefficients->handle(), 0,
                                 range(payload.count, row_bytes));
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(5, spare.masks.handle(), 0,
                                 blocks * kMaskBytes);
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(6, spare.coefficients.handle(), 0,
                                 blocks * row_bytes);
  apply.set.write_storage_buffer(7, faults_.handle(), 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t));
  ApplyPush push;
  push.num_blocks = n;
  push.coefficient_count = k;
  push.reference_count = m;
  push.payload_count = payload.count;
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(batch, apply, push,
                                                        slices, stage));
  return out;
}

core::Status ReferenceStore::check_faults(std::uint32_t faults) {
  if (faults != 0) {
    return fail("record_apply", std::to_string(faults) +
                                    " of the frame's blocks read past the "
                                    "reference or the payload");
  }
  return {};
}

core::Result<ResidentBlocks> ReferenceStore::record_diff(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const volume::DeviceCount& target,
    std::uint32_t k, core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  if (!held_) return fail("record_diff", "no reference is held");
  // The target's bound, which every buffer and the second pass are sized
  // for; its count stays on the device.
  const std::uint32_t n = target.bound;
  if (target.buffer == nullptr || !target.buffer->valid() ||
      target.offset % kWordBytes != 0 ||
      target.buffer->size() < target.offset + kWordBytes) {
    return fail("record_diff",
                "the target's count word is missing, misaligned or past its "
                "buffer");
  }
  const std::uint32_t held_k = reference_.header.params.coefficient_count;
  if (k != held_k) {
    return fail("record_diff", "a frame at K " + std::to_string(k) +
                                   " on a reference at K " +
                                   std::to_string(held_k));
  }
  const std::uint32_t m = reference_.header.block_count;
  const Slot& reference = slots_[current_];
  const Slot& spare = slots_[current_ ^ 1u];
  const VkDeviceSize row_bytes = coefficient_bytes(k);
  if (VkDeviceSize(n) * kMaskBytes > spare.masks.size() ||
      VkDeviceSize(n) * row_bytes > spare.coefficients.size() ||
      VkDeviceSize(n) * kEntryBytes > spare.list.size()) {
    return fail("record_diff",
                std::to_string(n) + " blocks, more than were reserved");
  }
  // The stream positions: the M reference entries, then at most n new
  // blocks.
  const std::uint64_t entries = std::uint64_t(m) + n;
  if (entries > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
    return fail("record_diff", "more than 2^32 - 1 entries");
  }
  struct Scratch {
    core::Buffer& buffer;
    VkDeviceSize bytes;
    const char* name;
  };
  const Scratch scratch[] = {
      {diff_masks_, range(entries, kMaskBytes), "codec.diff_masks"},
      {diff_coefficients_, range(entries, row_bytes),
       "codec.diff_coefficients"},
      {modes_, range(m, kWordBytes), "codec.diff_modes"},
      {ranks_, (VkDeviceSize(m) + 1) * kWordBytes, "codec.diff_ranks"},
      {added_, range(n, kEntryBytes), "codec.diff_added"},
  };
  // Every range first, so a frame the device cannot hold grows nothing.
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(b.name, b.bytes,
                                             max_storage_buffer_range_));
  }
  for (const Scratch& b : scratch) {
    VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, b.buffer,
                                        b.bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                        b.name));
  }
  const VkDeviceSize rank_bytes = (VkDeviceSize(m) + 1) * kWordBytes;
  const core::DescriptorSet& diff = diff_kernel_.set;
  diff.write_storage_buffer(0, reference.list.handle(), 0,
                            range(m, kEntryBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(1, spare.list.handle(), 0, range(n, kEntryBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(2, reference.masks.handle(), 0,
                            range(m, kMaskBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(3, reference.coefficients.handle(), 0,
                            range(m, row_bytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(4, spare.masks.handle(), 0, range(n, kMaskBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(5, spare.coefficients.handle(), 0,
                            range(n, row_bytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(6, diff_masks_.handle(), 0,
                            range(entries, kMaskBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(7, diff_coefficients_.handle(), 0,
                            range(entries, row_bytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(8, modes_.handle(), 0, range(m, kWordBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(9, ranks_.handle(), 0, rank_bytes);
  diff.write_storage_buffer(10, added_.handle(), 0, range(n, kEntryBytes));
  diff.write_storage_buffer(11, target.buffer->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  const core::DescriptorSet& ranks = ranks_kernel_.set;
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(0, modes_.handle(), 0, range(m, kWordBytes));
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(1, ranks_.handle(), 0, rank_bytes);
  ranks.write_storage_buffer(2, survivors_.handle(), 0, kSurvivorBytes);

  DiffPush push;
  push.reference_count = m;
  push.target_bound = n;
  push.coefficient_count = k;
  push.target_word = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(target.offset / kWordBytes);
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, diff_kernel_, push, m, kDiffLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  RansPush ranks_push;
  ranks_push.reference_count = m;
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch(ranks_kernel_, &ranks_push, sizeof(ranks_push), 1,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  push.pass = 1;
  VKC_TRY(dispatch_items(batch, diff_kernel_, push, n, kDiffLanes,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  ResidentBlocks out;
  out.list = &added_;
  out.masks = &diff_masks_;
  out.coefficients = &diff_coefficients_;
  out.modes = &modes_;
  out.ranks = &ranks_;
  out.count = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(entries);
  out.coefficient_count = k;
  out.reference_count = m;
  out.bounded = true;
  return out;
}

void ReferenceStore::commit(const FrameReference& reference) {
  current_ ^= 1u;
  held_ = true;
  reference_ = reference;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/reference_store.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file reference_store.hpp
/// @brief The frame a P-frame is coded or decoded against, kept where the
///        transforms read and write it: the decoder's apply that makes each
///        decoded frame from it, and the encoder's diff that codes each
///        P-frame against it.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed). The frame's quantized
/// coefficients and masks, and its block list, stay on the device, in the
/// transform's layout; the host keeps its @ref FrameReference alone. A
/// reference is never rebuilt from a grid: the grid holds dequantized SDF,
/// and a residual adds to the q the reference was coded with.

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "dct_transform.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_hash_map.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// @brief Where the next frame's blocks go, as @ref ReferenceStore::reserve
///        last sized them: the store's spare, and the apply's sources. The
///        decoder's merge writes the list and the sources
///        (@ref BlockLists::record_merge) and its apply the masks and
///        coefficients; the encoder's sort writes the list
///        (@ref BlockLists::record_sort) and its forward the masks and
///        coefficients (@ref DctTransform::record_forward).
struct FrameBuffers {
  const core::Buffer* list = nullptr;     ///< `volume::BlockIndex` a block.
  const core::Buffer* sources = nullptr;  ///< An @ref ApplySource a block.
  const core::Buffer* masks = nullptr;    ///< `kMaskWordsPerBlock` words.
  /// @ref coefficient_words "coefficient_words(K)" words a block.
  const core::Buffer* coefficients = nullptr;
};

/// @brief The held reference frame and the frame being coded or decoded, in
///        two slots of device memory that swap at each @ref commit.
///
/// The current slot holds the reference: each block's 16 mask words and
/// @ref coefficient_words(K) coefficient words, and its block list, in the
/// reference's order. The spare receives the next frame (@ref frame_buffers)
/// and becomes the current slot only at @ref commit. So until a frame
/// commits, the reference stays as it was, whatever was recorded or failed.
///
/// A decoder's frame comes from its merge and @ref record_apply
/// (`inter_apply.comp`); an intra frame takes the same apply, from its
/// payload alone, so every decoded frame lands in the store by one path. An
/// encoder's comes from its sort and forward transform, intra or P alike,
/// and a P-frame's entries are coded from it against the reference by
/// @ref record_diff (`inter_diff.comp`). Every frame either side commits is
/// the q and masks the next one is coded or decoded against.
///
/// Each slot takes `80 + 4 * coefficient_words(K)` bytes a block, and the
/// sources `8`; the diff takes `64 + 4 * coefficient_words(K)` an entry it
/// codes (a reference entry, and a block of the frame), and 16 more a block
/// of the frame and 8 a reference entry. Every buffer is device-local and
/// retained, growing as @ref reserve and @ref record_diff ask
/// (`ensure_device_scratch`).
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one frame at a time.
class VGRID_CODEC_API ReferenceStore {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the apply's and the diff's kernels and the store's first,
  ///        smallest buffers.
  /// @return The store, holding no reference; or a pipeline, pool or
  ///         allocation failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<ReferenceStore>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~ReferenceStore() = default;
  ReferenceStore(const ReferenceStore&) = delete;
  ReferenceStore& operator=(const ReferenceStore&) = delete;
  ReferenceStore(ReferenceStore&&) = delete;
  ReferenceStore& operator=(ReferenceStore&&) = delete;

  /// @return The held reference, for @ref parse_frame; null until the first
  ///         @ref commit.
  const FrameReference* held() const noexcept {
    return held_ ? &reference_ : nullptr;
  }

  /// @return The held reference's block list, `volume::BlockIndex` each,
  ///         `ptr` 0, its coordinates strictly increasing: its M entries'
  ///         places, which the merge searches. With none held, M is 0.
  const core::Buffer& reference_list() const noexcept {
    return slots_[current_].list;
  }

  /// @return The held reference as the inverse reads it: its list, masks
  ///         and coefficients, block count and K, valid until the next
  ///         @ref commit; no blocks with none held. What `Decoder::rebuild`
  ///         reconstructs.
  ResidentBlocks reference_blocks() const noexcept {
    ResidentBlocks out;
    if (!held_) return out;
    const Slot& reference = slots_[current_];
    out.list = &reference.list;
    out.masks = &reference.masks;
    out.coefficients = &reference.coefficients;
    out.count = reference_.header.block_count;
    out.coefficient_count = reference_.header.params.coefficient_count;
    return out;
  }

  /// @return The spare and the sources, as @ref reserve last sized them.
  FrameBuffers frame_buffers() const noexcept {
    const Slot& spare = slots_[current_ ^ 1u];
    return FrameBuffers{&spare.list, &sources_, &spare.masks,
                        &spare.coefficients};
  }

  /// @brief Make the spare hold a frame of @p n blocks of @p k
  ///        coefficients before anything is recorded: what lets a decoder
  ///        refuse before it touches the grid, and gives an encoder's forward
  ///        its output.
  /// @return OK; `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a buffer past
  ///         `maxStorageBufferRange`; or an allocation's failure. The held
  ///         reference is untouched either way.
  core::Status reserve(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t k);

  /// @brief Record the apply of a decoded frame of @p n blocks into the
  ///        spare, from the sources at @ref frame_buffers, which the caller
  ///        recorded the writing of into @p batch before this, over
  ///        @p slices: an invocation a block, sized and gated on the device.
  ///
  /// A source past what is bound -- a reference entry when @p payload holds
  /// none, or past its M; a payload entry past its count -- is read as
  /// absent and counted in @ref faults, which @ref check_faults words.
  /// @param batch    The batch to record into; submitted by the caller.
  /// @param payload  The frame's entries by stream position, where the
  ///                 device frame reader decoded them: a P-frame's M must be
  ///                 the held reference's, at its K.
  /// @param n        The frame's blocks.
  /// @param slices   The apply's slices, a group a block, for @p n blocks.
  /// @param stage    Optional scope the apply's device span records into.
  /// @return The spare, valid until the next call, as the inverse reads it
  ///         (no reference entries); `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for
  ///         more blocks than @ref reserve made room for, no payload
  ///         buffers, or a P-frame of another M or K than the held
  ///         reference's.
  core::Result<ResidentBlocks> record_apply(
      core::CommandBatch& batch, const ResidentBlocks& payload, std::uint32_t n,
      const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices& slices,
      core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @return The blocks the last @ref record_apply found a source past what
  ///         was bound for, a u32, once its batch has run.
  const core::Buffer& faults() const noexcept { return faults_; }

  /// @return OK for no faults, or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for
  ///         @p faults blocks whose source was past what was bound.
  static core::Status check_faults(std::uint32_t faults);

  /// @brief Record a P-frame's entries against the held reference, coded
  ///        from the frame the spare holds once the commands @p batch already
  ///        holds have run (an encoder's sort, into the spare's list, and its
  ///        forward), into this store's own buffers; its blocks are
  ///        @p target's word.
  ///
  /// `inter_diff.comp` gives each reference entry its mode -- remove when
  /// the frame lacks its block, skip when the block is unchanged, keep or
  /// zero otherwise -- and the payload keep and zero carry; then the
  /// survivor ranks; then each block the reference lacks its place among
  /// the new blocks, its coordinate and its payload (the kernel has the
  /// rules and the price that picks zero over keep). The frame's blocks must
  /// be strictly increasing, as the encoder's sort leaves them. Reads
  /// nothing back: only the device knows how many blocks the frame holds and
  /// how many are new, so the second pass runs over the bound.
  /// @param batch   The batch to record into; submitted by the caller.
  /// @param target  The frame's blocks: a word a kernel wrote, at most its
  ///                bound, `n`.
  /// @param k       Their K, the held reference's.
  /// @param stage   As @ref record_apply.
  /// @return The P-frame's entries by stream position once @p batch has
  ///         run, valid until the next call, bounded
  ///         (@ref ResidentBlocks::bounded): M + `n` of them, of which the
  ///         device frame writer, counting in the same batch, takes off the
  ///         blocks the frame lacks and the `ranks[M]` survivors to leave
  ///         M + A. Or `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for no reference held,
  ///         a K other than its, a count word missing, misaligned or past its
  ///         buffer, a bound past what @ref reserve made room for, more than
  ///         2^32 - 1 entries, or a buffer past `maxStorageBufferRange`;
  ///         otherwise a buffer failure.
  core::Result<ResidentBlocks> record_diff(
      core::CommandBatch& batch, const volume::DeviceCount& target,
      std::uint32_t k, core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @brief Hold the spare as the reference: the only call that changes
  ///        @ref held and @ref reference_list.
  /// @pre The batch that made the spare's frame -- the last
  ///      @ref record_apply's, or an encoder's forward -- was submitted and
  ///      succeeded, and the spare's list holds the frame's
  ///      `reference.header.block_count` blocks.
  void commit(const FrameReference& reference);

 private:
  ReferenceStore() = default;

  /// A frame's coefficients and masks, in the transform's layout, and its
  /// block list.
  struct Slot {
    core::Buffer masks;
    core::Buffer coefficients;
    core::Buffer list;
  };

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel apply_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel diff_kernel_;
  core::ComputeKernel ranks_kernel_;  // survivor_ranks.comp, between passes
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;

  // slots_[current_] holds the reference; the other is the spare.
  Slot slots_[2];
  std::uint32_t current_ = 0;
  core::Buffer sources_;  // the apply's, an ApplySource a block
  core::Buffer faults_;   // the apply's out-of-range sources, a u32
  // The diff's P-frame entries: masks and coefficients by stream position,
  // a mode a reference entry, the survivor ranks (M + 1), the new blocks'
  // list, and the ranks' two words (survivor_ranks.comp's verdict layout,
  // the survivor count second), which nothing reads back.
  core::Buffer diff_masks_;
  core::Buffer diff_coefficients_;
  core::Buffer modes_;
  core::Buffer ranks_;
  core::Buffer added_;
  core::Buffer survivors_;

  bool held_ = false;
  FrameReference reference_;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/step_layout.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "step_layout.hpp"

#include <string>

#include "bitstream.hpp"
#include "rans_dispatch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/device_requirements.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "rans_layout_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {
namespace {

constexpr VkDeviceSize kTotalsBytes = sizeof(StepLayout::Totals);

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StepLayout>> StepLayout::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "StepLayout::create"));
  std::unique_ptr<StepLayout> owned(new StepLayout());
  StepLayout& l = *owned;
  l.device_ = &device;
  l.allocator_ = &allocator;
  VkPushConstantRange push{};
  push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push.size = sizeof(RansPush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(l.kernel_, "codec_rans_layout", vgrid_rans_layout_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_rans_layout_comp_spv_size, 5, &push));
  VKC_ASSIGN(l.pool_, kb.build());
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  l.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  l.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  VKC_ASSIGN(l.totals_, core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, kTotalsBytes));
  device.set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                         core::debug_object_handle(l.totals_.handle()),
                         "codec.rans_layout_totals");
  return owned;
}

core::Status StepLayout::record(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::Buffer& steps,
    const core::Buffer& words, std::uint32_t entries,
    std::uint32_t reference_count, std::uint32_t update_size,
    std::uint32_t segment_size, core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const std::uint32_t m = reference_count;
  VKC_TRY(
      check_segment_size("StepLayout::record", "segment_size", segment_size));
  if (m > entries) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "StepLayout::record: " + std::to_string(m) +
        " reference entries, more than the " + std::to_string(entries) +
        " entries");
  }
  if (m != 0) {
    VKC_TRY(
        check_segment_size("StepLayout::record", "update_size", update_size));
  }
  // No entries lays out nothing, and its totals are 0.
  if (entries == 0) return batch.fill(totals_, 0, kTotalsBytes, 0u);

  // The bound's, which the frame's never exceed; below 2^32 together, as
  // m + (entries - m) is.
  const std::uint64_t segments = frame_segment_count(m, update_size) +
                                 frame_segment_count(entries - m, segment_size);
  const VkDeviceSize range = max_storage_buffer_range_;
  const VkDeviceSize step_bytes = VkDeviceSize(entries) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize start_bytes = step_bytes + sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  const VkDeviceSize offset_bytes =
      (VkDeviceSize(segments) + 1) * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  VKC_TRY(core::StorageInput(steps).check("StepLayout::record: the steps",
                                          step_bytes));
  VKC_TRY(core::StorageInput(words).check("StepLayout::record: the frame words",
                                          kFrameWordsBytes));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, starts_,
                                      start_bytes, range, "codec.rans_starts",
                                      &batch));
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, slot_offsets_,
                                      offset_bytes, range,
                                      "codec.rans_slot_offsets", &batch));
  kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(0, steps.handle(), 0, step_bytes);
  kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(1, starts_.handle(), 0, start_bytes);
  kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(2, slot_offsets_.handle(), 0, offset_bytes);
  kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(3, words.handle(), 0, kFrameWordsBytes);
  kernel_.set.write_storage_buffer(4, totals_.handle(), 0, kTotalsBytes);
  RansPush push;
  push.num_entries = entries;
  push.segment_size = segment_size;
  push.reference_count = m;
  push.update_size = update_size;
  return batch.dispatch(kernel_, &push, sizeof(push), 1, max_workgroup_count_x_,
                        stage);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/step_layout.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file step_layout.hpp
/// @brief Where a frame's rANS coder steps go, laid out on the device: the
///        device frame writer's layout, which the host only sizes from.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed).

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/buffer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/descriptor.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/fwd.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/export.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail {

/// @brief A frame's coder steps laid out from each entry's step count, on
///        the device (`rans_layout.comp`): where each entry's steps go in the
///        one array the encoder streams through, and each segment's output
///        slot.
///
/// The rANS encoder takes a segment's steps last first, so a segment's
/// entries are laid out last first: with E the exclusive scan of the entries'
/// steps in stream order (@ref starts), segment `[x, y)` takes steps `E[x]`
/// to `E[y]`, and entry p of it ends its steps at `E[x] + E[y] - E[p]`. Each
/// segment's slot holds a 16-bit word a step and the final state's two,
/// rounded up to whole 32-bit words so no two segments share one: a second
/// scan, of those sizes (@ref slot_offsets). Both run in one workgroup on
/// `scan.glsl`, recorded into the batch that counted the steps; their two
/// totals, which size the coding's buffers, reach the host with that batch's
/// results.
///
/// The kernel takes N on the device, from the frame words: its M reference
/// entries and a blocks word of the bound's blocks, less a surplus word, so
/// a frame whose blocks only the device knows (the encoder's forward), or a
/// bounded P-frame's count (@ref ResidentBlocks::bounded), lays out in the
/// batch that counted it. Its segments follow from N, and it writes both
/// totals to a buffer of their own, for a later command of the batch to
/// gather; nothing is read back.
///
/// Every buffer is device-local and retained, grown as a call needs
/// (`ensure_device_scratch`).
///
/// @warning The `Device` and `Allocator` passed to @ref create must
///          outlive this object. Not thread-safe: one call at a time.
class VGRID_CODEC_API StepLayout {
 public:
  /// @brief Build the kernel.
  /// @return The layout, or a pipeline or pool failure.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StepLayout>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator);

  ~StepLayout() = default;
  StepLayout(const StepLayout&) = delete;
  StepLayout& operator=(const StepLayout&) = delete;
  StepLayout(StepLayout&&) = delete;
  StepLayout& operator=(StepLayout&&) = delete;

  /// @brief What @ref totals holds once the batch ran.
  struct Totals {
    /// Every entry's steps, exact below 2^30, where it stops: 2^30 steps of
    /// 4 bytes reach 4 GiB, which no frame may code.
    std::uint32_t steps = 0;
    /// Every slot's 16-bit words, exact while @ref steps is below 2^30.
    std::uint32_t slot_words = 0;
  };

  /// The frame words' bytes: the surplus, then the blocks (@ref record).
  static constexpr VkDeviceSize kFrameWordsBytes = 2 * sizeof(std::uint32_t);

  /// @brief Record the layout of a frame's entries' coder steps into
  ///        @p batch, its totals left in @ref totals.
  ///
  /// The segments are the frame's (`frame_models.glsl`'s `segment_range`):
  /// @p reference_count update segments of @p update_size entries, then the
  /// rest in segments of @p segment_size. The kernel binds a set this object
  /// keeps, so a batch holds at most one of these calls.
  /// @param batch            The batch to record into; submitted by the
  ///                         caller.
  /// @param steps            Each entry's coder steps by stream position,
  ///                         at most 2^20 each (an entry of the grammar
  ///                         takes at most 1,685), so no sum past the step
  ///                         total's stop wraps; read, never written.
  /// @param words            The frame words, two u32: how many of the
  ///                         frame's blocks are past its entries, clamped
  ///                         to its blocks -- 0, or a bounded P-frame's
  ///                         survivors -- then the frame's blocks, clamped
  ///                         to the bound's, `entries` less M; read, never
  ///                         written.
  /// @param entries          A bound on N: every stream position @p steps
  ///                         holds.
  /// @param reference_count  M: its reference entries.
  /// @param update_size      U: reference entries an update segment, read
  ///                         only when M is nonzero.
  /// @param segment_size     R: new blocks a segment.
  /// @param stage            Optional scope the caller's stage row is open
  ///                         under; the dispatch records its device span
  ///                         into it.
  /// @return OK, recording only the totals' zeroing for no entries; or
  ///         `Status::Code::InvalidArgument` for a size
  ///         @ref check_segment_size refuses, more reference entries than
  ///         entries, a @p steps or @p words `StorageInput::check` refuses,
  ///         or a buffer past `maxStorageBufferRange`; otherwise a buffer
  ///         failure.
  core::Status record(core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::Buffer& steps,
                      const core::Buffer& words, std::uint32_t entries,
                      std::uint32_t reference_count, std::uint32_t update_size,
                      std::uint32_t segment_size,
                      core::GpuStageScope* stage = nullptr);

  /// @return The last @ref record's @ref Totals, once its batch ran.
  const core::Buffer& totals() const noexcept { return totals_; }
  /// @return E, once the batch ran: the steps before each entry in stream
  ///         order, N of them, then their total at N.
  const core::Buffer& starts() const noexcept { return starts_; }
  /// @return Each segment's slot's first 16-bit word, even, then their total
  ///         at the segment count, once the batch ran.
  const core::Buffer& slot_offsets() const noexcept { return slot_offsets_; }

 private:
  StepLayout() = default;

  // Borrowed (must outlive this).
  core::Device* device_ = nullptr;
  core::Allocator* allocator_ = nullptr;
  std::uint32_t max_workgroup_count_x_ = 0;
  VkDeviceSize max_storage_buffer_range_ = 0;

  // Declared before pool_, so the pool is destroyed first.
  core::ComputeKernel kernel_;
  core::DescriptorPool pool_;

  // Device-local, retained.
  core::Buffer starts_;        // N + 1, of the bound
  core::Buffer slot_offsets_;  // segment count + 1, of the bound
  core::Buffer totals_;        // starts_[N] and slot_offsets_[S]
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec_stream/codec_stream.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec_stream/codec_stream.hpp"

#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>
#include <system_error>
#include <utility>

#include "stream_coder.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/log.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/log.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decode_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec_stream {

namespace detail {
namespace {

// Whether `rows` holds a row named `name`.
bool has_row(const core::StageMetrics& rows, const char* name) {
  for (const core::StageRow& row : rows.rows()) {
    if (std::strcmp(row.name, name) == 0) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// Close a stream that holds no record and remove its file at `path`, so a
// rerun is refused for its real cause, not for this empty stream.
void take_back(std::unique_ptr<stream::StreamWriter>& writer,
               const std::string& path) {
  if (!writer) return;
  writer.reset();
  std::error_code ignored;
  std::filesystem::remove(path, ignored);
}

// A frame `set` at `pts_ns` that does not follow the last one coded.
core::Status out_of_order(std::uint64_t set, std::uint64_t pts_ns,
                          std::uint64_t last_set, std::uint64_t last_pts_ns) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(
      "CodecStream: frame " + std::to_string(set) + " at " +
      std::to_string(pts_ns) + " ns does not follow frame " +
      std::to_string(last_set) + " at " + std::to_string(last_pts_ns) + " ns");
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamCoder>> StreamCoder::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
    const codec::EncoderConfig& config, const stream::Session& session,
    const CodecOutputs& outputs) {
  if (session.tracks.size() != 1 ||
      session.tracks[0].kind != stream::TrackKind::Geometry) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "CodecStream: the session must be one Geometry track");
  }
  std::unique_ptr<networking::StreamServer> server;
  if (outputs.serve) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(server,
               networking::StreamServer::start(session, *outputs.serve));
  }
  std::unique_ptr<stream::StreamWriter> writer;
  if (!outputs.stream.empty()) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(writer, stream::StreamWriter::create(outputs.stream, session));
  }
  // A codec error takes back the file made above.
  core::Result<codec::Encoder> enc =
      codec::Encoder::create(device, allocator, config);
  if (!enc.ok()) {
    take_back(writer, outputs.stream);
    return enc.status();
  }
  std::optional<codec::Decoder> dec;
  if (outputs.decode) {
    core::Result<codec::Decoder> made =
        codec::Decoder::create(device, allocator);
    if (!made.ok()) {
      take_back(writer, outputs.stream);
      return made.status();
    }
    dec.emplace(std::move(made).value());
  }
  return std::unique_ptr<StreamCoder>(
      new StreamCoder(device, allocator, std::move(enc).value(), std::move(dec),
                      outputs.stream, std::move(server), std::move(writer)));
}

StreamCoder::StreamCoder(core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
                         codec::Encoder enc, std::optional<codec::Decoder> dec,
                         std::string path,
                         std::unique_ptr<networking::StreamServer> server,
                         std::unique_ptr<stream::StreamWriter> writer)
    : device_(&device),
      allocator_(&allocator),
      encoder_(std::move(enc)),
      decoder_(std::move(dec)),
      path_(std::move(path)),
      server_(std::move(server)),
      writer_(std::move(writer)) {}

StreamCoder::~StreamCoder() {
  if (!finished_ && coded_ == 0) take_back(writer_, path_);
}

core::Result<SentFrame> StreamCoder::code(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                          std::uint64_t set,
                                          std::uint64_t pts_ns) {
  // Refused here, not by the writer once the encoder holds the frame.
  if (finished_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("CodecStream: finished");
  }
  if (coded_ > 0 && (set <= last_set_ || pts_ns < last_pts_ns_)) {
    return out_of_order(set, pts_ns, last_set_, last_pts_ns_);
  }
  key_on_request();
  core::StageMetrics encoded;
  VKC_ASSIGN(const std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes,
             encoder_.encode(grid, &encoded));
  const bool tail = has_row(encoded, "  ..tail");
  core::Result<SentFrame> played =
      play(stream::RecordPayload::of(bytes.data(), bytes.size()), set, pts_ns,
           std::move(encoded), tail,
           static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().num_blocks), nullptr, {});
  if (!played.ok()) encoder_.force_intra();
  return played;
}

core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> StreamCoder::record_front(
    core::CommandBatch& front, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid) {
  if (finished_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("CodecStream: finished");
  }
  key_on_request();
  front_rows_ = core::StageMetrics{};
  max_blocks_ = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().num_blocks);
  return encoder_.record_front(front, grid, &front_rows_);
}

void StreamCoder::front_ran(const std::vector<core::StageRow>& device_rows,
                            core::StageMetrics* rest) {
  std::vector<core::StageRow> encode;
  std::vector<core::StageRow> others;
  for (const core::StageRow& row : device_rows) {
    (has_row(front_rows_, row.name) ? encode : others).push_back(row);
  }
  front_rows_.merge_device(encode);
  if (rest != nullptr) rest->merge_device(others);
}

core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> StreamCoder::redo(
    const codec::PendingEncode& pending, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
    core::StageMetrics* rows) {
  encoder_.abandon(pending);
  const core::StageMetrics first = std::move(front_rows_);
  core::CommandBatch front(*device_, *allocator_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::PendingEncode again, record_front(front, grid));
  const core::Status ran = [&]() -> core::Status {
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch done, front.submit_async({}, {}));
    {
      const core::WaitScope wait(rows, "wait: redo");
      VKC_TRY(done.wait());
    }
    front_ran(done.device_rows(), nullptr);
    return {};
  }();
  if (!ran.ok()) {
    encoder_.abandon(again);
    return ran;
  }
  core::StageMetrics both = first;
  both.merge(front_rows_);
  front_rows_ = std::move(both);
  return again;
}

core::Result<SentFrame> StreamCoder::finish_frame(
    const codec::PendingEncode& pending, std::uint64_t set,
    std::uint64_t pts_ns, core::StageMetrics* rows,
    const std::function<void()>& sent) {
  if (finished_) {
    encoder_.abandon(pending);
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("CodecStream: finished");
  }
  if (coded_ > 0 && (set <= last_set_ || pts_ns < last_pts_ns_)) {
    encoder_.abandon(pending);
    return out_of_order(set, pts_ns, last_set_, last_pts_ns_);
  }
  core::StageMetrics back_rows;
  core::CommandBatch back(*device_, *allocator_);
  const core::Status coded = [&]() -> core::Status {
    VKC_TRY(encoder_.record_back(back, pending, &back_rows));
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch done, back.submit_async({}, {}));
    {
      // The output: waited on at once.
      const core::WaitScope wait(rows, "wait: frame");
      VKC_TRY(done.wait());
    }
    back_rows.merge_device(done.device_rows());
    return {};
  }();
  if (!coded.ok()) {
    encoder_.abandon(pending);
    return coded;
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::EncodedFrame encoded,
             encoder_.finish(pending, &back_rows));
  core::StageMetrics frame_rows = front_rows_;
  frame_rows.merge(back_rows);
  if (rows != nullptr) rows->merge(frame_rows);
  const bool tail = has_row(back_rows, "  ..tail");
  const stream::RecordPayload payload = [&] {
    // The record's one CRC, for the file and the viewers alike.
    const core::StageScope crc(rows, "crc");
    return stream::RecordPayload::of(encoded.head.data(), encoded.head.size(),
                                     encoded.payload, encoded.payload_size);
  }();
  core::Result<SentFrame> played =
      play(payload, set, pts_ns, std::move(frame_rows), tail, max_blocks_, rows,
           sent);
  if (!played.ok()) encoder_.force_intra();
  return played;
}

core::Status StreamCoder::finish() {
  if (finished_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("CodecStream: finished");
  }
  finished_ = true;
  server_.reset();
  return writer_ ? writer_->finish() : core::Status{};
}

void StreamCoder::key_on_request() noexcept {
  if (!server_) return;
  const std::uint64_t wanted = server_->key_wanted();
  if (wanted == key_wanted_) return;
  key_wanted_ = wanted;
  encoder_.force_intra();
}

core::Result<SentFrame> StreamCoder::play(
    const stream::RecordPayload& bytes, std::uint64_t set, std::uint64_t pts_ns,
    core::StageMetrics encoded, bool tail, std::uint32_t max_blocks,
    core::StageMetrics* rows, const std::function<void()>& sent) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const codec::FrameInfo info,
             codec::read_frame_info(bytes.first(), bytes.first_size()));
  stream::RecordInfo record;
  // A reader starts, or seeks, at a key: a frame that decodes alone.
  record.key = info.type == codec::FrameType::kIntra;
  record.pts_ns = pts_ns;
  record.seq = coded_;
  record.set = set;
  if (writer_) {
    const core::StageScope write(rows, "write");
    VKC_TRY(writer_->append(record, bytes));
  }
  // After the file, so no viewer gets a frame the file lacks. Returning a
  // refusal would leave coded_ behind the file, whose writer would then
  // refuse the next seq.
  if (server_) {
    const core::StageScope publish(rows, "publish");
    const core::Status served = server_->publish(record, bytes);
    if (!served.ok()) {
      log_message(core::LogLevel::Warning,
                  "CodecStream: frame " + std::to_string(set) +
                      " not served: " + served.message());
    }
  }
  ++coded_;
  last_set_ = set;
  last_pts_ns_ = pts_ns;
  if (sent) sent();
  SentFrame frame;
  frame.type = info.type;
  frame.bytes = bytes.size();
  frame.blocks = info.block_count;
  frame.tail = tail;
  frame.encode = std::move(encoded);
  if (decoder_) {
    // The frame's one copy on the way to the decoder: into its input buffer.
    VKC_ASSIGN(const core::HostSlot input, decoder_->claim_input(bytes.size()));
    if (bytes.first_size() != 0) {
      std::memcpy(input.data(), bytes.first(), bytes.first_size());
    }
    if (bytes.second_size() != 0) {
      std::memcpy(input.data() + bytes.first_size(), bytes.second(),
                  bytes.second_size());
    }
    if (!player_) {
      VKC_ASSIGN(volume::VoxelBlockGrid grid,
                 codec::make_decode_grid(*device_, *allocator_, input.data(),
                                         bytes.size(), max_blocks));
      player_.emplace(std::move(grid));
    }
    VKC_TRY(codec::decode_growing(*decoder_, input, bytes.size(), *player_,
                                  max_blocks, &frame.decode));
  }
  return frame;
}

}  // namespace detail

core::Result<CodecStream> CodecStream::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
    const codec::EncoderConfig& config, const stream::Session& session,
    CodecOutputs outputs) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(
      std::unique_ptr<detail::StreamCoder> coder,
      detail::StreamCoder::create(device, allocator, config, session, outputs));
  return CodecStream(std::move(coder));
}

CodecStream::CodecStream(std::unique_ptr<detail::StreamCoder> coder) noexcept
    : coder_(std::move(coder)) {}

CodecStream::CodecStream(CodecStream&& other) noexcept = default;

CodecStream::~CodecStream() = default;

core::Result<SentFrame> CodecStream::code(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                          std::uint64_t set,
                                          std::uint64_t pts_ns) {
  if (!coder_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("CodecStream: moved from");
  }
  return coder_->code(grid, set, pts_ns);
}

core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> CodecStream::record_front(
    core::CommandBatch& front, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid) {
  if (!coder_) {

}

void CodecStream::front_ran(const std::vector<core::StageRow>& device_rows,
                            core::StageMetrics* rest) {

core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> CodecStream::redo(

core::Result<SentFrame> CodecStream::finish_frame(

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

#pragma once

// What a CodecStream holds and does, its calls each CodecStream's of the same
// name, the frame in halves included. Internal: CodecStream owns one and
// forwards to it, and only the tier's sources include this header.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/stage_metrics.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/decoder.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec/encoder.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/codec_stream/codec_stream.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/session.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_writer.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec_stream::detail {

class StreamCoder {
 public:
  // As CodecStream::create.
  static core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamCoder>> create(
      core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
      const codec::EncoderConfig& config, const stream::Session& session,
      const CodecOutputs& outputs);

  StreamCoder(const StreamCoder&) = delete;
  StreamCoder& operator=(const StreamCoder&) = delete;
  StreamCoder(StreamCoder&&) = delete;
  StreamCoder& operator=(StreamCoder&&) = delete;
  // As ~CodecStream.
  ~StreamCoder();

  // As CodecStream::code.
  core::Result<SentFrame> code(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::uint64_t set,
                               std::uint64_t pts_ns);

  // As CodecStream::record_front, ::front_ran, ::redo and ::finish_frame.
  core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> record_front(core::CommandBatch& front,
                                                  volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid);
  void front_ran(const std::vector<core::StageRow>& device_rows,
                 core::StageMetrics* rest);
  core::Result<codec::PendingEncode> redo(const codec::PendingEncode& pending,
                                          volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                          core::StageMetrics* rows);
  core::Result<SentFrame> finish_frame(const codec::PendingEncode& pending,
                                       std::uint64_t set, std::uint64_t pts_ns,
                                       core::StageMetrics* rows,
                                       const std::function<void()>& sent);

  // As CodecStream::finish, ::player, ::server, ::last_pts_ns and ::coded.
  core::Status finish();
  volume::VoxelBlockGrid* player() noexcept {
    return player_ ? &*player_ : nullptr;
  }
  const networking::StreamServer* server() const noexcept {
    return server_.get();
  }
  std::uint64_t last_pts_ns() const noexcept { return last_pts_ns_; }
  std::uint64_t coded() const noexcept { return coded_; }

 private:
  StreamCoder(core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
              codec::Encoder enc, std::optional<codec::Decoder> dec,
              std::string path,
              std::unique_ptr<networking::StreamServer> server,
              std::unique_ptr<stream::StreamWriter> writer);

  // Make the next frame an I-frame (Encoder::force_intra) when a viewer
  // joined or fell back since the last frame read the server's count: it
  // waits for a key. The request stands until a frame is returned, so a frame
  // refused or recorded again still makes it; joins between two frames make
  // one.
  void key_on_request() noexcept;

  // What code() and finish_frame() do once the encoder returns frame `set`'s
  // `bytes` -- its head, then its payload where the encoder left it, under
  // one CRC: write and serve them, run `sent`, and decode them into the
  // player if the stream decodes, from the decoder's input buffer they are
  // copied into. `encoded` is the encode's stage rows and `tail` whether its
  // payload took a tail. The source's block capacity, `max_blocks`, bounds
  // its frames' blocks: the player's ceiling. `rows`, when given, takes the
  // write's and the serve's rows.
  core::Result<SentFrame> play(const stream::RecordPayload& bytes,
                               std::uint64_t set, std::uint64_t pts_ns,
                               core::StageMetrics encoded, bool tail,
                               std::uint32_t max_blocks,
                               core::StageMetrics* rows,
                               const std::function<void()>& sent);

  core::Device* device_;
  core::Allocator* allocator_;
  codec::Encoder encoder_;
  std::optional<codec::Decoder> decoder_;  // with CodecOutputs::decode
  std::string path_;                       // the file's, or empty
  // Null when not serving, or once finished.
  std::unique_ptr<networking::StreamServer> server_;
  std::unique_ptr<stream::StreamWriter> writer_;  // null without a file
  // The server's key_wanted() when a frame last read it (key_on_request).
  std::uint64_t key_wanted_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t coded_ = 0;     // frames encoded and written: the next seq
  std::uint64_t last_set_ = 0;  // the last of them, once coded_ > 0
  std::uint64_t last_pts_ns_ = 0;
  bool finished_ = false;
  std::optional<volume::VoxelBlockGrid> player_;
  // The frame in flight between record() and finish_frame(): its front
  // half's rows, and its source's block capacity.
  core::StageMetrics front_rows_;
  std::uint32_t max_blocks_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::codec_stream::detail
