#include "volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/marching_cubes_tables.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_map_internal.hpp"

// Embedded SPIR-V (generated by vgrid_embed_shaders onto a PRIVATE include
// path).
#include "marching_cubes_sparse_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "marching_cubes_sparse_shared_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "mc_args_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "mc_finalize_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh {
namespace {

// The public entry point a diagnostic reports under. Every extract funnels
// through extract_device_impl, so without this the whole tier would name that
// -- or, as it did until this was threaded, a `MarchingCubes::extract` the
// header no longer declares, leaving a user with a message they cannot grep
// back to any of the entry points. Carried as a parameter rather than a member
// so it cannot outlive the call it describes.
constexpr const char* kEntryHost = "MarchingCubes::extract_host";
constexpr const char* kEntryDevice = "MarchingCubes::extract_device";
constexpr const char* kEntryRecord = "MarchingCubes::record_extract";
constexpr const char* kEntryFinish = "MarchingCubes::finish";

// Worst-case triangles a single marching-cubes cell can emit (5 per the table).
constexpr std::uint64_t kMaxTrisPerCell = 5;

// The draw command is an ABI across three languages now -- the host resets it
// and reads it back, the GLSL kernel aliases its first field as the append
// atomic (`buffer DrawCommand { uint index_count; ... }`, offset 0 under scalar
// block layout), and the renderer's vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect consumes the whole
// struct. Vulkan fixes this layout, but the 4-byte fill in
// disarm_indirect_command() and the IndirectWords readback assume it here, and
// this file already pins every other cross-language struct the same way.
static_assert(sizeof(VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand) == 20,
              "VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand must be 20 bytes -- the kernel's "
              "DrawCommand mirror and the host reset/readback assume it");
static_assert(offsetof(VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand, indexCount) == 0,
              "indexCount must be field 0 -- the kernel's append atomic bumps "
              "it through a storage binding at offset 0, and the host clamps "
              "it with a 4-byte write to the start of the buffer");

// Triangles per active block the first extract plans for, before any
// measurement is available. A real scan measures 54-68 (Replica room0) against
// the 5*block_size^3 worst case -- 2560 for the default 8-voxel block, ~40x
// higher -- and the estimate self-corrects from the first completed extract, so
// this only has to be the right order of magnitude. Guessing low costs one
// extra dispatch on the first call; guessing high costs resident memory for the
// extractor's whole lifetime, since the arena never shrinks.
constexpr std::uint64_t kSeedTrisPerBlock = 64;

// Vertices per 1000 triangles to assume before anything has been measured.
//
// Deliberately OPTIMISTIC -- below the ~750 in-block sharing settles at --
// because the arena is grow-only: a first extract that over-allocates never
// gives the memory back, which would defeat the point. Under-shooting instead
// costs one refit dispatch, which is the backstop the capacity plan already
// has. Unshared extracts never consult this; they know the answer is 3000.
constexpr std::uint32_t kSeedVertsPer1000 = 700;

// Cells the sharing kernel's shared owned-edge table holds -- block_size 8.
//
// Mirrors kMaxSharedCells in marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp, and a comment
// is all that could tie a C++ constant to a GLSL one. So the drift is
// *detected* rather than asserted: the kernel reports whether it actually
// shared
// (`sharing_applied`, byte 24 of the command buffer) and extract_device fails
// if it did not. Raising this alone would otherwise admit a block the kernel
// silently meshes unshared -- correct geometry, feature quietly gone. The other
// direction (lowering this alone) merely refuses grids the kernel could handle,
// and the kernel's own `vpb <= kMaxSharedCells` test is what keeps either from
// indexing past the shared array.
constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxSharedCells = 512;

// A corner with weight below this is treated as unintegrated (the kernel's test
// is `weight < weight_threshold`), and any cell touching it is skipped. The
// volume tier defines it, so the codec's observed mask reads the same value.
// The `tsdf` tier will surface this as a tunable knob.
constexpr float kWeightThreshold = volume::kObservedWeight;

// The lookup tables, flattened for upload -- byte-identical to the GLSL
// `Tables` block (scalar layout, all-int so std430 and scalar agree). One
// definition of the tables (the constexpr arrays in the header) feeds both
// sides.
struct McTables {
  std::int32_t tri_table[256 * 16];
  std::int32_t corner_offset[8 * 3];
  std::int32_t edge_to_vert[12 * 2];
};
static_assert(sizeof(McTables) ==
                  (256 * 16 + 8 * 3 + 12 * 2) * sizeof(std::int32_t),
              "McTables must be tightly packed for the shader ABI");

// The push-constant block the sparse kernel reads (mirrors `PushConstants` in
// marching_cubes_sparse.comp under scalar layout). The grid geometry rides here
// (block_size / voxel_size); the block coordinates and per-voxel data come
// through the bound buffers.
struct SparsePushConstants {
  std::int32_t block_size;
  std::int32_t voxels_per_block;
  float voxel_size;
  float iso;
  std::uint32_t num_active_blocks;
  std::uint32_t capacity;
  float weight_threshold;
  std::uint32_t has_color;  // 0 = no color attribute; vertices get opaque white
  // Vertices the arena holds. Its own budget rather than `capacity * 3`: once
  // cells share a vertex the two stop being proportional, and sizing the arena
  // from the triangle plan is exactly what would make sharing save nothing.
  //
  // Defaulted and assigned by name, not filled positionally, for the same
  // reason the three below are: adjacent same-typed scalars make a positional
  // slip compile clean.
  std::uint32_t vertex_capacity = 0;
  // The hash-table shape, for the kernel's on-device neighbour probe. The
  // sparse kernel resolves the 2x2x2 neighbourhood itself now, so it needs to
  // traverse the table the same way the volume tier does.
  //
  // Defaulted, and deliberately NOT filled from the aggregate initializer at
  // the dispatch: these three are same-typed adjacent scalars copied out of
  // another tier's private table shape, so a positional transposition of
  // num_buckets and bucket_size would satisfy every static_assert below (both
  // int32, at 32 and 36) and compile. They are assigned by name instead.
  std::int32_t num_buckets = 0;
  std::int32_t bucket_size = 0;
  std::int32_t max_chain = 0;
  // Block slots this grid's heap holds (VoxelGridParams::num_blocks). The
  // extract binds only a list this grid's map compacted
  // (check_device_block_subset), so every ptr is one the heap handed out;
  // this is a one-comparison-per-workgroup guard against a corrupted list,
  // since robustBufferAccess is enabled nowhere. Assigned by name, like the
  // four above.
  std::uint32_t num_block_slots = 0;
  // The first active block this dispatch covers, written by
  // vgrid::detail::dispatch_items.
  std::uint32_t item_base = 0;
};
// Pin every field offset (all 4-byte scalars): a same-size reorder would keep
// sizeof unchanged but silently drift the host<->GLSL push-constant ABI, so
// guard each one.
static_assert(sizeof(SparsePushConstants) == 56,
              "SparsePushConstants must be 56 bytes");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, vertex_capacity) == 32,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, block_size) == 0,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, voxels_per_block) == 4,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, voxel_size) == 8,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, iso) == 12,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, num_active_blocks) == 16,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, capacity) == 20,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, weight_threshold) == 24,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, has_color) == 28,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, num_buckets) == 36,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, bucket_size) == 40,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, max_chain) == 44,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, num_block_slots) == 48,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(SparsePushConstants, item_base) == 52,
              "SparsePushConstants layout drift");

// The command buffer: the draw command plus two words of grid scratch,
// immediately past it. Keeping them in this buffer costs no second allocation
// per ring slot and leaves a well-formed command at offset 0, which is all
// vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect binds. The host resets it and reads it back whole,
// in one transfer each way.
struct IndirectWords {
  VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand command;
  // The vertex counter, which the sharing kernel allocates through. It cannot
  // be derived from indexCount any more -- that held only while every
  // triangle owned three private vertices.
  std::uint32_t vertex_count;
  // The sharing kernel's report that it really did share (see
  // kMaxSharedCells). This and vertex_count are written only by
  // marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp; the default kernel leaves them at the
  // host's reset.
  std::uint32_t sharing_applied;
};
// Packed, as the kernels' scalar-layout mirror assumes.
static_assert(sizeof(IndirectWords) == sizeof(VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand) +
                                           2 * sizeof(std::uint32_t),
              "IndirectWords must mirror the command buffer's layout");
constexpr VkDeviceSize kIndirectBufferBytes = sizeof(IndirectWords);

// What the finalize (mc_finalize.comp) writes into an extract's result slot,
// whole.
struct McResults {
  std::uint32_t index_count;      // the field's, past the capacity included
  std::uint32_t vertex_count;     // the sharing kernel's
  std::uint32_t sharing_applied;  // the sharing kernel's report
  std::uint32_t meshed;           // the blocks meshed
  std::uint32_t opened;           // whether the gate was open
};
static_assert(sizeof(McResults) == 4 * 5,
              "McResults is five words, as mc_finalize.comp writes it");

// mc_args.comp's and mc_finalize.comp's push blocks.
struct ArgsPush {
  std::uint32_t count_word;
  std::uint32_t gate_word;
  std::uint32_t bound;
  std::uint32_t per_dispatch;
  std::uint32_t dispatches;
};
static_assert(sizeof(ArgsPush) == 20, "ArgsPush must be 20 bytes");
struct FinalizePush {
  std::uint32_t capacity;
  std::uint32_t vertex_capacity;
  std::uint32_t share;
};
static_assert(sizeof(FinalizePush) == 12, "FinalizePush must be 12 bytes");

// mc_args.comp's word index that names no word.
constexpr std::uint32_t kNoWord = ~0u;

// The sparse kernel's push constants for @p blocks listed blocks of @p grid
// at @p iso, into a slot that meshes @p capacity triangles and holds
// @p vertex_capacity vertices.
SparsePushConstants sparse_push(const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, float iso,
                                std::uint32_t blocks, std::uint32_t capacity,
                                std::uint32_t vertex_capacity) {
  const volume::VoxelGridParams& gp = grid.grid();
  SparsePushConstants push{
      gp.block_size,    gp.voxels_per_block,
      gp.voxel_size,    iso,
      blocks,           capacity,
      kWeightThreshold, grid.has_attribute(volume::kColorAttribute) ? 1u : 0u};
  // Assigned by name, not appended to the aggregate above. These three are
  // same-typed adjacent scalars copied out of another tier's private table
  // shape, so a transposition of num_buckets and bucket_size would keep every
  // offsetof static_assert true (both are int32 at 32/36) and still compile,
  // and the kernel would then hash into `h % 50` over a 30000-bucket table --
  // every probe resolving against the wrong bucket, every seam losing its
  // surface, Status::ok.
  push.num_buckets = gp.num_buckets;
  push.bucket_size = gp.bucket_size;
  push.max_chain = gp.max_chain;
  // Assigned by name for the same reason the three above are: they are
  // same-typed adjacent scalars, so a positional slip would compile.
  push.vertex_capacity = vertex_capacity;
  push.num_block_slots = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.num_blocks);
  return push;
}

// The extracts' result slots: the batch in flight and the one recorded.
constexpr std::uint32_t kResultSlots = 2;

// How long finish waits, after the extract's batch has resolved, for the
// timeline value it set: a driver may signal the fence first.
constexpr std::uint64_t kSignalGraceNs = 1'000'000'000ull;

// Bytes a vertex arena needs to hold @p vertex_capacity VERTICES.
//
// Vertices, not triangles. The two were interchangeable while every triangle
// owned three private ones, and the whole point of vertex sharing is that they
// stop being: the arena is now sized by its own budget and the index run by the
// triangle count, independently.
std::uint64_t arena_bytes_for(std::uint64_t vertex_capacity) {
  return vertex_capacity * sizeof(Vertex);
}

// Bytes the index run needs to hold @p triangle_capacity triangles.
std::uint64_t index_run_bytes_for(std::uint64_t triangle_capacity) {
  return triangle_capacity * kIndicesPerTriangle * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
}

// The most VERTICES an arena may hold under a binding-range limit. Never zero
// for any conformant device -- Vulkan's guaranteed floor of 2^27 covers
// 2097152 vertices at 64 B each.
std::uint64_t max_vertices_for(std::uint64_t max_range) {
  return max_range / sizeof(Vertex);
}

// The most triangles an INDEX RUN may hold under the same limit. Not the whole
// triangle ceiling: the vertices those triangles need have to fit the arena
// too, which at three private vertices each is 16x tighter. plan_capacity takes
// the minimum of the two -- taking this one alone is what let a *predicted*
// capacity be rejected by ensure_output_buffers instead of clamped, which fails
// an extractor permanently (the density is recorded only on success, and a
// scan's active set only grows).
std::uint64_t max_triangles_for(std::uint64_t max_range) {
  return max_range / (kIndicesPerTriangle * sizeof(std::uint32_t));
}

// Stopwatch for the opt-in ExtractTimings: host wall clock alone. Reading the
// clock is cheap, but it is skipped entirely when the caller wants no
// measurement, so the untimed path costs one branch per phase. The device
// halves are the stage rows' (extract_device's metrics), tiled inside the
// submits the phases already make.
class PhaseClock {
 public:
  explicit PhaseClock(bool enabled) : enabled_(enabled) { restart(); }

  void restart() {
    if (enabled_) start_ = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  }

  // Milliseconds since the last restart, then restart for the next phase.
  double lap() {
    if (!enabled_) return 0.0;
    const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const double ms =
        std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - start_).count();
    start_ = now;
    return ms;
  }

 private:
  bool enabled_;
  std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point start_{};
};

}  // namespace

std::uint32_t MarchingCubes::plan_capacity(std::uint32_t num_active,
                                           std::uint64_t worst_case) const {
  // Predict from density rather than react to an overflow: the last extract
  // measured how many triangles an active block carries, and scaling that by
  // THIS call's active set moves the plan ahead of a growing surface. A purely
  // reactive plan (whatever the arena happens to hold) discovers every size
  // increase by overflowing, which throws a whole dispatch away each time.
  const std::uint64_t per_block =
      tris_per_block_ != 0 ? tris_per_block_ : kSeedTrisPerBlock;
  const std::uint64_t estimate =
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(num_active) * per_block;
  // Bounded above by the worst case and by nothing else. This is a *request*,
  // and ensure_output_buffers is the only thing that reads it: it keeps
  // whatever the slot already holds and grows only when the request is larger,
  // so a floor at the held capacity would change no allocation it makes.
  //
  // That floor is gone rather than repositioned, and its absence is the fix.
  // Floored at arena_capacity() this number depends on *which slot is
  // current*, so with a ring it read the slot just written while a different
  // one was about to be grown -- every extract then asked for 1.5x the last,
  // geometrically, with the measured density never getting a say (an iPad Pro
  // reached a 1.1 GB arena for 36904 triangles, 0.59% full, in a few hundred
  // remeshes). A purely positional invariant inside a 340-line function is one
  // reordering away from coming back; with the floor deleted the plan reads no
  // slot at all and cannot compound in any call order.
  //
  // Bounded below the device's binding limit too, and that is a *clamp rather
  // than a rejection* on purpose. This number is a guess -- a density measured
  // on the previous call, scaled by this one's active set -- so rejecting it
  // fails extracts whose real surface fits: on a driver at Vulkan's guaranteed
  // 2^27 the seed density plans 704000 triangles for 11000 blocks against a
  // ceiling of 699050, for a surface that emits ~660000 and would have been
  // fine. Worse, it failed *permanently*: tris_per_block_ is written only on
  // the success path, so the estimate never corrected, and a scan's active set
  // only grows, so every later extract recomputed the same rejected number.
  // Clamped instead, the dispatch runs, the kernel reports the field's true
  // total, and an arena that genuinely cannot fit is rejected by
  // ensure_output_buffers against that *measured* count -- which is what the
  // error has always claimed to mean.
  // BOTH output buffers bound the triangle count, and taking only the index
  // run's was the bug: the arena has to hold whatever vertices those triangles
  // need, which unshared is three each -- 16x tighter than the run's 12 bytes
  // per triangle. Left uncoupled, the plan could hand ensure_output_buffers a
  // vertex request 16x past the device limit, which it rejects rather than
  // clamps, and that rejection is permanent (see above).
  const std::uint64_t device_cap = std::min(
      max_triangles_for(max_storage_buffer_range_), triangles_fitting_arena());
  return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(
      std::min({estimate, worst_case, device_cap}));
}

std::uint64_t MarchingCubes::triangles_fitting_arena() const {
  // The inverse of plan_vertex_capacity: the most triangles whose vertices fit
  // one binding. Derived from the same density the plan uses, so the two agree
  // by construction and the plan can never ask for an arena the guard refuses.
  const std::uint64_t max_verts = max_vertices_for(max_storage_buffer_range_);
  if (!config_.share_vertices) {
    return max_verts / kIndicesPerTriangle;
  }
  const std::uint64_t per_1000 =
      verts_per_1000_tris_ != 0 ? verts_per_1000_tris_ : kSeedVertsPer1000;
  return max_verts * 1000 / per_1000;
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::claim_output_slot(const char* entry) {
  // Called once at the top of each extract, before anything is touched, with
  // `++generation_` as the very next statement. Both halves of that are
  // load-bearing and they pull in opposite directions, which is why they are
  // adjacent rather than merely ordered.
  //
  // Before the bump: refusing here must cost the caller nothing. This is the
  // path that protects slots a consumer is still reading, so a refused extract
  // has written no buffer, freed no allocation, and must leave every
  // outstanding DeviceMesh exactly as valid as it was. Bumping first would
  // break that on its own -- download()'s currency check would then refuse a
  // mesh whose slot this call deliberately did not touch, so the refusal meant
  // to protect the consumer's live mesh would instead retire it.
  //
  // Immediately before it: this advances slot_, and download() reads the
  // current slot on the strength of a *generation* comparison. Anything
  // fallible in between leaves a window where slot_ has moved and generation_
  // has not, so an outstanding DeviceMesh passes the currency check and is
  // copied out of a slot that may never have been sized, or from an older,
  // smaller arena once the ring has turned.
  //
  // Once per extract, not once per call, is structural now rather than
  // conditional: ensure_output_buffers runs twice when a call refits against
  // its measured triangle count, and advancing there would strand the first
  // dispatch's output in the previous slot. It also makes the refit's grow safe
  // for free -- the buffer it frees is one only this extract has written.
  if (slot_count_ == 1) {
    // One slot never moves, and the contract is what it always was: a
    // DeviceMesh is superseded by the next extract, and `generation` enforces
    // it.
    return {};
  }
  // Round-robin from the slot after the current one, so growth spreads evenly
  // over the ring and the oldest slot is tried first. It *scans* rather than
  // taking that one on faith: "the next slot is always the oldest" holds only
  // while every claim goes on to publish a mesh, and two paths do not -- an
  // extract that fails after claiming, and extract_host, which gives its slot
  // straight back once the copy is taken (free_slot_of). Both leave a free slot
  // behind the cursor, and assuming would refuse with one in hand.
  //
  // Everything downstream is free to overwrite the slot this picks, and a grow
  // will *free* it outright, so it must have been released first.
  std::uint64_t oldest = 0;
  for (std::size_t i = 1; i <= slot_count_; ++i) {
    const std::size_t candidate = (slot_ + i) % slot_count_;
    if (slots_[candidate].generation <= released_through_) {
      slot_ = candidate;
      return {};
    }
    if (oldest == 0 || slots_[candidate].generation < oldest) {
      oldest = slots_[candidate].generation;
    }
  }
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(
      std::string(entry) +
      ": every output slot is still outstanding (oldest is generation " +
      std::to_string(oldest) + ", released through " +
      std::to_string(released_through_) +
      "); call release_through as meshes are finished with, or configure "
      "more slots than the consumer keeps in flight");
}

void MarchingCubes::free_slot_of(std::uint64_t generation) noexcept {
  // Give one slot back without moving released_through_. That distinction is
  // the whole reason this exists beside release_through: the high-water mark is
  // the *consumer's* statement about what it has finished reading, so using it
  // to retire a slot this class allocated for itself would also mark every
  // older slot released -- including one holding a DeviceMesh an extract_device
  // caller is still drawing out of, on the same extractor.
  //
  // Generations are pre-incremented from 0, so 0 is "never written" and matches
  // every untouched slot; refuse it rather than freeing the whole ring.
  if (generation == 0) return;
  for (Slot& slot : slots_) {
    if (slot.generation == generation) slot.generation = 0;
  }
}

void MarchingCubes::release_through(std::uint64_t generation) noexcept {
  // Monotonic: an older report never un-releases a slot. A consumer finishing
  // frames out of order, or reporting a stale value after a newer one, would
  // otherwise make a freed slot look busy again -- and, worse, could not make a
  // busy one look free, so the failure would be a stall rather than corruption.
  // Cheap to make impossible either way.
  released_through_ = std::max(released_through_, generation);
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::ensure_indirect_command() {
  if (!indirect().valid()) {
    // INDIRECT_BUFFER beside STORAGE_BUFFER: the kernel counts into field 0
    // through the storage binding, and a renderer issues
    // vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect from the very same bytes. Both unconditional
    // rather than config-gated -- 20 bytes, and a consumer that never draws
    // indirectly pays a usage bit nobody reads. The queue families *are* the
    // consumer's, though: a renderer on a second family reads this buffer as
    // surely as it reads the arena, so it takes the same sharing treatment.
    VKC_ASSIGN(
        indirect(),
        core::device_storage_buffer(
            *allocator_, kIndirectBufferBytes,
            VK_BUFFER_USAGE_INDIRECT_BUFFER_BIT | config_.extra_indirect_usage,
            config_.queue_families, config_.queue_family_count));
    name_slot_buffer(indirect(), "mesh.indirect[%u]");
  }
  return {};
}

void MarchingCubes::disarm_indirect_command() {
  if (!indirect().valid()) return;
  // Zero, not clamped to the arena. A clamp bounds how many indices a draw
  // READS; it says nothing about their VALUES, and on every path that reaches
  // here the values are the problem: a triangle whose vertex claim overflowed
  // is counted but never written, so its three index slots hold whatever the
  // VMA block last did. Those are arbitrary uint32s indexing a
  // 64-byte-stride arena with
  // robustBufferAccess enabled nowhere -- an out-of-bounds device read, i.e. a
  // GPU fault, where the honest statement is "this slot has no drawable
  // geometry".
  //
  // Field 0 only: the other four are still the drawable values the reset wrote,
  // so the command stays well-formed and simply draws nothing. Its own batch,
  // and best effort: every caller is already returning a failure, and one the
  // device refuses leaves nothing drawable anyway.
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  if (batch.fill(indirect(), 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u).ok()) {
    (void)batch.submit();
  }
}

std::uint32_t MarchingCubes::plan_vertex_capacity(
    std::uint32_t triangle_capacity) const {
  std::uint64_t estimate = 0;
  if (!config_.share_vertices) {
    // Exact, not estimated: every triangle owns three private vertices, and the
    // kernel writes them at `tri * 3` rather than through a counter, so this is
    // the budget the dispatch *requires* rather than one it can overflow.
    estimate =
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(triangle_capacity) * kIndicesPerTriangle;
  } else {
    const std::uint64_t per_1000 =
        verts_per_1000_tris_ != 0 ? verts_per_1000_tris_ : kSeedVertsPer1000;
    // Rounded up, so a non-zero triangle budget never plans zero vertices.
    estimate =
        (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(triangle_capacity) * per_1000 + 999) / 1000;
  }
  // Clamped -- for BOTH modes, which is the fix. The unshared branch used to
  // clamp only to uint32, so a triangle plan that passed the index run's
  // (16x looser) device limit produced a vertex request ensure_output_buffers
  // then REJECTED, permanently: the 2026-08-04 rule is that a predicted
  // quantity is clamped and only a measured one is rejected. plan_capacity
  // keeps the triangle plan inside triangles_fitting_arena(), so in practice
  // this clamp is already satisfied; it is here so neither can drift into
  // rejecting a plan on its own.
  //
  // Never zero: a capacity of 0 drops every vertex and refits forever.
  return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(
      std::min(std::max<std::uint64_t>(estimate, 1),
               max_vertices_for(max_storage_buffer_range_)));
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::ensure_output_buffers(
    std::uint32_t triangle_capacity, std::uint32_t vertex_capacity,
    const char* entry, core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  // Guard the REQUESTED capacity against the device's binding limit before any
  // growth headroom is added, so a surface that legitimately fits is never
  // rejected because the growth policy overshot.
  if (arena_bytes_for(vertex_capacity) > max_storage_buffer_range_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) + ": a vertex arena for " +
        std::to_string(vertex_capacity) +
        " vertices exceeds the device maxStorageBufferRange");
  }
  // The index run has its own limit, not implied by the arena's: sharing
  // shrinks the vertices and leaves the triangles alone, so on a heavily shared
  // surface the run is what reaches the ceiling first.
  if (index_run_bytes_for(triangle_capacity) > max_storage_buffer_range_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) + ": an index run for " +
        std::to_string(triangle_capacity) +
        " triangles exceeds the device maxStorageBufferRange");
  }
  // No slot stamp here, deliberately. Marking the slot outstanding is the
  // publishing return's job (it sits beside `device_mesh.generation`), because
  // the stamp says "a consumer holds a mesh in this slot" and only a path that
  // hands one out can make that true. Stamping here instead made every failure
  // exit below -- and the dispatch, the refit, and the out_of_memory return
  // above the caller -- leave a slot marked with a generation no DeviceMesh
  // ever carried, which nothing could then release: slot_count such failures
  // and the extractor refuses forever, quoting generations it never handed out.
  //
  // The command's buffer, which every dispatch resets before it counts: 28
  // bytes, against an arena whose stale tail is never read (indexCount bounds
  // the readback).
  VKC_TRY(ensure_indirect_command());

  // Two buffers, two budgets, and each is grown ON ITS OWN.
  //
  // They used to be released and reallocated together, justified by
  // arena_capacity() being derived from the ARENA's size -- so dropping the
  // arena was what marked the pair unsized. That stopped being true when vertex
  // sharing broke the three-per-triangle identity and arena_capacity() moved to
  // the index run, and keeping the coupling then cost real memory: a
  // triangle-only overflow grew the arena to 1.5x what it ALREADY HELD, having
  // needed no growth at all, and the next such grow multiplied the inflated
  // value again -- numerically the ring runaway the 2026-08-03
  // slot-independence decision exists to prevent, reintroduced one buffer over.
  // It also refaulted the arena, the phase DECISIONS.md measured at 49.8 ms of
  // a 55 ms extract.
  const bool grow_index_run =
      !index_run().valid() || triangle_capacity > arena_capacity();
  const bool grow_arena =
      !arena().valid() || vertex_capacity > arena_vertex_capacity();
  if (!grow_index_run && !grow_arena) {
    return {};  // the steady state -- no allocation at all
  }
  // Grow geometrically rather than to the exact request: the active set climbs
  // steadily through a scan, so exact sizing would reallocate (and re-fault)
  // this large buffer on most frames. The headroom multiplies the LARGER of
  // the request and what is held, so a refit to a measured count gets headroom
  // too (it is the request that a growing scan will outgrow next). Fall back to
  // the exact request whenever the headroom would not fit -- the request itself
  // already passed the guard above, so a surface that legitimately fits is
  // never rejected by an overshoot. Both tests run in 64-bit *before*
  // narrowing: 1.5x a near-uint32 capacity does not fit a uint32, and
  // truncating first could turn an over-large request into a small one that
  // passes the byte check.
  // Only a buffer that is actually short is grown; the other keeps exactly what
  // it holds. `std::max(request, held)` would be the same thing on this path --
  // a buffer only reaches here when the request exceeds what it holds -- so the
  // request alone is what the headroom multiplies, and neither target reads the
  // other buffer's capacity.
  const std::uint64_t grown_tris =
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(triangle_capacity) * 3 / 2;
  const bool tri_headroom_fits =
      grown_tris <= 0xFFFFFFFFull &&
      index_run_bytes_for(grown_tris) <= max_storage_buffer_range_;
  const std::uint32_t target_capacity =
      !grow_index_run
          ? arena_capacity()
          : (tri_headroom_fits ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grown_tris)
                               : triangle_capacity);
  const std::uint64_t grown_verts =
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(vertex_capacity) * 3 / 2;
  const bool vert_headroom_fits =
      grown_verts <= 0xFFFFFFFFull &&
      arena_bytes_for(grown_verts) <= max_storage_buffer_range_;
  const std::uint32_t target_vertex_capacity =
      !grow_arena
          ? arena_vertex_capacity()
          : (vert_headroom_fits ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grown_verts)
                                : vertex_capacity);

  // Drop a buffer BEFORE allocating its replacement, so a grow asks the driver
  // for one arena rather than two. VMA pools an emptied block instead of
  // returning it (see tests/core_memory_stats_test.cpp), so this holds against
  // the *driver* for an arena large enough to get a dedicated allocation; a
  // small one lives in a pooled block that VMA keeps, and process RSS can still
  // show both across the grow. Failing here leaves the extractor with no arena
  // rather than a capacity claiming a buffer that was never allocated.
  //
  // These assignments call vmaDestroyBuffer *immediately* -- there is no fence
  // wait and no deferred retire. Safe for this tier's own work, whose batches
  // are fence-blocked at submit, and safe for an external consumer only because
  // the slot was released first (MarchingCubesConfig::slot_count).
  core::Buffer grown_arena;
  core::Buffer indices_buf;
  if (grow_arena) {
    arena() = core::Buffer{};
    // config_ is applied on every grow, not just the first, so the consumer's
    // usage survives a reallocation (see MarchingCubesConfig).
    VKC_ASSIGN(
        grown_arena,
        core::device_storage_buffer(
            *allocator_,
            static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(arena_bytes_for(target_vertex_capacity)),
            config_.extra_vertex_usage, config_.queue_families,
            config_.queue_family_count));
  }
  if (grow_index_run) {
    index_run() = core::Buffer{};
    VKC_ASSIGN(
        indices_buf,
        core::device_storage_buffer(
            *allocator_,
            static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(index_run_bytes_for(target_capacity)),
            config_.extra_index_usage, config_.queue_families,
            config_.queue_family_count));
    if (!config_.share_vertices) {
      // The kernel writes vertices at `tri * 3`, so the run IS the identity
      // 0,1,2,..., uploaded once per grow; download() regenerates it rather
      // than reading it back. With sharing only the kernel knows the mapping,
      // and it writes the run itself.
      //
      // Submitted here, before the run is committed below, not recorded into
      // @p batch: nothing refills a run that has been committed, so a batch
      // that failed after committing it would leave the draw indexing
      // uninitialized memory for the extractor's lifetime.
      std::vector<std::uint32_t> identity(
          static_cast<std::size_t>(target_capacity) * kIndicesPerTriangle);
      std::iota(identity.begin(), identity.end(), std::uint32_t{0});
      core::CommandBatch fill(*device_, *allocator_);
      VKC_TRY(fill.upload(indices_buf, 0, identity.data(),
                          index_run_bytes_for(target_capacity), stage));
      VKC_TRY(fill.submit());
    }
  }
  // Committed after both allocations, so a failure on the second cannot leave
  // one buffer resized against the other's capacity.
  if (grow_arena) arena() = std::move(grown_arena);
  if (grow_index_run) index_run() = std::move(indices_buf);
  // Each buffer named only where its own handle changed. Naming is idempotent
  // and cheap, but this runs per extract, and a driver call per buffer per
  // frame to re-state an unchanged name is pure overhead in the hot path.
  if (grow_arena) name_slot_buffer(arena(), "mesh.arena[%u]");
  if (grow_index_run) name_slot_buffer(index_run(), "mesh.index_run[%u]");
  return {};
}

void MarchingCubes::name_slot_buffer(const core::Buffer& buffer,
                                     const char* form) const noexcept {
  if (device_ == nullptr || !buffer.valid()) {
    return;
  }
  // The slot index belongs in the name: the ring hands the consumer one slot
  // while the next extract writes another, so a capture showing "mesh.arena"
  // three times over would not say which generation it had caught.
  //
  // Cast rather than %zu: slot_ is a std::size_t and the forms say %u, so the
  // pair must be made to agree. This direction, because the value is a ring
  // index bounded by kMaxSlots and %zu's worst case (20 digits) would not fit
  // the buffer below.
  char name[32];
  std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), form, static_cast<unsigned>(slot_));
  device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                           core::debug_object_handle(buffer.handle()), name);
}

core::Result<MarchingCubes> MarchingCubes::create(
    core::Device& device, core::Allocator& allocator,
    const MarchingCubesConfig& config) {
  VKC_TRY(check_device_requirements(device, "MarchingCubes::create"));
  // Reject the one usage bit this repo's Device provably cannot honour, here
  // where the caller supplied it rather than inside the first extract's arena
  // grow (AGENTS.md's "validate before creating"). Device::create never enables
  // bufferDeviceAddress, and the allocator is built without
  // VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_BUFFER_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT, so this bit trips a VMA
  // assert in a debug build and drops VK_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT in
  // NDEBUG. Other bits are gated by features/extensions an adopted device may
  // legitimately have enabled, so they are the embedder's call, not ours.
  const VkBufferUsageFlags unsupported =
      VK_BUFFER_USAGE_SHADER_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT;
  // All three output buffers, not two: the indirect command takes consumer
  // usage the same way the arena and index run do, so leaving it out of the
  // guard would let the bit through on the one buffer nothing else checks.
  if (((config.extra_vertex_usage | config.extra_index_usage |
        config.extra_indirect_usage) &
       unsupported) != 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "MarchingCubes::create: VK_BUFFER_USAGE_SHADER_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT is "
        "not supported -- Device::create does not enable bufferDeviceAddress");
  }

  // Caught here rather than at the first arena grow, where it would surface as
  // a buffer-creation failure several frames into a scan.
  VKC_TRY(core::check_queue_family_count(config.queue_family_count,
                                         "MarchingCubes::create"));

  if (config.slot_count == 0 || config.slot_count > kMaxSlots) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "MarchingCubes::create: slot_count must be 1.." +
        std::to_string(kMaxSlots) + " (got " +
        std::to_string(config.slot_count) +
        "); 1 is the default and the single-arena behaviour, and the ceiling "
        "is what the slot array holds");
  }

  MarchingCubes mc;
  mc.device_ = &device;
  mc.allocator_ = &allocator;

  // Cache the 1-D dispatch's groupCountX ceiling so an extract can split a
  // large active set across dispatches, plus the storage-buffer binding limit
  // so it can reject a worst-case vertex arena that would exceed it before
  // the allocation fails opaquely.
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device.physical_device(), &props);
  mc.max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  mc.max_storage_buffer_range_ = props.limits.maxStorageBufferRange;
  mc.config_ = config;
  // Sized once and never resized: slot_ indexes it on every extract, and the
  // buffers are filled lazily by the first extract that needs each one, so an
  // unused slot costs a Buffer's worth of null handles rather than an arena.
  mc.slot_count_ = config.slot_count;

  // The two sparse variants agree on bindings 0..7 -- tables (persistent) +
  // the per-extract active blocks / hash entries / tsdf / weight / color /
  // vertices / command. The sharing variant adds 8, the index run it writes
  // itself; the default one has no index-run binding because its run is the
  // identity the host filled on the last grow. The count below and the two
  // shaders' `binding =` literals are the only statement of this, so they are
  // maintained together.
  // KernelSetBuilder (core/vulkan/compute_kernel.hpp) builds each
  // layout + pipeline and allocates its set from a shared pool sized to the
  // exact descriptor total.
  //
  // ONE of the two sparse variants is built, chosen here rather than branched
  // per dispatch. Sharing needs ~8 KiB of `shared` arrays, and a `shared` array
  // is reserved when the pipeline is created whatever a push constant later
  // says: folding both into one kernel made the default path pay sharing's
  // threadgroup budget (44 B -> 8452 B, which bounds residency to 3 workgroups
  // on Apple's ~32 KiB and to 1 at Vulkan's guaranteed 16 KiB floor) and its
  // per-corner vertex atomic, for a feature it does not use.
  VkPushConstantRange push_sparse{};
  push_sparse.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  push_sparse.offset = 0;
  push_sparse.size = sizeof(SparsePushConstants);
  VkPushConstantRange push_args = push_sparse;
  push_args.size = sizeof(ArgsPush);
  VkPushConstantRange push_finalize = push_sparse;
  push_finalize.size = sizeof(FinalizePush);
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(device);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(
      mc.kernel_sparse_,
      config.share_vertices ? "marching_cubes_sparse_shared"
                            : "marching_cubes_sparse",
      config.share_vertices ? vgrid_marching_cubes_sparse_shared_comp_spv
                            : vgrid_marching_cubes_sparse_comp_spv,
      config.share_vertices ? vgrid_marching_cubes_sparse_shared_comp_spv_size
                            : vgrid_marching_cubes_sparse_comp_spv_size,
      config.share_vertices ? 9 : 8, &push_sparse));
  // The sizing: count, gate, the draw command, the slices and the state; the
  // finalize: the draw command, the state and the result.
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(mc.args_kernel_, "mc_args", vgrid_mc_args_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_mc_args_comp_spv_size, 5, &push_args));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(mc.finalize_kernel_, "mc_finalize", vgrid_mc_finalize_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_mc_finalize_comp_spv_size, 3, &push_finalize));
  VKC_ASSIGN(mc.pool_, kb.build());
  VKC_ASSIGN(mc.state_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, 2 * sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  mc.device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                              core::debug_object_handle(mc.state_.handle()),
                              "mesh.extract_state");
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::TimelineSemaphore timeline,
             core::TimelineSemaphore::create(device));
  mc.timeline_ = std::make_unique<core::TimelineSemaphore>(std::move(timeline));

  // Upload the lookup tables once and bind them at set binding 0 of the one
  // kernel this extractor built. The constexpr header arrays are the single
  // source; flatten them into the shader block layout.
  // Device-local, like everything the kernel reads, and filled in one batch
  // with the two dummies below.
  core::CommandBatch batch(device, allocator);
  VKC_ASSIGN(mc.tables_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, sizeof(McTables)));
  McTables host_tables;
  std::memcpy(host_tables.tri_table, kTriTable, sizeof(kTriTable));
  std::memcpy(host_tables.corner_offset, kCornerOffset, sizeof(kCornerOffset));
  std::memcpy(host_tables.edge_to_vert, kEdgeToVert, sizeof(kEdgeToVert));
  VKC_TRY(batch.upload(mc.tables_, 0, &host_tables, sizeof(McTables)));
  mc.device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                              core::debug_object_handle(mc.tables_.handle()),
                              "mesh.mc_tables");
  mc.kernel_sparse_.set.write_storage_buffer(0, mc.tables_.handle(), 0,
                                             VK_WHOLE_SIZE);

  // A 1-element dummy for the sparse kernel's color slot when a grid carries no
  // color attribute; bound now so binding 5 is always valid, overwritten with a
  // real color buffer per extract when one exists.
  VKC_ASSIGN(mc.color_dummy_,
             core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(mc.color_dummy_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u));
  mc.device_->set_object_name(
      VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
      core::debug_object_handle(mc.color_dummy_.handle()), "mesh.color_dummy");
  mc.kernel_sparse_.set.write_storage_buffer(5, mc.color_dummy_.handle(), 0,
                                             VK_WHOLE_SIZE);

  VKC_TRY(batch.submit());

  return mc;
}

core::Result<Mesh> MarchingCubes::extract_host(volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                               float iso,
                                               ExtractTimings* timings) {
  // Straight to the implementation rather than through extract_device, for the
  // name alone: everything below the entry points reports under whichever one
  // the caller actually called, and borrowing extract_device's would tell a
  // host-only caller to release a slot it never saw.
  VKC_ASSIGN(
      const DeviceMesh device_mesh,
      extract_device_impl(grid, iso, nullptr, timings, nullptr, kEntryHost));
  // The host copy is part of this call's readback, so it belongs in the phase
  // that names it -- the device path's readback_ms is near zero, its command
  // read riding the dispatch's submit, which is right for that entry point but
  // would leave the host path's ~45 MB copy uncounted in
  // ExtractTimings::total_ms.
  PhaseClock download_clock(timings != nullptr);
  core::Result<Mesh> mesh = download(device_mesh);
  if (timings != nullptr) timings->readback_ms += download_clock.lap();
  // This call's whole product is the host copy, so the slot the extract
  // claimed and stamped is finished with as soon as download() has run -- and
  // given back whether it succeeded or not, since a failure that stranded the
  // slot would starve the ring just as surely. A host-only caller never sees a
  // generation (the return type carries none), so it cannot honour the release
  // contract itself; this is what keeps it off that contract entirely.
  //
  // free_slot_of, not release_through: this slot is the only one to give back.
  // The high-water mark is the consumer's statement about what *it* has
  // finished reading, so using it here would also retire every older slot --
  // including one holding a DeviceMesh an extract_device caller on this same
  // extractor is still drawing out of, whose arena the next grow would then
  // vmaDestroyBuffer under a live draw.
  free_slot_of(device_mesh.generation);
  return mesh;
}

core::Result<Mesh> MarchingCubes::download(
    const DeviceMesh& device_mesh) const {
  // Moved-from, like both extract entry points -- and this one needs it most.
  // The defaulted moves reset every *owned* member (Buffer and the pipeline
  // wrappers each self-empty), but generation_ and slot_ are plain scalars a
  // defaulted move copies rather than zeroes, and a DeviceMesh holds raw
  // VkBuffer values copied out at extract time, so valid() is still true on it.
  // The currency check below would therefore pass on a moved-from extractor and
  // the readback would name an empty buffer. Guarding here rather than
  // hand-writing the moves keeps the rule-of-zero note above intact -- the
  // scalars are unobservable once every entry point gates on valid().
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "MarchingCubes::download: moved-from");
  }
  // An empty mesh copies to an empty Mesh without touching the buffers, which
  // a grid with no active blocks never even allocated.
  if (device_mesh.empty()) {
    return Mesh{};
  }
  // Only this extractor's newest extract may be downloaded, and the check is by
  // generation, NOT by buffer handle. With one slot the arena is grow-only and
  // reused in place, so a superseded view names the very same VkBuffer as the
  // live one and a handle comparison would accept it, handing back the newer
  // extract's geometry under this view's stale counts. With a ring it is the
  // other way round -- a superseded view names a *different* buffer -- and the
  // generation check is what makes the unqualified arena() below correct: an
  // extract advances slot_ and generation_ in the same breath and nothing moves
  // slot_ again until the next claim, so "this mesh is the current generation"
  // and "this mesh lives in the current slot" are the same statement. That is
  // why those two lines are adjacent: anything fallible between them opens a
  // window where they disagree and this memcpy reads the wrong slot -- one that
  // may never have been sized. A DeviceMesh does not carry
  // its slot, so that invariant is the only thing tying the copy below to the
  // right buffer. Widening this to accept an older generation therefore means
  // indexing slots_ by it, not just relaxing the comparison.
  if (device_mesh.generation != generation_ || !device_mesh.valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "MarchingCubes::download: the DeviceMesh is not this extractor's "
        "current extract (superseded by a later one, or from another "
        "extractor)");
  }
  Mesh mesh;
  const auto vertex_count = static_cast<std::size_t>(device_mesh.vertex_count);
  const auto index_count =
      static_cast<std::size_t>(device_mesh.triangle_count) *
      kIndicesPerTriangle;
  mesh.vertices.resize(vertex_count);
  mesh.indices.resize(index_count);
  // Copied back through a batch, never read through a mapping: the buffers are
  // device-local, and a host read of VRAM is uncached (6.6 s for this mesh
  // from BAR memory on an RTX 5090, the 2026-09-28 residency decision). A
  // batch per buffer, so no staging buffer is larger than a device buffer that
  // was already allocated.
  if (vertex_count > 0) {
    core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
    VKC_TRY(batch.readback(arena(), 0,
                           VkDeviceSize(vertex_count) * sizeof(Vertex),
                           mesh.vertices.data()));
    VKC_TRY(batch.submit());
  }
  if (index_count > 0) {
    if (config_.share_vertices) {
      // READ BACK. A shared vertex is referenced by several triangles from
      // several cells, so the mapping is a property of the dispatch and only
      // the kernel knows it -- there is no run to regenerate.
      core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
      VKC_TRY(batch.readback(index_run(), 0,
                             VkDeviceSize(index_count) * sizeof(std::uint32_t),
                             mesh.indices.data()));
      VKC_TRY(batch.submit());
    } else {
      // Regenerated, not read back: the default kernel writes each triangle's
      // three vertices at `tri * 3`, so the run is the identity 0,1,2,...
      std::iota(mesh.indices.begin(), mesh.indices.end(), std::uint32_t{0});
    }
  }
  return mesh;
}

core::Result<DeviceMesh> MarchingCubes::extract_device(
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, float iso, ExtractTimings* timings,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  return extract_device_impl(grid, iso, nullptr, timings, metrics,
                             kEntryDevice);
}

core::Result<DeviceMesh> MarchingCubes::extract_device(
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, float iso,
    const volume::DeviceBlockList& blocks, ExtractTimings* timings,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  return extract_device_impl(grid, iso, &blocks, timings, metrics,
                             kEntryDevice);
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::check_grid(const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                       const char* entry) const {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(entry) + ": moved-from");
  }
  if (!grid.valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(entry) +
                                          ": grid is moved-from");
  }
  // The grid must carry the float tsdf + weight the sparse kernel samples; the
  // uint32 color attribute is optional (its absence -> opaque-white vertices).
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView tsdf,
             grid.attribute(volume::kTsdfAttribute));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView weight,
             grid.attribute(volume::kWeightAttribute));
  if (tsdf.element_size != sizeof(float) ||
      weight.element_size != sizeof(float)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) + ": tsdf/weight must be float attributes");
  }
  if (grid.has_attribute(volume::kColorAttribute)) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView color,
               grid.attribute(volume::kColorAttribute));
    if (color.element_size != sizeof(std::uint32_t)) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          std::string(entry) + ": color must be a uint32 attribute");
    }
  }
  const auto vpb = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().voxels_per_block);
  // Sharing keeps one vertex slot per cell per axis in THREADGROUP memory,
  // which needs a compile-time size, so the kernel's table is sized for
  // block_size 8 -- the only shape any in-tree caller uses. Refused rather than
  // silently ignored: the kernel would index past the end of a shared array,
  // which no validation layer sees and which reads back as a plausible mesh.
  // Checked here rather than in create() because the grid, and therefore the
  // block size, only arrives with the extract.
  //
  // ABOVE the empty-set return, not below it, and that ordering is load-bearing
  // now that a caller supplies the set: an empty active set used to mean an
  // empty map, so the two could not both happen, but an empty CULL is a routine
  // per-frame outcome. Checked below, this misconfiguration would surface only
  // on the frames the camera happens to see geometry -- reporting Status::ok
  // while pointed at nothing and InvalidArgument a frame later, which reads as
  // the camera move having caused it. It is a property of the config and the
  // grid, so it answers the same on every frame.
  if (config_.share_vertices && vpb > kMaxSharedCells) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) + ": share_vertices needs voxels_per_block <= " +
        std::to_string(kMaxSharedCells) + " (this grid has " +
        std::to_string(vpb) + ")");
  }
  return {};
}

void MarchingCubes::drop_pending() noexcept {
  // The claimed slot was never stamped, so it is as claimable as it was.
  pending_generation_ = 0;
  pending_signal_ = 0;
  pending_results_ = core::HostSlot();
  pending_list_ = nullptr;
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::bind_sparse(const volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
                                        const core::Buffer& list,
                                        std::uint32_t bound,
                                        const char* entry) {
  // The hash entries bind straight from the map, and the kernel resolves each
  // block's 2x2x2 neighbourhood itself -- so the host builds nothing here.
  // Bound with their real size rather than VK_WHOLE_SIZE, and range-checked:
  // this is the one binding whose buffer ANOTHER tier sized (an entry a slot,
  // doubled by every VoxelHashMap::resize), so the mesh tier cannot reason
  // about it the way it does about its own arena.
  const VkDeviceSize entries_bytes =
      volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer_size(grid.map());
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(
      (std::string(entry) + ": hash entries").c_str(), entries_bytes,
      static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(max_storage_buffer_range_)));
  // The list, bound to the blocks the push constant names, at least one entry
  // so an empty list still binds a range.
  const VkDeviceSize list_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(std::max<std::uint32_t>(bound, 1)) *
      sizeof(volume::BlockIndex);
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(
      (std::string(entry) + ": active blocks").c_str(), list_bytes,
      static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(max_storage_buffer_range_)));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView tsdf,
             grid.attribute(volume::kTsdfAttribute));
  VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView weight,
             grid.attribute(volume::kWeightAttribute));
  const core::Buffer* color = &color_dummy_;
  if (grid.has_attribute(volume::kColorAttribute)) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(const volume::AttributeView view,
               grid.attribute(volume::kColorAttribute));
    color = view.buffer;
  }
  const core::DescriptorSet& set = kernel_sparse_.set;
  set.write_storage_buffer(1, list.handle(), 0, list_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(
      2, volume::VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer(grid.map()), 0,
      entries_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(3, tsdf.buffer->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(4, weight.buffer->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(5, color->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  // Both output bindings name the claimed slot's buffers, so both move when
  // slot_ does. The sharing kernel's ninth binding is the index run it writes
  // itself, because a shared vertex is referenced by several triangles from
  // several cells and only the kernel knows which; the default kernel's run is
  // the identity the host filled on the last grow.
  set.write_storage_buffer(6, arena().handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(7, indirect().handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  if (config_.share_vertices) {
    set.write_storage_buffer(8, index_run().handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status MarchingCubes::record_body(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, float iso,
    const core::Buffer& list, const core::Buffer* count_buffer,
    std::uint32_t bound, std::uint32_t expected_blocks,
    const volume::DeviceCount* gate, core::GpuStageScope* stage,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics, ExtractTimings* timings, const char* entry) {
  PhaseClock clock(timings != nullptr);
  // The arena is sized to what the surface should emit, not to the
  // 5-triangles-per-cell worst case: the last extract's density scaled by the
  // blocks expected, which reads no slot, so it cannot compound across the
  // ring (plan_capacity). Correctness does not depend on the guess: the kernel
  // counts every triangle and drops those past the capacity, so an undersized
  // arena is detected by the finalize and refitted at finish. At least one
  // triangle, so every buffer exists for an empty set too.
  const auto vpb = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().voxels_per_block);
  const std::uint64_t worst_case =
      std::uint64_t(expected_blocks) * vpb * kMaxTrisPerCell;
  const std::uint32_t capacity =
      std::max(plan_capacity(expected_blocks, worst_case), 1u);
  // A grow's identity fill is a submit of its own, the stage's alone.
  VKC_TRY(ensure_output_buffers(capacity, plan_vertex_capacity(capacity), entry,
                                stage));
  if (timings != nullptr) timings->arena_alloc_ms = clock.lap();
  core::GpuStageScope dispatch(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..dispatch");
  VKC_TRY(bind_sparse(grid, list, bound, entry));
  if (results_ == nullptr) {
    core::HostRingDesc desc;
    desc.slot_bytes = sizeof(McResults);
    desc.slots = kResultSlots;
    desc.name = "mesh.extract_results";
    VKC_ASSIGN(results_, core::HostRing::create(*device_, *allocator_, desc));
  }
  core::Result<core::HostSlot> claimed = results_->claim(sizeof(McResults));
  VKC_CHECK(claimed.ok(),
            "MarchingCubes: the last extract's batch has resolved and its "
            "claim was dropped, so a result slot is free");
  // A workgroup a block, in slices for the bound.
  const std::uint32_t per_dispatch =
      volumetric_kit::grid::detail::groups_per_dispatch(max_workgroup_count_x_);
  const std::uint32_t dispatches =
      volumetric_kit::grid::detail::slice_count(bound, 1, per_dispatch);
  const VkDeviceSize slice_bytes =
      VkDeviceSize(dispatches) * sizeof(VkDispatchIndirectCommand);
  if (slices_.size() < slice_bytes) {
    // This extractor's last batch has resolved, so none reads it.
    VKC_ASSIGN(slices_, core::device_storage_buffer(
                            *allocator_, slice_bytes,
                            VK_BUFFER_USAGE_INDIRECT_BUFFER_BIT));
    device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                             core::debug_object_handle(slices_.handle()),
                             "mesh.extract_slices");
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const VkBuffer result,
             batch.output(*claimed, 0, sizeof(McResults)));
  const core::DescriptorSet& args = args_kernel_.set;
  args.write_storage_buffer(
      0, count_buffer != nullptr ? count_buffer->handle() : state_.handle(), 0,
      VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  args.write_storage_buffer(
      1, gate != nullptr ? gate->buffer->handle() : state_.handle(), 0,
      VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  args.write_storage_buffer(2, indirect().handle(), 0, kIndirectBufferBytes);
  args.write_storage_buffer(3, slices_.handle(), 0, slice_bytes);
  args.write_storage_buffer(4, state_.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  const core::DescriptorSet& finalize = finalize_kernel_.set;
  finalize.write_storage_buffer(0, indirect().handle(), 0,
                                kIndirectBufferBytes);
  finalize.write_storage_buffer(1, state_.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  finalize.write_storage_buffer(2, result, 0, sizeof(McResults));
  if (timings != nullptr) timings->descriptor_ms = clock.lap();

  const ArgsPush sizing{
      count_buffer != nullptr ? 0u : kNoWord,
      gate != nullptr ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gate->offset / 4) : kNoWord,
      bound, per_dispatch, dispatches};
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch(args_kernel_, &sizing, sizeof(sizing), 1,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, &dispatch));
  // One workgroup per block, not one thread per voxel: the kernel resolves
  // the block's 2x2x2 neighbourhood into shared memory, which only works when
  // every thread in the group belongs to the same block. Each block reserves
  // its own output range, so the slices' order does not matter, and the
  // slices hold exactly the blocks counted, so the bound the push names is
  // never reached past them.
  const volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices blocks{
      &slices_, 0, dispatches, per_dispatch, 1};
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(
      batch, kernel_sparse_,
      sparse_push(grid, iso, bound, usable_triangle_capacity(),
                  arena_vertex_capacity()),
      blocks, &dispatch));
  const FinalizePush checks{usable_triangle_capacity(), arena_vertex_capacity(),
                            config_.share_vertices ? 1u : 0u};
  VKC_TRY(batch.dispatch(finalize_kernel_, &checks, sizeof(checks), 1,
                         max_workgroup_count_x_, &dispatch));
  if (timings != nullptr) timings->dispatch_ms = clock.lap();
  pending_generation_ = generation_;
  pending_results_ = std::move(*claimed);
  pending_list_ = &list;
  pending_iso_ = iso;
  return {};
}

core::Result<PendingExtract> MarchingCubes::record_extract(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
    std::uint32_t expected_blocks, const volume::DeviceCount* gate, float iso,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  // An extract recorded and never finished gives its claim back first, so a
  // dropped token costs no slot.
  drop_pending();
  // The first timed call makes the timer, so an extractor nobody times holds
  // no query pool: a device layered on Metal backs each with one of its few
  // counter sample buffers. Then the row, before any refusal.
  if (metrics != nullptr && valid() && !gpu_timer_.valid()) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(gpu_timer_, core::GpuTimer::create(*device_));
  }
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "marching cubes");
  VKC_TRY(check_grid(grid, kEntryRecord));
  if (gate != nullptr) {
    constexpr VkDeviceSize word_bytes = sizeof(std::uint32_t);
    if (gate->buffer == nullptr || gate->offset % word_bytes != 0 ||
        gate->buffer->size() < word_bytes ||
        gate->offset > gate->buffer->size() - word_bytes) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          std::string(kEntryRecord) +
          ": the gate has no complete aligned word");
    }
    VKC_TRY(core::StorageInput(*gate->buffer)
                .check(kEntryRecord, gate->offset + word_bytes));
    // The descriptor binds the whole buffer. This also keeps the word index
    // representable in ArgsPush and below the shader's kNoWord sentinel.
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(kEntryRecord, gate->buffer->size(),
                                             max_storage_buffer_range_));
  }
  // Claim and bump before anything is recorded, as every extract does
  // (claim_output_slot): a refusal costs the caller nothing.
  VKC_TRY(claim_output_slot(kEntryRecord));
  ++generation_;
  volume::RecordedBlockList list;
  {
    core::GpuStageScope compact(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..compact");
    VKC_ASSIGN(list, grid.map().record_compaction(batch, nullptr, &compact));
  }
  VKC_TRY(record_body(batch, grid, iso, *list.buffer, list.count,
                      static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().num_blocks),
                      expected_blocks, gate, &stage, metrics, nullptr,
                      kEntryRecord));
  pending_signal_ = ++timeline_value_;
  return PendingExtract{generation_, {timeline_.get(), pending_signal_}};
}

core::Result<std::optional<DeviceMesh>> MarchingCubes::finish(
    const PendingExtract& pending, volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid,
    ExtractTimings* timings, core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  if (timings != nullptr) *timings = ExtractTimings{};
  // The call is the mesh stage's too, so a refit's row is a breakdown of its
  // row, which comes first.
  if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->seed("marching cubes");
  const core::StageScope stage(metrics, "marching cubes");
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(kEntryFinish) +
                                          ": moved-from");
  }
  if (pending.generation == 0 || pending.generation != pending_generation_ ||
      pending.signal.semaphore != timeline_.get() ||
      pending.signal.value != pending_signal_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(kEntryFinish) +
        ": the pending extract is not this extractor's last record (finished, "
        "abandoned, superseded, or another extractor's)");
  }
  return finish_pending(grid, timings, metrics, kEntryFinish);
}

void MarchingCubes::abandon(const PendingExtract& pending) noexcept {
  if (pending.generation != 0 && pending.generation == pending_generation_ &&
      pending.signal.semaphore == timeline_.get()) {
    drop_pending();
  }
}

core::Result<std::optional<DeviceMesh>> MarchingCubes::finish_pending(
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, ExtractTimings* timings,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics, const char* entry) {
  // The batch resolved, so a value it set is reached, or about to be: MoltenVK
  // reaches it before the fence's completion handler runs, but lavapipe can
  // signal the fence first. A mesh handed over is a reached value, which the
  // consumer's GPU wait then never stalls on; one the batch did not set is
  // refused once the grace is over.
  if (!timeline_->wait(pending_signal_, kSignalGraceNs).ok()) {
    drop_pending();
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) +
        ": the extract's batch did not set its signal "
        "(PendingExtract::signal)");
  }
  McResults r;
  std::memcpy(&r, pending_results_.data(), sizeof(r));
  if (r.opened == 0) {
    drop_pending();
    return std::optional<DeviceMesh>();
  }
  // The kernel's own statement that it shared. It is the only thing tying
  // this file's kMaxSharedCells to the GLSL constant that sizes the shared
  // table, and the failure it catches is silent: the kernel falls back to
  // meshing nothing rather than emitting an unshared surface, so without this
  // the caller would get an empty mesh and no reason. The finalize zeroed the
  // command already.
  if (config_.share_vertices && r.meshed != 0 && r.sharing_applied == 0) {
    drop_pending();
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) +
        ": the sharing kernel declined this grid -- its compile-time cell "
        "table is smaller than this tier's kMaxSharedCells, so the two have "
        "drifted");
  }
  // The thread index and the triangle counter are 32-bit shader values. The
  // bound is in INDICES, not triangles: the atomic counts kIndicesPerTriangle
  // at a time (it is the draw command's indexCount), and 2^32 % 3 == 1, so a
  // wrapped counter would also desynchronise the `/ 3` that makes it a slot
  // index. A set past it may have wrapped, so its counts mean nothing.
  const auto vpb = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.grid().voxels_per_block);
  const std::uint32_t active = r.meshed;
  const std::uint64_t threads = std::uint64_t(active) * vpb;
  if (threads > 0xFFFFFFFFull ||
      threads * kMaxTrisPerCell > 0xFFFFFFFFull / kIndicesPerTriangle) {
    drop_pending();
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        std::string(entry) + ": active set too large for this slice");
  }
  std::uint32_t produced = r.index_count / kIndicesPerTriangle;
  // The sharing kernel's vertex counter is its own overflow condition; the
  // default kernel writes each triangle's three vertices at `tri * 3`.
  std::uint32_t produced_verts =
      config_.share_vertices ? r.vertex_count : produced * kIndicesPerTriangle;
  std::uint64_t ready = pending_signal_;
  std::uint32_t dispatches = 1;
  if (produced > usable_triangle_capacity() ||
      produced_verts > arena_vertex_capacity()) {
    // The surface outgrew the slot. Refit to the measured count -- the count
    // is a property of the field, not of the atomic ordering, so the refitted
    // run cannot overflow again -- in a batch of its own that sets the next
    // timeline value. The slot was never published, so a grow's immediate
    // free is safe.
    core::GpuStageScope refit(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..refit");
    PhaseClock clock(timings != nullptr);
    if (core::Status sized = ensure_output_buffers(
            produced, std::max(produced_verts, plan_vertex_capacity(produced)),
            entry, &refit);
        !sized.ok()) {
      disarm_indirect_command();
      drop_pending();
      return sized;
    }
    if (timings != nullptr) timings->arena_alloc_ms += clock.lap();
    VKC_TRY(bind_sparse(grid, *pending_list_, active, entry));
    if (timings != nullptr) timings->descriptor_ms += clock.lap();
    IndirectWords reset{};
    reset.command.instanceCount = 1;
    IndirectWords words{};
    core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
    static_cast<void>(batch.upload(indirect(), 0, &reset, sizeof(reset)));
    static_cast<void>(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_items(
        batch, kernel_sparse_,
        sparse_push(grid, pending_iso_, active, usable_triangle_capacity(),
                    arena_vertex_capacity()),
        active, 1, max_workgroup_count_x_, &refit));
    static_cast<void>(batch.readback(indirect(), 0, sizeof(words), &words));
    ready = ++timeline_value_;
    core::Status ran = [&]() -> core::Status {
      VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch pending,
                 batch.submit_async({}, {{timeline_.get(), ready}}));
      VKC_TRY(pending.wait());
      if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->merge_device(pending.device_rows());
      return {};
    }();
    if (!ran.ok()) {
      disarm_indirect_command();
      drop_pending();
      return ran;
    }
    produced = words.command.indexCount / kIndicesPerTriangle;
    produced_verts = config_.share_vertices ? words.vertex_count
                                            : produced * kIndicesPerTriangle;
    if (timings != nullptr) timings->dispatch_ms += clock.lap();
    ++dispatches;
    if (produced > usable_triangle_capacity() ||
        produced_verts > arena_vertex_capacity()) {
      // Cannot happen -- the same field emits the same count -- but report
      // rather than hand back a truncated mesh if that is ever broken.
      disarm_indirect_command();
      drop_pending();
      return core::Status::out_of_memory(
          std::string(entry) +
          ": the vertex arena still overflowed after refitting it to the "
          "measured triangle count");
    }
  }
  // Everything fallible is behind us, so the mesh below is certain to be
  // handed out -- which is exactly when the slot may be marked outstanding: a
  // slot stamped with a generation no DeviceMesh ever carried is one nothing
  // can release.
  slots_[slot_].generation = generation_;
  drop_pending();
  // The density this surface actually had, so the next plan scales it by the
  // next set instead of discovering the size by overflowing. Rounded up, so
  // any non-empty surface records at least one triangle per block; a surface
  // that emitted nothing records 0, and the next plan falls back to the seed.
  // A culled pass records too (2026-10-06): the viewers only ever cull.
  if (active != 0) {
    tris_per_block_ = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(
        (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(produced) + active - 1) / active);
  }
  if (produced > 0) {
    verts_per_1000_tris_ = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(
        (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(produced_verts) * 1000 + produced - 1) /
        produced);
  }
  DeviceMesh device_mesh;
  device_mesh.vertices = arena().handle();
  device_mesh.indices = index_run().handle();
  device_mesh.indirect = indirect().handle();
  device_mesh.vertex_usage = arena().usage();
  device_mesh.index_usage = index_run().usage();
  device_mesh.indirect_usage = indirect().usage();
  // One config creates all three, so any of them answers for the set.
  device_mesh.sharing_mode = arena().sharing_mode();
  device_mesh.triangle_count = produced;
  device_mesh.vertex_count = produced_verts;
  device_mesh.shares_vertices = config_.share_vertices;
  device_mesh.generation = generation_;
  device_mesh.live_generation = &generation_;
  device_mesh.ready = core::TimelinePoint{timeline_.get(), ready};
  if (timings != nullptr) {
    timings->active_blocks = active;
    timings->dispatches = dispatches;
    timings->triangle_capacity = usable_triangle_capacity();
    timings->emitted_triangles = produced;
    timings->vertex_capacity = arena_vertex_capacity();
    timings->emitted_vertices = produced_verts;
    // What the extractor is holding, summed over the whole ring: every slot
    // holds its own arena, grown geometrically and never shrunk, so one of N
    // would under-report resident memory N-fold.
    timings->arena_bytes = resident_output_bytes();
  }
  return std::optional<DeviceMesh>(device_mesh);
}

core::Result<DeviceMesh> MarchingCubes::extract_device_impl(
    volume::VoxelBlockGrid& grid, float iso,
    const volume::DeviceBlockList* blocks, ExtractTimings* timings,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics, const char* entry) {
  drop_pending();
  if (metrics != nullptr && valid() && !gpu_timer_.valid()) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(gpu_timer_, core::GpuTimer::create(*device_));
  }
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "marching cubes");
  // Fully overwrite the caller's struct up front, so one instance can be
  // reused across frames; a failed call reports zeros.
  if (timings != nullptr) *timings = ExtractTimings{};
  VKC_TRY(check_grid(grid, entry));
  // A caller's list is checked before this call claims an output slot -- a
  // refusal must leave every outstanding DeviceMesh as valid as it found it.
  // A stale list is the one that matters: the block heap is LIFO, so after a
  // remove() its in-range ptrs name different blocks, and the extract would
  // mesh whatever voxels now live there and report Status::ok.
  if (blocks != nullptr) {
    VKC_TRY(grid.map().check_device_block_subset(*blocks, entry));
  }
  // Claim the slot and bump the generation before anything else, the compact
  // below included: a refusal must cost the caller nothing, and a live
  // consumer one frame behind refuses on every frame (claim_output_slot).
  VKC_TRY(claim_output_slot(entry));
  ++generation_;
  // The caller's subset of the map, or the map's last list while it holds
  // (the encoder's, say), each bound with its host count; else the
  // compaction, recorded into this batch as this stage's "  ..compact", its
  // count left on the device for the sizing, as record_extract's is.
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  PhaseClock clock(timings != nullptr);
  std::optional<volume::DeviceBlockList> listed;
  if (blocks != nullptr) {
    listed = *blocks;
  } else {
    listed = grid.map().held_device_list();
  }
  if (listed) {
    // Empty subsets may have no buffer at all. The lookup table is a valid
    // storage binding large enough for one BlockIndex; zero groups read none
    // of it, while the sizing/finalize path still resets the reused draw slot.
    const core::Buffer& list = listed->count == 0 ? tables_ : *listed->buffer;
    VKC_TRY(record_body(batch, grid, iso, list, nullptr, listed->count,
                        listed->count, nullptr, &stage, metrics, timings,
                        entry));
  } else {
    volume::RecordedBlockList list;
    {
      core::GpuStageScope compact(metrics, gpu_timer_, "  ..compact");
      VKC_ASSIGN(list, grid.map().record_compaction(batch, nullptr, &compact));
    }
    if (timings != nullptr) timings->compact_ms = clock.lap();
    VKC_TRY(record_body(batch, grid, iso, *list.buffer, list.count,
                        static_cast<std::uint32_t>(grid.grid().num_blocks),
                        grid.map().allocated_blocks(), nullptr, &stage, metrics,
                        timings, entry));
  }
  clock.restart();
  pending_signal_ = ++timeline_value_;
  const core::Status ran = [&]() -> core::Status {
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch pending,
               batch.submit_async({}, {{timeline_.get(), pending_signal_}}));
    VKC_TRY(pending.wait());
    if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->merge_device(pending.device_rows());
    return {};
  }();
  if (!ran.ok()) {
    // The sizing may not have reset the command this slot's draw reads.
    disarm_indirect_command();
    drop_pending();
    return ran;
  }
  if (timings != nullptr) timings->dispatch_ms += clock.lap();
  // A gate-less extract always ends with a mesh.
  VKC_ASSIGN(std::optional<DeviceMesh> mesh,
             finish_pending(grid, timings, metrics, entry));
  return *std::move(mesh);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh
