// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/mesh_io/mesh_io.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cctype>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <functional>
#include <limits>
#include <optional>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <assimp/DefaultIOSystem.h>
#include <assimp/postprocess.h>
#include <assimp/scene.h>
#include <assimp/version.h>
#include <assimp/Importer.hpp>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/file_io.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/mesh_io/textured_mesh.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io {
namespace {

// A vertex: its position and, in a textured load, its texture coordinates
// (zero otherwise). Each is finite and none is negative zero, so equal bits
// mean equal values.
using VertexKey = std::array<float, 5>;

struct VertexKeyHash {
  std::size_t operator()(const VertexKey& key) const noexcept {
    std::size_t seed = 0;
    for (const float value : key) {
      std::uint32_t bits = 0;
      std::memcpy(&bits, &value, sizeof(bits));
      seed ^= std::hash<std::uint32_t>{}(bits) + 0x9e3779b9u + (seed << 6) +
              (seed >> 2);
    }
    return seed;
  }
};

core::Result<bool> reflected(const aiMatrix4x4& m) {
  const std::array<ai_real, 16> values = {m.a1, m.a2, m.a3, m.a4, m.b1, m.b2,
                                          m.b3, m.b4, m.c1, m.c2, m.c3, m.c4,
                                          m.d1, m.d2, m.d3, m.d4};
  for (const auto value : values) {
    if (!std::isfinite(value)) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "load_mesh: nonfinite node transform");
    }
  }
  if (m.d1 != 0 || m.d2 != 0 || m.d3 != 0 || m.d4 != 1) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "load_mesh: non-affine node transform");
  }
  const double determinant =
      double(m.a1) * (double(m.b2) * m.c3 - double(m.b3) * m.c2) -
      double(m.a2) * (double(m.b1) * m.c3 - double(m.b3) * m.c1) +
      double(m.a3) * (double(m.b1) * m.c2 - double(m.b2) * m.c1);
  if (!std::isfinite(determinant) || determinant == 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("load_mesh: singular node transform");
  }
  return determinant < 0;
}

core::Result<std::array<float, 3>> transform_position(const aiMatrix4x4& m,
                                                      const aiVector3D& p) {
  const std::array<double, 3> transformed = {
      double(m.a1) * p.x + double(m.a2) * p.y + double(m.a3) * p.z + m.a4,
      double(m.b1) * p.x + double(m.b2) * p.y + double(m.b3) * p.z + m.b4,
      double(m.c1) * p.x + double(m.c2) * p.y + double(m.c3) * p.z + m.c4};
  std::array<float, 3> result{};
  for (std::size_t axis = 0; axis < result.size(); ++axis) {
    const double value = transformed[axis];
    if (!std::isfinite(value) ||
        std::abs(value) > std::numeric_limits<float>::max()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "load_mesh: nonfinite/overflowing position");
    }
    result[axis] = static_cast<float>(value);
    if (result[axis] == 0) result[axis] = 0;  // Canonicalize negative zero.
  }
  return result;
}

// Assimp's own file access, noting each OBJ material library it opens.
class MaterialLibraries final : public Assimp::IOSystem {
 public:
  explicit MaterialLibraries(std::vector<std::string>* opened)
      : opened_(opened) {}

  bool Exists(const char* file) const override { return files_.Exists(file); }
  char getOsSeparator() const override { return files_.getOsSeparator(); }
  Assimp::IOStream* Open(const char* file, const char* mode) override {
    Assimp::IOStream* handle = files_.Open(file, mode);
    std::string extension = std::filesystem::path(file).extension().string();
    for (char& c : extension) {
      c = static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
    }
    if (handle != nullptr && extension == ".mtl") opened_->push_back(file);
    return handle;
  }
  void Close(Assimp::IOStream* handle) override { files_.Close(handle); }
  bool ComparePaths(const char* one, const char* second) const override {
    return files_.ComparePaths(one, second);
  }

 private:
  Assimp::DefaultIOSystem files_;
  std::vector<std::string>* opened_;
};

// The asset as load_mesh reads it, its errors named "load_mesh". A textured
// load joins vertices on their texture coordinates too, and reports its own
// refusals only for an asset load_mesh accepts.
core::Result<TexturedMesh> import_mesh(const std::string& path, bool textured) {
  VKC_TRY(check_mesh_file(path));

  std::vector<std::string> libraries;
  Assimp::Importer importer;
  // The importer owns and deletes it.
  if (textured) importer.SetIOHandler(new MaterialLibraries(&libraries));
  // Keep source coordinates: Collada and FBX importers otherwise apply the
  // file's unit and up axis. Literal names build against releases that lack a
  // property. Assimp before 5.3 still applies Collada's <unit>, and 5.4.x
  // converts FBX regardless.
  importer.SetPropertyBool("IMPORT_COLLADA_IGNORE_UP_DIRECTION", true);
  importer.SetPropertyBool("IMPORT_COLLADA_IGNORE_UNIT_SIZE", true);
  importer.SetPropertyBool("AI_CONFIG_IMPORT_FBX_IGNORE_UP_DIRECTION", true);
  // Avoid repair, approximate vertex joining and automatic scene scaling.
  // Exact joining below ignores normal and material seams, and UV seams but
  // in a textured load.
  const aiScene* scene = importer.ReadFile(
      path, aiProcess_Triangulate | aiProcess_ValidateDataStructure);
  if (scene == nullptr) {
    return core::Status::io_error("load_mesh: " + path + ": " +
                                  importer.GetErrorString());
  }
  if (scene->mRootNode == nullptr || scene->mNumMeshes == 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "load_mesh: asset has no mesh geometry");
  }
  if (scene->mNumAnimations != 0) {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "load_mesh: animation requires an evaluated static asset");
  }

  struct Node {
    const aiNode* source;
    aiMatrix4x4 parent;
  };
  std::vector<Node> pending{{scene->mRootNode, aiMatrix4x4{}}};
  std::size_t source_vertices = 0;
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < scene->mNumMeshes; ++i) {
    if (scene->mMeshes[i] != nullptr)
      source_vertices += scene->mMeshes[i]->mNumVertices;
  }
  std::unordered_map<VertexKey, std::uint32_t, VertexKeyHash> vertices;
  vertices.reserve(source_vertices);
  TexturedMesh textured_result;
  TriangleMesh& result = textured_result.geometry;
  core::Status refusal;  // A textured load's first own refusal.
  const auto refuse = [&refusal](core::Status status) {
    if (refusal.ok()) refusal = std::move(status);
  };
  std::optional<std::string> diffuse;
  while (!pending.empty()) {
    const Node node = pending.back();
    pending.pop_back();
    const aiMatrix4x4 world = node.parent * node.source->mTransformation;
    // Only transforms that place geometry are validated; helper, camera or
    // hidden nodes without meshes do not refuse the asset.
    bool flip = false;
    if (node.source->mNumMeshes != 0) {
      VKC_ASSIGN(flip, reflected(world));
    }
    for (unsigned index = 0; index < node.source->mNumMeshes; ++index) {
      const unsigned mesh_index = node.source->mMeshes[index];
      if (mesh_index >= scene->mNumMeshes ||
          scene->mMeshes[mesh_index] == nullptr) {
        return core::Status::invalid_argument(
            "load_mesh: invalid scene mesh index");
      }
      const aiMesh& mesh = *scene->mMeshes[mesh_index];
      if (mesh.HasBones() || mesh.mNumAnimMeshes != 0) {
        return core::Status::unsupported(
            "load_mesh: skinning/morphs require an evaluated static asset");
      }
      if (mesh.mNumVertices == 0 || mesh.mVertices == nullptr) {
        return core::Status::invalid_argument(
            "load_mesh: mesh has no positions");
      }
      const aiVector3D* uvs = textured ? mesh.mTextureCoords[0] : nullptr;
      if (textured) {
        if (uvs == nullptr) {
          refuse(core::Status::not_found(
              "load_textured_mesh: a mesh has no texture coordinates: " +
              path));
        }
        std::string map;
        aiString file;
        if (mesh.mMaterialIndex >= scene->mNumMaterials ||
            scene->mMaterials[mesh.mMaterialIndex] == nullptr) {
          refuse(core::Status::invalid_argument(
              "load_textured_mesh: invalid material index"));
        } else if (scene->mMaterials[mesh.mMaterialIndex]->GetTexture(
                       aiTextureType_DIFFUSE, 0, &file) == AI_SUCCESS) {
          map = file.C_Str();
        }
        if (!diffuse) {
          diffuse = map;
        } else if (*diffuse != map) {
          refuse(core::Status::unsupported(
              "load_textured_mesh: meshes name different diffuse maps"));
        }
      }
      std::vector<std::uint32_t> remap(mesh.mNumVertices);
      for (unsigned vertex = 0; vertex < mesh.mNumVertices; ++vertex) {
        VKC_ASSIGN(const auto position,
                   transform_position(world, mesh.mVertices[vertex]));
        VertexKey key{position[0], position[1], position[2], 0, 0};
        if (uvs != nullptr) {
          const float u = static_cast<float>(uvs[vertex].x);
          const float v = static_cast<float>(uvs[vertex].y);
          if (!std::isfinite(u) || !std::isfinite(v)) {
            refuse(core::Status::invalid_argument(
                "load_textured_mesh: nonfinite texture coordinate"));
          } else {
            key[3] = u == 0 ? 0 : u;  // Canonicalize negative zero.
            key[4] = v == 0 ? 0 : v;
          }
        }
        auto found = vertices.find(key);
        if (found == vertices.end()) {
          if (result.positions.size() >=
              std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
            return core::Status::out_of_memory(
                "load_mesh: geometry exceeds 32-bit indexing");
          }
          const auto id = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(result.positions.size());
          found = vertices.emplace(key, id).first;
          result.positions.push_back({key[0], key[1], key[2]});
          if (textured) textured_result.uvs.push_back({key[3], key[4]});
        }
        remap[vertex] = found->second;
      }
      for (unsigned face_index = 0; face_index < mesh.mNumFaces; ++face_index) {
        const aiFace& face = mesh.mFaces[face_index];
        if (face.mNumIndices != 3 || face.mIndices == nullptr) {
          return core::Status::unsupported(
              "load_mesh: asset contains non-triangle primitives");
        }
        if (result.indices.size() / 3 >=
            std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
          return core::Status::out_of_memory("load_mesh: too many triangles");
        }
        std::array<std::uint32_t, 3> triangle{};
        for (std::size_t corner = 0; corner < triangle.size(); ++corner) {
          if (face.mIndices[corner] >= remap.size()) {
            return core::Status::invalid_argument(
                "load_mesh: out-of-range vertex index");
          }
          triangle[corner] = remap[face.mIndices[corner]];
        }
        if (flip) std::swap(triangle[1], triangle[2]);
        result.indices.insert(result.indices.end(), triangle.begin(),
                              triangle.end());
      }
    }
    // Reverse the push order to preserve the source's child traversal order.
    for (unsigned child = node.source->mNumChildren; child != 0; --child) {
      const aiNode* next = node.source->mChildren[child - 1];
      if (next == nullptr)
        return core::Status::invalid_argument("load_mesh: null scene node");
      pending.push_back({next, world});
    }
  }
  if (result.indices.empty()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("load_mesh: asset has no triangles");
  }
  VKC_TRY(refusal);
  if (!diffuse || diffuse->empty()) return textured_result;
  // Assimp names a texture held in the asset "*<index>".
  if ((*diffuse)[0] == '*') {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "load_textured_mesh: embedded diffuse map: " + path);
  }
  // Either separator divides the map's path, as when Assimp opens a file.
  std::string map = *diffuse;
  std::replace(map.begin(), map.end(), '\\', '/');
  // An OBJ's texture paths are relative to its material library; other
  // formats define their materials in the asset itself.
  const std::filesystem::path asset = std::filesystem::path(path).parent_path();
  std::filesystem::path base = asset;
  if (!libraries.empty()) {
    const std::filesystem::path library =
        std::filesystem::path(libraries.front()).parent_path();
    for (const std::string& other : libraries) {
      if (std::filesystem::path(other).parent_path() != library) {
        return core::Status::unsupported(
            "load_textured_mesh: material libraries in more than one "
            "directory: " +
            path);
      }
    }
    base = library;
    // Assimp 6 prefixes the library's directory as the OBJ names it, even to
    // an absolute path; earlier releases report the path as the library
    // writes it. An absolute prefix (a bare OBJ name, a library named by an
    // absolute path) already makes the map absolute.
    const std::filesystem::path relative = library.lexically_relative(asset);
    const std::string prefix = relative.generic_string() + '/';
    if (aiGetVersionMajor() >= 6 && !relative.empty() &&
        map.compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) == 0) {
      map.erase(0, prefix.size());
    }
  }
  textured_result.diffuse_texture = (base / map).string();
  return textured_result;
}

}  // namespace

core::Status check_mesh_file(const std::string& path) try {
  VKC_TRY(core::check_path("check_mesh_file", path));
  std::error_code error;
  const auto file = std::filesystem::status(path, error);
  if (error == std::errc::no_such_file_or_directory ||
      (!error && !std::filesystem::exists(file))) {
    return core::Status::not_found("check_mesh_file: missing file: " + path);
  }
  if (error) {
    return core::Status::io_error("check_mesh_file: " + path + ": " +
                                  error.message());
  }
  if (!std::filesystem::is_regular_file(file)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "check_mesh_file: not a regular file: " + path);
  }
  return {};
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("check_mesh_file", core::Status::Code::IoError);
}

core::Result<TriangleMesh> load_mesh(const std::string& path) {
  try {
    VKC_ASSIGN(TexturedMesh mesh, import_mesh(path, false));
    return std::move(mesh.geometry);
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status("load_mesh", core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Result<TexturedMesh> load_textured_mesh(const std::string& path) {
  try {
    return import_mesh(path, true);
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status("load_textured_mesh",
                                  core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/mesh_io/mesh_normalization.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <map>
#include <numeric>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <glm/glm.hpp>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"

// CMake compiles this file with -ffp-contract=off: no multiply-add is fused,
// so a transform's doubles do not depend on the compiler.

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io {
namespace {

bool finite(const Vec3d& v) {
  return std::isfinite(v.x) && std::isfinite(v.y) && std::isfinite(v.z);
}
// Within this, the axes are a rotation: camera/geometry.cpp's tolerance.
constexpr double kOrthonormalTolerance = 1e-6;

// Orthonormal, with a positive determinant; false for a non-finite axis.
bool proper(const MeshAxes& axes) {
  const Vec3d* const rows[] = {&axes.x, &axes.up, &axes.z};
  for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
    for (int b = 0; b < 3; ++b) {
      const double d = glm::dot(*rows[a], *rows[b]);
      if (!(std::abs(d - (a == b ? 1.0 : 0.0)) <= kOrthonormalTolerance)) {
        return false;
      }
    }
  }
  return glm::dot(axes.x, glm::cross(axes.up, axes.z)) > 0.0;
}
// A position in the rotated frame.
Vec3d measure(const MeshAxes& axes, const Vec3d& p) {
  return {glm::dot(axes.x, p), glm::dot(axes.up, p), glm::dot(axes.z, p)};
}

core::Status invalid(const char* api, const char* reason) {
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(api) + ": " + reason);
}

// What apply_transform, and so a stored transform, needs.
core::Status check_transform(const char* api, const MeshTransform& transform) {
  if (!proper(transform.axes)) {
    return invalid(api, "the axes are not a proper rotation");
  }
  if (!finite(transform.origin) || !std::isfinite(transform.metres_per_unit) ||
      !(transform.metres_per_unit > 0.0)) {
    return invalid(api,
                   "the transform needs a finite origin and a positive scale");
  }
  return {};
}

constexpr char kTransformTag[4] = {'V', 'R', 'M', 'T'};
constexpr std::uint32_t kTransformVersion = 1;

// Little-endian words, whatever the host's order.
void put_word(std::string& out, std::uint64_t word, int bytes) {
  for (int i = 0; i < bytes; ++i) out.push_back(char((word >> (8 * i)) & 0xff));
}
std::uint64_t get_word(const std::string& in, std::size_t at, int bytes) {
  std::uint64_t word = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < bytes; ++i) {
    word |= std::uint64_t(std::uint8_t(in[at + std::size_t(i)])) << (8 * i);
  }
  return word;
}

// Rotate to the bounds' axes, centre X/Z, floor Y, then scale.
core::Result<MeshTransform> place(const char* api, const MeshBounds& bounds,
                                  double metres_per_unit) {
  if (!proper(bounds.axes)) {
    return invalid(api, "the axes are not a proper rotation");
  }
  for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
    if (std::isnan(bounds.min[a]) || std::isnan(bounds.max[a])) {
      return invalid(api, "a measured position is not finite");
    }
    if (!(bounds.min[a] <= bounds.max[a])) {
      return invalid(api, "the bounds hold no positions");
    }
  }
  MeshTransform transform;
  transform.axes = bounds.axes;
  transform.origin = {0.5 * (bounds.min.x + bounds.max.x), bounds.min.y,
                      0.5 * (bounds.min.z + bounds.max.z)};
  transform.metres_per_unit = metres_per_unit;
  if (!finite(transform.origin)) {
    return invalid(api, "the bounds are not finite");
  }
  return transform;
}

// The bounds' corners placed as apply_transform places a position: if they
// land in float range, so does every position they bound.
core::Status check_range(const char* api, const MeshBounds& bounds,
                         const MeshTransform& transform) {
  for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
    for (const double r : {bounds.min[a], bounds.max[a]}) {
      const double placed =
          (r - transform.origin[a]) * transform.metres_per_unit;
      if (!std::isfinite(placed) ||
          std::abs(placed) > std::numeric_limits<float>::max()) {
        return invalid(api, "the bounds would be placed past float range");
      }
    }
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<MeshAxes> up_axes(const Vec3d& up) {
  const double largest =
      std::max({std::abs(up.x), std::abs(up.y), std::abs(up.z)});
  if (!finite(up) || !(largest > 0.0)) {
    return invalid("up_axes", "up must be finite and nonzero");
  }
  // Scaling by a power of two is exact, and it keeps the squared length from
  // overflowing or underflowing, so every finite, nonzero up normalizes.
  const int exponent = std::ilogb(largest);
  const Vec3d scaled{std::ldexp(up.x, -exponent), std::ldexp(up.y, -exponent),
                     std::ldexp(up.z, -exponent)};
  MeshAxes axes;
  axes.up = glm::normalize(scaled);
  const Vec3d reference =
      std::abs(axes.up.z) < 0.9 ? Vec3d{0.0, 0.0, 1.0} : Vec3d{1.0, 0.0, 0.0};
  axes.x = glm::normalize(glm::cross(axes.up, reference));
  axes.z = glm::cross(axes.x, axes.up);
  return axes;
}

MeshBounds mesh_bounds(const TriangleMesh& mesh, const MeshAxes& axes) {
  MeshBounds bounds;
  bounds.axes = axes;
  extend_bounds(bounds, mesh);
  return bounds;
}

void extend_bounds(MeshBounds& bounds, const TriangleMesh& mesh) {
  constexpr double kNaN = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
  for (const auto& position : mesh.positions) {
    const Vec3d r = measure(bounds.axes, Vec3d(position));
    for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
      // NaN stays: std::min and std::max return their first argument when
      // a comparison with it is false.
      if (!std::isfinite(r[a])) {
        bounds.min[a] = bounds.max[a] = kNaN;
      } else {
        bounds.min[a] = std::min(bounds.min[a], r[a]);
        bounds.max[a] = std::max(bounds.max[a], r[a]);
      }
    }
  }
}

core::Result<MeshTransform> fit_transform(const MeshBounds& bounds,
                                          double height_m) {
  if (!std::isfinite(height_m) || !(height_m > 0.0)) {
    return invalid("fit_transform", "height_m must be finite and positive");
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(MeshTransform transform, place("fit_transform", bounds, 0.0));
  const double extent = bounds.max.y - bounds.min.y;
  if (!(extent > 0.0)) {
    return invalid("fit_transform", "zero extent along up");
  }
  transform.metres_per_unit = height_m / extent;
  if (!std::isfinite(transform.metres_per_unit) ||
      !(transform.metres_per_unit > 0.0)) {
    return invalid("fit_transform",
                   "height_m over the extent along up is not a finite, "
                   "positive scale");
  }
  VKC_TRY(check_range("fit_transform", bounds, transform));
  return transform;
}

core::Result<MeshTransform> scale_transform(const MeshBounds& bounds,
                                            double metres_per_unit) {
  if (!std::isfinite(metres_per_unit) || !(metres_per_unit > 0.0)) {
    return invalid("scale_transform",
                   "metres_per_unit must be finite and positive");
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(MeshTransform transform,
             place("scale_transform", bounds, metres_per_unit));
  VKC_TRY(check_range("scale_transform", bounds, transform));
  return transform;
}

core::Status apply_transform(TriangleMesh& mesh,
                             const MeshTransform& transform) try {
  VKC_TRY(check_transform("apply_transform", transform));
  std::vector<Vec3f> positions;
  positions.reserve(mesh.positions.size());
  // The extent along up before and after, for the collapse check.
  double low = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
  double high = -low;
  float placed_low = std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity();
  float placed_high = -placed_low;
  for (const auto& position : mesh.positions) {
    const Vec3d r = measure(transform.axes, Vec3d(position));
    Vec3d placed{0.0};
    for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
      if (!std::isfinite(r[a])) {
        return invalid("apply_transform", "a position is not finite");
      }
      placed[a] = (r[a] - transform.origin[a]) * transform.metres_per_unit;
      if (!std::isfinite(placed[a]) ||
          std::abs(placed[a]) > std::numeric_limits<float>::max()) {
        return invalid("apply_transform", "output overflows float");
      }
    }
    positions.push_back(Vec3f(placed));
    low = std::min(low, r.y);
    high = std::max(high, r.y);
    placed_low = std::min(placed_low, positions.back().y);
    placed_high = std::max(placed_high, positions.back().y);
  }
  if (high > low && !(placed_high > placed_low)) {
    return invalid("apply_transform",
                   "the height along up collapses at float precision");
  }
  mesh.positions = std::move(positions);
  return {};
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("apply_transform",
                                core::Status::Code::InvalidArgument);
}

core::Result<std::string> encode_transform(const MeshTransform& transform) try {
  VKC_TRY(check_transform("encode_transform", transform));
  std::string out(kTransformTag, sizeof kTransformTag);
  out.reserve(kTransformBytes);
  put_word(out, kTransformVersion, 4);
  const double values[13] = {
      transform.axes.x.x,       transform.axes.x.y,  transform.axes.x.z,
      transform.axes.up.x,      transform.axes.up.y, transform.axes.up.z,
      transform.axes.z.x,       transform.axes.z.y,  transform.axes.z.z,
      transform.origin.x,       transform.origin.y,  transform.origin.z,
      transform.metres_per_unit};
  for (const double value : values) {
    std::uint64_t bits = 0;
    std::memcpy(&bits, &value, sizeof bits);
    put_word(out, bits, 8);
  }
  return out;
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("encode_transform",
                                core::Status::Code::InvalidArgument);
}

core::Result<MeshTransform> decode_transform(const std::string& bytes) try {
  if (bytes.size() != kTransformBytes ||
      bytes.compare(0, sizeof kTransformTag, kTransformTag,
                    sizeof kTransformTag) != 0) {
    return invalid("decode_transform",
                   "expected the 112 bytes of a VRMT transform");
  }
  const auto version = std::uint32_t(get_word(bytes, 4, 4));
  if (version != kTransformVersion) {
    return core::Status::unsupported("decode_transform: version " +
                                     std::to_string(version));
  }
  double values[13];
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 13; ++i) {
    const std::uint64_t bits = get_word(bytes, 8 + 8 * i, 8);
    std::memcpy(&values[i], &bits, sizeof bits);
  }
  MeshTransform transform;
  transform.axes.x = {values[0], values[1], values[2]};
  transform.axes.up = {values[3], values[4], values[5]};
  transform.axes.z = {values[6], values[7], values[8]};
  transform.origin = {values[9], values[10], values[11]};
  transform.metres_per_unit = values[12];
  VKC_TRY(check_transform("decode_transform", transform));
  return transform;
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("decode_transform",
                                core::Status::Code::InvalidArgument);
}

core::Result<MeshTopology> audit_mesh_topology(const TriangleMesh& mesh) try {
  if (mesh.indices.size() % 3 != 0) {
    return invalid("audit_mesh_topology", "incomplete triangle indices");
  }
  for (const std::uint32_t index : mesh.indices) {
    if (index >= mesh.positions.size()) {
      return invalid("audit_mesh_topology",
                     "an index names a missing position");
    }
  }
  struct Edge {
    std::size_t count = 0;
    int direction = 0;
  };
  std::map<std::pair<std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t>, Edge> edges;
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> parents(mesh.positions.size());
  std::iota(parents.begin(), parents.end(), 0u);
  auto root = [&parents](std::uint32_t v) {
    while (parents[v] != v) {
      parents[v] = parents[parents[v]];
      v = parents[v];
    }
    return v;
  };
  MeshTopology result;
  for (std::size_t t = 0; t < mesh.indices.size(); t += 3) {
    const auto a = mesh.indices[t];
    const auto b = mesh.indices[t + 1];
    const auto c = mesh.indices[t + 2];
    parents[root(b)] = root(a);
    parents[root(c)] = root(a);
    const Vec3d pa(mesh.positions[a]);
    const Vec3d area = glm::cross(Vec3d(mesh.positions[b]) - pa,
                                  Vec3d(mesh.positions[c]) - pa);
    const double twice_area_squared = glm::dot(area, area);
    if (!(std::isfinite(twice_area_squared) && twice_area_squared > 0.0)) {
      ++result.degenerate_triangles;
    }
    for (std::size_t e = 0; e < 3; ++e) {
      const auto from = mesh.indices[t + e];
      const auto to = mesh.indices[t + (e + 1) % 3];
      auto& edge = edges[std::minmax(from, to)];
      ++edge.count;
      edge.direction += from < to ? 1 : -1;
    }
  }
  result.edges = edges.size();
  for (const auto& item : edges) {
    const auto& edge = item.second;
    if (edge.count == 1) ++result.boundary_edges;
    if (edge.count > 2) ++result.nonmanifold_edges;
    if (edge.count == 2 && edge.direction != 0) ++result.inconsistent_edges;
  }
  std::map<std::uint32_t, double> volumes;
  for (std::size_t t = 0; t < mesh.indices.size(); t += 3) {
    const auto a = mesh.indices[t];
    const auto b = mesh.indices[t + 1];
    const auto c = mesh.indices[t + 2];
    // Translate to one component vertex to avoid cancellation far from origin.
    const auto component = root(a);
    const Vec3d origin(mesh.positions[component]);
    const Vec3d p = Vec3d(mesh.positions[a]) - origin;
    const Vec3d q = Vec3d(mesh.positions[b]) - origin;
    const Vec3d r = Vec3d(mesh.positions[c]) - origin;
    volumes[component] += glm::dot(p, glm::cross(q, r)) / 6.0;
  }
  if (result.boundary_edges > 0) {
    // Close each hole before taking the volume: every group of boundary
    // edges that share vertices gets a fan to the centroid of its vertices,
    // run against the edges' own direction. A closed surface's volume does
    // not depend on the point it is taken about, so neither the root vertex
    // nor the index order changes it. The edges and the centroid sums go in
    // index order, so the caps do not depend on triangle order either.
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> groups(mesh.positions.size());
    std::iota(groups.begin(), groups.end(), 0u);
    auto group = [&groups](std::uint32_t v) {
      while (groups[v] != v) {
        groups[v] = groups[groups[v]];
        v = groups[v];
      }
      return v;
    };
    std::vector<bool> on_rim(mesh.positions.size());
    for (const auto& item : edges) {
      if (item.second.count != 1) continue;
      groups[group(item.first.second)] = group(item.first.first);
      on_rim[item.first.first] = on_rim[item.first.second] = true;
    }
    struct Rim {
      Vec3d sum{0.0};
      std::size_t count = 0;
    };
    std::map<std::uint32_t, Rim> rims;
    for (std::uint32_t v = 0; v < mesh.positions.size(); ++v) {
      if (!on_rim[v]) continue;
      auto& rim = rims[group(v)];
      rim.sum += Vec3d(mesh.positions[v]);
      ++rim.count;
    }
    for (const auto& item : edges) {
      if (item.second.count != 1) continue;
      // Its one triangle runs the edge low to high when the direction is +1;
      // the cap runs it the other way.
      const auto low = item.first.first;
      const auto high = item.first.second;
      const bool forward = item.second.direction > 0;
      const auto& rim = rims[group(low)];
      const auto component = root(low);
      const Vec3d origin(mesh.positions[component]);
      const Vec3d p = Vec3d(mesh.positions[forward ? high : low]) - origin;
      const Vec3d q = Vec3d(mesh.positions[forward ? low : high]) - origin;
      const Vec3d r = rim.sum / double(rim.count) - origin;
      volumes[component] += glm::dot(p, glm::cross(q, r)) / 6.0;
    }
  }
  result.components = volumes.size();
  for (const auto& volume : volumes) {
    result.signed_volume += volume.second;
    if (!(volume.second > 0.0)) ++result.nonpositive_components;
  }
  return result;
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("audit_mesh_topology",
                                core::Status::Code::InvalidArgument);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh_io/ply_writer.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/mesh_io/ply_writer.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <fstream>
#include <limits>
#include <ostream>
#include <vector>

#include "tinyply_backend.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/file_io.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io {
namespace {

namespace tinyply = detail::tinyply;

// The exact piecewise sRGB encode, one channel: the published formula, the
// mesh files' own copy so they need no camera or colour vocabulary.
// grid_io_ply holds it to the voxel colour format's curve
// (volume/voxel_color.hpp), code for code.
float linear_to_srgb(float l) {
  return l <= 0.0031308f ? l * 12.92f
                         : 1.055f * std::pow(l, 1.0f / 2.4f) - 0.055f;
}

// Encode a LINEAR vertex-color channel to an 8-bit canonical-encoded code.
//
// PLY is a presentation site. `mesh::Vertex::color` is linear working values
// (the 2026-08-02 color-space decision -- what glTF calls COLOR_0), but a PLY's
// `uchar` red/green/blue properties carry no color-space tag and every external
// viewer (MeshLab, Blender, CloudCompare) reads them as sRGB. Writing the
// linear value straight out would therefore render visibly dark, so the encode
// happens here. glTF export does the opposite and passes COLOR_0 through
// unchanged, which is why the two exporters cannot share one path.
//
// Out-of-range values clamp, and NaN writes 0, so one bad color never costs
// the export.
std::uint8_t to_u8(float linear_channel) {
  if (!(linear_channel > 0.0f)) return 0;
  if (linear_channel >= 1.0f) return 255;
  return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(linear_to_srgb(linear_channel) * 255.0f +
                                   0.5f);
}

bool finite(Vec3f v) {
  return std::isfinite(v.x) && std::isfinite(v.y) && std::isfinite(v.z);
}

}  // namespace

core::Status write_ply(const std::string& path, const mesh::Mesh& mesh) try {
  VKC_TRY(core::check_path("write_ply", path));
  if (mesh.indices.size() % 3 != 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "write_ply: incomplete triangle indices");
  }
  const std::size_t vertex_count = mesh.vertices.size();
  const std::size_t face_count = mesh.indices.size() / 3;
  if (vertex_count > std::vector<float>().max_size() / 3 ||
      mesh.indices.size() > std::vector<std::int32_t>().max_size()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "write_ply: mesh exceeds host array limits");
  }
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < vertex_count; ++i) {
    const mesh::Vertex& v = mesh.vertices[i];
    if (!finite(v.position) || !finite(v.normal)) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "write_ply: nonfinite position or normal at vertex " +
          std::to_string(i));
    }
  }
  for (std::uint32_t index : mesh.indices) {
    if (index >= vertex_count ||
        index > static_cast<std::uint32_t>(
                    std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max())) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "write_ply: invalid signed int32 index");
    }
  }
  // tinyply labels newly written files little-endian but writes native values.
  const std::uint16_t endian = 1;
  if (*reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(&endian) != 1) {
    return core::Status::unsupported(
        "write_ply: requires a little-endian host");
  }

  // tinyply writes each property group from a tightly-packed array, so
  // de-interleave the Mesh's array-of-Vertex-struct into per-attribute buffers
  // (position, normal, and the u8-quantized colour). One-shot final export, so
  // the extra copies are inconsequential.
  std::vector<float> positions(vertex_count * 3);
  std::vector<float> normals(vertex_count * 3);
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> colors(vertex_count * 3);
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < vertex_count; ++i) {
    const mesh::Vertex& v = mesh.vertices[i];
    positions[i * 3 + 0] = v.position.x;
    positions[i * 3 + 1] = v.position.y;
    positions[i * 3 + 2] = v.position.z;
    normals[i * 3 + 0] = v.normal.x;
    normals[i * 3 + 1] = v.normal.y;
    normals[i * 3 + 2] = v.normal.z;
    colors[i * 3 + 0] = to_u8(v.color.x);
    colors[i * 3 + 1] = to_u8(v.color.y);
    colors[i * 3 + 2] = to_u8(v.color.z);
  }
  // PLY's conventional face-index type is signed int32. Mesh indices are
  // uint32, so the explicit range check above is required before conversion.
  std::vector<std::int32_t> faces(mesh.indices.begin(), mesh.indices.end());

  tinyply::PlyFile ply;
  // The comment keeps the name the writer had when the format was fixed, so
  // a file is byte for byte what it was before the writer moved to grid.
  ply.get_comments().push_back("volumetric_kit_recon");
  ply.add_properties_to_element(
      "vertex", {"x", "y", "z"}, tinyply::Type::FLOAT32, vertex_count,
      reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(positions.data()),
      tinyply::Type::INVALID, 0);
  ply.add_properties_to_element(
      "vertex", {"nx", "ny", "nz"}, tinyply::Type::FLOAT32, vertex_count,
      reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(normals.data()),
      tinyply::Type::INVALID, 0);
  ply.add_properties_to_element("vertex", {"red", "green", "blue"},
                                tinyply::Type::UINT8, vertex_count,
                                colors.data(), tinyply::Type::INVALID, 0);
  ply.add_properties_to_element(
      "face", {"vertex_indices"}, tinyply::Type::INT32, face_count,
      reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(faces.data()), tinyply::Type::UINT8,
      3);

  std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary);
  if (!out) {
    return core::Status::io_error("write_ply: cannot open " + path);
  }
  // tinyply's writer is noexcept: only its small per-property tables allocate
  // there, so the large buffers above carry the allocation failure contract.
  ply.write(out, /*isBinary=*/true);
  // Explicit close includes the final flush and reports a delayed write error.
  out.close();
  if (!out) {
    return core::Status::io_error("write_ply: write failed for " + path);
  }
  return {};
} catch (...) {
  return core::exception_status("write_ply", core::Status::Code::IoError);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::mesh_io
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/gop_log.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "gop_log.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <utility>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail {

GopLog::GopLog(std::uint64_t max_gop_bytes, bool replay) noexcept
    : max_gop_bytes_(max_gop_bytes), replay_(replay) {}

void GopLog::join(Cursor* cursor) {
  if (replay_) return;
  *cursor = {};
  viewers_.push_back(cursor);
  ++key_wanted_;
}

void GopLog::leave(const Cursor* cursor) noexcept {
  viewers_.erase(std::remove(viewers_.begin(), viewers_.end(), cursor),
                 viewers_.end());
}

bool GopLog::append(Chunk chunk, bool key) {
  return replay_ ? append_replay(std::move(chunk), key)
                 : append_on_demand(std::move(chunk), key);
}

bool GopLog::append_replay(Chunk chunk, bool key) {
  if (key) {
    ++gop_;
    chunks_.clear();
    bytes_ = 0;
    open_ = true;
  }
  if (!open_) return false;
  const std::uint64_t size = chunk->size();
  if (size > max_gop_bytes_ - bytes_) {
    break_gop(key);
    return false;
  }
  try {
    chunks_.push_back(std::move(chunk));
  } catch (...) {
    break_gop(key);
    throw;
  }
  bytes_ += size;
  return true;
}

bool GopLog::append_on_demand(Chunk chunk, bool key) {
  const std::uint64_t size = chunk->size();
  if (key && size <= max_gop_bytes_) {
    // Newest key wins: every viewer goes on from this key, the waiting ones
    // let in, so what came before goes and none falls behind by it.
    first_ = head();
    held_.clear();
    if (viewers_.empty()) return false;
    try {
      held_.push_back({std::move(chunk), kept_});
    } catch (...) {
      break_gop(true);
      throw;
    }
    kept_ += size;
    for (Cursor* viewer : viewers_) *viewer = {0, first_, false};
    return true;
  }
  // Every viewer in has at most max_gop_bytes behind it, so none of these
  // differences wraps; one chunk past the limit alone, a key too, takes
  // every viewer.
  for (Cursor* viewer : viewers_) {
    if (!viewer->waiting && size > max_gop_bytes_ - behind(*viewer)) {
      fall_back(viewer);
    }
  }
  trim();
  if (!open()) return false;
  try {
    held_.push_back({std::move(chunk), kept_});
  } catch (...) {
    break_gop(key);
    throw;
  }
  kept_ += size;
  return true;
}

void GopLog::break_gop(bool key) noexcept {
  if (replay_) {
    chunks_.clear();
    bytes_ = 0;
    open_ = false;
    return;
  }
  for (Cursor* viewer : viewers_) {
    if (!viewer->waiting || key) fall_back(viewer);
  }
  trim();
}

Chunk GopLog::next(Cursor* cursor) const noexcept {
  if (!replay_) {
    if (cursor->waiting || cursor->next >= head()) return nullptr;
    return held_[cursor->next++ - first_].chunk;
  }
  if (cursor->gop != gop_) *cursor = {gop_, 0, false};
  if (cursor->next >= chunks_.size()) return nullptr;
  return chunks_[cursor->next++];
}

bool GopLog::open() const noexcept {
  if (replay_) return open_;
  return std::any_of(viewers_.begin(), viewers_.end(),
                     [](const Cursor* viewer) { return !viewer->waiting; });
}

bool GopLog::joined() const noexcept { return !viewers_.empty(); }

std::uint64_t GopLog::key_wanted() const noexcept { return key_wanted_; }

std::uint64_t GopLog::bytes() const noexcept {
  if (replay_) return bytes_;
  return held_.empty() ? 0 : kept_ - held_.front().start;
}

std::uint64_t GopLog::head() const noexcept { return first_ + held_.size(); }

std::uint64_t GopLog::behind(const Cursor& cursor) const noexcept {
  if (cursor.next >= head()) return 0;
  return kept_ - held_[cursor.next - first_].start;
}

void GopLog::trim() noexcept {
  std::uint64_t needed = head();
  for (const Cursor* viewer : viewers_) {
    if (!viewer->waiting) needed = std::min(needed, viewer->next);
  }
  while (first_ < needed) {
    held_.pop_front();
    ++first_;
  }
}

void GopLog::fall_back(Cursor* cursor) noexcept {
  cursor->waiting = true;
  ++key_wanted_;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/gop_log.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

// What a StreamServer holds for its viewers, as whole chunks that every
// viewer still to send them shares, and each viewer's place in them. No
// sockets, threads or clock: the server calls it under its lock.
//
// Replaying the GOP (ServerOptions::replay_gop): one GOP, the newest key
// record and every record after it. Newest key wins: a viewer that has not
// sent the GOP when a newer key arrives skips the rest, at a chunk boundary,
// and goes on from that key, so no P-frame is ever handed out without the
// records it is predicted from.
//
// Keys on demand (replay_gop false): a viewer joins waiting for the next key,
// then gets every record after it, in order, while it stays within
// max_gop_bytes of the newest; one that would fall further behind waits for
// the next key again. Newest key wins here too: a key lets every waiting
// viewer in, and a viewer in that has not sent what came before it goes on
// from it, at a chunk boundary. The log keeps only the records some viewer
// still has to send, none before the newest key. Each join and each
// fall-back counts in key_wanted(), which a sender reads to make its next
// frame a key; a key within max_gop_bytes counts none, as every viewer goes
// on from it.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail {

// A record's whole chunk (stream::ChunkEncoder's header, the payload and its
// padding), shared by the log and every viewer sending it.
using Chunk = std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<std::uint8_t>>;

class GopLog {
 public:
  // A viewer's place. Replaying: the GOP it is in, and the index of the next
  // chunk of it to hand out; a new viewer's, {}, is in no GOP: it starts at
  // the key of the GOP there is at its first chunk, or of the next. Keys on
  // demand: whether it waits for a key, and once one let it in, the number
  // of its next record (the log numbers the records it keeps).
  struct Cursor {
    std::uint64_t gop = 0;
    std::uint64_t next = 0;
    bool waiting = true;
  };

  // A log keeping chunks of at most `max_gop_bytes`: one GOP while
  // `replay`, else what the joined viewers still need, as above.
  explicit GopLog(std::uint64_t max_gop_bytes, bool replay = true) noexcept;

  // Keys on demand: count `cursor`'s viewer in, waiting for the next key,
  // until it leaves. Throws what the viewers' vector throws, counting none.
  // Replaying: nothing, as a viewer starts at the GOP's key.
  void join(Cursor* cursor);
  // The viewer at `cursor` has left: forget it, if it joined.
  void leave(const Cursor* cursor) noexcept;

  // Take one record's chunk; returns whether it was kept. Replaying, a key
  // starts a new GOP, replacing the log, and any other record joins the
  // GOP, unless no key has come yet or the GOP is broken; a chunk that would
  // take the GOP past max_gop_bytes breaks it: the chunk and the GOP's are
  // dropped, and every record until the next key. Keys on demand, a key
  // within max_gop_bytes drops what came before and is kept while a viewer
  // has joined, every viewer going on from it; any other chunk makes a
  // viewer it would leave more than max_gop_bytes behind fall back to
  // waiting, and is kept only while a viewer is in, what no viewer still
  // needs dropped. A chunk the log has no room to hold is lost (break_gop),
  // and what its container threw is thrown on.
  bool append(Chunk chunk, bool key);

  // A record is lost (it could not be copied), a key when `key`: replaying,
  // break the GOP, dropping its chunks; keys on demand, every viewer in falls
  // back to waiting, its chunks dropped, and, for a key, every viewer that
  // waited for it is counted again.
  void break_gop(bool key) noexcept;

  // The next chunk for the viewer at `cursor`, which it moves on: replaying,
  // from the key of a newer GOP than the cursor's, else the GOP's next; keys
  // on demand, its next record unless it waits. Null when the viewer has
  // every chunk there is for it. Called at a chunk boundary.
  Chunk next(Cursor* cursor) const noexcept;

  // Replaying: whether a GOP is open, a key has come and the GOP is not
  // broken. Keys on demand: whether a viewer is in.
  bool open() const noexcept;

  // Keys on demand: whether a viewer has joined, in or waiting. Replaying:
  // false.
  bool joined() const noexcept;

  // Keys on demand: the joins and fall-backs so far. Replaying: 0.
  std::uint64_t key_wanted() const noexcept;

  // The chunk bytes the log holds.
  std::uint64_t bytes() const noexcept;

 private:
  // A chunk kept on demand, and the bytes kept before it since the start.
  struct Held {
    Chunk chunk;
    std::uint64_t start = 0;
  };

  bool append_replay(Chunk chunk, bool key);
  bool append_on_demand(Chunk chunk, bool key);
  // Keys on demand: the number the next record kept takes.
  std::uint64_t head() const noexcept;
  // Keys on demand: the bytes kept from the viewer at `cursor`'s next record
  // on, none for a viewer that has them all.
  std::uint64_t behind(const Cursor& cursor) const noexcept;
  // Keys on demand: drop the records no viewer still needs.
  void trim() noexcept;
  void fall_back(Cursor* cursor) noexcept;

  std::uint64_t max_gop_bytes_;
  bool replay_;
  // Replaying.
  std::uint64_t gop_ = 0;  // the GOP's number: the keys taken
  bool open_ = false;
  std::uint64_t bytes_ = 0;  // the GOP's chunk bytes
  std::vector<Chunk> chunks_;
  // Keys on demand.
  std::vector<Cursor*> viewers_;  // the joined viewers' cursors
  std::deque<Held> held_;
  std::uint64_t first_ = 0;  // held_.front()'s number, or head() when empty
  std::uint64_t kept_ = 0;   // the chunk bytes kept since the start
  std::uint64_t key_wanted_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/socket.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "socket.hpp"

#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <netdb.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <sys/types.h>  // IWYU pragma: keep (ssize_t on Linux)
#include <unistd.h>
#ifndef __APPLE__
#include <linux/sockios.h>
#endif

#include <algorithm>
#include <cerrno>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <system_error>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail {
namespace {

#ifdef __APPLE__
constexpr int kSendFlags = 0;  // SO_NOSIGPIPE is set on every socket
#else
constexpr int kSendFlags = MSG_NOSIGNAL;
#endif

// Connections the kernel queues before the accept thread takes them.
constexpr int kBacklog = 8;
// One send or recv moves at most this much: macOS refuses a count above
// INT_MAX.
constexpr std::size_t kMaxIo = std::size_t{1} << 30;

// "<api>: <what>: <the system's reason>": OutOfMemory for the kernel's
// memory, IoError for the rest.
core::Status failure(std::string_view api, std::string_view what, int error) {
  std::string message(api);
  message += ": ";
  message += what;
  message += ": ";
  message += std::generic_category().message(error);
  if (error == ENOMEM || error == ENOBUFS) {
    return core::Status::out_of_memory(std::move(message));
  }
  return core::Status::io_error(std::move(message));
}

core::Status set_option(std::string_view api, int fd, int level, int name,
                        int value, std::string_view what) {
  if (::setsockopt(fd, level, name, &value, sizeof value) != 0) {
    return failure(api, what, errno);
  }
  return {};
}

// Close-on-exec, non-blocking, and on Apple no SIGPIPE.
core::Status prepare(std::string_view api, int fd) {
  const int fd_flags = ::fcntl(fd, F_GETFD);
  if (fd_flags < 0 || ::fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, fd_flags | FD_CLOEXEC) != 0) {
    return failure(api, "cannot set FD_CLOEXEC", errno);
  }
  const int flags = ::fcntl(fd, F_GETFL);
  if (flags < 0 || ::fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK) != 0) {
    return failure(api, "cannot set O_NONBLOCK", errno);
  }
#ifdef __APPLE__
  VKC_TRY(set_option(api, fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_NOSIGPIPE, 1,
                     "cannot set SO_NOSIGPIPE"));
#endif
  return {};
}

core::Result<core::UniqueFd> new_socket(std::string_view api) {
  core::UniqueFd fd(::socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0));
  if (!fd.valid()) return failure(api, "cannot make a socket", errno);
  VKC_TRY(prepare(api, fd.get()));
  return fd;
}

const sockaddr* as_sockaddr(const Address& address) {
  return reinterpret_cast<const sockaddr*>(&address.in);
}

}  // namespace

bool parse_ipv4(const std::string& host, std::uint16_t port, Address* out) {
  Address address;
  address.in.sin_family = AF_INET;
  address.in.sin_port = htons(port);
  if (::inet_pton(AF_INET, host.c_str(), &address.in.sin_addr) != 1) {
    return false;
  }
  *out = address;
  return true;
}

core::Result<std::vector<Address>> resolve(std::string_view api,
                                           const std::string& host,
                                           std::uint16_t port) {
  addrinfo hints{};
  hints.ai_family = AF_INET;
  hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
  hints.ai_protocol = IPPROTO_TCP;
  hints.ai_flags = AI_NUMERICSERV;
  addrinfo* found = nullptr;
  const int error =
      ::getaddrinfo(host.c_str(), std::to_string(port).c_str(), &hints, &found);
  const int system_error = errno;  // before the message's allocations
  const std::unique_ptr<addrinfo, void (*)(addrinfo*)> owned(found,
                                                             ::freeaddrinfo);
  if (error != 0) {
    const std::string why =
        std::string(api) + ": cannot look up the name: " +
        (error == EAI_SYSTEM ? std::generic_category().message(system_error)
                             : std::string(::gai_strerror(error)));
    if (error == EAI_NONAME) return core::Status::not_found(why);
    if (error == EAI_MEMORY) return core::Status::out_of_memory(why);
    return core::Status::io_error(why);
  }
  std::vector<Address> addresses;
  for (const addrinfo* a = found; a != nullptr; a = a->ai_next) {
    if (a->ai_family != AF_INET || a->ai_addrlen != sizeof(sockaddr_in)) {
      continue;
    }
    Address address;
    std::memcpy(&address.in, a->ai_addr, sizeof address.in);
    addresses.push_back(address);
  }
  if (addresses.empty()) {
    return core::Status::not_found(
        std::string(api) +
        ": cannot look up the name: no IPv4 address for TCP");
  }
  return addresses;
}

std::string to_string(const Address& address) {
  char text[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] = {};
  ::inet_ntop(AF_INET, &address.in.sin_addr, text, sizeof text);
  return std::string(text) + ":" + std::to_string(ntohs(address.in.sin_port));
}

core::Result<core::UniqueFd> listen_on(std::string_view api,
                                       const Address& address) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::UniqueFd fd, new_socket(api));
  VKC_TRY(set_option(api, fd.get(), SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, 1,
                     "cannot set SO_REUSEADDR"));
  if (::bind(fd.get(), as_sockaddr(address), sizeof address.in) != 0 ||
      ::listen(fd.get(), kBacklog) != 0) {
    const int error = errno;  // before the message's allocations
    return failure(api, "cannot listen on " + to_string(address), error);
  }
  return fd;
}

core::Result<std::uint16_t> bound_port(std::string_view api, int fd) {
  Address address;
  socklen_t size = sizeof address.in;
  if (::getsockname(fd, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&address.in), &size) != 0) {
    return failure(api, "cannot name the socket", errno);
  }
  return ntohs(address.in.sin_port);
}

core::Result<core::UniqueFd> accept_next(std::string_view api, int listener,
                                         Address* peer) {
  for (;;) {
    *peer = {};
    socklen_t size = sizeof peer->in;
    core::UniqueFd fd(
        ::accept(listener, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&peer->in), &size));
    if (!fd.valid()) {
      switch (errno) {
        case EINTR:
          continue;
        // None waiting, or one that failed in the queue: Linux passes a
        // pending network error up through accept.
        case EAGAIN:
#if EWOULDBLOCK != EAGAIN
        case EWOULDBLOCK:
#endif
        case ECONNABORTED:
        case EPROTO:
        case ENETDOWN:
        case ENETUNREACH:
        case EHOSTUNREACH:
#ifdef EHOSTDOWN
        case EHOSTDOWN:
#endif
#ifdef ENONET
        case ENONET:
#endif
        case ENOPROTOOPT:
        case EOPNOTSUPP:
          return core::UniqueFd();
        default:
          return failure(api, "cannot accept", errno);
      }
    }
    // One that cannot be set up failed after it was queued, as macOS shows
    // one its peer reset (EINVAL at the first setsockopt): it goes too.
    if (!prepare(api, fd.get()).ok() ||
        !set_option(api, fd.get(), IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, 1,
                    "cannot set TCP_NODELAY")
             .ok() ||
        !set_option(api, fd.get(), IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT,
                    kSendLowWater, "cannot set TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT")
             .ok()) {
      return core::UniqueFd();
    }
    return fd;
  }
}

core::Result<core::UniqueFd> start_connect(std::string_view api,
                                           const Address& address,
                                           bool* connected) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::UniqueFd fd, new_socket(api));
  VKC_TRY(set_option(api, fd.get(), SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, kReceiveBuffer,
                     "cannot set SO_RCVBUF"));
  *connected =
      ::connect(fd.get(), as_sockaddr(address), sizeof address.in) == 0;
  const int error = errno;  // before the message's allocations
  // Interrupted, a non-blocking connect goes on as one in progress does.
  if (!*connected && error != EINPROGRESS && error != EINTR) {
    return failure(api, "cannot connect", error);
  }
  return fd;
}

core::Status finish_connect(std::string_view api, int fd) {
  int error = 0;
  socklen_t size = sizeof error;
  if (::getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, &error, &size) != 0) {
    error = errno;
  }
  if (error != 0) return failure(api, "cannot connect", error);
  return {};
}

core::Result<short> wait_for(std::string_view api, int fd, short events,
                             std::chrono::milliseconds timeout) {
  using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
  const Clock::time_point deadline = after(Clock::now(), timeout);
  for (;;) {
    pollfd p{fd, events, 0};
    const auto left =
        std::chrono::ceil<std::chrono::milliseconds>(deadline - Clock::now());
    // A poll waits at most INT_MAX ms (24 days), then the next goes on.
    const std::int64_t ms = std::clamp<std::int64_t>(
        left.count(), 0, std::numeric_limits<int>::max());
    const int n = ::poll(&p, 1, static_cast<int>(ms));
    if (n > 0) return p.revents;
    if (n == 0 && Clock::now() >= deadline) return short{0};
    if (n < 0 && errno != EINTR) return failure(api, "cannot poll", errno);
  }
}

core::Result<std::size_t> send_some(std::string_view api, int fd,
                                    const std::uint8_t* data,
                                    std::size_t size) {
  for (;;) {
    const ssize_t n = ::send(fd, data, std::min(size, kMaxIo), kSendFlags);
    if (n >= 0) return static_cast<std::size_t>(n);
    if (errno == EINTR) continue;
    if (errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK) return std::size_t{0};
    return failure(api, "cannot send", errno);
  }
}

core::Result<std::size_t> unacknowledged(std::string_view api, int fd) {
  int bytes = 0;
#ifdef __APPLE__
  socklen_t size = sizeof bytes;
  const int failed = ::getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_NWRITE, &bytes, &size);
#else
  const int failed = ::ioctl(fd, SIOCOUTQ, &bytes);
#endif
  if (failed != 0) return failure(api, "cannot read the send queue", errno);
  return static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(bytes, 0));
}

core::Result<Received> receive_some(std::string_view api, int fd,
                                    std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size) {
  for (;;) {
    const ssize_t n = ::recv(fd, out, std::min(size, kMaxIo), 0);
    if (n > 0) return Received{static_cast<std::size_t>(n), false};
    if (n == 0) return Received{0, true};
    if (errno == EINTR) continue;
    if (errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK) return Received{};
    return failure(api, "cannot receive", errno);
  }
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/socket.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

// The BSD socket calls the server and the client make, each failure a Status
// naming the caller, what failed and the system's reason. Every socket is
// non-blocking and close-on-exec, set explicitly, accepted ones included
// (Linux does not inherit the flags, and macOS has no accept4), and never
// raises SIGPIPE: SO_NOSIGPIPE on Apple, MSG_NOSIGNAL elsewhere, chosen by
// platform since Apple's SDKs define MSG_NOSIGNAL too. Every call is retried
// on EINTR: an application's signal handler, as fuse_orbbec's for Ctrl+C,
// interrupts poll, which is never restarted.

#include <netinet/in.h>

#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/result.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/unique_fd.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail {

// The longest a thread waits on a socket at a time, so it sees a stop within
// it with no shutdown semantics that differ by OS.
inline constexpr std::chrono::milliseconds kPollSlice{20};
// What a sender's socket may hold unsent before poll stops calling it
// writable (TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT): a viewer takes its next record only below it.
inline constexpr int kSendLowWater = 128 << 10;
// A client's receive buffer, set before the connect so the window scale fits
// it: the most a stream carries a round trip, and what a reader that falls
// behind can hide from the sender's drop rule. Sized for the rig's stream
// over the VPN (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-21 networking).
inline constexpr int kReceiveBuffer = 2 << 20;

// `from` + `limit`, saturating: a limit past the clock's end, as
// milliseconds::max() ("never"), gives that end; one of 0 or less, `from`.
inline std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point after(
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point from,
    std::chrono::milliseconds limit) {
  using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
  if (limit <= std::chrono::milliseconds{0}) return from;
  // Compared in milliseconds: the limit in the clock's nanoseconds may not
  // fit.
  if (limit >= std::chrono::floor<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
                   Clock::time_point::max() - from)) {
    return Clock::time_point::max();
  }
  return from + limit;
}

// An IPv4 socket address. A StreamServer listens on IPv4 alone, so a client
// tries no other family: an IPv6 address could only be refused, or stall a
// connect where IPv6 is broken.
struct Address {
  sockaddr_in in{};
};

// `host`, a numeric IPv4 address ("192.168.21.217"), with `port`; false for
// anything else.
bool parse_ipv4(const std::string& host, std::uint16_t port, Address* out);

// Every IPv4 address `host` resolves to for TCP (getaddrinfo), with `port`.
// Blocks for as long as the resolver takes. NotFound for a name that does not
// resolve; IoError for a lookup that fails otherwise; `api` names the host.
core::Result<std::vector<Address>> resolve(std::string_view api,
                                           const std::string& host,
                                           std::uint16_t port);

// "a.b.c.d:port".
std::string to_string(const Address& address);

// A socket listening on `address` (SO_REUSEADDR, so a restarted sender takes
// its port back at once). IoError for an address that cannot be bound.
core::Result<core::UniqueFd> listen_on(std::string_view api,
                                       const Address& address);

// The port `fd` is bound to.
core::Result<std::uint16_t> bound_port(std::string_view api, int fd);

// The next connection waiting on `listener`, set up to send (TCP_NODELAY,
// TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT at kSendLowWater), and its peer; an empty fd when none
// is waiting, or one failed before it was taken or cannot be set up, which
// is closed.
core::Result<core::UniqueFd> accept_next(std::string_view api, int listener,
                                         Address* peer);

// A socket, its receive buffer kReceiveBuffer, connecting to `address`
// without waiting: `*connected` says whether it already has, else poll it
// writable and call finish_connect. `api` names the address.
core::Result<core::UniqueFd> start_connect(std::string_view api,
                                           const Address& address,
                                           bool* connected);

// The outcome of the connect start_connect began on `fd`, once it polls
// writable.
core::Status finish_connect(std::string_view api, int fd);

// Wait up to `timeout` for `events` on `fd` (poll): the events that came, 0
// when none did.
core::Result<short> wait_for(std::string_view api, int fd, short events,
                             std::chrono::milliseconds timeout);

// Send what `fd` takes now of `size` bytes at `data`: the bytes sent, 0 when
// it takes none.
core::Result<std::size_t> send_some(std::string_view api, int fd,
                                    const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);

// The bytes sent on `fd` that its peer has not acknowledged, unsent ones
// included: SO_NWRITE on Apple, SIOCOUTQ elsewhere.
core::Result<std::size_t> unacknowledged(std::string_view api, int fd);

// What one receive found.
struct Received {
  std::size_t bytes = 0;  // read; 0 when none had come
  bool closed = false;    // the peer closed its side
};

// Receive what has come on `fd`, up to `size` bytes, without waiting.
core::Result<Received> receive_some(std::string_view api, int fd,
                                    std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size);

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking::detail
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_client.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_client.hpp"

#include <poll.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <mutex>
#include <string_view>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>

#include "socket.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/check.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking {
namespace {

using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

constexpr std::string_view kClient = "StreamClient";
// What one receive reads at most: as much as the receive buffer, so one
// next(0) takes a key (about 230 KB) already in the socket.
constexpr std::size_t kReceiveBytes = detail::kReceiveBuffer;

std::chrono::milliseconds until(Clock::time_point when) {
  return std::max(
      std::chrono::ceil<std::chrono::milliseconds>(when - Clock::now()),
      std::chrono::milliseconds{0});
}

}  // namespace

struct StreamClient::Impl {
  // A name's lookup, which a detached thread fills and the client takes: it
  // outlives whichever of the two lets it go last.
  struct Lookup {
    std::mutex mutex;
    std::condition_variable done_cv;
    bool done = false;  // under the mutex, as the two below
    core::Status failure;
    std::vector<detail::Address> addresses;
  };

  Impl(const std::string& host_, std::uint16_t port_,
       const ClientOptions& options_)
      : options(options_),
        name(host_ + ":" + std::to_string(port_)),
        api(std::string(kClient) + ": " + name),
        last_byte(Clock::now()),
        buffer(kReceiveBytes) {}

  // Make one move toward the next record, waiting no later than `deadline`:
  // the lookup's end, the next address's connect, or a receive. True when
  // it moved: the lookup taken, a connect started or ended, or bytes read.
  core::Result<bool> step(Clock::time_point deadline);
  // The idle limit's failure, naming the stage it ended: the lookup, the
  // connect, the session or the stream.
  core::Status idle_failure() const;
  // Close the connection and save `status`, which every later call returns.
  core::Status fail(core::Status status);

  const ClientOptions options;
  const std::string name;                  // "host:port"
  const std::string api;                   // what every message starts with
  Clock::time_point last_byte;             // connect, then each byte's arrival
  std::shared_ptr<Lookup> lookup;          // a name's, until it is taken
  std::vector<detail::Address> addresses;  // to try, in order
  std::size_t tried = 0;                   // those tried, fd's included
  core::Status refused;  // why the last address tried did not connect
  core::UniqueFd fd;
  bool connected = false;
  stream::ChunkParser parser;
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> buffer;  // what a receive reads into
  core::Status failure;
};

core::Result<bool> StreamClient::Impl::step(Clock::time_point deadline) {
  if (lookup) {
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(lookup->mutex);
    if (!lookup->done_cv.wait_until(lock, deadline,
                                    [&] { return lookup->done; })) {
      return false;
    }
    if (!lookup->failure.ok()) return lookup->failure;
    addresses = std::move(lookup->addresses);
    lock.unlock();
    lookup.reset();
    return true;
  }
  if (!fd.valid()) {
    if (tried == addresses.size()) {
      return refused.ok() ? core::Status::io_error(api + ": no address")
                          : refused;
    }
    core::Result<core::UniqueFd> started =
        detail::start_connect(api, addresses[tried++], &connected);
    if (!started.ok()) {
      refused = std::move(started).status();
      return true;
    }
    fd = std::move(started).value();
    return true;
  }
  if (!connected) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(const short ready,
               detail::wait_for(api, fd.get(), POLLOUT, until(deadline)));
    if (ready == 0) return false;
    core::Status done = detail::finish_connect(api, fd.get());
    if (!done.ok()) {
      refused = std::move(done);
      fd.reset();
      return true;
    }
    connected = true;
    return true;
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const short ready,
             detail::wait_for(api, fd.get(), POLLIN, until(deadline)));
  if (ready == 0) return false;
  VKC_ASSIGN(const detail::Received got,
             detail::receive_some(api, fd.get(), buffer.data(), buffer.size()));
  if (got.closed) {
    // A sender at its most viewers closes a connection before any byte.
    return core::Status::io_error(
        api + ": the sender closed the connection" +
        (parser.session() == nullptr
             ? " before its session (it may already serve its most viewers)"
             : ""));
  }
  if (got.bytes == 0) return false;
  last_byte = Clock::now();
  VKC_TRY(parser.feed(buffer.data(), got.bytes).with_context(api));
  return true;
}

core::Status StreamClient::Impl::idle_failure() const {
  const std::string limit = std::to_string(options.idle_limit.count()) + " ms";
  if (lookup) {
    return core::Status::io_error(api + ": the lookup gave no answer within " +
                                  limit);
  }
  if (!connected) {
    return core::Status::io_error(api + ": cannot connect within " + limit);
  }
  if (parser.session() == nullptr) {
    return core::Status::io_error(api + ": connected, but no session within " +
                                  limit);
  }
  return core::Status::io_error(api + ": no byte for " + limit);
}

core::Status StreamClient::Impl::fail(core::Status status) {
  fd.reset();
  failure = std::move(status);
  return failure;
}

StreamClient::StreamClient(std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl) noexcept
    : impl_(std::move(impl)) {}

StreamClient::~StreamClient() = default;

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamClient>> StreamClient::connect(
    const std::string& host, std::uint16_t port, const ClientOptions& options) {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamClient::connect";
  try {
    if (host.empty()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(kApi) +
                                            ": an empty host");
    }
    if (port == 0) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(kApi) + ": port 0");
    }
    if (options.idle_limit <= std::chrono::milliseconds{0}) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          std::string(kApi) + ": an idle_limit of " +
          std::to_string(options.idle_limit.count()) + " ms");
    }
    auto impl = std::make_unique<Impl>(host, port, options);
    detail::Address address;
    if (detail::parse_ipv4(host, port, &address)) {
      impl->addresses.push_back(address);
    } else {
      auto lookup = std::make_shared<Impl::Lookup>();
      std::thread([lookup, host, port, api = impl->api] {
        core::Status failure;
        std::vector<detail::Address> addresses;
        try {
          core::Result<std::vector<detail::Address>> found =
              detail::resolve(api, host, port);
          if (found.ok()) {
            addresses = std::move(found).value();
          } else {
            failure = std::move(found).status();
          }
        } catch (...) {
          failure = core::exception_status(api, core::Status::Code::IoError);
        }
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(lookup->mutex);
        lookup->failure = std::move(failure);
        lookup->addresses = std::move(addresses);
        lookup->done = true;
        lookup->done_cv.notify_all();
      }).detach();
      impl->lookup = std::move(lookup);
    }
    return std::unique_ptr<StreamClient>(new StreamClient(std::move(impl)));
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

const stream::Session* StreamClient::session() const noexcept {
  return impl_->parser.session();
}

core::Result<bool> StreamClient::next(std::chrono::milliseconds wait,
                                      stream::Record* record,
                                      std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload) {
  return next(wait, record, payload, nullptr);
}

core::Result<bool> StreamClient::next(std::chrono::milliseconds wait,
                                      stream::Record* record,
                                      std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload,
                                      bool* progressed) {
  if (progressed != nullptr) *progressed = false;
  VKC_CHECK(record != nullptr, "StreamClient::next takes a record");
  Impl& s = *impl_;
  try {
    if (!s.failure.ok()) return s.failure;
    const Clock::time_point deadline = detail::after(Clock::now(), wait);
    // At least one step, so a wait of 0 still reads what has come. The idle
    // limit is judged only after a step that moved nothing, so a caller back
    // late first takes what came meanwhile: the lookup's answer, the
    // connect's end or bytes. The deadline ends the loop, though bytes keep
    // coming, and the parser keeps a part chunk for the next call.
    for (bool stepped = false, moved = false;; stepped = true) {
      core::Result<bool> got = s.parser.next(record, payload);
      if (!got.ok()) return s.fail(std::move(got).status().with_context(s.api));
      if (*got) {
        if (progressed != nullptr) *progressed = true;
        return true;
      }
      const Clock::time_point idle =
          detail::after(s.last_byte, s.options.idle_limit);
      if (stepped && !moved && Clock::now() >= idle) {
        return s.fail(s.idle_failure());
      }
      if (stepped && Clock::now() >= deadline) return false;
      core::Result<bool> progress = s.step(std::min(deadline, idle));
      if (!progress.ok()) return s.fail(std::move(progress).status());
      moved = *progress;
      if (progressed != nullptr && moved) *progressed = true;
    }
  } catch (...) {
    // Saved and returned, each by its own call: a copy may find no memory.
    s.fd.reset();
    if (s.failure.ok()) {
      s.failure = core::exception_status(s.api, core::Status::Code::IoError);
    }
    return core::exception_status(s.api, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamClient::read(const stream::Record& record, std::uint8_t* dst,
                                std::size_t capacity) {
  Impl& s = *impl_;
  if (!s.failure.ok()) return s.failure;
  // A refusal leaves the record held and the connection open: the caller's
  // to correct.
  return s.parser.read(record, dst, capacity);
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/networking/stream_server.hpp"

#include <poll.h>

#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <list>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <string_view>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "gop_log.hpp"
#include "socket.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/log.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/chunks.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::networking {
namespace {

using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

constexpr std::string_view kServer = "StreamServer";
constexpr std::uint8_t kZeros[8] = {};
// What a viewer thread reads at a time of the bytes a viewer sends, which it
// drops.
constexpr std::size_t kDrainBytes = 4096;
// The least time between two refusals logged at Warning; the rest go at Debug.
constexpr std::chrono::seconds kRefusalWarningEvery{10};

// grid's log_message, from a thread or a catch no exception may leave.
// Viewers come and go at Info, which the core's default sink drops and a
// sender prints, as serve_stream and fuse_orbbec do.
void log_at(core::LogLevel level, const std::string& message) noexcept {
  try {
    log_message(level, message);
  } catch (...) {
  }
}

}  // namespace

struct StreamServer::Impl {
  // One viewer: its socket and its thread.
  struct Viewer {
    core::UniqueFd fd;  // its thread's, which closes it
    std::string name;   // its address, for the log
    bool done = false;  // under the mutex: its thread has ended
    // Under the mutex: its place in the log, which it joins as its thread
    // starts and leaves as it ends.
    detail::GopLog::Cursor cursor;
    std::thread thread;
  };

  Impl(stream::ChunkEncoder encoder_, const ServerOptions& options_,
       detail::Chunk session_chunk_, core::UniqueFd listener_,
       std::uint16_t port_)
      : encoder(std::move(encoder_)),
        options(options_),
        session_chunk(std::move(session_chunk_)),
        listener(std::move(listener_)),
        port(port_),
        log(options_.max_gop_bytes, options_.replay_gop) {}

  // The accept thread: take each connection, admit it or close it, and join
  // the threads of viewers that have ended, until the stop.
  void accept_loop() noexcept;
  // Count `fd`'s viewer in and start its thread, or close it past
  // max_viewers.
  void admit(core::UniqueFd fd, std::string name);
  // Join the threads of the viewers that have ended.
  void reap();
  // A viewer's thread: join the log, send it everything, then close it, leave
  // the log and say why.
  void serve(Viewer& viewer) noexcept;
  // Send the session chunk, then the log's chunks as the socket takes them,
  // until the viewer leaves, fails or stalls, or the server stops: why.
  std::string send_all(Viewer& viewer);
  // Publish the log's count of the viewers that wanted a key. Under the
  // mutex.
  void count_key_wanted() noexcept { key_wanted = log.key_wanted(); }

  stream::ChunkEncoder encoder;  // the publishing thread's
  const ServerOptions options;
  const detail::Chunk session_chunk;
  const core::UniqueFd listener;
  const std::uint16_t port;

  std::mutex mutex;
  std::condition_variable wake;   // a record published, or the stop
  detail::GopLog log;             // under the mutex
  std::atomic<bool> stop{false};  // set under the mutex
  // The log's key_wanted(), set under the mutex and read from any thread.
  std::atomic<std::uint64_t> key_wanted{0};
  // The viewers being served: added by the accept thread, taken off by each
  // viewer's thread as it ends, read from any thread.
  std::atomic<std::size_t> live{0};

  std::list<Viewer> viewers;  // the accept thread's, then the destructor's
  // The accept thread's: when a refusal was last logged at Warning.
  std::optional<Clock::time_point> refusal_warned;
  std::thread acceptor;
};

void StreamServer::Impl::accept_loop() noexcept {
  while (!stop) {
    try {
      reap();
      const core::Result<short> ready =
          detail::wait_for(kServer, listener.get(), POLLIN, detail::kPollSlice);
      if (ready.ok() && *ready == 0) continue;
      detail::Address peer;
      core::Result<core::UniqueFd> accepted =
          ready.ok() ? detail::accept_next(kServer, listener.get(), &peer)
                     : core::Result<core::UniqueFd>(ready.status());
      if (!accepted.ok()) {
        // A failure that may pass (out of descriptors): say so, wait a
        // slice and try again.
        log_at(core::LogLevel::Warning, accepted.status().message());
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(detail::kPollSlice);
        continue;
      }
      if (accepted->valid()) {
        admit(std::move(accepted).value(), detail::to_string(peer));
      }
    } catch (...) {
      log_at(core::LogLevel::Warning,
             core::exception_status(kServer, core::Status::Code::IoError)
                 .message());
      std::this_thread::sleep_for(detail::kPollSlice);
    }
  }
}

void StreamServer::Impl::admit(core::UniqueFd fd, std::string name) {
  // Only this thread adds viewers, so one admitted after this check still
  // fits.
  std::size_t serving = live;
  if (serving >= options.max_viewers) {
    fd.reset();  // closed at accept: the viewer sees its end before any byte
    // At Warning, which the default sink prints, so the owner sees why a
    // viewer gets nothing: the first refusal, then one in 10 s at most. The
    // rest at Debug, so a sender that prints Info is not flooded either.
    const Clock::time_point now = Clock::now();
    const bool warn =
