### src/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_reader.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <iterator>
#include <utility>

#include "chunk.hpp"
#include "file.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/check.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/file_io.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {
namespace {

// What a footer's key entries are read in: whole entries.
constexpr std::size_t kFooterBlock = std::size_t{1} << 20;
static_assert(kFooterBlock % detail::kKeyEntryBytes == 0,
              "a footer block holds whole key entries");

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamReader>> StreamReader::open(
    const std::string& path, const ReaderOptions& options) {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::open";
  try {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_path(kApi, path));
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::UniqueFd fd, detail::open_file(kApi, path));
    VKC_ASSIGN(const std::uint64_t size,
               detail::regular_file_size(kApi, path, fd.get()));
    std::unique_ptr<StreamReader> reader(new StreamReader());
    const detail::FileView file{fd.get(), &path, size, 0};
    VKC_ASSIGN(reader->begin_,
               detail::read_session(kApi, file, &reader->session_));
    reader->fd_ = std::move(fd);
    reader->path_ = path;
    reader->options_ = options;
    reader->file_size_ = size;
    VKC_ASSIGN(const bool finished, reader->read_footer());
    if (!finished) VKC_TRY(reader->scan());
    return reader;
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Result<bool> StreamReader::read_footer() {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::open";
  const std::size_t tracks = session_.tracks.size();
  const detail::FileView file{fd_.get(), &path_, file_size_,
                              static_cast<std::uint32_t>(tracks)};
  if (begin_ > file_size_ ||
      file_size_ - begin_ < detail::kIndexHeaderBytes + detail::kTailBytes) {
    return false;  // a cut inside the session header's padding, or no room
  }
  // The offset chain, all that makes the two a footer: the TAIL ends the
  // file and names the INDX, which ends where the TAIL starts.
  const std::uint64_t tail_at = file_size_ - detail::kTailBytes;
  detail::Chunk tail;
  VKC_ASSIGN(bool valid, detail::read_chunk(kApi, file, tail_at, &tail));
  if (!valid || tail.tag != detail::kTailTag || tail.body_bytes != 0 ||
      tail.body_crc != 0) {
    return false;  // its H is 40: no more is left, and no TAIL has less
  }
  const std::uint64_t index_at = tail.index_offset;
  if (index_at % 8 != 0 || index_at < begin_ || index_at >= tail_at) {
    return false;
  }
  detail::Chunk index;
  VKC_ASSIGN(valid, detail::read_chunk(kApi, file, index_at, &index));
  // A key record takes at least its header's 56 bytes, which bounds K before
  // anything is sized by it.
  if (!valid || index.tag != detail::kIndexTag || index.tracks != tracks ||
      index.keys > file_size_ / detail::kRecordHeaderBytes ||
      index.header_bytes > tail_at - index_at ||
      index.body_bytes != tail_at - index_at - index.header_bytes ||
      index.body_bytes != detail::kSummaryBytes * tracks +
                              detail::kKeyEntryBytes * index.keys) {
    return false;
  }

  // The track summaries, then the key entries: in file order, each a chunk
  // position between the session header and the index (begin_ > 0, so the
  // first passes `last`), of a track the session has, no track's pts
  // decreasing; and as many of each track as its summary counts.
  std::uint64_t at = index_at + index.header_bytes;
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> block(
      static_cast<std::size_t>(detail::kSummaryBytes * tracks));
  VKC_TRY(
      detail::read_at(kApi, path_, fd_.get(), at, block.data(), block.size()));
  at += block.size();
  std::uint32_t crc = detail::crc32(block.data(), block.size());
  stats_.assign(tracks, TrackStats{});
  keys_.assign(tracks, {});
  keys_unordered_.assign(tracks, false);
  for (std::size_t t = 0; t < tracks; ++t) {
    stats_[t] = detail::load_summary(block.data() + detail::kSummaryBytes * t);
  }
  std::uint64_t last = 0;
  block.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(std::min<std::uint64_t>(
      kFooterBlock, detail::kKeyEntryBytes * index.keys)));
  for (std::uint64_t left = index.keys; left > 0;) {
    const auto n = static_cast<std::size_t>(
        std::min<std::uint64_t>(block.size() / detail::kKeyEntryBytes, left));
    const std::size_t bytes = n * detail::kKeyEntryBytes;
    VKC_TRY(detail::read_at(kApi, path_, fd_.get(), at, block.data(), bytes));
    at += bytes;
    left -= n;
    crc = detail::crc32(block.data(), bytes, crc);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      const detail::KeyEntry e =
          detail::load_key_entry(block.data() + detail::kKeyEntryBytes * i);
      if (e.offset % 8 != 0 || e.offset <= last || e.offset < begin_ ||
          e.offset >= index_at || e.track >= tracks) {
        return false;
      }
      std::vector<KeyPoint>& keys = keys_[e.track];
      if (!keys.empty() && e.pts_ns < keys.back().pts_ns) return false;
      keys.push_back({e.offset, e.pts_ns});
      last = e.offset;
    }
  }
  if (crc != index.body_crc) return false;
  for (std::size_t t = 0; t < tracks; ++t) {
    if (keys_[t].size() != stats_[t].keys) return false;
  }
  recovery_.finished = true;
  recovery_.end = file_size_;
  return true;
}

core::Status StreamReader::scan() {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::open";
  const std::size_t tracks = session_.tracks.size();
  stats_.assign(tracks, TrackStats{});
  keys_.assign(tracks, {});
  keys_unordered_.assign(tracks, false);
  const detail::FileView file{fd_.get(), &path_, file_size_,
                              static_cast<std::uint32_t>(tracks)};
  // Where a footer's TAIL starts, and whether the scan looked for a chunk
  // there; elsewhere those bytes are inside a chunk (a payload, perhaps).
  const std::uint64_t tail_at = file_size_ - detail::kTailBytes;
  bool tail_reached = false;
  std::uint64_t pos = begin_;
  while (pos < file_size_) {
    tail_reached = tail_reached || pos == tail_at;
    detail::Chunk c;
    VKC_ASSIGN(const bool valid, detail::read_chunk(kApi, file, pos, &c));
    if (!valid) {
      VKC_ASSIGN(const std::uint64_t found,
                 detail::resync(kApi, file, pos, file_size_));
      if (found == file_size_) break;  // the rest is torn
      recovery_.damaged_bytes += found - pos;
      ++recovery_.damaged_spans;
      pos = found;
      continue;
    }
    if (c.body_bytes > file_size_ - pos - c.header_bytes) break;  // torn
    if (detail::known_record(c)) {
      detail::count_record(stats_[c.record.track], c.record, c.body_bytes);
      if (c.record.key) {
        std::vector<KeyPoint>& keys = keys_[c.record.track];
        if (!keys.empty() && c.record.pts_ns < keys.back().pts_ns) {
          keys_unordered_[c.record.track] = true;
        }
        keys.push_back({pos, c.record.pts_ns});
      }
    }
    pos += c.header_bytes + c.body_bytes + detail::padding(c.body_bytes);
  }
  recovery_.end = std::min(pos, file_size_);
  recovery_.torn_bytes = file_size_ - recovery_.end;
  // A chunk tagged TAIL where the footer's starts, intact or not: the file
  // was finished, and read_footer refused its footer.
  if (tail_reached) {
    std::uint8_t tag[4];
    VKC_TRY(detail::read_at(kApi, path_, fd_.get(), tail_at, tag, sizeof(tag)));
    recovery_.footer_damaged = detail::load_le32(tag) == detail::kTailTag;
  }
  return {};
}

const Session& StreamReader::session() const noexcept { return session_; }

const Recovery& StreamReader::recovery() const noexcept { return recovery_; }

const std::vector<TrackStats>& StreamReader::stats() const noexcept {
  return stats_;
}

std::size_t StreamReader::key_count(std::uint16_t track) const noexcept {
  return track < keys_.size() ? keys_[track].size() : 0;
}

core::Result<Position> StreamReader::key(std::uint16_t track,
                                         std::size_t n) const {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::key";
  try {
    if (track >= keys_.size()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "StreamReader::key: " + path_ + ": track " + std::to_string(track) +
          ", but the session has " + std::to_string(keys_.size()));
    }
    if (n >= keys_[track].size()) {
      return core::Status::not_found(
          "StreamReader::key: " + path_ + ": track " + std::to_string(track) +
          " has " + std::to_string(keys_[track].size()) + " key records, no " +
          std::to_string(n));
    }
    return Position{keys_[track][n].offset};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Result<Position> StreamReader::key_at(std::uint16_t track,
                                            std::uint64_t pts_ns) const {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::key_at";
  try {
    const auto where = [&] {
      return "StreamReader::key_at: " + path_ + ": track " +
             std::to_string(track);
    };
    if (track >= keys_.size()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(where() + ", but the session has " +
                                            std::to_string(keys_.size()));
    }
    if (keys_unordered_[track]) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          where() + "'s key pts decrease, so no key is found by its pts");
    }
    const std::vector<KeyPoint>& keys = keys_[track];
    const auto after =
        std::upper_bound(keys.begin(), keys.end(), pts_ns,
                         [](std::uint64_t pts, const KeyPoint& key) {
                           return pts < key.pts_ns;
                         });
    if (after == keys.begin()) {
      return core::Status::not_found(where() +
                                     " has no key record at or before pts " +
                                     std::to_string(pts_ns));
    }
    return Position{std::prev(after)->offset};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

Position StreamReader::begin() const noexcept { return Position{begin_}; }

core::Result<bool> StreamReader::next(Position* pos, Record* record) const {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::next";
  VKC_CHECK(pos != nullptr && record != nullptr,
            "StreamReader::next takes a position and a record");
  try {
    if (pos->offset % 8 != 0 || pos->offset < begin_) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(kApi) + ": " + path_ +
                                            ": " + std::to_string(pos->offset) +
                                            " is not a chunk position");
    }
    const detail::FileView file{
        fd_.get(), &path_, file_size_,
        static_cast<std::uint32_t>(session_.tracks.size())};
    while (pos->offset < recovery_.end) {
      const std::uint64_t at = pos->offset;
      detail::Chunk c;
      VKC_ASSIGN(const bool valid, detail::read_chunk(kApi, file, at, &c));
      if (!valid) {
        VKC_ASSIGN(pos->offset, detail::resync(kApi, file, at, recovery_.end));
        return core::Status::invalid_argument(
            std::string(kApi) + ": " + path_ + ": a damaged chunk header at " +
            std::to_string(at) + "; reading resumes at " +
            std::to_string(pos->offset));
      }
      if (c.body_bytes > file_size_ - at - c.header_bytes) {
        pos->offset = recovery_.end;  // the torn tail, as the scan found it
        return false;
      }
      pos->offset =
          at + c.header_bytes + c.body_bytes + detail::padding(c.body_bytes);
      if (c.tag != detail::kRecordTag) continue;
      if (!detail::known_record(c)) {
        return core::Status::unsupported(
            std::string(kApi) + ": " + path_ + ": the record at " +
            std::to_string(at) + " sets flags " + std::to_string(c.flags) +
            ", which version 0 does not define");
      }
      record->info = c.record;
      record->offset = at;
      record->size = c.body_bytes;
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamReader::read(const Record& record,
                                std::vector<std::uint8_t>* payload) const {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::read";
  VKC_CHECK(payload != nullptr, "StreamReader::read takes a payload");
  try {
    if (record.size > options_.max_payload_bytes ||
        record.size > payload->max_size()) {
      return core::Status::out_of_memory(
          std::string(kApi) + ": " + path_ + ": the record at " +
          std::to_string(record.offset) + " holds " +
          std::to_string(record.size) + " bytes, above the limit of " +
          std::to_string(options_.max_payload_bytes));
    }
    payload->resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(record.size));
    return read(record, payload->data(), payload->size());
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamReader::read(const Record& record, std::uint8_t* dst,
                                std::size_t capacity) const {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamReader::read";
  try {
    const auto where = [&] {
      return std::string(kApi) + ": " + path_ + ": the record at " +
             std::to_string(record.offset);
    };
    if (capacity < record.size || (dst == nullptr && record.size != 0)) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          where() + " holds " + std::to_string(record.size) +
          " bytes, more than the " + std::to_string(capacity) +
          " bytes given (or none)");
    }
    const detail::FileView file{
        fd_.get(), &path_, file_size_,
        static_cast<std::uint32_t>(session_.tracks.size())};
    detail::Chunk c;
    bool valid = false;
    if (record.offset % 8 == 0 && record.offset >= begin_) {
      VKC_ASSIGN(valid, detail::read_chunk(kApi, file, record.offset, &c));
    }
    const RecordInfo& info = record.info;
    if (!valid || c.tag != detail::kRecordTag || c.body_bytes != record.size ||
        c.body_bytes > file_size_ - record.offset - c.header_bytes ||
        c.record.track != info.track || c.record.key != info.key ||
        c.record.pts_ns != info.pts_ns || c.record.seq != info.seq ||
        c.record.set != info.set) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(where() +
                                            " does not match its header");
    }
    const auto bytes = static_cast<std::size_t>(record.size);
    VKC_TRY(detail::read_at(kApi, path_, fd_.get(),
                            record.offset + c.header_bytes, dst, bytes));
    if (detail::crc32(dst, bytes) != c.body_crc) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(where() +
                                            ": its payload fails its CRC");
    }
    return {};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_writer.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/stream/stream_writer.hpp"

#include <unistd.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <utility>

#include "chunk.hpp"
#include "file.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/exception_status.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/base/file_io.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream {
namespace {

constexpr std::uint8_t kZeros[8] = {};

}  // namespace

StreamWriter::StreamWriter(core::UniqueFd fd, std::string path,
                           ChunkEncoder encoder, std::size_t tracks)
    : fd_(std::move(fd)),
      path_(std::move(path)),
      encoder_(std::move(encoder)),
      size_(encoder_.session_chunk().size()),
      stats_(tracks) {}

StreamWriter::~StreamWriter() = default;

core::Result<std::unique_ptr<StreamWriter>> StreamWriter::create(
    const std::string& path, const Session& session) {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamWriter::create";
  bool created = false;
  try {
    VKC_TRY(core::check_path(kApi, path));
    core::Result<ChunkEncoder> encoder = ChunkEncoder::create(session);
    if (!encoder.ok()) {
      return std::move(encoder).status().with_context(std::string(kApi) + ": " +
                                                      path);
    }
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::UniqueFd fd, detail::create_new_file(kApi, path));
    created = true;
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& header = encoder->session_chunk();
    const detail::Bytes part{header.data(), header.size()};
    core::Status written = detail::write_all(kApi, path, fd.get(), &part, 1);
    if (written.ok()) written = detail::flush_file(kApi, path, fd.get());
    if (!written.ok()) {
      fd.reset();
      ::unlink(path.c_str());
      return written;
    }
    detail::flush_directory_of(path);
    return std::unique_ptr<StreamWriter>(
        new StreamWriter(std::move(fd), path, std::move(encoder).value(),
                         session.tracks.size()));
  } catch (...) {
    core::Status failure =
        core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
    if (created) ::unlink(path.c_str());
    return failure;
  }
}

core::Status StreamWriter::check_open(std::string_view api) const {
  if (!failure_.ok()) return failure_;
  if (finished_) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(std::string(api) + ": " + path_ +
                                          " is finished");
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status StreamWriter::append(const RecordInfo& info,
                                  const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamWriter::append";
  try {
    VKC_TRY(check_open(kApi));
    if (data == nullptr && size != 0) {
      return detail::null_payload(size).with_context(std::string(kApi) + ": " +
                                                     path_);
    }
    return append(info, RecordPayload::of(data, size));
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamWriter::append(const RecordInfo& info,
                                  const RecordPayload& payload) {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamWriter::append";
  try {
    VKC_TRY(check_open(kApi));
    const std::size_t size = payload.size();
    // The index entry's room comes first, before the encoder counts the
    // record, so a refused allocation leaves the writer unchanged and a
    // record once written is always indexed.
    if (info.key &&
        index_keys_.capacity() - index_keys_.size() < detail::kKeyEntryBytes) {
      index_keys_.reserve(std::max<std::size_t>(2 * index_keys_.capacity(),
                                                64 * detail::kKeyEntryBytes));
    }
    core::Result<ChunkEncoder::RecordFraming> framed =
        encoder_.frame(info, payload);
    if (!framed.ok()) {
      return std::move(framed).status().with_context(std::string(kApi) + ": " +
                                                     path_);
    }
    const ChunkEncoder::RecordFraming& framing = *framed;
    const detail::Bytes parts[4] = {
        {framing.header.data(), framing.header.size()},
        {payload.first(), payload.first_size()},
        {payload.second(), payload.second_size()},
        {kZeros, framing.padding}};
    core::Status written = detail::write_all(kApi, path_, fd_.get(), parts, 4);
    if (!written.ok()) {
      failure_ = std::move(written);
      return failure_;
    }
    const std::uint64_t offset = size_;
    size_ += framing.header.size() + std::uint64_t{size} + framing.padding;
    if (info.key) detail::append_key_entry(index_keys_, offset, info);
    detail::count_record(stats_[info.track], info, size);
    return {};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamWriter::sync() {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamWriter::sync";
  try {
    VKC_TRY(check_open(kApi));
    core::Status flushed = detail::flush_file(kApi, path_, fd_.get());
    if (!flushed.ok()) {
      failure_ = std::move(flushed);
      return failure_;
    }
    return {};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

core::Status StreamWriter::finish() {
  constexpr std::string_view kApi = "StreamWriter::finish";
  try {
    VKC_TRY(check_open(kApi));
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> footer =
        detail::encode_footer(stats_, index_keys_, size_);
    const detail::Bytes part{footer.data(), footer.size()};
    core::Status done = detail::write_all(kApi, path_, fd_.get(), &part, 1);
    if (done.ok()) done = detail::flush_file(kApi, path_, fd_.get());
    if (done.ok()) done = detail::close_file(kApi, path_, fd_);
    if (!done.ok()) {
      failure_ = std::move(done);
      return failure_;
    }
    size_ += footer.size();
    finished_ = true;
    return {};
  } catch (...) {
    return core::exception_status(kApi, core::Status::Code::IoError);
  }
}

std::uint64_t StreamWriter::size() const noexcept { return size_; }

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::stream
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/grid_growth.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/grid_growth.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <new>

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

core::Status grow_grid(VoxelBlockGrid& grid, std::int32_t at_least,
                       core::StageMetrics* metrics) try {
  if (!grid.valid() || at_least < 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "grow_grid: requires a live grid and a non-negative minimum");
  }
  const std::int32_t ceiling = grid.max_num_buckets();
  if (grid.grid().num_buckets >= ceiling || at_least > ceiling) {
    return core::Status::out_of_memory("grow_grid: grid capacity limit");
  }
  const auto target = static_cast<std::int32_t>(std::min<std::int64_t>(
      std::max<std::int64_t>(2 * std::int64_t(grid.grid().num_buckets),
                             at_least),
      ceiling));
  core::StageScope span(metrics, "resize");
  return grid.resize(target);
} catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
  return core::Status::out_of_memory("grow_grid: host allocation failed");
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file volume/hash.hpp
/// @brief The device hash table's entry layout and fail-tally slots.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed): the map sizes its table by
/// @ref HashEntry and splits its retry tally by these slots, and its kernels
/// read both through `volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl`, which mirrors them.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/math/vector_types.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// Hash-table entry -- one per slot in the table. `hash_common.glsl`'s
/// `HashEntry` is its device half, byte-identical under scalar block layout
/// (the 2026-07-05 ABI; DESIGN.md's gotchas say why not `std430`).
struct HashEntry {
  std::int32_t ptr;     ///< A block pointer, or `hash_common.glsl`'s
                        ///< `kFreeEntry` / `kLockEntry`.
  Vec3i pos;            ///< Block coordinate (signed, 32-bit per axis).
  std::int32_t offset;  ///< Collision offset for linked-list chaining.
};
static_assert(sizeof(HashEntry) == 20, "HashEntry must be 20 bytes");
static_assert(offsetof(HashEntry, ptr) == 0, "HashEntry layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(HashEntry, pos) == 4, "HashEntry layout drift");
static_assert(offsetof(HashEntry, offset) == 16, "HashEntry layout drift");

/// @name Fail-count slots
/// The layout of the per-dispatch failure tally the allocate and delete kernels
/// share, mirrored from `volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl`.
///
/// Every slot but @ref kFailTerminal is **retryable**: the host re-dispatches
/// while the total keeps dropping, because the element that failed is still
/// unprocessed and so restates itself next round. @ref kFailTerminal does not,
/// and the split is what keeps the reported count honest -- a delete whose heap
/// append fails has already cleared its table entry, so the next round finds
/// the coord absent and counts nothing. Accumulated across rounds rather than
/// read from the last one, or a permanently leaked block index would be
/// reported as a clean delete.
///
/// Retryable is not the same as *resolvable*: @ref kFailChain, @ref kFailHeap
/// and @ref kFailTable restate themselves honestly every round and are answered
/// by @ref VoxelHashMap::resize, not by another dispatch. Only @ref kFailLock
/// can clear on its own.
/// @{
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailTotal = 0;     ///< Retryable total.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailLock = 1;      ///< Lock contention.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailChain = 2;     ///< Collision chain full.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailHeap = 3;      ///< Block heap (too) low.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailTerminal = 4;  ///< Non-retryable.
/// No free non-anchor slot anywhere in the table: the overflow scan swept every
/// entry and every one it may use was occupied. Proof of exhaustion rather than
/// a heuristic -- the scan is deliberately uncapped, and one that skipped a
/// free-looking slot because another thread held its bucket reports
/// @ref kFailLock instead, so this reason never stands in for contention.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailTable = 5;
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFailSlots = 6;  ///< Slots in the tally.
/// @}

/// @brief What a recorded removal's or allocation's rounds leave in its
///        result slot: `hash_rounds.comp`'s `RoundsResult`, written whole by
///        its gather, and @ref VoxelHashMap::settle's input.
struct RoundsResult {
  std::uint32_t total;      ///< The last round's retryable failures.
  std::uint32_t lock;       ///< Of them, lost bucket-lock races.
  std::uint32_t chain;      ///< Collision chain full.
  std::uint32_t heap;       ///< Block heap (too) low.
  std::uint32_t table;      ///< No free non-anchor slot.
  std::uint32_t terminal;   ///< Non-retryable, over every round.
  std::uint32_t rounds;     ///< Rounds run.
  std::uint32_t heap_free;  ///< The heap counter after them.
};
static_assert(sizeof(RoundsResult) == 4 * 8,
              "RoundsResult is eight words, as hash_rounds.comp writes it");

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_map_internal.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file hash_map_internal.hpp
/// @brief @ref VoxelHashMap::Internal: the hash-entry array, for the voxel
///        grid's own kernels that resolve blocks by coordinate on the device.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed): the codec, mesh and voxelize tiers
/// include it on their private `src/` path and read the table through
/// `volume/shaders/hash_lookup.glsl` or `hash_common.glsl`, whose layout is
/// internal too. A consumer's kernel gets the grid's contract alone
/// (`grid_types.glsl`), never a slot.

#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_hash_map.hpp"

#include "table_sizes.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

class VoxelHashMap::Internal {
 public:
  Internal() = delete;

  /// @brief The device hash-entry array, for a kernel that resolves blocks by
  ///        coordinate itself instead of being handed a host-built table.
  ///
  /// The alternative is worse. A kernel that needs the neighbourhood of N
  /// blocks otherwise pays an O(N) serial host pass of coordinate lookups
  /// plus an upload -- 102 ms of a 133 ms mesh extract at 107k blocks,
  /// measured on an M5 iPad Pro -- to hand the GPU a table it could have
  /// built itself in parallel. `volume/shaders/hash_lookup.glsl` is the
  /// read-only traversal, mirroring `find_block` and taking the table shape
  /// as arguments.
  ///
  /// @warning Read-only, and only safe while **nothing is mutating the
  ///          table** -- no allocate / remove / clear / resize dispatch in
  ///          flight. Probing concurrently with an insert would race the
  ///          bucket locks this deliberately does not expose. A meshing pass
  ///          qualifies because it is quiescent by construction; a pass that
  ///          also allocates does not.
  /// @warning **Do not cache the handle.** A completed @ref resize replaces
  ///          the entry buffer outright -- the old allocation is destroyed, so
  ///          a handle held in a persistent descriptor set then names freed
  ///          memory, which is a validation-layer-only diagnostic and
  ///          undefined with layers off. Both shipped examples resize mid-scan
  ///          on block-heap overflow. Re-fetch on every use, exactly as
  ///          @ref AttributeView requires across a @ref VoxelBlockGrid::resize;
  ///          a move of the map has the same effect.
  /// @return The entry buffer, or `VK_NULL_HANDLE` on a moved-from map.
  static VkBuffer entries_buffer(const VoxelHashMap& map) noexcept {
    return map.entries_.valid() ? map.entries_.handle() : VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  }

  /// @brief Bytes in @ref entries_buffer, for a `VK_WHOLE_SIZE`-free binding.
  ///
  /// Pair it with @ref entries_buffer: bind the range rather than
  /// `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` so the caller can check it against the device's
  /// `maxStorageBufferRange` first. That limit matters here -- the table holds
  /// an entry a slot and @ref resize doubles `num_buckets`, while Vulkan
  /// guarantees only 2^27 (128 MiB), which is what Android-class drivers
  /// report and no driver this repo tests on does.
  /// @return The size in bytes, or 0 on a moved-from map (so the pair stays
  ///         consistent: a null handle never carries a non-zero range).
  static VkDeviceSize entries_buffer_size(const VoxelHashMap& map) noexcept {
    // Gated on the same `valid()` as entries_buffer(), not on grid_ alone:
    // grid_ is a POD the defaulted move COPIES, so a moved-from map still
    // knows its table shape while owning no buffer. Reporting the shape there
    // would pair a VK_NULL_HANDLE with a non-zero range in exactly the
    // descriptor write these two exist to spell -- invalid usage this repo
    // cannot detect (neither nullDescriptor nor robustBufferAccess is
    // enabled), and one that looks well-formed in a debugger.
    if (!map.entries_.valid()) return 0;
    return table_sizes(std::uint64_t(map.grid_.num_buckets),
                       std::uint64_t(map.grid_.bucket_size))
        .entries;
  }
};

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/table_sizes.hpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#pragma once

/// @file table_sizes.hpp
/// @brief The sizes of a @ref VoxelHashMap's buffers that scale with its
///        grid.
///
/// Internal (under src/, never installed): the map allocates its buffers at
/// these sizes, and @ref VoxelBlockGrid::bytes_at reports what a grid of
/// another size would take, so the two read one table.

#include <cstdint>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/hash_types.hpp"

#include "hash.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {

/// The map's grid-sized buffers, in bytes, for one grid.
struct TableSizes {
  VkDeviceSize entries = 0;            ///< A @ref HashEntry a slot.
  VkDeviceSize heap = 0;               ///< A block index a block.
  VkDeviceSize bucket_mutex = 0;       ///< A lock a bucket.
  VkDeviceSize compacted = 0;          ///< A @ref BlockIndex a block.
  VkDeviceSize frustum_compacted = 0;  ///< A @ref BlockIndex a block.
  VkDeviceSize stamps = 0;             ///< A @ref BlockStamp a block.

  /// @return Every buffer above, together.
  VkDeviceSize total() const noexcept {
    return entries + heap + bucket_mutex + compacted + frustum_compacted +
           stamps;
  }
};

/// @param num_buckets  The grid's bucket count.
/// @param bucket_size  Its slots a bucket; a grid holds a block a slot
///                     (@ref VoxelGridParams::validate).
/// @return Its buffers' sizes.
inline TableSizes table_sizes(std::uint64_t num_buckets,
                              std::uint64_t bucket_size) noexcept {
  const VkDeviceSize blocks = num_buckets * bucket_size;
  TableSizes sizes;
  sizes.entries = blocks * sizeof(HashEntry);
  sizes.heap = blocks * sizeof(std::uint32_t);
  sizes.bucket_mutex = num_buckets * sizeof(std::int32_t);
  sizes.compacted = blocks * sizeof(BlockIndex);
  sizes.frustum_compacted = blocks * sizeof(BlockIndex);
  sizes.stamps = blocks * sizeof(BlockStamp);
  return sizes;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/triangle_candidates.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/triangle_candidates.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <limits>
#include <string>

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_coords.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {
namespace {

// Every component finite. A mesh vertex is caller data, and one NaN turns a
// bounding box into a block range of garbage extent -- so it is tested before
// the box is formed rather than after.
bool all_finite(Vec3f v) {
  return std::isfinite(v.x) && std::isfinite(v.y) && std::isfinite(v.z);
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<std::vector<std::uint32_t>> triangle_candidate_offsets(
    const VoxelGridParams& grid, const Vec3f* vertices,
    std::uint32_t vertex_count, const std::uint32_t* indices,
    std::uint32_t triangle_count, const char* who) {
  const std::string name =
      who != nullptr ? who : "volume::triangle_candidate_offsets";
  // Refused before the offsets are allocated: a null mesh with a large count
  // would otherwise spend gigabytes to report an argument error.
  if (triangle_count != 0 && (vertices == nullptr || indices == nullptr)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(name +
                                          ": vertices or indices is null");
  }
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> offsets(std::size_t{triangle_count} + 1, 0u);
  if (triangle_count == 0) {
    return offsets;
  }

  std::uint64_t total = 0;
  for (std::uint32_t t = 0; t < triangle_count; ++t) {
    offsets[t] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(total);

    const std::uint32_t i0 = indices[3 * std::size_t{t}];
    const std::uint32_t i1 = indices[3 * std::size_t{t} + 1];
    const std::uint32_t i2 = indices[3 * std::size_t{t} + 2];
    if (i0 >= vertex_count || i1 >= vertex_count || i2 >= vertex_count) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          name + ": a triangle index is at or past vertex_count");
    }
    const Vec3f v0 = vertices[i0];
    const Vec3f v1 = vertices[i1];
    const Vec3f v2 = vertices[i2];

    // Skipped triangles keep their offsets[t] and contribute no work item; the
    // kernel's search steps over the resulting zero-length run. A non-finite
    // vertex has no bounding box, and a zero-area one is what would divide by
    // zero in the closest-point solve.
    if (!all_finite(v0) || !all_finite(v1) || !all_finite(v2)) {
      continue;
    }
    const Vec3f normal = cross(v1 - v0, v2 - v0);
    if (dot(normal, normal) <= 0.0f) {
      continue;
    }

    // Mirrored bit-for-bit by vgridCandidateBlock, which recomputes rather than
    // reads this back -- see triangle_candidates.glsl.
    const Vec3f lo = glm::min(v0, glm::min(v1, v2)) - Vec3f(grid.trunc_dist);
    const Vec3f hi = glm::max(v0, glm::max(v1, v2)) + Vec3f(grid.trunc_dist);
    const Vec3i bmin = world_to_block(lo, grid);
    const Vec3i bmax = world_to_block(hi, grid);
    const std::uint64_t n = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(bmax.x - bmin.x + 1) *
                            static_cast<std::uint64_t>(bmax.y - bmin.y + 1) *
                            static_cast<std::uint64_t>(bmax.z - bmin.z + 1);

    total += n;
    // One work item per candidate block, so the total is the dispatch width.
    // Reaching 2^32 of them means the mesh is enormously out of scale with the
    // grid -- a model in millimetres read as metres is the usual cause -- and
    // saying so beats truncating the count and covering a fraction of it.
    if (total > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          name +
          ": candidate blocks exceed 2^32 -- is the mesh scaled to the grid's "
          "units (metres)?");
    }
  }
  offsets[triangle_count] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(total);
  return offsets;
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.cpp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/voxel_block_grid.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <limits>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/command_batch.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/compute_util.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/device.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/core/vulkan/vulkan.hpp"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/base/dispatch.hpp"

#include "hash_map_internal.hpp"
#include "table_sizes.hpp"

#include "block_stamp_comp.spv.hpp"
#include "block_zero_comp.spv.hpp"

namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume {
namespace {

// Both kernels run a workgroup a listed block, item_base the first block a
// dispatch covers (vgrid::detail::dispatch_items).
struct StampPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base;
  std::uint32_t voxels_per_block;
  std::uint32_t tick;
  std::uint32_t max_age;
  float observed_weight;
};

struct ZeroPush {
  std::uint32_t item_base;
  std::uint32_t voxels_per_block;
  std::uint32_t words_per_block;
  std::uint32_t num_words;
  std::int32_t num_buckets;
  std::int32_t bucket_size;
  std::int32_t max_chain;
};

// The per-voxel count backing every attribute: one element per voxel across the
// whole block pool. Grid dimensions are validated positive by
// VoxelHashMap::create (VoxelGridParams::validate), so this is well-defined.
std::uint64_t voxel_count(const VoxelGridParams& grid) {
  return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.num_blocks) *
         static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.voxels_per_block);
}

}  // namespace

core::Result<VoxelBlockGrid> VoxelBlockGrid::create(core::Device& device,
                                                    core::Allocator& allocator,
                                                    const VoxelGridParams& grid,
                                                    const AttributeSpec* attrs,
                                                    std::size_t attr_count) {
  if (attr_count > 0 && attrs == nullptr) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::create: attrs is null");
  }

  // Validate every spec up front, before building the map or allocating any
  // buffer, so a malformed spec (empty name, zero size, duplicate) is rejected
  // without the (potentially multi-GB) allocations the rest of create() does.
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < attr_count; ++i) {
    const AttributeSpec& spec = attrs[i];
    if (spec.name.empty()) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "VoxelBlockGrid::create: attribute name must be non-empty");
    }
    if (spec.element_size == 0) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "VoxelBlockGrid::create: attribute element_size must be positive");
    }
    // Whole words a block, so the zero kernel can clear one block alone.
    if (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.voxels_per_block) * spec.element_size %
            4 !=
        0) {
      return core::Status::invalid_argument(
          "VoxelBlockGrid::create: an attribute's block must fill whole 4-byte "
          "words (voxels_per_block * element_size a multiple of 4)");
    }
    for (std::size_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) {
      if (attrs[j].name == spec.name) {
        return core::Status::invalid_argument(
            "VoxelBlockGrid::create: duplicate attribute name");
      }
    }
  }

  const VkDeviceSize max_range = core::max_storage_buffer_range(device);

  // Check every attribute against the binding limit before building the map or
  // allocating anything, for the same reason the spec validation above runs
  // first: these are the largest allocations in the repo, and rejecting one
  // after the others have been made wastes gigabytes. Bound here rather than at
  // the consumers because this is where the size is chosen -- tsdf integration
  // and meshing bind these VK_WHOLE_SIZE, so what they could check is the same
  // number decided here.
  const std::uint64_t elements = voxel_count(grid);
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < attr_count; ++i) {
    const auto bytes = static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(elements) *
                       static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(attrs[i].element_size);
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::create: attribute array", bytes, max_range));
  }

  VKC_ASSIGN(VoxelHashMap map, VoxelHashMap::create(device, allocator, grid));
  VoxelBlockGrid vbg(std::move(map), &device, &allocator, max_range);

  // Device-local, and zeroed on the device, so a fresh attribute reads as
  // all-zero without the host ever touching it.
  vbg.attributes_.reserve(attr_count);
  core::CommandBatch zero(device, allocator);
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < attr_count; ++i) {
    const AttributeSpec& spec = attrs[i];
    const auto bytes = static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(elements) *
                       static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(spec.element_size);
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::Buffer buffer,
               core::device_storage_buffer(allocator, bytes));
    VKC_TRY(zero.zero(buffer, 0, bytes));
    vbg.attributes_.push_back(Attribute{std::string(spec.name),
                                        spec.element_size, std::move(buffer)});
  }
  VKC_TRY(zero.submit());
  vbg.name_attribute_buffers();
  if (!vbg.attributes_.empty()) {
    VKC_TRY(vbg.build_block_kernels());
  }
  return vbg;
}

void VoxelBlockGrid::name_attribute_buffers() const noexcept {
  if (device_ == nullptr) {
    return;
  }
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    // c_str() rather than the string_view the spec was declared with: the
    // driver reads a null-terminated string, and Attribute::name is the owned
    // copy made at create() precisely so one outlives the declaration.
    device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                             core::debug_object_handle(attr.buffer.handle()),
                             attr.name.c_str());
  }
}

core::Result<AttributeView> VoxelBlockGrid::attribute(
    std::string_view name) const {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::attribute: moved-from grid");
  }
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    if (attr.name == name) {
      // element_count is derived from the buffer this view carries, not the
      // live grid, so it always matches attr.buffer and never inflates past it.
      const std::uint64_t count = attr.buffer.size() / attr.element_size;
      // ...and *because* it describes the buffer rather than the grid, it is
      // also what makes the two comparable. Every consumer that binds an
      // attribute comes through here, so this is the one place a desync can be
      // caught -- and it has to be caught, because both consumers bind
      // VK_WHOLE_SIZE over the stale, smaller buffer while the kernels address
      // it by BlockIndex::ptr derived from the grown grid, and
      // robustBufferAccess is enabled nowhere. Only VoxelHashMap::resize
      // reached through map() can produce this; VoxelBlockGrid::resize grows
      // both sides together.
      if (count < voxel_count(map_.grid())) {
        return core::Status::invalid_argument(
            "VoxelBlockGrid::attribute: the attribute array is smaller than "
            "the live grid's num_blocks * voxels_per_block -- the map was "
            "resized through map() instead of VoxelBlockGrid::resize");
      }
      return AttributeView{&attr.buffer, attr.element_size, count};
    }
  }
  return core::Status::invalid_argument(
      "VoxelBlockGrid::attribute: no attribute of that name");
}

bool VoxelBlockGrid::has_attribute(std::string_view name) const noexcept {
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    if (attr.name == name) {
      return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::resize(std::int32_t new_num_buckets) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::resize: moved-from grid");
  }
  // A value copy, not a reference: map_.resize() below mutates map_'s grid in
  // place, so a reference would start reporting the grown dimensions mid-way.
  const VoxelGridParams grid = map_.grid();
  if (new_num_buckets <= grid.num_buckets) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::resize: new_num_buckets must exceed the current "
        "count");
  }

  // Validate the grown grid FIRST, against the same contract map_.resize will
  // apply. It runs that check too -- but only after this function has already
  // built every enlarged attribute buffer beside the live ones, which at the
  // examples' defaults is gigabytes committed and then thrown away to report an
  // invalid_argument the parameters could have been rejected on.
  //
  // This overlaps the maxStorageBufferRange guard below, and on real hardware
  // that guard fires first -- an attribute array large enough to overflow the
  // block-pointer bound is at least 8 GB, far past any device's binding limit.
  // Kept anyway because it says something the other cannot: the grown grid is
  // illegal *arithmetically*, on a machine of any size and a device of any
  // limit, and it reports that rather than a limit the caller might read as
  // "this hardware is too small".
  VoxelGridParams grown_grid = grid;
  grown_grid.num_buckets = new_num_buckets;
  const std::int64_t grown_blocks =
      static_cast<std::int64_t>(new_num_buckets) * grid.bucket_size;
  if (grown_blocks > std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::resize: new_num_buckets * bucket_size overflows a "
        "signed 32-bit num_blocks");
  }
  grown_grid.num_blocks = static_cast<std::int32_t>(grown_blocks);
  VKC_TRY(grown_grid.validate());

  // The grown per-voxel count: new num_blocks = bucket_size * new_num_buckets
  // (the invariant VoxelHashMap::create validates), one attribute element per
  // voxel of the pool.
  const std::uint64_t new_elements =
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.bucket_size) *
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(new_num_buckets) *
      static_cast<std::uint64_t>(grid.voxels_per_block);

  // Build each grown attribute buffer off to the side: copy the old contents
  // into the head (bounded by the source buffer's own size, so it can never
  // over-read even if map_ and the attributes were ever out of lockstep) and
  // zero only the grown tail. map_.resize below preserves every block's index
  // (BlockIndex::ptr < the old count), so the copied data stays correctly
  // addressed and the tail stays zero for future blocks. Commit only once the
  // map resize succeeds -- and map_.resize is itself all-or-nothing -- so a
  // failure leaves the grid untouched.
  // Every doubling takes the arrays further past the binding limit, so the
  // grown size is checked exactly as the initial one is -- before any of the
  // (potentially multi-GB) allocations below.
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    const auto new_bytes = static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(new_elements) *
                           static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(attr.element_size);
    VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::resize: grown attribute array", new_bytes,
        max_storage_buffer_range_));
  }

  // One batch for every attribute: each old array copied into its grown one
  // on the device, the tail zeroed there too.
  std::vector<core::Buffer> grown;
  grown.reserve(attributes_.size());
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    const auto new_bytes = static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(new_elements) *
                           static_cast<VkDeviceSize>(attr.element_size);
    VKC_ASSIGN(core::Buffer buffer,
               core::device_storage_buffer(*allocator_, new_bytes));
    const VkDeviceSize old_bytes = attr.buffer.size();
    VKC_TRY(batch.copy(attr.buffer, 0, buffer, 0, old_bytes));
    VKC_TRY(batch.zero(buffer, old_bytes, new_bytes - old_bytes));
    grown.push_back(std::move(buffer));
  }
  VKC_TRY(batch.submit());

  VKC_TRY(map_.resize(new_num_buckets));
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < attributes_.size(); ++i) {
    attributes_[i].buffer = std::move(grown[i]);
  }
  // Every attribute now sits on a fresh handle, and a debug-utils name lives on
  // the handle -- so without this a capture taken after the first grow shows
  // exactly the arrays a bandwidth question is about as unnamed.
  name_attribute_buffers();
  return {};
}

std::int32_t VoxelBlockGrid::max_num_buckets() const noexcept {
  if (!valid()) return 0;
  const VoxelGridParams& grid = map_.grid();
  // validate(): num_blocks, and num_blocks * voxels_per_block (a block
  // pointer), each within int32.
  constexpr std::uint64_t kInt32Max = std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max();
  std::uint64_t blocks = kInt32Max / std::uint64_t(grid.voxels_per_block);
  // resize(): every attribute array within one binding.
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    blocks = std::min<std::uint64_t>(
        blocks, max_storage_buffer_range_ /
                    (std::uint64_t(grid.voxels_per_block) * attr.element_size));
  }
  return static_cast<std::int32_t>(blocks / std::uint64_t(grid.bucket_size));
}

std::uint64_t VoxelBlockGrid::bytes_at(
    std::int32_t num_buckets) const noexcept {
  if (!valid() || num_buckets <= 0) return 0;
  const VoxelGridParams& grid = map_.grid();
  const auto buckets = std::uint64_t(num_buckets);
  const auto bucket_size = std::uint64_t(grid.bucket_size);
  const std::uint64_t voxels =
      buckets * bucket_size * std::uint64_t(grid.voxels_per_block);
  std::uint64_t bytes = table_sizes(buckets, bucket_size).total();
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    bytes += voxels * attr.element_size;
  }
  return bytes;
}

core::Result<std::uint32_t> VoxelBlockGrid::remove(const core::Buffer& coords,
                                                   std::uint32_t count,
                                                   AllocFailures* out_failures,
                                                   core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::remove: moved-from grid");
  }
  if (count == 0) {
    return std::uint32_t{0};
  }
  // Before anything is zeroed or freed, so a refused input changes nothing.
  const VkDeviceSize bytes = VkDeviceSize(count) * sizeof(BlockIndex);
  VKC_TRY(core::StorageInput(coords).check("VoxelBlockGrid::remove: the coords",
                                           bytes));
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("VoxelBlockGrid::remove: the coords",
                                           bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_));
  return zero_and_remove(coords, count, out_failures, stage);
}

core::Result<std::uint32_t> VoxelBlockGrid::zero_and_remove(
    const core::Buffer& list, std::uint32_t count, AllocFailures* out_failures,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  // The topology epoch moves inside VoxelHashMap::remove -- where the index is
  // actually freed -- so there is nothing to bump here, and no way for the raw
  // map() path to skip it (see VoxelHashMap::topology_epoch).
  if (attributes_.empty()) {
    return map_.remove(list, count, out_failures, {}, stage);
  }
  // The zero kernel finds each coord's block in the table itself, so this
  // costs the count, not the grid. It rides the map's first recording, ahead
  // of the delete in the same submit, so every block is zeroed before its
  // index is freed.
  return map_.remove(
      list, count, out_failures,
      [&](core::CommandBatch& batch) {
        return record_zero(batch, list, count, nullptr, nullptr, stage);
      },
      stage);
}

core::Result<RecordedRounds> VoxelBlockGrid::record_remove(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, const core::Buffer& coords,
    const DeviceCount& count, const DeviceCount* gate,
    core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::record_remove: moved-from grid");
  }
  if (attributes_.empty()) {
    return map_.record_remove(batch, coords, count, gate, stage);
  }
  // Zeroed in the map's recording once nothing more can refuse it, ahead of
  // its rounds, so a refused recording zeroes nothing.
  return map_.record_remove(
      batch, coords, count, gate, stage, [&](core::CommandBatch& b) {
        return record_zero(b, coords, count.bound, &count, gate, stage);
      });
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::clear() {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::clear: moved-from grid");
  }
  // Zero first, then free: a failure between the two leaves every block
  // still owning its index, at worst reading as unobserved. Freeing first
  // would hand the indices back over the old surface if the zeroing then
  // failed, and the LIFO heap would re-draw them onto it at full weight.
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  for (const Attribute& attr : attributes_) {
    VKC_TRY(batch.zero(attr.buffer, 0, attr.buffer.size()));
  }
  VKC_TRY(batch.submit());
  return map_.clear();  // moves the topology epoch; see topology_epoch()
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::prepare_block_pass() {
  if (!valid()) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument("VoxelBlockGrid: moved-from grid");
  }
  VKC_ASSIGN(const AttributeView weight, attribute(kWeightAttribute));
  if (weight.element_size != sizeof(float)) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid: the block pass needs a float weight attribute");
  }
  return {};
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::build_block_kernels() {
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::Buffer count,
             core::device_storage_buffer(*allocator_, sizeof(std::uint32_t)));
  VkPushConstantRange stamp_push{};
  stamp_push.stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT;
  stamp_push.size = sizeof(StampPush);
  VkPushConstantRange zero_push = stamp_push;
  zero_push.size = sizeof(ZeroPush);
  core::ComputeKernel stamp;
  core::ComputeKernel zero;
  core::ComputeKernel zero_args;
  core::ComputeKernel stamp_args;
  core::KernelSetBuilder kb(*device_);
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(stamp, "block_stamp", vgrid_block_stamp_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_block_stamp_comp_spv_size, 5, &stamp_push));
  VKC_TRY(kb.add(zero, "block_zero", vgrid_block_zero_comp_spv,
                 vgrid_block_zero_comp_spv_size, 3, &zero_push));
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::add_dispatch_args(kb, zero_args,
                                                          "block_zero_args"));
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::add_dispatch_args(kb, stamp_args,
                                                          "block_stamp_args"));
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::DescriptorPool pool, kb.build());
  core::KernelSets sets;
  VKC_TRY(sets.reserve(*device_, zero,
                       static_cast<std::uint32_t>(attributes_.size())));
  VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props{};
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(device_->physical_device(), &props);
  device_->set_object_name(VK_OBJECT_TYPE_BUFFER,
                           core::debug_object_handle(count.handle()),
                           "grid.stale_count");
  stale_count_ = std::move(count);
  block_pool_ = std::move(pool);
  zero_kernel_ = std::move(zero);
  zero_sets_ = std::move(sets);
  zero_args_kernel_ = std::move(zero_args);
  stamp_args_kernel_ = std::move(stamp_args);
  max_workgroup_count_x_ = props.limits.maxComputeWorkGroupCount[0];
  stamp_kernel_ = std::move(stamp);
  return {};
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::prepare_free_pass(
    std::uint32_t max_age, const core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  if (max_age == 0) {
    return core::Status::invalid_argument(
        "VoxelBlockGrid::free_stale_blocks: max_age must be at least 1");
  }
  VKC_TRY(prepare_block_pass());
  // The first timed pass makes the timer, so a grid nobody times holds no
  // query pool: a device layered on Metal backs each with one of its few
  // counter sample buffers.
  if (metrics != nullptr && !gpu_timer_.valid()) {
    VKC_ASSIGN(gpu_timer_, core::GpuTimer::create(*device_));
  }
  return {};
}

void VoxelBlockGrid::place_free_pass_rows(core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  // The stage's row and its compaction's, placed as the pass opens, so a
  // batch's later stages, whose device halves come back with theirs, do not
  // come between them.
  if (metrics == nullptr) return;
  metrics->add_cpu("block stamps", 0.0);
  metrics->add_cpu("  ..stale set", 0.0);
}

core::Result<RecordedRounds> VoxelBlockGrid::record_stale(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, std::uint32_t max_age,
    core::GpuStageScope& stage, std::uint32_t* initial_count) {
  VKC_ASSIGN(const AttributeView weight, attribute(kWeightAttribute));
  // Every block slot's room, since only the device knows how many are stale;
  // every batch this grid recorded into before has resolved (the @pre).
  const auto slots = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(map_.grid().num_blocks);
  const VkDeviceSize list_bytes = VkDeviceSize(slots) * sizeof(BlockIndex);
  VKC_TRY(core::ensure_device_scratch(*device_, *allocator_, stale_list_,
                                      list_bytes, max_storage_buffer_range_,
                                      "grid.stale_list"));
  // The active set, on the device: the compaction's own breakdown, its
  // device half alone, as the stage's row holds its host time.
  core::StageMetrics parts;
  RecordedBlockList active;
  {
    core::GpuStageScope compaction(stage.timer() != nullptr ? &parts : nullptr,
                                   gpu_timer_, "  ..stale set");
    VKC_ASSIGN(active, map_.record_compaction(batch, nullptr, &compaction));
  }
  // The stamp pass, a group an active block, sized from the compaction's
  // count; it lists the stale blocks and counts them.
  volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices groups;
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::record_dispatch_args(
      batch, *device_, *allocator_, stamp_args_kernel_, stamp_slices_,
      "grid.stamp_slices",
      volumetric_kit::grid::detail::SlicedCount{active.count, 0, slots, 1}, 1,
      &groups, 0, nullptr, max_workgroup_count_x_, &stage));
  const core::DescriptorSet& set = stamp_kernel_.set;
  set.write_storage_buffer(0, weight.buffer->handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(1, active.buffer->handle(), 0, list_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(2, map_.stamps_buffer().handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  set.write_storage_buffer(3, stale_list_.handle(), 0, list_bytes);
  set.write_storage_buffer(4, stale_count_.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
  const StampPush push{0,
                       static_cast<std::uint32_t>(map_.grid().voxels_per_block),
                       map_.tick(), max_age, kObservedWeight};
  VKC_TRY(batch.fill(stale_count_, 0, sizeof(std::uint32_t), 0u));
  VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(batch, stamp_kernel_,
                                                        push, groups, &stage));
  // Each stale block zeroed, then freed, from the list and count the pass
  // left: the removal needs no host coordinate or count.
  VKC_ASSIGN(
      RecordedRounds removed,
      record_remove(batch, stale_list_, DeviceCount{&stale_count_, 0, slots},
                    nullptr, &stage));
  if (initial_count != nullptr) {
    // The removal leaves the compaction's count unchanged. Read it beside
    // the result, since an earlier unsettled recording can leave the host's
    // occupancy stale in either direction.
    VKC_TRY(batch.readback(*active.count, 0, sizeof(*initial_count),
                           initial_count));
  }
  return removed;
}

core::Result<RecordedRounds> VoxelBlockGrid::record_free_stale(
    core::CommandBatch& batch, std::uint32_t max_age,
    core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  VKC_TRY(prepare_free_pass(max_age, metrics));
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "block stamps");
  place_free_pass_rows(metrics);
  return record_stale(batch, max_age, stage);
}

core::Result<std::uint32_t> VoxelBlockGrid::free_stale_blocks(
    std::uint32_t max_age, core::StageMetrics* metrics) {
  VKC_TRY(prepare_free_pass(max_age, metrics));
  // The row spans the wait too, and takes the batch's device halves after.
  core::GpuStageScope stage(metrics, gpu_timer_, "block stamps");
  place_free_pass_rows(metrics);
  std::uint32_t held = 0;
  core::CommandBatch batch(*device_, *allocator_);
  VKC_ASSIGN(const RecordedRounds removed,
             record_stale(batch, max_age, stage, &held));
  VKC_ASSIGN(core::PendingBatch pending, batch.submit_async({}, {}));
  VKC_TRY(pending.wait());
  if (metrics != nullptr) metrics->merge_device(pending.device_rows());
  VKC_TRY(map_.settle(removed).status());
  return held - std::min(held, map_.allocated_blocks());
}

core::Status VoxelBlockGrid::record_zero(core::CommandBatch& batch,
                                         const core::Buffer& list,
                                         std::uint32_t count,
                                         const DeviceCount* words,
                                         const DeviceCount* gate,
                                         core::GpuStageScope* stage) {
  const VoxelGridParams& gp = map_.grid();
  const auto voxels_per_block = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(gp.voxels_per_block);
  const VkDeviceSize list_bytes = VkDeviceSize(count) * sizeof(BlockIndex);
  const VkDeviceSize entries_bytes =
      VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer_size(map_);
  VKC_TRY(core::check_storage_buffer_range("VoxelBlockGrid: the hash entries",
                                           entries_bytes,
                                           max_storage_buffer_range_));
  // A workgroup a block, as many as the device's count says behind its gate.
  volumetric_kit::grid::detail::IndirectSlices slices;
  if (words != nullptr) {
    VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::record_dispatch_args(
        batch, *device_, *allocator_, zero_args_kernel_, zero_slices_,
        "grid.zero_slices",
        volumetric_kit::grid::detail::SlicedCount{
            words->buffer, words->offset, count, 1,
            gate != nullptr ? gate->buffer : nullptr,
            gate != nullptr ? gate->offset : 0},
        1, &slices, 0, nullptr, max_workgroup_count_x_, stage));
  }
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < attributes_.size(); ++i) {
    const Attribute& attr = attributes_[i];
    const core::DescriptorSet& set = zero_sets_[i];
    set.write_storage_buffer(0, attr.buffer.handle(), 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE);
    set.write_storage_buffer(1, list.handle(), 0, list_bytes);
    set.write_storage_buffer(2, VoxelHashMap::Internal::entries_buffer(map_), 0,
                             entries_bytes);
    const ZeroPush push{0,
                        voxels_per_block,
                        voxels_per_block * attr.element_size / 4,
                        static_cast<std::uint32_t>(attr.buffer.size() / 4),
                        gp.num_buckets,
                        gp.bucket_size,
                        gp.max_chain};
    if (words != nullptr) {
      // An indirect dispatch binds the kernel's own set.
      zero_kernel_.set = set;
      VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_slices(
          batch, zero_kernel_, push, slices, stage));
    } else {
      VKC_TRY(volumetric_kit::grid::detail::dispatch_items(
          batch, zero_kernel_, push, count, 1, max_workgroup_count_x_, stage,
          &set));
    }
  }
  return {};
}

}  // namespace volumetric_kit::grid::volume
```
