### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/grid_diff.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The grid's block set against a decoded frame's (block_lists.hpp), in two
// passes over the hash table, which must be quiescent (hash_lookup.glsl):
//   pass 0, an invocation a slot: an occupied slot (vgridEntryActive) whose
//     coordinate a binary search of the frame's sorted list misses is gone;
//   pass 1, an invocation a frame block: one the table does not hold
//     (vgridFindBlockPtr) is missing, ptr 0.
// Each list is appended in no order: the grid removes the one and allocates
// the other, and both draw heap slots atomically anyway.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

#define VGRID_HASH_ENTRIES_BINDING 0
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_lookup.glsl"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl"

#include "block_lists_push.glsl"

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer Frame {
  BlockIndex frame[];  // N, strictly increasing
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, scalar) writeonly buffer Gone {
  BlockIndex gone[];  // at most a slot each
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, scalar) writeonly buffer Missing {
  BlockIndex missing[];  // at most N
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) buffer Counts {
  uint gone_count;
  uint missing_count;
};

VGRID_COORD_SEARCH(in_frame, frame)

void main() {
  const uint i = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (i >= pc.count) return;
  if (pc.pass == 0u) {
    const int ptr = vgrid_hash_entries[i].ptr;
    if (!vgridEntryActive(ptr)) return;
    const ivec3 c = vgrid_hash_entries[i].pos;
    const uint at = in_frame_lower(c, 0u, pc.block_count);
    if (at < pc.block_count && frame[at].coord == c) return;
    const uint slot = atomicAdd(gone_count, 1u);
    gone[slot].coord = c;
    gone[slot].ptr = ptr;
    return;
  }
  const ivec3 c = frame[i].coord;
  if (vgridFindBlockPtr(c, pc.num_buckets, pc.bucket_size, pc.max_chain) >= 0) {
    return;
  }
  const uint slot = atomicAdd(missing_count, 1u);
  missing[slot].coord = c;
  missing[slot].ptr = 0;
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/inter_apply.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// A decoded frame's blocks, made from its reference and its payload: one
// workgroup per block, in frame order, each writing the block's mask and
// coefficients into the reference store's spare (reference_store.hpp). Its
// ApplySource (bitstream.hpp) says where the block comes from:
//   keep    reference e and payload e: the mask XOR the reference's, and each
//           coefficient the reference's plus its residual, mod 2^16;
//   skip    reference e alone: the reference block as it is;
//   zero, a new block, an intra frame's block: the payload alone.
// An absent side reads as zero, so one formula serves all three. Integer
// only, so a P-frame decodes to exactly what the intra frame of the same
// content does, on any device. An odd K's pad half-word is written 0. A
// source past what is bound -- the reference's M entries, the payload's
// entries -- reads as absent and is counted: the merge never makes one, so a
// count is a bug the store refuses, never a read out of bounds.

#version 450
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

layout(local_size_x = 64) in;

// Mirrors kMaskWordsPerBlock (codec_params.hpp) and kNoSource
// (bitstream.hpp).
const uint kMaskWords = 16u;
const uint kNoSource = 0xFFFFFFFFu;

// Mirrors ApplyPush in reference_store.cpp.
layout(push_constant, std430) uniform Push {
  uint item_base;          // first block this dispatch covers
  uint num_blocks;         // N, the frame's blocks
  uint coefficient_count;  // K
  uint reference_count;    // the reference entries a source may read
  uint payload_count;      // the payload entries a source may read
}
pc;

// Mirrors ApplySource in bitstream.hpp.
struct ApplySource {
  uint reference;
  uint payload;
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, scalar) readonly buffer Sources {
  ApplySource sources[];  // one a block, in frame order
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) readonly buffer ReferenceMasks {
  uint reference_masks[];  // kMaskWords an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) readonly buffer ReferenceCoefficients {
  uint reference_coefficients[];  // two int16 a word, (K + 1) / 2 an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer PayloadMasks {
  uint payload_masks[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) readonly buffer PayloadCoefficients {
  uint payload_coefficients[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) writeonly buffer Masks {
  uint masks[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, std430) writeonly buffer Coefficients {
  uint coefficients[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, std430) buffer Faults {
  uint faults;  // the blocks with a source past what is bound
};

// Each 16-bit half of a and b added mod 2^16: a carry out of the low half
// is dropped, not carried into the high one.
uint add_halves(uint a, uint b) {
  return ((a + b) & 0xFFFFu) | (((a >> 16u) + (b >> 16u)) << 16u);
}

void main() {
  const uint block = pc.item_base + gl_WorkGroupID.x;
  // Uniform across the workgroup.
  if (block >= pc.num_blocks) {
    return;
  }
  const ApplySource s = sources[block];
  const bool past_reference =
      s.reference != kNoSource && s.reference >= pc.reference_count;
  const bool past_payload =
      s.payload != kNoSource && s.payload >= pc.payload_count;
  if ((past_reference || past_payload) && gl_LocalInvocationIndex == 0u) {
    atomicAdd(faults, 1u);
  }
  const bool from_reference = s.reference != kNoSource && !past_reference;
  const bool from_payload = s.payload != kNoSource && !past_payload;
  const uint words = (pc.coefficient_count + 1u) / 2u;  // coefficient_words
  // The last word's high half is an odd K's pad.
  const uint last = (pc.coefficient_count & 1u) != 0u ? 0xFFFFu : 0xFFFFFFFFu;
  // The mask's words, then the coefficients', a lane each.
  for (uint i = gl_LocalInvocationIndex; i < kMaskWords + words;
       i += gl_WorkGroupSize.x) {
    if (i < kMaskWords) {
      const uint r =
          from_reference ? reference_masks[s.reference * kMaskWords + i] : 0u;
      const uint p =
          from_payload ? payload_masks[s.payload * kMaskWords + i] : 0u;
      masks[block * kMaskWords + i] = r ^ p;
    } else {
      const uint w = i - kMaskWords;
      const uint r =
          from_reference ? reference_coefficients[s.reference * words + w]
                         : 0u;
      const uint p =
          from_payload ? payload_coefficients[s.payload * words + w] : 0u;
      coefficients[block * words + w] =
          add_halves(r, p) & (w + 1u == words ? last : 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    }
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/inter_diff.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// A P-frame's entries, made by the encoder against its reference
// (reference_store.hpp): the target -- the frame the forward made, in frame
// order, in the store's spare -- split against the reference's blocks, each
// reference entry coded against the target block on its coordinate. Two
// passes, an invocation an item, with the survivor ranks
// (survivor_ranks.comp) between them:
//   pass 0, reference entry e: a binary search of the target's list for its
//     coordinate. None is remove. A target block whose mask words and
//     coefficient words all equal the reference's is skip. Otherwise the
//     mask XOR and the residuals r_j = (q_t - q_ref) mod 2^16: an r_j of
//     -32768, which no class carries, makes it zero, the target as it is;
//     else it is keep, unless the target's payload prices strictly below the
//     residual's, which is zero too. Keep and zero write their payload at
//     stream position e, and every entry its mode.
//   pass 1, target block t: a binary search of the reference's list. A block
//     on a reference coordinate survives, pass 0's; any other is new block
//     q = t - ranks[e] (the survivors below it), its coordinate added[q] and
//     its payload at position M + q, as the forward made it.
// The price is a static stand-in for the frame's tables, which do not exist
// yet: emit_payload walked with a symbol costing bit_length(symbol) + 1
// bits, a byte model's 8, and a raw field its bits. Integer only, so every
// device chooses alike; it changes the encoder's bytes, never what a frame
// decodes to. Writes stay below the bound buffers' entries. Pass 1 runs
// over the target's bound, an invocation past its count returning.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

#define VGRID_HASH_COMMON_NO_PUSH_CONSTANTS
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl"

layout(local_size_x = 64) in;

// Mirrors DiffPush in reference_store.cpp.
layout(push_constant, std430) uniform Push {
  uint item_base;          // first item this dispatch covers
  uint reference_count;    // M, the reference's blocks
  uint target_bound;       // the most the target holds
  uint coefficient_count;  // K, the reference's and the target's
  uint pass;               // 0 the reference's entries, 1 the target's blocks
  uint target_word;        // the target's blocks' word in TargetCount
}
pc;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, scalar) readonly buffer ReferenceList {
  BlockIndex reference_list[];  // M, strictly increasing
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer TargetList {
  BlockIndex target_list[];  // strictly increasing
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) readonly buffer ReferenceMasks {
  uint reference_masks[];  // kMaskWords an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer ReferenceCoefficients {
  uint reference_coefficients[];  // two int16 a word, (K + 1) / 2 an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) readonly buffer TargetMasks {
  uint target_masks[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) readonly buffer TargetCoefficients {
  uint target_coefficients[];
};
// By stream position: the M reference entries, then the new blocks.
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, std430) writeonly buffer Masks {
  uint masks[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, std430) writeonly buffer Coefficients {
  uint coefficients[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 8, std430) writeonly buffer Modes {
  uint modes[];  // M
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 9, std430) readonly buffer Ranks {
  uint ranks[];  // M + 1: the survivors before each reference entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 10, scalar) writeonly buffer Added {
  BlockIndex added[];  // the new blocks, ptr 0
};
// The target's blocks, a word a kernel wrote, read as at most target_bound:
// only the device knows how many the forward made.
layout(set = 0, binding = 11, std430) readonly buffer TargetCount {
  uint target_words[];
};

uint target_count() {
  return min(target_words[pc.target_word], pc.target_bound);
}

VGRID_COORD_SEARCH(in_reference, reference_list)
VGRID_COORD_SEARCH(in_target, target_list)

#define VGRID_FRAME_WRITER
#include "frame_grammar.glsl"

// What the price walks: the target entry's first coefficient word, the
// reference entry's, and whether it walks keep's residuals or zero's values.
uint g_target = 0u;
uint g_reference = 0u;
bool g_residual = false;
uint g_bits = 0u;

int coefficient(uint j) {
  const int at = int(16u * (j & 1u));
  const int t =
      bitfieldExtract(int(target_coefficients[g_target + j / 2u]), at, 16);
  if (!g_residual) return t;
  const int r = bitfieldExtract(
      int(reference_coefficients[g_reference + j / 2u]), at, 16);
  return bitfieldExtract(t - r, 0, 16);  // (t - r) mod 2^16, as int16
}

void sink_symbol(uint model, uint symbol) {
  g_bits += model >= kByte && model < kFirstCoef ? 8u : bit_length(symbol) + 1u;
}

void sink_bits(uint value, uint bits) { g_bits += bits; }

// The bits emit_payload's walk over g_mask prices.
uint price(bool residual) {
  g_residual = residual;
  g_bits = 0u;
  emit_payload(pc.coefficient_count);
  return g_bits;
}

// Each 16-bit half of a less b's, mod 2^16: a borrow out of the low half is
// dropped, not taken from the high one.
uint sub_halves(uint a, uint b) {
  return ((a - b) & 0xFFFFu) | (((a >> 16u) - (b >> 16u)) << 16u);
}

void reference_entry(uint e, uint words) {
  const ivec3 c = reference_list[e].coord;
  const uint n = target_count();
  const uint t = in_target_lower(c, 0u, n);
  if (t >= n || target_list[t].coord != c) {
    modes[e] = kModeRemove;
    return;
  }
  const uint k = pc.coefficient_count;
  bool same = true;
  for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
    g_mask[w] = target_masks[t * kMaskWords + w] ^
                reference_masks[e * kMaskWords + w];
    same = same && g_mask[w] == 0u;
  }
  bool wraps = false;
  for (uint w = 0u; w < words; ++w) {
    const uint r = sub_halves(target_coefficients[t * words + w],
                              reference_coefficients[e * words + w]);
    same = same && r == 0u;
    // The high half of an odd K's last word is its pad, not a residual.
    wraps = wraps || (r & 0xFFFFu) == 0x8000u ||
            (2u * w + 1u < k && (r >> 16u) == 0x8000u);
  }
  if (same) {
    modes[e] = kModeSkip;
    return;
  }
  g_target = t * words;
  g_reference = e * words;
  bool zero = wraps;
  if (!zero) {
    const uint keep = price(true);  // over the XOR mask
    for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
      g_mask[w] = target_masks[t * kMaskWords + w];
    }
    zero = price(false) < keep;
  }
  modes[e] = zero ? kModeZero : kModeKeep;
  for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
    const uint target = target_masks[t * kMaskWords + w];
    masks[e * kMaskWords + w] =
        zero ? target : target ^ reference_masks[e * kMaskWords + w];
  }
  for (uint w = 0u; w < words; ++w) {
    const uint target = target_coefficients[t * words + w];
    coefficients[e * words + w] =
        zero ? target
             : sub_halves(target, reference_coefficients[e * words + w]);
  }
}

void target_block(uint t, uint words) {
  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const ivec3 c = target_list[t].coord;
  const uint e = in_reference_lower(c, 0u, m);
  if (e < m && reference_list[e].coord == c) return;
  const uint q = t - ranks[e];
  added[q].coord = c;
  added[q].ptr = 0;
  const uint p = m + q;
  for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
    masks[p * kMaskWords + w] = target_masks[t * kMaskWords + w];
  }
  for (uint w = 0u; w < words; ++w) {
    coefficients[p * words + w] = target_coefficients[t * words + w];
  }
}

void main() {
  const uint i = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  const uint words = (pc.coefficient_count + 1u) / 2u;  // coefficient_words
  if (pc.pass == 0u) {
    if (i < pc.reference_count) reference_entry(i, words);
  } else if (i < target_count()) {
    target_block(i, words);
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_count.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The device frame's pass 1: every model's symbol counts, each entry's coder
// steps, which rans_layout.comp lays out, and what check_entries refuses
// (bitstream.hpp). One invocation per position of num_entries, a bound the
// frame words take the frame's entries from (counted_entries): a position
// past the frame's returns.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

layout(local_size_x = 64) in;

#include "rans_walk.glsl"

// Bindings 0-3 are the walk's.
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) buffer Counts {
  uint counts[];  // per model, per symbol, at model_base, a P-frame's layout
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) writeonly buffer Steps {
  uint steps[];  // per entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, std430) buffer Refusal {
  uint largest_mode;  // the largest mode past the alphabet, else 0
  uint out_of_range;  // nonzero when a written value is -32768
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, std430) readonly buffer FrameWords {
  uint surplus;  // counted_entries' words
  uint frame_blocks;
};

uint g_steps = 0u;

void sink_symbol(uint model, uint symbol) {
  atomicAdd(counts[model_base(model, pc.coefficient_count) + symbol], 1u);
  g_steps += 1u;
}

void sink_bits(uint value, uint bits) { g_steps += (bits + 11u) / 12u; }

void main() {
  const uint p = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (p >= counted_entries(surplus, frame_blocks)) return;
  walk_entry(p);
  steps[p] = g_steps;
  if (g_bad_mode != 0u) atomicMax(largest_mode, g_bad_mode);
  if (g_out_of_range) atomicOr(out_of_range, 1u);
}

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_decode.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The device frame's decode: one invocation per segment runs the rANS decoder
// rans.hpp describes, in 32-bit integer arithmetic, under frame_grammar.glsl's
// reader half over the segment's stream. Each entry's mask and coefficients
// land at its stream position (segment_range), a P-frame's reference entry's
// mode beside them and a new block's coordinate at its place in the list. The
// tests' CPU oracle is the reference: the same frame decodes to the same
// entries, and a segment fails here exactly when it fails there, which the
// device frame test checks.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

layout(local_size_x = 1) in;

#define VGRID_HASH_COMMON_NO_PUSH_CONSTANTS
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl"

#include "rans_push.glsl"

#define VGRID_FRAME_READER
#include "frame_grammar.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Slots {
  uint slots[];  // rans_slots.comp's, 4096 a model
};
// The record, from its offset aligned down: the segment streams,
// little-endian 16-bit words, start at byte pc.payload_byte.
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) readonly buffer Payload {
  uint payload[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) readonly buffer SegmentWords {
  uint segment_words[];  // each segment's first word, segment_count + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, scalar) writeonly buffer Blocks {
  BlockIndex blocks[];  // the new blocks in frame order: coord, ptr 0
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) writeonly buffer Masks {
  uint masks[];  // kMaskWords an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) writeonly buffer Coefficients {
  uint coefficients[];  // two int16 a word, (K + 1) / 2 words an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, std430) writeonly buffer Faults {
  uint faults[];  // a SegmentFault per segment
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, std430) writeonly buffer Modes {
  uint modes[];  // a P-frame's, one a reference entry
};

const uint kRansLower = 1u << 16u;
const uint kFaultNone = 0u;
const uint kFaultCoordOverflow = 1u;
const uint kFaultCorrupt = 2u;

// The decoder's state, its failure sticky.
uint g_x = 0u;
uint g_pos = 0u;  // the next word
uint g_end = 0u;  // one past the segment's last word
bool g_failed = false;

uint byte_at(uint b) { return (payload[b >> 2u] >> (8u * (b & 3u))) & 0xFFu; }

// The stream's 16-bit word q: one load at an even byte, two bytes at an odd
// one, which may straddle two words.
uint word_at(uint q) {
  const uint b = pc.payload_byte + 2u * q;
  if ((b & 1u) == 0u) return (payload[b >> 2u] >> (8u * (b & 2u))) & 0xFFFFu;
  return byte_at(b) | (byte_at(b + 1u) << 8u);
}

void renormalize() {
  if (g_x < kRansLower) {
    if (g_pos >= g_end) {
      g_failed = true;
      return;
    }
    g_x = (g_x << 16u) | word_at(g_pos);
    g_pos += 1u;
  }
}

uint get(uint model) {
  if (g_failed) return 0u;
  const uint slot = g_x & 4095u;
  const uint entry = slots[(model << 12u) + slot];
  const uint freq = ((entry >> 8u) & 0xFFFu) + 1u;
  const uint offset = entry >> 20u;
  if (offset >= freq) {  // an empty table
    g_failed = true;
    return 0u;
  }
  g_x = freq * (g_x >> 12u) + offset;
  renormalize();
  return g_failed ? 0u : (entry & 0xFFu);
}

uint get_bits(uint bits) {
  uint value = 0u;
  uint shift_out = 0u;
  while (bits > 0u && !g_failed) {
    const uint n = min(bits, 12u);
    const uint shift = 12u - n;
    const uint slot = g_x & 4095u;
    const uint chunk = slot >> shift;
    g_x = ((g_x >> 12u) << shift) + slot - (chunk << shift);
    renormalize();
    value |= chunk << shift_out;
    shift_out += n;
    bits -= n;
  }
  return g_failed ? 0u : value;
}

bool coder_failed() { return g_failed; }

uint g_coefficients = 0u;  // the entry's first word
uint g_low = 0u;           // an even coefficient, waiting for the odd one

// Two coefficients a word, low first.
void store_coefficient(uint j, int value) {
  const uint v = uint(value) & 0xFFFFu;
  if ((j & 1u) == 0u) {
    g_low = v;
  } else {
    coefficients[g_coefficients + j / 2u] = g_low | (v << 16u);
  }
}

void main() {
  const uint s = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (s >= pc.segment_count) return;
  const uint begin = segment_words[s];
  g_end = segment_words[s + 1u];
  // The parser checked every length is even and at least 4 bytes.
  g_x = (word_at(begin) << 16u) | word_at(begin + 1u);
  g_pos = begin + 2u;
  g_failed = g_x < kRansLower;

  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const uvec2 range = segment_range(s, m, pc.update_size, pc.num_entries - m,
                                    pc.segment_size);
  const uint k = pc.coefficient_count;
  uint fault = kFaultNone;
  g_coord = ivec3(0);
  for (uint p = range.x; p < range.y && !g_failed; ++p) {
    g_coefficients = p * ((k + 1u) / 2u);
    if (p < m) {
      // A skip or a remove has no payload, and writes none.
      const uint mode = read_entry(k);
      modes[p] = mode;
      if (mode != kModeKeep && mode != kModeZero) continue;
    } else {
      if (!read_block(p == range.x, k)) {
        fault = kFaultCoordOverflow;
        break;
      }
      blocks[p - m].coord = g_coord;
      blocks[p - m].ptr = 0;
    }
    for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
      masks[p * kMaskWords + w] = g_mask[w];
    }
    // An odd K's last word, its pad zero.
    if ((k & 1u) != 0u) coefficients[g_coefficients + k / 2u] = g_low;
  }
  if (fault == kFaultNone &&
      (g_failed || g_pos != g_end || g_x != kRansLower)) {
    fault = kFaultCorrupt;
  }
  faults[s] = fault;
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_encode.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The device frame's coding: one invocation per segment runs the rANS encoder
// rans.hpp describes over the segment's coder steps (rans_ops.comp), already
// in the order it takes them, in 32-bit integer arithmetic: the run from its
// first entry's start to the start past its last (rans_layout.comp). Words
// go down from the top of the segment's slot, so the stream lands in decode
// order: the final state's two words, then the words last emitted first.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

layout(local_size_x = 32) in;

#include "frame_models.glsl"
#include "rans_push.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Steps {
  uint steps[];  // start | freq << 16
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) readonly buffer Starts {
  uint starts[];  // the steps before each entry, then their total
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) readonly buffer SlotOffsets {
  uint slot_offsets[];  // in 16-bit words, segment_count + 1, each even
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) writeonly buffer Slots {
  uint slots[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) writeonly buffer Lengths {
  uint lengths[];  // bytes of each segment's stream
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) buffer Status {
  uint failed;  // nonzero when a step has frequency 0 or outgrows the slot
};

const uint kScaleBits = 12u;
const uint kRenormShift = 32u - kScaleBits;

uint g_high = 0u;  // an odd word waiting for the even one below it

// Words go down from an even slot top, so each odd word arrives first and is
// held until its even partner completes the 32-bit word: no read back.
void put16(uint at, uint word) {
  if ((at & 1u) != 0u) {
    g_high = word;
  } else {
    slots[at >> 1u] = word | (g_high << 16u);
  }
}

void main() {
  const uint s = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (s >= pc.segment_count) return;
  const uint floor16 = slot_offsets[s];
  uint out16 = slot_offsets[s + 1u];  // the next free word is out16 - 1
  uint x = 1u << 16u;                 // L (rans.hpp)
  bool bad = false;
  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const uvec2 range = segment_range(s, m, pc.update_size, pc.num_entries - m,
                                    pc.segment_size);
  const uint end = starts[range.y];
  // Four steps a round, the next four loaded while these are coded: with
  // one chain per invocation, a load consumed at once would stall it.
  uint at = starts[range.x];
  uvec4 batch = uvec4(at < end ? steps[at] : 0u,
                      at + 1u < end ? steps[at + 1u] : 0u,
                      at + 2u < end ? steps[at + 2u] : 0u,
                      at + 3u < end ? steps[at + 3u] : 0u);
  while (at < end && !bad) {
    const uint ahead = at + 4u;
    const uvec4 next = uvec4(ahead < end ? steps[ahead] : 0u,
                             ahead + 1u < end ? steps[ahead + 1u] : 0u,
                             ahead + 2u < end ? steps[ahead + 2u] : 0u,
                             ahead + 3u < end ? steps[ahead + 3u] : 0u);
    for (uint c = 0u; c < 4u && at + c < end; ++c) {
      const uint start = batch[c] & 0xFFFFu;
      const uint freq = batch[c] >> 16u;
      if (freq == 0u || out16 <= floor16 + 2u) {
        bad = true;
        break;
      }
      if ((x >> kRenormShift) >= freq) {
        out16 -= 1u;
        put16(out16, x & 0xFFFFu);
        x >>= 16u;
      }
      x = ((x / freq) << kScaleBits) + (x % freq) + start;
    }
    batch = next;
    at = ahead;
  }
  if (bad) {
    atomicOr(failed, 1u);
    lengths[s] = 0u;
    return;
  }
  put16(out16 - 1u, x & 0xFFFFu);
  put16(out16 - 2u, x >> 16u);
  // A stream starting on an odd word leaves that word's low half unused.
  if (((out16 - 2u) & 1u) != 0u) put16(out16 - 3u, 0u);
  lengths[s] = 2u * (slot_offsets[s + 1u] - (out16 - 2u));
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_gather.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// Pack every segment's stream into one payload: each invocation writes a
// 32-bit word at a time, finding the segment each of its two 16-bit halves
// came from. Streams are 16-bit aligned, so no word is written twice.
// rans_scan.comp sizes the dispatch from the payload, so no invocation starts
// past it; a payload past the group cap loops. The words before
// pc.payload_byte are left as they are: a tail's gather writes only the
// window past what its frame's batch copied out.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

#include "rans_push.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer SlotOffsets {
  uint slot_offsets[];  // in 16-bit words, segment_count + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) readonly buffer Slots {
  uint slots[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) readonly buffer Lengths {
  uint lengths[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer PayloadOffsets {
  uint payload_offsets[];  // bytes, segment_count + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) writeonly buffer Payload {
  uint payload[];
};

// The payload's 16-bit word q, from the segment whose stream holds it.
uint payload16(uint q) {
  const uint at = 2u * q;
  uint lo = 0u;  // payload_offsets[lo] <= at < payload_offsets[hi]
  uint hi = pc.segment_count;
  while (hi - lo > 1u) {
    const uint mid = (lo + hi) / 2u;
    if (payload_offsets[mid] <= at) {
      lo = mid;
    } else {
      hi = mid;
    }
  }
  const uint begin = slot_offsets[lo + 1u] - lengths[lo] / 2u;
  const uint src = begin + (at - payload_offsets[lo]) / 2u;
  return (slots[src >> 1u] >> (16u * (src & 1u))) & 0xFFFFu;
}

void main() {
  const uint total = payload_offsets[pc.segment_count];
  const uint words = (total + 3u) / 4u;
  const uint stride = gl_NumWorkGroups.x * gl_WorkGroupSize.x;
  for (uint w = pc.payload_byte / 4u + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x; w < words;
       w += stride) {
    const uint low = payload16(2u * w);
    const uint high = 4u * w + 2u < total ? payload16(2u * w + 1u) : 0u;
    payload[w] = low | (high << 16u);
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_layout.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The device frame's step layout (step_layout.hpp), one workgroup on
// scan.glsl, over the frame's N entries, which the frame words take from
// the bound num_entries (counted_entries), so a frame whose count only the
// device knows lays out only its own.
// First each entry's first step, starts[p]: the steps of the entries before
// it in stream order, an exclusive scan, with their total at starts[N]. Then
// each segment's output slot, in 16-bit words: a word a step and the final
// state's two, rounded up to whole 32-bit words so no two segments share
// one, scanned into slot_offsets, with their total at [S], S the frame's
// segments (segment_of its last entry, plus one). Lane 0 also writes both
// totals to Totals, where the host reads them whatever N the device took.
// The second scan reads the first's starts at the segments' ends, which
// other lanes wrote, hence the coherent buffer and the barrier between. Each
// lane sums kRun values in a row before a chunk's scan and places them after
// it, so a chunk covers 2,048 values: room0's 21,771 entries take 11 chunks'
// barrier rounds, not 86.
//
// The step total stops at the first value whose steps reach 4 GiB, 4 bytes
// each, which the writer refuses. Below it every value is exact: the slot
// words stay below 2^32, since a slot holds its steps and at most three words
// more, and a frame has fewer than 2^30 segments; past it, the entries' bound
// (step_layout.hpp) keeps a chunk's sum from wrapping.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

#include "frame_models.glsl"
#include "rans_push.glsl"
#include "scan.glsl"

layout(local_size_x = kScanLanes) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Steps {
  uint steps[];  // each entry's coder steps, of the bound
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) coherent buffer Starts {
  uint starts[];  // N + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) writeonly buffer SlotOffsets {
  uint slot_offsets[];  // in 16-bit words, S + 1, each even
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer FrameWords {
  uint surplus;  // counted_entries' words
  uint frame_blocks;
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) writeonly buffer Totals {
  uint step_total;  // starts[N]
  uint slot_total;  // slot_offsets[S]
};

const uint kStepCap = 1u << 30u;
const uint kRun = 8u;  // a chunk spans kScanLanes * kRun values

void main() {
  const uint lane = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
  const uint n = counted_entries(surplus, frame_blocks);
  uint carry = 0u;
  for (uint base = 0u; base < n; base += kScanLanes * kRun) {
    const uint first = base + lane * kRun;
    uint run[kRun];
    uint sum = 0u;
    for (uint i = 0u; i < kRun; ++i) {
      run[i] = first + i < n ? steps[first + i] : 0u;
      sum += run[i];
    }
    uint at = vgridScanChunk(sum, carry);
    carry = min(carry, kStepCap);
    for (uint i = 0u; i < kRun && first + i < n; ++i) {
      starts[first + i] = at;
      at += run[i];
    }
  }
  if (lane == 0u) {
    starts[n] = carry;
    step_total = carry;
  }
  memoryBarrierBuffer();
  barrier();

  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const uint segments =
      n == 0u ? 0u
              : segment_of(n - 1u, m, pc.update_size, pc.segment_size) + 1u;
  carry = 0u;
  for (uint base = 0u; base < segments; base += kScanLanes * kRun) {
    const uint first = base + lane * kRun;
    uint run[kRun];
    uint sum = 0u;
    for (uint i = 0u; i < kRun; ++i) {
      run[i] = 0u;
      if (first + i < segments) {
        const uvec2 range = segment_range(first + i, m, pc.update_size, n - m,
                                          pc.segment_size);
        run[i] = (starts[range.y] - starts[range.x] + 3u) & ~1u;
      }
      sum += run[i];
    }
    uint at = vgridScanChunk(sum, carry);
    for (uint i = 0u; i < kRun && first + i < segments; ++i) {
      slot_offsets[first + i] = at;
      at += run[i];
    }
  }
  if (lane == 0u) {
    slot_offsets[segments] = carry;
    slot_total = carry;
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_ops.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The device frame's coder steps: one invocation per entry walks its symbols
// in the order the grammar emits them and writes each one's steps, as
// `start | freq << 16` words, downward from the end of the entry's run. The
// encoder takes steps last first, so each segment's entries are laid out last
// first: entry p of segment [x, y) ends its run at
// starts[x] + starts[y] - starts[p] (rans_layout.comp's starts), and the
// segment's steps are one run, starts[x] to starts[y], in the encoder's order
// that rans_encode.comp streams through. The branchy symbol walk runs here,
// an entry per invocation, and only the rANS state's chain stays serial.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

layout(local_size_x = 64) in;

#include "rans_walk.glsl"

// Bindings 0-3 are the walk's.
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) readonly buffer Tables {
  uint tables[];  // per model, per symbol, at model_base: cum | freq << 16
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, std430) readonly buffer Starts {
  uint starts[];  // the steps before each entry, then their total
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, std430) writeonly buffer Steps {
  uint steps[];
};

const uint kScaleBits = 12u;

uint g_at = 0u;  // the step written last: the next goes below it

void sink_symbol(uint model, uint symbol) {
  steps[--g_at] = tables[model_base(model, pc.coefficient_count) + symbol];
}

// A raw field's steps (rans.hpp): chunks of at most 12 bits, low first.
void sink_bits(uint value, uint bits) {
  for (uint low = 0u; low < bits; low += 12u) {
    const uint n = min(bits - low, 12u);
    const uint chunk = (value >> low) & ((1u << n) - 1u);
    const uint shift = kScaleBits - n;
    steps[--g_at] = (chunk << shift) | ((1u << shift) << 16u);
  }
}

void main() {
  const uint p = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (p >= pc.num_entries) return;
  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const uvec2 range =
      segment_range(segment_of(p, m, pc.update_size, pc.segment_size), m,
                    pc.update_size, pc.num_entries - m, pc.segment_size);
  g_at = starts[range.x] + starts[range.y] - starts[p];
  walk_entry(p);
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_push.glsl
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// Every rANS kernel's push constants. Mirrors `RansPush` in
// rans_dispatch.hpp.

#ifndef VGRID_RANS_PUSH_GLSL
#define VGRID_RANS_PUSH_GLSL

layout(push_constant, std430) uniform Push {
  uint item_base;  // first entry or segment this dispatch covers
  // M + A: a P-frame's reference entries, then blocks; or for the count and
  // layout a bound whose words they bind (counted_entries)
  uint num_entries;
  uint coefficient_count;  // K
  uint segment_size;       // R
  uint segment_count;
  uint frame_type;       // header byte 6
  uint reference_count;  // M, 0 for an intra frame
  uint update_size;      // U
  // The decode's: the payload's first byte in its binding, which starts at
  // the record's offset aligned down to minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment.
  // The gather's: the first byte it writes, 4-aligned.
  uint payload_byte;
}
pc;

// The frame's entries, on the device: its M reference entries and @p blocks
// of the bound's blocks (num_entries less M), less @p surplus of those: the
// survivors a bounded P-frame's bound counts twice
// (ResidentBlocks::bounded), 0 otherwise. Each word is clamped, so every
// read stays inside the bound whatever it holds; the writer refuses a word
// that needed it.
uint counted_entries(uint surplus, uint blocks) {
  const uint found = min(blocks, pc.num_entries - pc.reference_count);
  return pc.reference_count + found - min(surplus, found);
}

#endif  // VGRID_RANS_PUSH_GLSL
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_scan.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// Each segment's byte offset in the payload: an exclusive scan of the stream
// lengths (scan.glsl), then the total and the gather's dispatch size. The
// host's results go out with them, as one struct in the back half's results
// slot: whether a table refused a symbol, the payload's bytes, and each
// segment's length, so nothing is read back per buffer.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

#include "rans_push.glsl"
#include "scan.glsl"

layout(local_size_x = kScanLanes) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Lengths {
  uint lengths[];
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) writeonly buffer PayloadOffsets {
  uint payload_offsets[];  // segment_count + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) writeonly buffer GatherArgs {
  uvec3 gather_groups;  // rans_gather.comp's VkDispatchIndirectCommand
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer Status {
  uint failed;  // rans_encode.comp's
};
// Mirrors detail::BackResults (device_frame_writer.hpp), then the lengths.
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, std430) writeonly buffer Results {
  uint result_failed;
  uint result_total;  // the payload's bytes
  uint result_lengths[];
};

// rans_gather.comp's width, and the fewest groups every device dispatches.
const uint kGatherLanes = 256u;
const uint kMaxGroups = 65535u;

void main() {
  const uint lane = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
  uint carry = 0u;
  for (uint base = 0u; base < pc.segment_count; base += kScanLanes) {
    const uint i = base + lane;
    const uint length = i < pc.segment_count ? lengths[i] : 0u;
    const uint offset = vgridScanChunk(length, carry);
    if (i < pc.segment_count) {
      payload_offsets[i] = offset;
      result_lengths[i] = length;
    }
  }
  if (lane == 0u) {
    payload_offsets[pc.segment_count] = carry;
    result_failed = failed;
    result_total = carry;
    const uint words = (carry + 3u) / 4u;
    gather_groups =
        uvec3(min((words + kGatherLanes - 1u) / kGatherLanes, kMaxGroups), 1u,
              1u);
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_slots.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// The decoder's lookup: for each model and each of its 4096 slots, the
// symbol whose [cum, cum + freq) holds the slot, packed with what the decode
// step needs. Built on the device
// from the frame's tables, so only those (8 KB at K = 64) cross the bus. One
// invocation per model and slot.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

#include "frame_models.glsl"
#include "rans_push.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Tables {
  uint tables[];  // per model, per symbol, at model_base: cum | freq << 16
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) writeonly buffer Slots {
  // symbol | (freq - 1) << 8 | (slot - cum) << 20, 4096 a model. An empty
  // model's slots hold kEmptySlot, whose offset is not below its freq.
  uint slots[];
};

const uint kEmptySlot = 0xFFF00000u;

void main() {
  const uint item = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  const uint model = item >> 12u;
  if (model >= model_count(pc.frame_type, pc.coefficient_count)) return;
  const uint slot = item & 4095u;
  const uint base = model_base(model, pc.coefficient_count);
  // The last symbol whose cum is at most the slot: every later one starts
  // past it, and one of frequency 0 before it shares its cum.
  uint lo = 0u;  // the first symbol whose cum exceeds the slot
  uint hi = model_alphabet(model, pc.coefficient_count);
  while (lo < hi) {
    const uint mid = (lo + hi) / 2u;
    if ((tables[base + mid] & 0xFFFFu) <= slot) {
      lo = mid + 1u;
    } else {
      hi = mid;
    }
  }
  const uint s = lo - 1u;  // cum[0] = 0, so lo >= 1
  const uint entry = tables[base + s];
  const uint freq = entry >> 16u;
  slots[item] = freq == 0u ? kEmptySlot
                           : s | ((freq - 1u) << 8u) |
                                 ((slot - (entry & 0xFFFFu)) << 20u);
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_verdict.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// Rows 11 and 12's segment half, judged on the device after rans_decode.comp
// (device_frame_reader.hpp): an invocation a segment takes its fault, else,
// for a block segment with a block segment before it, whether its first
// coordinate follows that one's last, and keeps the smallest failing segment
// as s << 2 | kind, which check_segment words. The smallest is the segment
// the CPU oracle's walk stops at: every one before it decoded clean, so the
// coordinates it compares are real, and a later segment's comparison against
// a corrupt one never wins. Segments number below 2^30 (kMaxFrameSegments),
// so the word holds them.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

layout(local_size_x = 64) in;

#define VGRID_HASH_COMMON_NO_PUSH_CONSTANTS
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl"
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/coord_order.glsl"

#include "frame_models.glsl"
#include "rans_push.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Faults {
  uint faults[];  // a SegmentFault a segment
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer Blocks {
  BlockIndex blocks[];  // the new blocks, in frame order
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) buffer Verdict {
  uint verdict;    // the smallest s << 2 | kind, ~0 for none
  uint survivors;  // survivor_ranks.comp's
};

// Mirrors SegmentFault::kOutOfOrder (bitstream.hpp).
const uint kFaultOutOfOrder = 3u;

void main() {
  const uint s = pc.item_base + gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
  if (s >= pc.segment_count) return;
  uint kind = faults[s];
  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  const uvec2 range = segment_range(s, m, pc.update_size, pc.num_entries - m,
                                    pc.segment_size);
  if (kind == 0u && range.x > m &&
      !vgridCoordLess(blocks[range.x - m - 1u].coord, blocks[range.x - m].coord)) {
    kind = kFaultOutOfOrder;
  }
  if (kind != 0u) atomicMin(verdict, (s << 2u) | kind);
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/rans_walk.glsl
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// An entry's frame symbols on the device, shared by rans_count.comp and
// rans_ops.comp: frame_grammar.glsl's writer half over the forward output,
// in the order it emits them. The includer defines the two sinks.

#ifndef VGRID_RANS_WALK_GLSL
#define VGRID_RANS_WALK_GLSL

#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

#define VGRID_HASH_COMMON_NO_PUSH_CONSTANTS
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_common.glsl"

#include "rans_push.glsl"

#define VGRID_FRAME_WRITER
#include "frame_grammar.glsl"

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, scalar) readonly buffer Blocks {
  BlockIndex blocks[];  // the new blocks in frame order; only coord is read
};
// By stream position (segment_range): a P-frame's M reference entries, then
// its new blocks; an intra frame's blocks.
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer Masks {
  uint masks[];  // kMaskWords an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, scalar) readonly buffer Coefficients {
  uint coefficients[];  // two int16 a word, (K + 1) / 2 words an entry
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, std430) readonly buffer Modes {
  uint modes[];  // a P-frame's, one a reference entry
};

uint g_coefficients = 0u;  // the entry's first word
// What check_entries refuses, found on the way: the mode past the alphabet
// (0 for none), and an emitted -32768.
uint g_bad_mode = 0u;
bool g_out_of_range = false;

// Within +-32767 as the transform writes it, except a stale word in an entry
// the forward rejected, or a -32768 the caller wrote: clamped, so a count
// stays within the model's classes, and flagged, so the frame is refused.
int coefficient(uint j) {
  const uint word = coefficients[g_coefficients + j / 2u];
  const int v = bitfieldExtract(int(word), int(16u * (j & 1u)), 16);
  if (v < -32767) g_out_of_range = true;
  return max(v, -32767);
}

// Stream position p: reference entry p, or new block p - M, where every
// R-th starts a segment. A mode past the alphabet emits nothing.
void walk_entry(uint p) {
  for (uint w = 0u; w < kMaskWords; ++w) {
    g_mask[w] = masks[p * kMaskWords + w];
  }
  g_coefficients = p * ((pc.coefficient_count + 1u) / 2u);
  if (p < pc.reference_count) {
    const uint mode = modes[p];
    if (mode >= kModeSymbols) {
      g_bad_mode = mode;
      return;
    }
    emit_entry(mode, pc.coefficient_count);
    return;
  }
  const uint q = p - pc.reference_count;
  const bool first = q % pc.segment_size == 0u;
  const ivec3 cur = blocks[q].coord;
  ivec3 prev = cur;
  if (!first) prev = blocks[q - 1u].coord;
  emit_block(first, prev, cur, pc.coefficient_count);
}

#endif  // VGRID_RANS_WALK_GLSL
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/scan.glsl
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// One workgroup's exclusive scan of u32, a chunk of kScanLanes values a call:
// the codec's one scan, which rans_layout.comp runs over the entries' coder
// steps and the segments' slots, rans_scan.comp over the segments' lengths
// and survivor_ranks.comp over a P-frame's survivors. The includer declares
// local_size_x = kScanLanes, and every lane makes each call, with 0 past the
// end of its values: a frame has tens of thousands of entries, not millions,
// so one workgroup walks them a chunk at a time.

#ifndef VGRID_SCAN_GLSL
#define VGRID_SCAN_GLSL

const uint kScanLanes = 256u;

shared uint s_scan[kScanLanes];

// @return This lane's @p value's exclusive prefix within the chunk, plus
//         @p carry, which then advances by the chunk's total.
uint vgridScanChunk(uint value, inout uint carry) {
  const uint lane = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
  s_scan[lane] = value;
  barrier();
  for (uint step = 1u; step < kScanLanes; step <<= 1u) {
    const uint left = lane >= step ? s_scan[lane - step] : 0u;
    barrier();
    s_scan[lane] += left;
    barrier();
  }
  const uint prefix = carry + s_scan[lane] - value;
  carry += s_scan[kScanLanes - 1u];
  barrier();
  return prefix;
}

#endif  // VGRID_SCAN_GLSL
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/codec/shaders/survivor_ranks.comp
```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Tao Jin

// A frame's survivor ranks (device_frame_reader.hpp): ranks[e], how many of
// the reference entries before e survive -- keep, skip or zero -- for
// e = 0..M, so ranks[M] is the survivor count, which goes beside the verdict
// for check_survivors. An intra frame is M = 0: ranks[0] = 0. One workgroup,
// scan.glsl a chunk at a time.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

#include "frame_models.glsl"
#include "rans_push.glsl"
#include "scan.glsl"

layout(local_size_x = kScanLanes) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std430) readonly buffer Modes {
  uint modes[];  // M
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, std430) writeonly buffer Ranks {
  uint ranks[];  // M + 1
};
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, std430) buffer Verdict {
  uint verdict;  // rans_verdict.comp's
  uint survivors;
};

void main() {
  const uint lane = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
  const uint m = pc.reference_count;
  uint carry = 0u;
  for (uint base = 0u; base <= m; base += kScanLanes) {
    const uint e = base + lane;
    const bool survives = e < m && modes[e] <= kModeZero;  // keep, skip, zero
    const uint rank = vgridScanChunk(survives ? 1u : 0u, carry);
    if (e <= m) ranks[e] = rank;
  }
  if (lane == 0u) survivors = carry;
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/shaders/marching_cubes_common.glsl
```
#ifndef VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_COMMON_GLSL
#define VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_COMMON_GLSL

// Shared marching-cubes per-cell body for the two sparse kernels:
// marching_cubes_sparse.comp (three private vertices per triangle) and
// marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp (in-block sharing). What differs between
// them is how a vertex slot is CLAIMED, not how the vertex is computed, so
// that stays in each kernel's main(); everything downstream of the gathered
// `sdf[8]` / `corner_color[8]` is identical and lives here as one source, so a
// fix to the numerically load-bearing math (the near-tangent edge guard, the
// 8-corner gradient, the reversed winding) can never be applied to only one
// path. Mirrors the volume tier's hash_common.glsl / the tsdf tier's
// tsdf_common.glsl shared-include discipline.
//
// The includer must, *before* the include, declare the binding-0 `Tables`
// block (`int tri_table[4096]`, `corner_offset[24]`, `edge_to_vert[24]`), the
// `Vertex` struct, and the writeonly `vertices[]` buffer -- all by those
// names. They are identical in both kernels; only the binding indices differ,
// which is why the declarations stay in each shader.

// Indices one triangle contributes. Each kernel bumps `index_count` by exactly
// this per triangle, which is what makes the counter the draw command's
// indexCount rather than a triangle total a host would have to convert.
// Mirrors mesh::kIndicesPerTriangle on the host -- the two must not drift,
// since the host divides by it to recover the triangle count.
//
// And the count is of the FIELD, not of what fitted: past `capacity` a
// triangle is dropped but still counted, so `index_count` always ends as this
// times the true triangle total rather than a lower bound. That is what the
// host sizes its arena from when it fits the arena to the surface instead of
// the 5-tri/cell worst case, and what it refits against after an undersized
// guess -- a total that stopped at the capacity would make the refit undershoot
// and the retry overflow again. Both kernels take a whole block's count, and
// add it to `index_count`, before any slot in it is claimed, which is what
// makes that hold through a range the arena cannot hold.
const uint kIndicesPerTriangle = 3u;

// Corner c's step (0/1 per axis) from the cell base.
ivec3 mcCornerShift(int corner) {
  return ivec3(corner_offset[corner * 3 + 0], corner_offset[corner * 3 + 1],
               corner_offset[corner * 3 + 2]);
}

// Which cell owns edge `edge`, and along which axis it runs.
//
// Every marching-cubes edge is the +x/+y/+z edge of exactly one cell: the one
// at the componentwise MINIMUM of its two endpoint corners. That cell is `delta`
// steps from the cell asking, so a vertex-sharing kernel can name an edge by
// (owner cell, axis) and have every cell touching it agree -- which is the whole
// basis of sharing.
//
// DERIVED from the tables rather than tabulated beside them, deliberately. A
// fourth mirror of the edge/corner numbering is exactly the drift hazard the
// volume tier hit with hash_lookup.glsl: a divergence would silently resolve the
// wrong owner and split vertices that should share, under Status::ok. Here the
// answer is a pure function of `edge_to_vert` + `corner_offset`, so it cannot
// disagree with them.
void mcEdgeOwner(int edge, out ivec3 delta, out int axis) {
  ivec3 sa = mcCornerShift(edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 0]);
  ivec3 sb = mcCornerShift(edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 1]);
  delta = min(sa, sb);
  ivec3 d = abs(sa - sb);  // exactly one component is 1 -- edges are axis-aligned
  axis = d.x != 0 ? 0 : (d.y != 0 ? 1 : 2);
}

// Write one vertex at an already-claimed slot. The appearance fields are
// constants, kept in this one body so no emitter can drift from another --
// mcWriteTriangle reaches them for every private vertex, and the sharing kernel
// for every shared one:
// uv0 is the "use vertex colour" sentinel until projective texturing runs, and
// tangent is the placeholder the renderer's slot needs (meshing has no surface
// parameterisation to derive a real one from, and a slot left unwritten would
// carry whatever the previous, larger mesh put there).
void mcWriteVertex(uint slot, vec3 position, vec3 normal, vec3 color) {
  vertices[slot].position = position;
  vertices[slot].normal = normal;
  vertices[slot].tangent = vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  vertices[slot].uv0 = vec2(-1.0);
  vertices[slot].color = vec4(color, 1.0);
}

// Clamped iso-crossing ratio along the edge sa -> sb. Guards the near-tangent
// case so the ratio stays finite (mirrors the prior engine's copysign(kEpsilon)
// guard); clamp keeps the interpolant on the segment.
//
// NOT symmetric under swapping its endpoints, which is why mcEdgeVertex below
// orders them canonically before calling it. `1 - mcEdgeRatio(sb, sa, iso)`
// equals `mcEdgeRatio(sa, sb, iso)` only in exact arithmetic, and under the
// near-tangent guard not even approximately: at sa = -1e-9, sb = +1e-9, iso = 0
// the guard forces denom to +1e-6 one way and -1e-6 the other, and BOTH
// directions come out at ratio ~1e-3 -- i.e. hugging whichever endpoint was
// passed first, a full edge apart.
float mcEdgeRatio(float sa, float sb, float iso) {
  float denom = sb - sa;
  if (abs(denom) < 1e-6) {
    denom = denom < 0.0 ? -1e-6 : 1e-6;
  }
  return clamp((iso - sa) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// One normal per cell from the 8-corner central-difference gradient (points
// toward increasing distance, i.e. outward); shared by the cell's vertices. The
// 1/(4*voxel_size) scale is dropped -- it cancels under normalization. Falls
// back to +z when the gradient vanishes (a degenerate flat cell).
vec3 mcCellNormal(float sdf[8]) {
  vec3 grad =
      vec3((sdf[1] + sdf[2] + sdf[5] + sdf[6]) - (sdf[0] + sdf[3] + sdf[4] + sdf[7]),
           (sdf[2] + sdf[3] + sdf[6] + sdf[7]) - (sdf[0] + sdf[1] + sdf[4] + sdf[5]),
           (sdf[4] + sdf[5] + sdf[6] + sdf[7]) - (sdf[0] + sdf[1] + sdf[2] + sdf[3]));
  float glen = length(grad);
  return glen > 1e-6 ? grad / glen : vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// The position + colour of the iso-crossing on edge `edge` of the cell whose
// eight corner samples are `sdf` / `corner_color` and whose base voxel is
// `base_voxel` (in GLOBAL voxel coordinates -- see mcWriteTriangle's
// preconditions). The ONE interpolator: mcWriteTriangle calls it, and so do
// both halves of the sharing kernel's vertex claim (the owned-edge pass and
// the +face duplicate path), so a shared vertex and a duplicated one land on
// bit-identical coordinates -- which is what makes sharing a pure vertex-count
// change and leaves every triangle exactly where it was.
//
// Bit-identical needs the endpoints in a CANONICAL ORDER, not merely resolved
// to the same global voxels, and that is what the swap below is for. kEdgeToVert
// lists edges 2/3/6/7 max-corner-first, so one cell's owned +y edge (edge 3 =
// corners {3,0}) is its neighbour's edge 1 (corners {1,2}) -- the same segment,
// traversed in opposite directions. `mix` and mcEdgeRatio are both
// direction-dependent (see mcEdgeRatio's note: under the near-tangent guard the
// two directions land at OPPOSITE ENDS of the edge), so without this the two
// emitters would disagree, by ulps normally and by a whole voxel on a tangent
// cell. Ordering by corner shift is exactly the rule mcEdgeOwner uses to name
// the edge, so the two cannot disagree about which end is which.
//
// A corner whose distance IS the iso-value is the crossing, so the vertex is
// that corner, bit for bit, with that corner's attributes: selected, not
// interpolated, because the ratio reaches the corner only in exact
// arithmetic. At the high end it is (iso - sa) / (iso - sa), which a device's
// division need not round to 1: NVIDIA's and Apple's give 1 - 2^-24 for some
// distances, and not the same ones. mix() then stops 6e-8 of a step short,
// an ulp or more wherever the coordinate is small against the step (the
// corner at 0 comes out at -6e-10). Under the near-tangent guard, an inside
// corner within 1e-6 of the iso-value puts the vertex up to a step away.
// Only a crossing edge's outside corner can be at the iso-value.
//
// The corners are `precise`: each is one correctly rounded product,
// `vec3(ivec3) * vec3(voxel_size)`, before anything uses it, so a selected
// corner is the same bits on every device, and so is what mix() starts from.
// Without it NVIDIA's compiler fused the product into mix() (an FMA) where
// Apple's rounds it first, and an interpolated vertex differed between them by
// an ulp. The voxel size is splatted on purpose: MoltenVK drops `precise` on a
// vector times a scalar (DESIGN.md, Key gotchas), so `* voxel_size` would
// reach Metal unguarded.
void mcEdgeVertex(int edge, float sdf[8], vec3 corner_color[8],
                  ivec3 base_voxel, float voxel_size, float iso, uint has_color,
                  out vec3 position, out vec3 color) {
  int a = edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 0];
  int b = edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 1];
  ivec3 shift_a = mcCornerShift(a);
  ivec3 shift_b = mcCornerShift(b);
  // Edges are axis-aligned, so the shifts differ in exactly one component (0 vs
  // 1): `any(greaterThan(...))` is true precisely when `a` is the high end.
  if (any(greaterThan(shift_a, shift_b))) {
    int swap_corner = a;
    a = b;
    b = swap_corner;
    ivec3 swap_shift = shift_a;
    shift_a = shift_b;
    shift_b = swap_shift;
  }
  precise vec3 pa = vec3(base_voxel + shift_a) * vec3(voxel_size);
  precise vec3 pb = vec3(base_voxel + shift_b) * vec3(voxel_size);
  if (sdf[a] == iso || sdf[b] == iso) {
    bool at_b = sdf[b] == iso;
    position = at_b ? pb : pa;
    color = has_color != 0u ? corner_color[at_b ? b : a] : vec3(1.0);
    return;
  }
  float ratio = mcEdgeRatio(sdf[a], sdf[b], iso);
  position = mix(pa, pb, ratio);
  // LINEAR working values (each kernel decodes at the gather), because this is
  // an average -- the 2026-08-02 colour decision. White is 1.0 either way.
  color = has_color != 0u ? mix(corner_color[a], corner_color[b], ratio)
                          : vec3(1.0);
}

// How many triangles cell `cube_index` contributes.
//
// Separable from the emission because the count is a property of the cube index
// ALONE -- it needs no interpolation and no world position -- which is what lets
// the sparse kernel count a whole block, reserve one range for it, and only then
// write. `tri_table` rows are -1-terminated in groups of three.
//
// The all-inside / all-outside reject stays a comparison on two registers, and
// is not left to the table's own -1. Both are correct today, but only one of
// them stays correct independently of the SSBO the host uploads: `tri_table`
// is DATA, so a truncated or edited `McTables` sends cube index 0 or 255 into
// the walk below and hands back a count for a cell with no surface in it,
// while this comparison cannot be wrong about a cell with no sign change. It
// is the whole check now rather than one of two -- the dense kernel used to
// keep the same guard inline and be the oracle every equivalence test compared
// against, and neither exists any more. It is also the cheap half of the
// counting phase, which runs over 100% of cells while ~92% of them are exactly
// this case.
// The walk is bounded by the row as well as by its terminator, and the bound is
// not belt-and-braces. `tri_table` is an SSBO the host uploads, so the -1 that
// stops this loop is DATA; the 0..5 range is what the sparse kernel packs into
// an 8-bit cache field and, since it reserves per block, what sizes a whole
// block's arena range. A row that lost its terminator would not merely spin --
// it would walk into `corner_offset` (no robustBufferAccess anywhere in this
// tier) and hand out a range the block then overruns. Five is a property of
// marching cubes, not of the upload: 15 of a row's 16 entries, the sixteenth
// always -1.
const int kMaxTrianglesPerCell = 5;

int mcCellTriangleCount(int cube_index) {
  if (cube_index == 0 || cube_index == 255) {
    return 0;  // no sign change -> no surface in this cell
  }
  int n = 0;
  while (n < kMaxTrianglesPerCell && tri_table[cube_index * 16 + n * 3] != -1) {
    ++n;
  }
  return n;
}

// Write the cell's `t`-th triangle (counted in triangles, not table entries)
// into the already-claimed slot `tri`, as three private vertices at `tri * 3`.
//
// The DEFAULT sparse kernel's writer, and its only caller: the sharing kernel
// claims each vertex through its own counter and calls mcEdgeVertex directly,
// because a shared vertex is not at `tri * 3`. What the two do share is
// everything this reaches -- mcEdgeVertex and mcWriteVertex -- so a private
// vertex and a shared one land on bit-identical coordinates carrying identical
// appearance fields. That is why those are one function each and not two: a
// duplicated emitter is what let two paths drift once already, and here a
// drift would separate the two while every triangle count still matched.
//
// The caller reserves the run and passes the slot; this never claims one.
//
// THE PRECONDITIONS, stated here because this is the entry point a third
// caller would reach for and neither is checkable from inside:
//
//   * Corner c's world position is `(base_voxel + cornerShift(c)) *
//     voxel_size`, so the caller passes the cell's base voxel in GLOBAL voxel
//     coordinates -- the base block's own voxel plus the local cell, which is
//     what lets a boundary cell's far corners land on the neighbour's voxels
//     without a second coordinate lookup. A block-RELATIVE base voxel compiles
//     and produces a surface displaced by the block.
//   * `corner_color` is in LINEAR working values (each kernel decodes the
//     canonical 8-bit attribute at the gather, the 2026-08-02 colour decision),
//     because the edge interpolation below is an average. Passing encoded sRGB
//     compiles and darkens every interpolated vertex. It is ignored entirely
//     when has_color == 0, where vertices get opaque white.
//
// Neither shows up as a wrong triangle count, which is what the tests key on.
//
// Winding is reversed (0, 2, 1) so the CCW front face points along the outward
// gradient `normal` -- the orientation gfx expects; colour follows the same
// reversal so each vertex keeps its own edge's colour, and uv0 stays the "use
// vertex colour" sentinel until projective texturing runs.
void mcWriteTriangle(int cube_index, int t, float sdf[8], vec3 corner_color[8],
                     ivec3 base_voxel, float voxel_size, vec3 normal, float iso,
                     uint has_color, uint tri) {
  vec3 p[3];
  vec3 col[3];
  for (int k = 0; k < 3; ++k) {
    mcEdgeVertex(tri_table[cube_index * 16 + t * 3 + k], sdf, corner_color,
                 base_voxel, voxel_size, iso, has_color, p[k], col[k]);
  }
  uint vbase = tri * 3u;
  mcWriteVertex(vbase + 0u, p[0], normal, col[0]);
  mcWriteVertex(vbase + 1u, p[2], normal, col[2]);
  mcWriteVertex(vbase + 2u, p[1], normal, col[1]);
}

#endif  // VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_COMMON_GLSL
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/shaders/marching_cubes_sparse.comp
```
#version 450

// Marching-cubes extraction straight off the sparse VoxelBlockGrid, with three
// PRIVATE vertices per triangle: one WORKGROUP per active block, striding over
// the block's voxels, where each voxel is the base corner of one marching-cubes
// cell. A cell whose base sits at a block's +face reaches its far corners into
// neighbouring blocks, so the block's 2x2x2 +neighbourhood (itself plus its
// seven +x/+y/+z neighbours, -1 when unallocated) is resolved into shared memory
// once per workgroup and read by every voxel.
//
// This is the DEFAULT kernel and what this tier has always done. Its sibling,
// marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp, shares a vertex between the cells that meet
// on an edge; MarchingCubes::create builds exactly one of the two, chosen by
// MarchingCubesConfig::share_vertices. Two kernels rather than one with a push
// constant, because a `shared` array is reserved at pipeline creation whatever a
// push constant later says -- see the note in marching_cubes_sparse_common.glsl,
// which is where everything the two do identically lives.
//
// Because every triangle owns three consecutive vertices at `tri * 3`, the index
// run over this kernel's output IS the identity 0,1,2,...: the host fills it once
// per grow and MarchingCubes::download regenerates it rather than reading back.
//
// Emission is PER BLOCK: the block counts its triangles, reserves one range for
// all of them with a single global atomicAdd, and only then writes, so a block's
// triangles are contiguous in the arena. See the phase notes further down for
// what it costs (a second visit, cheaper than the first).
//
// It is resolved *here* rather than handed over by the host, which is what the
// workgroup-per-block shape exists for. The meshing dispatch is quiescent -- no
// concurrent allocation -- so a probe needs no bucket lock, and 8 probes amortise
// over voxels_per_block cells. The host-built table this replaced was an
// O(active_blocks * 8) serial pass of unordered_map lookups: measured at 102 ms
// of a 133 ms extract at 107k blocks on an M5 iPad Pro, against 26 ms for this
// kernel's own dispatch. Both prior CUDA and Metal implementations of this
// pipeline resolved neighbours on-device the same way.
//
// Only how a vertex slot is claimed differs from the sharing kernel; the
// per-cell body (cube index, gradient normal, reversed-winding triangle
// emission, hybrid vertex colour) is the shared marching_cubes_common.glsl
// both kernels include.
//
// Voxels are node-centred (world = voxel * voxel_size), matching
// tsdf_integrate.comp and volume/voxel_coords.hpp, so the extracted surface
// aligns with the fused field. BlockIndex / Vertex are read/written through
// scalar block layout to match the host structs byte-for-byte (BlockIndex:
// ivec3 coord@0, ptr@12, 16 B; mesh Vertex: position@0, normal@12,
// tangent@24, uv0@40, color@48, 64 B).

#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

// Cross-tier: the voxel colour attribute's format, from the volume tier.
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/voxel_color.glsl"

// One workgroup per block. 256 is fixed rather than sized from
// voxels_per_block, which is a push constant and so cannot set local_size
// without a specialization constant. That is exact at the default block_size 8
// (512 voxels = 2 cells per lane) and wasteful below it -- see the workgroup
// note in main().
layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// The hash entries + the read-only traversal that resolves a neighbouring
// block's voxel-array base, which also supplies the shared BlockIndex /
// HashEntry layouts and hash constants from the volume tier's hash_common.glsl
// (one definition, not a mirror -- see hash_lookup.glsl).
#define VGRID_HASH_ENTRIES_BINDING 2
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_lookup.glsl"

// One mesh vertex (mirrors mesh::Vertex).
struct Vertex {
  vec3 position;
  vec3 normal;
  vec4 tangent;  // renderer's slot; meshing has no parameterisation for one
  vec2 uv0;
  vec4 color;
};

// The marching-cubes tables (mirrors mesh::McTables): the flattened 256x16
// triangle table, the 8 corner offsets, and the 12 edge-endpoint pairs.
layout(set = 0, binding = 0, scalar) readonly buffer Tables {
  int tri_table[4096];    // [256][16]
  int corner_offset[24];  // [8][3]
  int edge_to_vert[24];   // [12][2]
};
// The compacted active blocks -- one WORKGROUP per block, so the 2x2x2
// neighbourhood can be resolved once into shared memory and amortised over every
// voxel of the block (see s_neighbour in block_neighbourhood.glsl).
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer Active {
  BlockIndex active_blocks[];
};
// Binding 2 is the hash entries, declared by the hash_lookup.glsl include above.
// Per-voxel SDF + integration weight (the tsdf tier's attributes), addressed by
// BlockIndex::ptr + local. Color is the packed-RGB attribute (low three bytes,
// unpackUnorm4x8 -> .rgb) read only when pc.has_color != 0 (else a dummy binds).
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, scalar) readonly buffer Tsdf { float tsdf[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, scalar) readonly buffer Weight { float weight[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, scalar) readonly buffer Color { uint color_attr[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, scalar) writeonly buffer Vertices {
  Vertex vertices[];
};
// The draw command's indexCount, which the kernel counts into directly -- one
// atomicAdd per block, in PHASE TWO below, of the whole block's count. The four
// fields after it are host-written once per extract and untouched here, as is
// `vertex_count` (only the sharing kernel allocates through it; here the vertex
// total is exactly three per triangle and the host derives it) and
// `sharing_applied` (only the sharing kernel reports it).
//
// Declared in full down to the one word this kernel does write. A struct that
// stopped at index_count could not name a later field, and naming it by byte
// offset is what the scalar-layout ABI exists to avoid.
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, scalar) buffer DrawCommand {
  uint index_count;
  uint instance_count;
  uint first_index;
  int vertex_offset;
  uint first_instance;
  uint vertex_count;     // the sharing kernel's; untouched here
  uint sharing_applied;  // the sharing kernel's; untouched here
};

layout(push_constant, scalar) uniform PushConstants {
  int block_size;          // voxels per block edge
  int voxels_per_block;    // block_size^3
  float voxel_size;        // metres between adjacent voxels
  float iso;               // iso-value to extract
  uint num_active_blocks;  // active_blocks length
  uint capacity;           // max triangles the index run holds
  float weight_threshold;  // corners below this weight invalidate the cell
  uint has_color;          // 0 = no color input; vertices get opaque white
  // Vertices the arena holds. Declared but UNUSED here, and that is deliberate:
  // this block is one ABI shared with marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp and
  // SparsePushConstants on the host, so omitting a field would shift every
  // offset after it. This kernel needs no bound of its own -- it writes
  // `vertices[tri * 3 + k]` under `tri < capacity`, and the host keeps the two
  // budgets locked at exactly three vertices per triangle whenever sharing is
  // off (see ensure_output_buffers).
  uint vertex_capacity;
  // The hash-table shape, for the on-device neighbour probe. Passed rather than
  // read from a VoxelGridParams block because hash_common.glsl's `pc` would
  // collide with this one -- see hash_lookup.glsl.
  int num_buckets;
  int bucket_size;
  int max_chain;
  // Block slots the grid's heap holds, to bound each block's ptr in one
  // comparison.
  uint num_block_slots;
  uint item_base;  // the first active block this dispatch covers
} pc;

// mcCornerShift / mcCellNormal / mcEdgeVertex / mcCellTriangleCount /
// mcWriteTriangle + the near-tangent edge guard, over the Tables / Vertices /
// DrawCommand bindings declared above.
#include "marching_cubes_common.glsl"

// vgridLocalIndex / vgridLocalBase / s_neighbour / vgridResolveNeighbourhood /
// vgridCornerStorage / mcGather / mcCellSigns -- everything this kernel and the
// sharing one do identically.
#include "marching_cubes_sparse_common.glsl"

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Per-block contiguous emission.
//
// The block counts its triangles, reserves ONE range for all of them with a
// single global atomicAdd, and only then writes -- instead of every triangle
// claiming its own slot. A block's triangles then land CONTIGUOUSLY, and a
// block whose whole range lies past the arena is rejected up front.
//
// Measured on room0 at `--voxel 0.012`, Release, interleaved samples, the
// restructure COSTS ~10% on the extract dispatch (1.17 -> 1.28 ms) against the
// per-triangle append it replaced. TODO(mesh): it was taken as the precondition
// for re-meshing only changed blocks, which the 2026-10-06 decision removed;
// going back to the per-triangle append is a measured follow-up.
//
// The cost is that a cell is visited twice, and the two visits are deliberately
// asymmetric so it is far less than twice the work:
//
//   PHASE ONE runs over 100% of cells and needs only the cube index, so it
//   gathers SIGNS ONLY (mcCellSigns) -- no sdf/colour array copy-out, no sRGB
//   decode -- and caches each cell's triangle count in one byte of a private
//   register.
//   PHASE THREE re-gathers in full, but only the ~8% of cells that actually
//   emit (the emit rate measured flat across a 4x resolution sweep); the other
//   ~92% are rejected on that byte, without touching memory of any kind.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Triangles this block's cells produce, the block's first triangle slot, and the
// cursor handing out slots within the reserved range.
shared uint s_block_tris;
shared uint s_block_base;
shared uint s_cursor;

// Per-cell TRIANGLE COUNT, carried from phase one to phase three so phase three
// can reject a cell without re-gathering its eight corners -- and, since the
// count is what the rejection tests, without walking `tri_table` either. Caching
// the cube index instead would make the rejection an SSBO read on the ~92% of
// cells that emit nothing, which is the path that has to be cheap.
//
// PRIVATE, not `shared`, and that is the whole of it: both phases walk the block
// with the SAME strided loop from the same `tid`, so the cell at slot k --
// `tid + k * group_threads` -- is handled by one invocation in both phases. The
// writer is the only reader, so a `shared` array would buy nothing and cost an
// atomicOr (four cells to a word, four different threads) plus a zeroing pass
// before the barrier. A count is 0..5, so four of them pack into one uint that
// stays in a register, and the cache adds ZERO bytes of `shared`.
//
// Zero bytes matters *here* and not in the vertex-sharing kernel, because this
// is the DEFAULT path: the 2026-08-08 decision split the two precisely so it
// would not carry sharing's ~8 KiB threadgroup budget, and a two-phase emitter
// must not reintroduce it by the back door.
//
// A block with more cells than the slots reach still meshes correctly: phase
// three re-gathers the uncached tail (see the loop below), which is slower but
// not wrong. Every in-tree caller uses block_size 8, where 512 cells over 256
// threads is two slots and nothing is uncached.
//
// Slower, and by enough to matter -- at block_size 16, 3072 of a block's 4096
// cells fall past the four slots and are gathered in FULL twice, so the ~1.08
// gathers per cell this design is chosen for becomes ~1.77. Nothing about that
// is visible from a correct-looking mesh; no caller uses such a block. It is
// not refused, unlike the sharing kernel's kMaxSharedCells -- there an
// oversized block would index past a shared array, here it only costs time.
const uint kCachedSlots = 4u;  // 8-bit counts to a uint

// Which strided iteration `local` is, i.e. which byte of the cache holds it.
// Both phases derive it the same way from the same `tid`; `group_threads` is a
// compile-time constant, so this is a shift.
uint mcCacheSlot(uint local, uint tid, uint group_threads) {
  return (local - tid) / group_threads;
}

void main() {
  int bs = pc.block_size;
  uint vpb = uint(pc.voxels_per_block);
  // The workgroup's linear thread index, and its size. gl_LocalInvocationIndex
  // rather than gl_LocalInvocationID.x, and the full dimension product rather
  // than gl_WorkGroupSize.x, because the two agree only while local_size_y/z
  // are 1. That is true today (the emitted SPIR-V is `LocalSize 256 1 1`) and
  // nothing states it, so a later y/z dimension -- to cut the idle lanes noted
  // below -- would silently race 8*Ny*Nz writers onto the 8 s_neighbour slots
  // and re-mesh every voxel Ny*Nz times through the append atomic. Both forms
  // compile; only this one stays correct.
  uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationIndex;
  uint group_threads =
      gl_WorkGroupSize.x * gl_WorkGroupSize.y * gl_WorkGroupSize.z;

  // One workgroup per block, NOT a flat voxel grid: shared memory is per
  // workgroup, so the neighbourhood can only be shared if every thread here
  // belongs to the same block.
  uint block_i = pc.item_base + gl_WorkGroupID.x;
  if (block_i >= pc.num_active_blocks) {
    return;
  }
  BlockIndex block = active_blocks[block_i];

  // Defensive: the host binds only a list this grid's map compacted, so every
  // ptr is in range; this keeps a corrupted one from reading past the
  // attribute arrays (robustBufferAccess is enabled nowhere).
  // The condition is uniform across the workgroup (every thread reads the same
  // `block`), so this returns as a whole group and reaches no barrier
  // divergently.
  if (block.ptr < 0 || uint(block.ptr) % uint(pc.voxels_per_block) != 0u ||
      uint(block.ptr) / uint(pc.voxels_per_block) >= pc.num_block_slots) {
    return;
  }

  // Zero the reservation state alongside resolving the neighbourhood -- one
  // barrier opens both. s_block_base is zeroed here rather than only on the
  // path that reserves, so it is never read uninitialised. The triangle-count
  // cache takes no pass of its own: it is a private uint, cleared where it is
  // declared below, which is a register write and not a threadgroup one.
  if (tid == 0u) {
    s_block_tris = 0u;
    s_block_base = 0u;
    s_cursor = 0u;
  }
  vgridResolveNeighbourhood(block.coord, block.ptr, tid, pc.num_buckets,
                         pc.bucket_size, pc.max_chain);
  barrier();

  // PHASE ONE -- count, and cache each cell's TRIANGLE COUNT for phase three.
  //
  // Signs only (mcCellSigns): this loop runs over every cell in the block, and
  // the count needs nothing but the cube index. Gathering in full here -- the
  // eight sdf values copied out of an `out float[8]`, and up to 24 sRGB decodes
  // for colours a count cannot use -- would be paid on 100% of cells to be
  // thrown away on ~92% of them.
  //
  // The COUNT is what is cached, not the cube index it came from, and that is
  // deliberate: the count is what phase three's rejection tests, so caching it
  // makes that rejection a shared-memory read, where caching the cube index
  // would make it an SSBO walk of `tri_table` on the ~92% of cells that emit
  // nothing. It also fits in one byte (0..5) where a cube index needs two.
  //
  // Stride over the block's voxels rather than assuming one thread each: the
  // workgroup is a fixed 256 while voxels_per_block is block_size^3 from the
  // grid params, so this is correct for any block size instead of only 8 (512,
  // which would need a 512-thread workgroup and still break at 16).
  //
  // Correct at any block size, but not equally efficient at one. Only
  // voxels_per_block lanes ever enter this loop, so below block_size 8 most of
  // the group idles -- 192 of 256 at block_size 4, 248 of 256 at block_size 2 --
  // and the host's one-workgroup-per-block dispatch multiplies the group count
  // by 256/voxels_per_block (see the dispatch in marching_cubes.cpp). Both
  // costs are booked rather than paid down: sizing the group from
  // voxels_per_block needs a specialization constant plumbed through
  // ComputePipeline::create, and every in-tree caller uses block_size 8, where
