  // this shape is a win. TODO(mesh): revisit if a consumer ships a smaller
  // block.
  uint mine = 0u;
  uint cache = 0u;  // this invocation's first kCachedSlots counts, one per byte
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    int n = mcCellTriangleCount(mcCellSigns(bs, vgridLocalBase(local, bs)));
    if (n != 0) {
      uint slot = mcCacheSlot(local, tid, group_threads);
      if (slot < kCachedSlots) {
        cache |= uint(n) << (slot * 8u);
      }
      mine += uint(n);
    }
  }
  if (mine != 0u) {
    atomicAdd(s_block_tris, mine);
  }
  barrier();

  // PHASE TWO -- one atomic for the whole block.
  //
  // `index_count` is bumped by the block's FULL count whatever `capacity` holds,
  // so it still ends as kIndicesPerTriangle times the field's true triangle
  // total -- the contract the host refits against. Triangles past the arena are
  // simply not written, which is a stronger form of the old
  // count-but-drop: overflow can no longer make the reported total a lower bound
  // by abandoning a cell early, because the count is taken before any slot is.
  if (tid == 0u && s_block_tris != 0u) {
    s_block_base = atomicAdd(index_count, s_block_tris * kIndicesPerTriangle) /
                   kIndicesPerTriangle;
  }
  barrier();

  // Nothing reserved, or the whole reservation lies past the arena. The second
  // is newly PROVABLE per block and worth proving: every slot this block hands
  // out is >= s_block_base, so if that is already past capacity not one
  // triangle of this block can be written, and the alternative is a full
  // re-gather per emitting cell to drop each triangle individually at the
  // bottom of the loop. That is the common case on a first extract and on every
  // refit, where the arena is planned at ~64 triangles per block against a
  // field that can emit ~1400. Both tests are uniform across the workgroup and
  // no barrier follows, so returning here is safe.
  if (s_block_tris == 0u || s_block_base >= pc.capacity) {
    return;
  }
  uint block_end = s_block_base + s_block_tris;

  // PHASE THREE -- emit into the reserved range.
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    // The cheap rejection, and the reason phase one caches at all: a cell with
    // no triangles is skipped WITHOUT gathering its eight corners, which is
    // ~92% of them. Cells past the four slots fall through and gather.
    uint slot = mcCacheSlot(local, tid, group_threads);
    if (slot < kCachedSlots && ((cache >> (slot * 8u)) & 0xFFu) == 0u) {
      continue;
    }
    ivec3 base = vgridLocalBase(local, bs);
    float sdf[8];
    vec3 corner_color[8];
    int cube_index;
    if (!mcGather(bs, base, sdf, corner_color, cube_index)) {
      continue;
    }
    // Recomputed from the cube index just gathered rather than read back from
    // the cache, even though phase one put the same number there. The cache is
    // a REJECTION HINT; this is the count that must match the `tri_table` row
    // mcWriteTriangle is about to walk, and only a count derived from this
    // cube_index is guaranteed to. With the all-inside/all-outside case already
    // rejected on a register, it costs one table read on the ~8% of cells that
    // reach here.
    int n = mcCellTriangleCount(cube_index);
    if (n == 0) {
      continue;
    }
    // Slots within this block's range. The cursor is shared, so the order
    // cells land in is still unspecified -- but every slot it hands out is
    // inside the range, because the range was sized from the same counts.
    //
    // "The same counts" is a convention between two different gathers --
    // mcCellSigns in phase one, mcGather here -- and not something the code
    // enforces, so this bound is what makes a disagreement between them fail
    // SAFE. Without it a range that overran would write over the next block's
    // triangles, with a correct-looking indexCount and no error anywhere: the
    // per-triangle append this replaced could not overrun by construction,
    // because counting and writing were one act, and that guarantee has to be
    // paid for somewhere.
    uint first = s_block_base + atomicAdd(s_cursor, uint(n));
    if (first + uint(n) > block_end) {
      continue;
    }
    vec3 normal = mcCellNormal(sdf);
    for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
      uint tri = first + uint(t);
      if (tri >= pc.capacity) {
        break;  // counted in phase one, dropped here -- and `tri` only grows
      }
      mcWriteTriangle(cube_index, t, sdf, corner_color,
                      block.coord * bs + base, pc.voxel_size, normal, pc.iso,
                      pc.has_color, tri);
    }
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/shaders/marching_cubes_sparse_common.glsl
```
#ifndef VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_SPARSE_COMMON_GLSL
#define VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_SPARSE_COMMON_GLSL

// What both sparse marching-cubes kernels do identically: address a block's
// voxels, resolve its 2x2x2 +neighbourhood on-device, and gather a cell's eight
// corners through it.
//
// TWO kernels, because vertex sharing is a pipeline choice rather than a
// runtime branch. `marching_cubes_sparse.comp` gives every triangle three
// private vertices (what this tier always did); `marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp`
// shares a vertex between the cells that meet on an edge. Sharing needs ~8 KiB
// of `shared` arrays, and a `shared` array is reserved at pipeline creation
// whatever a push constant later says -- so folding the two into one kernel
// made the DEFAULT path pay sharing's threadgroup budget (44 B -> 8452 B, which
// bounds residency to 3 workgroups on Apple's ~32 KiB and to 1 at Vulkan's
// guaranteed 16 KiB floor) plus its per-corner vertex atomic, for a feature it
// does not use. MarchingCubes::create builds exactly one of the two.
//
// Both figures are SPIR-V-verified and both move as the kernels grow, so treat
// the gap rather than the endpoints as the decision: 44 B is s_neighbour plus
// the default kernel's three-word block reservation, and the default kernel
// keeps its per-cell triangle-count cache in a private register precisely so
// this side of the gap stays a rounding error.
//
// The cost of two kernels is two copies of the code that is genuinely common,
// which is what this header exists to prevent: the neighbour probe and the
// corner gather are the cross-block-correctness-critical parts, and a fix to
// either must not be appliable to only one path. Mirrors marching_cubes_common.glsl,
// which plays the same role for the per-cell numerics.
//
// The includer must, *before* the include, declare the `pc` push block (fields
// `block_size`, `voxels_per_block`, `iso`, `weight_threshold`, `has_color`,
// `num_buckets`, `bucket_size`, `max_chain`), the `active_blocks` / `tsdf` /
// `weight` / `color_attr` buffers, and have included hash_lookup.glsl (for
// `BlockIndex` + `vgridFindBlockPtr`, which block_neighbourhood.glsl needs),
// voxel_color.glsl and marching_cubes_common.glsl (for `mcCornerShift`).

// vgridLocalIndex / vgridLocalBase / s_neighbour / vgridResolveNeighbourhood /
// vgridCornerStorage: the block's +neighbourhood and the one cross-block corner
// addressing, from the volume tier, which the codec's surface passes walk too.
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/block_neighbourhood.glsl"

// Gather a cell's eight corners through the shared neighbourhood: sdf values,
// linear colours, and the cube index. False when a corner is unavailable --
// its block unallocated, or the voxel unintegrated (weight below threshold).
//
// On that failure `cube_index` comes back 0, NOT the partial mask the loop had
// accumulated over the corners it did reach. That is load-bearing rather than
// tidy: mcCellTriangleCount reads 0 as "no triangles", so a caller that ignores
// the bool still cannot count, reserve, or emit for a cell whose corners were
// never all read.
bool mcGather(int bs, ivec3 base, out float sdf[8], out vec3 corner_color[8],
              out int cube_index) {
  cube_index = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    uint si;
    if (!vgridCornerStorage(bs, base + mcCornerShift(i), si) ||
        weight[si] < pc.weight_threshold) {
      cube_index = 0;  // drop the partial mask -- see the note above
      return false;
    }
    sdf[i] = tsdf[si];
    if (pc.has_color != 0u) {
      // A depth-integrated but colour-unobserved corner reads opaque white
      // rather than dragging the interpolated vertex toward black, mirroring
      // the integrator's first-observation-assigns anti-darkening rule.
      // Decoded to LINEAR working values, because the edge interpolation is
      // an average (the 2026-08-02 decision).
      corner_color[i] = vgridVoxelColorToLinear(color_attr[si]);
    }
    if (sdf[i] < pc.iso) {
      cube_index |= (1 << i);
    }
  }
  return true;
}

// The cube index ALONE -- what a caller that only needs a cell's TRIANGLE COUNT
// has to read. 0 for a cell whose corners are unavailable, exactly as mcGather
// returns on failure, so an invalid cell and an empty one need no separate
// encoding.
//
// Separate from mcGather rather than a flag on it because what it drops is the
// expensive part, and the sparse kernel's counting phase runs over 100% of
// cells: no `out float[8]` / `out vec3[8]` copy-out (GLSL passes arrays by
// value, so each is a real 128-byte copy at every call), and no colour decode --
// vgridUnpackSrgbToLinear is a transfer curve per corner, up to 24 of them per
// cell, for values a count cannot use.
//
// The sign test below is the one line this shares with mcGather by convention
// rather than by construction, and the two must agree exactly: the count taken
// here reserves the range mcGather's caller then writes into. Both read
// `tsdf[si] < pc.iso` over the same quiescent buffer through the same
// vgridCornerStorage, so they can only diverge if the two lines are edited apart --
// and the emitter bounds its writes to the reserved range, so even that drops
// triangles rather than writing over the next block's.
int mcCellSigns(int bs, ivec3 base) {
  int cube_index = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    uint si;
    if (!vgridCornerStorage(bs, base + mcCornerShift(i), si) ||
        weight[si] < pc.weight_threshold) {
      return 0;
    }
    if (tsdf[si] < pc.iso) {
      cube_index |= (1 << i);
    }
  }
  return cube_index;
}

#endif  // VGRID_MARCHING_CUBES_SPARSE_COMMON_GLSL
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/shaders/marching_cubes_sparse_shared.comp
```
#version 450

// Marching-cubes extraction off the sparse VoxelBlockGrid with IN-BLOCK VERTEX
// SHARING: the cells that meet on an edge index one vertex instead of emitting
// three private ones each. Same surface, same triangles, ~4x fewer vertices.
//
// The sibling of marching_cubes_sparse.comp, which is the default and shares
// nothing. MarchingCubes::create builds exactly one of the two, chosen by
// MarchingCubesConfig::share_vertices -- two kernels rather than one with a push
// constant, because the `shared` arrays below are reserved at pipeline creation
// whatever a push constant later says. Everything the two do identically (the
// neighbourhood probe, the corner gather, the block addressing) is
// marching_cubes_sparse_common.glsl; the per-cell numerics are
// marching_cubes_common.glsl, which the default sparse kernel also includes.
//
// FOUR passes over the block's cells, either side of one reservation. The block
// counts what it will produce,
// reserves ONE vertex range and ONE triangle range with a single atomicAdd each,
// and only then writes -- so its output is contiguous in both buffers and every
// vertex has a deterministic slot. Two ranges rather than the default kernel's
// one, because a shared vertex breaks `v = 3t`.
//
// The phase numbering below is main()'s, so that phase TWO -- the reservation
// itself, one atomic on one lane and no pass over the cells at all -- keeps a
// number here and in the code.
//
//   1.  mcCountCell -- classify (signs only, into `s_case`) and count the
//       vertices this cell OWNS and the triangles it will emit.
//   1b. mcCountDuplicates -- count the vertices it will DUPLICATE. A separate
//       pass because a duplicate is decided by the OWNER cell's state, which
//       phase 1 is still writing.
//   3.  mcOwnedEdgePass -- emit a vertex on each of the three edges the cell
//       OWNS (+x/+y/+z from its base corner). Every edge in the field is owned
//       by exactly one cell (mcEdgeOwner), so after this pass every in-block
//       edge carrying a crossing has exactly one vertex.
//   4.  mcTrianglePass -- emit the cell's triangles as indices into those
//       vertices. An edge whose owner lies outside the block (the +face), or
//       whose owner emitted nothing, is DUPLICATED inline -- which is why the
//       saving is ~4x rather than the ~6x full sharing would give.
//
// The two counting passes run over 100% of the block's cells, so they read the
// eight corner SIGNS (mcCellSigns) and nothing else: no `out float[8]` /
// `out vec3[8]` copy-out and no sRGB decode, for values a count cannot use.
// Passes 3 and 4 read pass 1's `s_case` and gather in full only the cells that
// actually produce something (~8% of them).
//
// Unlike the default kernel, the index run here is NOT the identity: a vertex is
// referenced by several triangles from several cells and only this kernel knows
// which, so it writes the real indices and MarchingCubes::download reads them
// back.

#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require

// Cross-tier: the voxel colour attribute's format, from the volume tier.
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/voxel_color.glsl"

// One workgroup per block. 256 is fixed rather than sized from
// voxels_per_block, which is a push constant and so cannot set local_size
// without a specialization constant. That is exact at the default block_size 8
// (512 voxels = 2 cells per lane) and wasteful below it -- see the workgroup
// note in main().
layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// The hash entries + the read-only traversal that resolves a neighbouring
// block's voxel-array base, which also supplies the shared BlockIndex /
// HashEntry layouts and hash constants from the volume tier's hash_common.glsl
// (one definition, not a mirror -- see hash_lookup.glsl).
#define VGRID_HASH_ENTRIES_BINDING 2
#include "volumetric_kit/grid/volume/shaders/hash_lookup.glsl"

// One mesh vertex (mirrors mesh::Vertex).
struct Vertex {
  vec3 position;
  vec3 normal;
  vec4 tangent;  // renderer's slot; meshing has no parameterisation for one
  vec2 uv0;
  vec4 color;
};

// The marching-cubes tables (mirrors mesh::McTables): the flattened 256x16
// triangle table, the 8 corner offsets, and the 12 edge-endpoint pairs.
layout(set = 0, binding = 0, scalar) readonly buffer Tables {
  int tri_table[4096];    // [256][16]
  int corner_offset[24];  // [8][3]
  int edge_to_vert[24];   // [12][2]
};
// The compacted active blocks -- one WORKGROUP per block, so the 2x2x2
// neighbourhood and the owned-edge table can be shared across the block.
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, scalar) readonly buffer Active {
  BlockIndex active_blocks[];
};
// Binding 2 is the hash entries, declared by the hash_lookup.glsl include above.
layout(set = 0, binding = 3, scalar) readonly buffer Tsdf { float tsdf[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 4, scalar) readonly buffer Weight { float weight[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 5, scalar) readonly buffer Color { uint color_attr[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 6, scalar) writeonly buffer Vertices {
  Vertex vertices[];
};
// The draw command, plus two words of grid scratch past it.
//
// `index_count` IS VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand::indexCount -- the kernel counts
// into the command rather than into a number a host would build one from. The
// three middle fields are host-written once per extract and untouched here.
//
// `vertex_count` sits at byte 20, immediately AFTER the 20-byte command, so the
// vertex allocator needs no second buffer, no second binding and no second
// per-slot allocation -- and `vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect` still reads a
// well-formed command at offset 0, which is all a consumer binds. It cannot be
// derived from `index_count`: that was only ever true because every triangle
// owned three private vertices, which is precisely what this kernel stops doing.
//
// `sharing_applied` at byte 24 is this kernel telling the host it really did
// share. kMaxSharedCells below is a compile-time GLSL constant mirrored by a
// host constant that gates the refusal, and nothing else ties the two together;
// raising the host's alone would admit a block this kernel then meshes UNSHARED,
// silently losing the feature the caller asked for. The host reads this back and
// fails instead. (The unsafe direction -- indexing past the shared array -- is
// closed by the `vpb <= kMaxSharedCells` test in main(), not by this report.)
layout(set = 0, binding = 7, scalar) buffer DrawCommand {
  uint index_count;
  uint instance_count;
  uint first_index;
  int vertex_offset;
  uint first_instance;
  uint vertex_count;
  uint sharing_applied;
};
// The real index buffer -- a property of this dispatch, since a shared vertex is
// referenced by several triangles from several cells.
layout(set = 0, binding = 8, scalar) writeonly buffer Indices { uint indices[]; };

layout(push_constant, scalar) uniform PushConstants {
  int block_size;          // voxels per block edge
  int voxels_per_block;    // block_size^3
  float voxel_size;        // metres between adjacent voxels
  float iso;               // iso-value to extract
  uint num_active_blocks;  // active_blocks length
  uint capacity;           // max triangles the index run holds
  float weight_threshold;  // corners below this weight invalidate the cell
  uint has_color;          // 0 = no color input; vertices get opaque white
  uint vertex_capacity;    // max vertices the arena holds
  // The hash-table shape, for the on-device neighbour probe. Passed rather than
  // read from a VoxelGridParams block because hash_common.glsl's `pc` would
  // collide with this one -- see hash_lookup.glsl.
  int num_buckets;
  int bucket_size;
  int max_chain;
  // Block slots the grid's heap holds, to bound each block's ptr in one
  // comparison.
  uint num_block_slots;
  uint item_base;  // the first active block this dispatch covers
} pc;

// mcCornerShift / mcCellNormal / mcEdgeOwner / mcEdgeVertex + the near-tangent
// edge guard, over the Tables / Vertices / DrawCommand bindings declared above.
#include "marching_cubes_common.glsl"

// vgridLocalIndex / vgridLocalBase / s_neighbour / vgridResolveNeighbourhood /
// mcGather.
#include "marching_cubes_sparse_common.glsl"

// The vertex this block emitted for each cell's three OWNED edges (+x, +y, +z
// from the cell's base corner), or kNoVertex below.
//
// Sized for block_size 8, the only shape any in-tree caller uses and the largest
// this can hold: a shared array needs a compile-time size while voxels_per_block
// is a push constant. Every MarchingCubes extract REFUSES a larger block rather
// letting it index past the end -- the library checks what the caller cannot see
// (the 2026-08-04 rule) -- and main() falls back to unshared as belt and braces,
// reporting through `sharing_applied` so the two constants cannot drift in
// silence.
const uint kMaxSharedCells = 512u;
// No vertex on this edge: it carries no crossing, or its owner cell emitted
// nothing, or the owner lies outside this block. A referencing cell duplicates.
// Also what mcClaimVertex returns when the block's own reservation is already
// spent -- see there.
const int kNoVertex = -1;
// There is deliberately no kVertexDropped any more. It existed because a
// per-vertex global atomic gave a dropped vertex no usable slot, so a
// referencing cell would claim a replacement and double-count -- reporting
// V_owned + ~3T instead of the true ~0.75T, MORE than not sharing at all, and
// the host would then refit a grow-only arena to that. Per-block reservation
// removes the failure at its source: the block counts first and reserves once,
// so every vertex has a deterministic slot whether or not it lands inside the
// arena, and the totals are exact by construction rather than by bookkeeping. A
// slot past `vertex_capacity` is simply not written, and the triangles that
// reference it decline to draw -- see mcTrianglePass.

// Per-block ranges. The block counts its vertices and triangles, reserves ONE
// range of each with a single global atomicAdd, and only then writes -- so a
// block's output is contiguous in both buffers. Sharing needs TWO ranges
// because a shared vertex breaks `v = 3t`.
shared uint s_vtotal;   // vertices this block will create (owned + duplicated)
shared uint s_ttotal;   // triangles this block will emit
shared uint s_vbase;    // first vertex slot, from the global counter
shared uint s_ibase;    // first triangle slot, from the global counter
shared uint s_vcursor;  // hands out slots within [s_vbase, s_vbase + s_vtotal)
shared uint s_icursor;  // ... and within [s_ibase, s_ibase + s_ttotal)
shared int s_edge_vtx[kMaxSharedCells * 3u];
// Phase 1's classification, so every later pass can skip a cell that produces
// nothing without re-reading eight corners -- and, for a cell whose edges are
// all shared, without touching global memory at all. Bits 0..7 are the cube
// index, 0 when the cell is invalid exactly as mcCellSigns returns; bits 8+ are
// mcCellTriangleCount of it, 0..5.
//
// Caching the COUNT beside the index is what lets phase 4 claim a cell's whole
// triangle run with ONE shared atomic instead of one per triangle, and what
// lets phases 2 and 4 walk a `tri_table` row by count rather than each
// re-finding its -1 terminator -- so the row's terminator is walked in exactly
// one place, mcCellTriangleCount, which is also where that walk is bounded
// against a truncated host upload.
//
// `(s_case >> kCaseTriShift) == 0` is then the single test for "this cell emits
// nothing", true of an invalid cell, an all-outside one and an all-inside one
// alike -- and the SAME test in all three passes, which is what stops the
// counting and emitting passes disagreeing about which cells they cover.
// Written on every path through phase 1, so it needs no separate zero-init
// pass.
const uint kCaseTriShift = 8u;
shared uint s_case[kMaxSharedCells];
// mcEdgeOwner's answer for each of the 12 edges: (delta.xyz, axis). A pure
// function of the tables, identical for every cell and every block, so it is
// derived ONCE per workgroup by lanes 0..11 rather than by all 256 lanes and
// then again three times per triangle -- 96 SSBO loads per lane, at the 107k-block
// scale the neighbour-probe decision measured.
shared ivec4 s_edge_owner[12];
// The edge each axis owns (the one whose owner delta is zero) -- {0, 3, 8} under
// this numbering, derived rather than tabulated for the reason mcEdgeOwner is.
shared int s_owned_edge[3];

// Claim one vertex slot from the block's reserved range and write it, returning
// the index -- or kNoVertex when the range is already spent.
//
// Past `vertex_capacity` the vertex is not written, but the slot is still
// consumed and still returned. `vertex_count` therefore ends as the field's true
// total whatever the arena holds -- the contract the host refits against -- and
// a triangle referencing an unwritten slot declines to draw, which
// mcTrianglePass decides by testing the range rather than by a sentinel.
//
// THE BOUND against the block's own reservation is what makes a disagreement
// between the counting and emitting passes fail SAFE, exactly as the sibling
// kernel's range bound does. The two are separate walks over one cached
// classification rather than one act, and one escape exists -- mcOwnedEdgePass'
// "cannot happen" gather, which fails in the UNDER-reservation direction,
// because an owner that emits nothing sends every cell referencing its edges
// down the duplicate path instead. Without this test the surplus would be
// written over the NEXT block's vertices, with exact counters and no error
// anywhere.
int mcClaimVertex(vec3 position, vec3 normal, vec3 color) {
  uint claimed = atomicAdd(s_vcursor, 1u);
  if (claimed >= s_vtotal) {
    return kNoVertex;  // over-consumption: drop rather than overrun
  }
  uint slot = s_vbase + claimed;
  if (slot < pc.vertex_capacity) {
    mcWriteVertex(slot, position, normal, color);
  }
  // Returned even when it lies past the arena: the slot is what a referencing
  // cell must NOT re-claim, and mcTrianglePass tests the range before drawing.
  return int(slot);
}

// PHASE ONE: classify the cell and count what it will produce -- nothing is
// written and nothing is interpolated.
//
// Counting needs the cube index alone, which is why both ranges can be sized
// before a single vertex exists, and why this reads mcCellSigns rather than
// mcGather: it is the pass that runs over 100% of the block's cells, and a full
// gather would copy eight sdf values out of every one of them -- plus up to 24
// sRGB decodes -- for a count that uses none of it. The emit passes below
// re-gather only the ~8% that produce something.
//
// Accumulated into the caller's registers across the whole strided loop and
// pushed to the shared totals once per lane, not once per cell.
void mcCountCell(int bs, uint local, inout uint verts, inout uint tris) {
  int cube_index = mcCellSigns(bs, vgridLocalBase(local, bs));
  int n = mcCellTriangleCount(cube_index);
  s_case[local] = uint(cube_index) | (uint(n) << kCaseTriShift);
  if (n == 0) {
    return;
  }

  // Vertices this cell OWNS: one per owned edge carrying a sign change.
  for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
    int edge = s_owned_edge[axis];
    bool inside_a = (cube_index & (1 << edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 0])) != 0;
    bool inside_b = (cube_index & (1 << edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 1])) != 0;
    if (inside_a != inside_b) {
      ++verts;
    }
  }
  tris += uint(n);
}

// PHASE ONE-B: count the vertices this cell will DUPLICATE.
//
// Separate from mcCountCell, and it has to be: a duplicate is decided by the
// OWNER cell's state, which mcCountCell is still writing. Reading `s_case` in
// the same pass that fills it races, and the race is invisible on a fixture
// whose surface never meets an unintegrated voxel -- it under-reserves the
// block's range, and the cursor then walks off the end of it.
//
// An edge is duplicated when its owner lies outside the block (the +face, where
// sharing would need the neighbouring workgroup) or when the owner emits no
// vertex at all. The second is not an edge case: an owner reaches corners the
// referencing cell does not, so at the frontier of the integrated region it can
// fail its gather while its neighbour succeeds. `(s_case >> kCaseTriShift) == 0`
// is the SAME test mcOwnedEdgePass returns on, so the two cannot disagree about
// which owners emitted; and an owner that DID emit always agrees about this
// particular crossing, because both cells read the same two voxels for the edge.
//
// The row is walked by the count phase 1 cached, from the same table and the
// same cached classification mcTrianglePass walks, so the two cannot disagree
// about how many slots to reserve and how many to consume.
uint mcCountDuplicates(int bs, uint local) {
  uint c = s_case[local];
  uint n = c >> kCaseTriShift;
  if (n == 0u) {
    return 0u;
  }
  int row = int(c & 0xFFu) * 16;
  ivec3 base = vgridLocalBase(local, bs);

  uint dupes = 0u;
  for (uint t = 0u; t < n; ++t) {
    int e = row + int(t) * 3;
    for (int k = 0; k < 3; ++k) {
      ivec3 owner = base + s_edge_owner[tri_table[e + k]].xyz;
      if (!all(lessThan(owner, ivec3(bs))) ||
          (s_case[vgridLocalIndex(owner, bs)] >> kCaseTriShift) == 0u) {
        ++dupes;
      }
    }
  }
  return dupes;
}

// PHASE THREE: emit a vertex on each of the cell's three OWNED edges.
//
// Owned edges are the ones running +x/+y/+z from the cell's base corner, i.e.
// corner 0 to corners 1/3/4 under this repo's corner numbering (the prior
// engine's, ported verbatim). Every edge in the field is owned by exactly one
// cell, so after this pass every in-block edge that carries a crossing has a
// vertex, and phase four does no work for it but a lookup.
void mcOwnedEdgePass(BlockIndex block, int bs, uint local) {
  // Cleared here rather than in a separate pass: this function writes every
  // slot it does not clear, and it runs over exactly the cells this thread will
  // process in phase 2, so a preliminary zero-init loop needed a barrier that
  // synchronised nothing.
  s_edge_vtx[local * 3u + 0u] = kNoVertex;
  s_edge_vtx[local * 3u + 1u] = kNoVertex;
  s_edge_vtx[local * 3u + 2u] = kNoVertex;

  // Classified by mcCountCell, so a cell that emits nothing -- invalid, or with
  // no crossing anywhere in it, so none on its owned edges either -- costs one
  // shared read and no gather at all. That is most of them.
  uint c = s_case[local];
  if ((c >> kCaseTriShift) == 0u) {
    return;
  }
  int cube_index = int(c & 0xFFu);

  ivec3 base = vgridLocalBase(local, bs);
  float sdf[8];
  vec3 corner_color[8];
  int regathered;
  if (!mcGather(bs, base, sdf, corner_color, regathered)) {
    // Cannot happen: mcCellSigns resolved the same eight corners through the
    // same vgridCornerStorage over the same quiescent buffers, and returned
    // non-zero. If it ever does, this cell emits none of the vertices it was
    // counted for, the cells referencing its edges duplicate instead, and
    // mcClaimVertex's bound is what keeps the surplus inside this block.
    return;
  }
  ivec3 base_voxel = block.coord * bs + base;
  // One normal per cell, as before. A shared vertex therefore carries the
  // gradient of the cell that OWNS its edge rather than of each cell that draws
  // it -- the prior engine's behaviour, and the reason sharing changes vertex
  // normals even though it leaves every triangle where it was. A genuine
  // per-vertex normal (the gradient at the crossing) is a further change and is
  // deliberately not folded in here; it deserves its own measurement.
  // TODO(mesh): per-vertex normals now that vertices are shared.
  vec3 normal = mcCellNormal(sdf);
  for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
    int edge = s_owned_edge[axis];
    int a = edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 0];
    int b = edge_to_vert[edge * 2 + 1];
    // Sign change across this edge, read off the cube index we just built.
    bool inside_a = (cube_index & (1 << a)) != 0;
    bool inside_b = (cube_index & (1 << b)) != 0;
    if (inside_a == inside_b) {
      continue;
    }
    vec3 position;
    vec3 color;
    mcEdgeVertex(edge, sdf, corner_color, base_voxel, pc.voxel_size,
                 pc.iso, pc.has_color, position, color);
    // Always a real slot now, in range or not -- see mcClaimVertex.
    s_edge_vtx[local * 3u + uint(axis)] = mcClaimVertex(position, normal, color);
  }
}

// PHASE FOUR: emit this cell's triangles as indices into the shared vertices.
//
// An edge whose owner cell lies inside this block is a lookup. One whose owner
// lies outside -- the block's +face, where sharing would need the neighbouring
// workgroup's shared memory -- is DUPLICATED: emitted inline from this cell's
// own corners. That is the accepted cost of in-block-only sharing, and it is
// why the win is ~4x rather than the ~6x full sharing would give.
void mcTrianglePass(BlockIndex block, int bs, uint local) {
  uint c = s_case[local];
  uint n = c >> kCaseTriShift;
  if (n == 0u) {
    return;  // invalid, or no crossing anywhere in this cell
  }
  int row = int(c & 0xFFu) * 16;

  ivec3 base = vgridLocalBase(local, bs);
  ivec3 base_voxel = block.coord * bs + base;
  // Gathered LAZILY: a cell all of whose edges are shared never touches global
  // memory here, which is most interior cells.
  float sdf[8];
  vec3 corner_color[8];
  vec3 normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  bool have_corners = false;

  // Triangles come from the block's reserved range, not from a per-triangle
  // global atomic, so this kernel's output is per-block contiguous in BOTH
  // buffers.
  //
  // ONE shared atomic for the cell's whole run, off the count phase 1 cached --
  // not one per triangle, which at room0 scale is ~766k threadgroup atomics
  // against ~320k. The cursor is shared, so the order cells land in is
  // unspecified; every slot it hands out is inside the range, because the range
  // was sized from this same count.
  //
  // The bound is what makes a disagreement between the counting and emitting
  // passes fail SAFE, and it is the reason the count is cached rather than
  // recomputed here from a second walk of the row. Without it a run that overran
  // would write over the NEXT block's triangles, with a correct-looking
  // indexCount and no error anywhere: the per-triangle append this replaced
  // could not overrun by construction, because counting and writing were one
  // act, and that guarantee has to be paid for somewhere.
  uint claimed = atomicAdd(s_icursor, n);
  if (claimed + n > s_ttotal) {
    return;
  }
  uint first_tri = s_ibase + claimed;

  for (uint t = 0u; t < n; ++t) {
    // `e` indexes TABLE ENTRIES, not triangles -- the row is walked three
    // entries at a time, and mcCellTriangleCount is what bounded that walk
    // against a truncated host upload when the count was taken.
    int e = row + int(t) * 3;
    // Resolve the three corners of this triangle to vertex indices first, then
    // write -- so a triangle is emitted exactly once whether or not its
    // vertices had to be duplicated.
    int vi[3];
    bool ok = true;
    for (int k = 0; k < 3; ++k) {
      int edge = tri_table[e + k];
      ivec4 owner_info = s_edge_owner[edge];
      ivec3 owner = base + owner_info.xyz;
      int axis = owner_info.w;
      int slot = kNoVertex;
      if (all(lessThan(owner, ivec3(bs)))) {
        slot = s_edge_vtx[uint(vgridLocalIndex(owner, bs)) * 3u + uint(axis)];
      }
      if (slot == kNoVertex) {
        // Duplicate: this cell's own corners describe the same edge, and
        // mcEdgeVertex orders that edge's endpoints canonically, so the
        // position is bit-identical to what the owner would have produced.
        if (!have_corners) {
          int ignored;
          if (!mcGather(bs, base, sdf, corner_color, ignored)) {
            ok = false;
            break;
          }
          have_corners = true;
          normal = mcCellNormal(sdf);
        }
        vec3 position;
        vec3 color;
        mcEdgeVertex(edge, sdf, corner_color, base_voxel,
                     pc.voxel_size, pc.iso, pc.has_color, position, color);
        slot = mcClaimVertex(position, normal, color);
      }
      // The vertex was never written, so a triangle referencing it cannot be
      // drawn: reserved but past the arena, or -- the fail-safe -- past the
      // block's own reservation, which mcClaimVertex reports as kNoVertex.
      // Counted already, in the phase that sized the range.
      //
      // UNSIGNED, so both land above `vertex_capacity`: `slot` round-trips
      // through `int`, and a signed compare would read kNoVertex as -1 and any
      // slot at or beyond 2^31 as negative -- publishing an index far outside a
      // 64-byte-stride arena with robustBufferAccess enabled nowhere.
      if (uint(slot) >= pc.vertex_capacity) {
        ok = false;
      }
      vi[k] = slot;
    }
    uint tri = first_tri + t;
    if (tri >= pc.capacity) {
      continue;  // past the arena; there is no slot to write at all
    }
    uint first = tri * kIndicesPerTriangle;
    if (!ok) {
      // Dropped -- a vertex this triangle needs was never written -- but the
      // slot itself is INSIDE the arena and the draw covers it, so it gets a
      // degenerate triple rather than whatever the arena held before. The
      // counters already carry this triangle.
      indices[first + 0u] = 0u;
      indices[first + 1u] = 0u;
      indices[first + 2u] = 0u;
      continue;
    }
    // Reversed winding (0, 2, 1) so the CCW front face points along the outward
    // gradient, matching mcWriteTriangle and what gfx expects.
    indices[first + 0u] = uint(vi[0]);
    indices[first + 1u] = uint(vi[2]);
    indices[first + 2u] = uint(vi[1]);
  }
}

void main() {
  int bs = pc.block_size;
  uint vpb = uint(pc.voxels_per_block);
  // The workgroup's linear thread index, and its size. gl_LocalInvocationIndex
  // rather than gl_LocalInvocationID.x, and the full dimension product rather
  // than gl_WorkGroupSize.x, because the two agree only while local_size_y/z
  // are 1. That is true today (the emitted SPIR-V is `LocalSize 256 1 1`) and
  // nothing states it, so a later y/z dimension would silently race 8*Ny*Nz
  // writers onto the 8 s_neighbour slots and re-mesh every voxel Ny*Nz times
  // through the append atomic. Both forms compile; only this one stays correct.
  uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationIndex;
  uint group_threads =
      gl_WorkGroupSize.x * gl_WorkGroupSize.y * gl_WorkGroupSize.z;

  // One workgroup per block, NOT a flat voxel grid: shared memory is per
  // workgroup, so the neighbourhood and the owned-edge table can only be shared
  // if every thread here belongs to the same block.
  uint block_i = pc.item_base + gl_WorkGroupID.x;
  if (block_i >= pc.num_active_blocks) {
    return;
  }
  BlockIndex block = active_blocks[block_i];

  // Defensive: the host binds only a list this grid's map compacted, so every
  // ptr is in range; this keeps a corrupted one from reading past the
  // attribute arrays (robustBufferAccess is enabled nowhere).
  // The condition is uniform across the workgroup (every thread reads the same
  // `block`), so this returns as a whole group and reaches no barrier
  // divergently.
  if (block.ptr < 0 || uint(block.ptr) % uint(pc.voxels_per_block) != 0u ||
      uint(block.ptr) / uint(pc.voxels_per_block) >= pc.num_block_slots) {
    return;
  }

  // Belt and braces against a push constant that disagrees with the pipeline it
  // was built for: the host refuses a block this table could not index, and the
  // report tells it whether that refusal is still doing its job (see the
  // DrawCommand block).
  bool sharing = vpb <= kMaxSharedCells;
  if (block_i == 0u && tid == 0u) {
    sharing_applied = sharing ? 1u : 0u;
  }

  if (tid == 0u) {
    s_vtotal = 0u;
    s_ttotal = 0u;
    s_vbase = 0u;
    s_ibase = 0u;
    s_vcursor = 0u;
    s_icursor = 0u;
  }
  vgridResolveNeighbourhood(block.coord, block.ptr, tid, pc.num_buckets,
                         pc.bucket_size, pc.max_chain);
  // Derived once per workgroup by the first 12 lanes, under the same barrier as
  // the neighbourhood: mcEdgeOwner is a pure function of the tables, so having
  // all 256 lanes run its 12-iteration, 96-load loop -- and then call it again
  // three times per triangle -- was that much redundant work per block.
  if (tid < 12u) {
    int e = int(tid);
    ivec3 delta;
    int axis;
    mcEdgeOwner(e, delta, axis);
    s_edge_owner[e] = ivec4(delta, axis);
    if (delta == ivec3(0)) {
      s_owned_edge[axis] = e;  // exactly one edge per axis, so no race
    }
  }
  barrier();

  // Stride over the block's voxels rather than assuming one thread each: the
  // workgroup is a fixed 256 while voxels_per_block is block_size^3 from the
  // grid params, so this is correct for any block size instead of only 8. See
  // the sibling kernel's note for the idle-lane and group-count costs below
  // block_size 8, which apply here unchanged.
  if (!sharing) {
    // Unreachable in practice -- the host refuses this grid before dispatching
    // -- so it meshes nothing rather than carrying a second emission path that
    // no test could reach. `sharing_applied` above is what turns it into a
    // clean host-side error.
    return;
  }

  // PHASE ONE -- classify every cell and size both ranges. Writes nothing but
  // `s_case`. Both counts are accumulated per LANE across the whole strided
  // loop and pushed once, as the sibling kernel does, rather than per cell.
  uint my_verts = 0u;
  uint my_tris = 0u;
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    mcCountCell(bs, local, my_verts, my_tris);
  }
  if (my_verts != 0u) {
    atomicAdd(s_vtotal, my_verts);
  }
  if (my_tris != 0u) {
    atomicAdd(s_ttotal, my_tris);
  }
  // Every cell's classification must be visible before any cell asks whether its
  // edge owners will emit.
  barrier();
  uint my_dupes = 0u;
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    my_dupes += mcCountDuplicates(bs, local);
  }
  if (my_dupes != 0u) {
    atomicAdd(s_vtotal, my_dupes);
  }
  barrier();

  // PHASE TWO -- one atomic per counter for the whole block.
  //
  // Both counters are bumped by the block's FULL totals whatever the arena
  // holds, so each still ends as the field's true total -- the contract the host
  // refits an undersized arena against. It is a stronger form of the old
  // count-but-drop: the totals are taken before any slot is, so an overflow can
  // no longer make either one a lower bound by abandoning a cell part-way.
  if (tid == 0u) {
    if (s_vtotal != 0u) {
      s_vbase = atomicAdd(vertex_count, s_vtotal);
    }
    if (s_ttotal != 0u) {
      s_ibase = atomicAdd(index_count, s_ttotal * kIndicesPerTriangle) /
                kIndicesPerTriangle;
    }
  }
  barrier();

  // Nothing reserved, or a whole reservation lies past its arena. The second is
  // newly PROVABLE per block and worth proving on both buffers: every slot this
  // block hands out is >= its base, so a base already past capacity means not
  // one vertex -- and therefore not one triangle -- of this block can be
  // written, where the alternative is a full re-gather per emitting cell to
  // drop each triangle individually at the bottom of the loop. That is the
  // common case on a first extract and on every refit, where the arena is
  // planned at ~64 triangles per block against a field that can emit ~1400.
  // Both counters were bumped by the block's FULL totals above, so returning
  // here costs the host's refit nothing.
  //
  // Safe because all three terms are read from `shared` AFTER the barrier and
  // are therefore identical in every invocation: the workgroup returns
  // all-or-none. There IS a barrier below, so that is the property that matters
  // -- a per-lane term added to this condition would leave part of the group at
  // it, which is undefined in SPIR-V and in practice a hang.
  if (s_ttotal == 0u || s_ibase >= pc.capacity ||
      s_vbase >= pc.vertex_capacity) {
    return;
  }

  // PHASE THREE -- emit a vertex on every owned edge, into the reserved range.
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    mcOwnedEdgePass(block, bs, local);
  }
  // Every owned edge in this block must be resolved before any cell reads a
  // neighbour's slot -- this barrier is the whole of what makes sharing safe.
  barrier();

  // PHASE FOUR -- emit triangles as indices into those vertices.
  for (uint local = tid; local < vpb; local += group_threads) {
    mcTrianglePass(block, bs, local);
  }
}
```

### src/volumetric_kit/grid/mesh/shaders/mc_args.comp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

// An extract's sizing (MarchingCubes::record_extract): one invocation takes
// the compaction's count -- or the host's, for a list the host counted -- at
// most its bound and 0 behind a closed gate, writes the marching cubes'
// slices, a workgroup a block, and resets the claimed slot's draw command, so
// no count reaches the host before the batch has run. The count and whether
// the gate was open land in the state the finalize reports.

#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
#extension GL_EXT_scalar_block_layout : require

layout(local_size_x = 1) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Counts { uint counts[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) readonly buffer Gates { uint gates[]; };
// The claimed slot's VkDrawIndexedIndirectCommand and the two scratch words
// past it (marching_cubes_sparse.comp's DrawCommand).
layout(set = 0, binding = 2, scalar) writeonly buffer DrawCommand {
  uint index_count;
  uint instance_count;
  uint first_index;
  int vertex_offset;
  uint first_instance;
  uint vertex_count;
  uint sharing_applied;
};
#define VGRID_SLICES_BINDING 3
